ARC01.blurb:
No tickets are sold for this one, but it writes the first draft of the entire archery program. Women's compound archers shoot ranking arrows at a Games for the first time, and their scores seed the debut compound mixed team bracket.

On the recurve side, the men's ranking round hands out the seeds that decide who meets whom later. Kim Woojin topped qualifying at the 2026 Madrid World Cup stage with a 695, and a high seed buys a softer early draw.

The real show starts with the brackets, but the numbers posted here shape every match that follows.

potentialContenders.name: Kim Woojin
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 men's individual gold medalist. He topped qualifying at the 2026 Madrid World Cup stage with 695. If he makes the team, he is a likely top seed.

potentialContenders.name: Brady Ellison
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalist and world No. 2 as of September 2026. A likely contender for a high seed if he makes a home team.

potentialContenders.name: Alexis Ruiz
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 women's compound World Cup Final in Saltillo. Could be a top seed for the debut compound event.

potentialContenders.name: Jyothi Surekha Vennam
potentialContenders.note: Part of India's women's compound team that equalled the world record of 238 at the 2026 Asian Games. A projected contender if she qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Chikitha Taniparthi
potentialContenders.note: Won 2026 Asian Games compound mixed team gold and women's compound team gold. Could appear if India selects her.

ARC02.blurb:
Ranking rounds don't sell tickets, but this morning's scores hand out the most valuable thing in the early bracket: a favorable draw. Men's compound archers shoot for the first time at a Games, and their totals seed the debut compound mixed team event.

Women's recurve qualifying matters just as much. The best score earns a 1/32 opponent who is the weakest in the field, and a seed that stays soft into the sharp end of the draw.

The Korean women have owned this event for years, and this is where the rest of the field first gets measured against them.
ARC02.potentialContendersIntro: Men's compound and women's recurve hold ranking rounds. The 2028 names below are projections based on 2025 and 2026 form.

potentialContenders.name: Kang Chaeyoung

potentialContenders.name: Zhu Jingyi

potentialContenders.name: Marie Horackova

potentialContenders.name: Nico Wiener
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 men's compound World Cup Final, the first Austrian champion there. Likely contender for a high compound seed.

potentialContenders.name: Sahil Jadhav
potentialContenders.note: Won compound mixed team and men's compound team gold at the 2026 Asian Games. Could help seed India's compound push.

ARC03.blurb:
Everything about this night is a first. Compound archery has never produced a medal at a Games, and the mixed team gold match is the opening medal event of archery in 2028. The whole bracket, from the 1/8 round to the gold match, is squeezed into one evening.

India is the story to follow. It has never won an archery medal at the Games, and its compound archers have said they hope this event delivers the first. At the 2026 Asian Games, Chikitha Taniparthi and Sahil Jadhav beat Korea 20-19 in a shoot-off after a 157-157 tie.

Compound bows with pulleys, magnifying sights and release aids rarely miss, so expect scorelines decided by a single millimeter.
ARC03.potentialContendersIntro: Twelve mixed teams will shoot, each pairing one man and one woman from a single nation. Projections below reflect 2026 form and are not confirmed rosters.

potentialContenders.name: Chikitha Taniparthi
potentialContenders.note: Won 2026 Asian Games compound mixed team gold with Sahil Jadhav, which secured India a place at the 2028 Games. A likely member of India's pair.

potentialContenders.name: Sahil Jadhav
potentialContenders.note: Won compound mixed team and men's compound team gold at the 2026 Asian Games. Likely contender if he is selected.

potentialContenders.name: Alexis Ruiz
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 women's compound World Cup Final in Saltillo. The host nation has one compound mixed team place if it enters the 2027 World Championships.

potentialContenders.name: Nico Wiener
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 men's compound World Cup Final, Austria's first. Could appear if Austria qualifies a team.

potentialContenders.name: Kang Yeon-seo
potentialContenders.note: A 15-year-old compound archer who made Korea's squad for the 2026 Asian Games. A wild-card storyline if Korea qualifies.

ARC04.blurb:
The 1/32 round is the first session where the brackets are real, and early morning archery has a feel of its own. Dozens of targets, dozens of matches, and a favorite can disappear in a single bad end.

This is the first chance to see the Paris 2024 champions, Kim Wu-Jin and Im Si-hyeon, in elimination play. Im's place is not guaranteed, though, since she finished 10th at Korea's 2026 trials and missed the national team.

The newcomers are worth tracking too. India's Kumkum Mohod won the 2026 Asian Games title at 17, and Dhiraj Bommadevara won the 2026 World Cup Final.
ARC04.potentialContendersIntro: Both men's and women's recurve individuals open here. Paris 2024 champions headline the field, but 2028 participation is not confirmed.

potentialContenders.name: Kim Wu-Jin

potentialContenders.name: Im Si-hyeon

potentialContenders.name: Brady Ellison

potentialContenders.name: Kumkum Mohod

potentialContenders.name: Dhiraj Bommadevara
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 World Cup Final in Saltillo, 6-5 in a shoot-off over Junya Nakanishi. Likely contender if he qualifies.

ARC05.blurb:
The sun is down, the lights are on, and the 1/32 matches give way to the 1/16 round. This is where the field starts to shrink and the big names meet real opposition.

Kim Woojin is the draw. Korea's most decorated athlete at the Games has five golds, and the 1/16 is the first stage where an upset can end the story early. Mete Gazoz, the Tokyo 2020 champion, won the 2026 Madrid World Cup stage, so a rematch between them would be worth the walk.

Carson Stadium hosted the 2003 FIFA Women's World Cup final, and there is something fitting about archery filling it under lights.

potentialContenders.name: Zhu Jingyi

ARC06.blurb:
Sunday morning at Carson brings a full slate of 1/32 and 1/16 matches, and the scores can swing on one arrow. It's the sort of session where you pick a target, follow one archer, and watch the whole match develop.

Korea won every recurve gold in Paris, but the cracks are showing. Triple gold medalist Lim Sihyeon finished 10th at the 2026 trials and missed the team. Kang Chaeyoung, the 2025 world champion, leads a new wave, while Lee Woo-seok keeps the men's side humming after his 2026 Asian Games individual gold.

Morning light and a half-empty-feeling schedule make this a good value pick.
ARC06.potentialContendersIntro: Individuals from both genders shoot in this block. Korea's selection fights are ongoing, so every 2028 name here is a projection.

potentialContenders.name: Lee Woo-seok

potentialContenders.name: Kang Chaeyoung

potentialContenders.name: Oh Yejin
potentialContenders.note: Won 2026 Asian Games individual silver and Madrid World Cup bronze. A projected member of Korea's women's squad.

potentialContenders.name: Im Si-hyeon
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 triple gold medalist. She finished 10th at the 2026 trials, so a 2028 spot would be a comeback.

ARC07.blurb:
For American fans, the headline might be Brady Ellison on home soil. The Paris 2024 silver medalist lost the gold match to Kim Wu-Jin in a shoot-off, and the 2028 Games would give him a home crowd to chase that unfinished business.

This evening session works through 1/32 and 1/16 matches for both genders, so you'll see a mix of names over a few hours. Lisa Barbelin, the French bronze medalist in Paris, would arrive with a crowd of her own supporters.

Mete Gazoz is the sleeper. The Tokyo 2020 champion lost to Kim in Paris, but won the 2026 Madrid World Cup stage.

ARC08.blurb:
A session for women's recurve alone means no men's matches to split your attention, just the strongest women's field in the sport shooting one after another. It runs a short two hours and change, perfect for a morning with a purpose.

The big question is who fills the Korean shadow. Im Si-hyeon won Paris gold over teammate Nam Su-hyeon, but neither was on Korea's 2026 national team. Kang Chaeyoung, the 2025 world champion, is the new standard, with China's Zhu Jingyi and Czechia's Marie Horackova pushing hard.

And keep an eye out for India's Kumkum Mohod, the 17-year-old Asian Games champion.
ARC08.potentialContendersIntro: Women's recurve only. 2028 participation is not confirmed for anyone; the list reflects 2025 and 2026 form.

potentialContenders.name: Kumkum Mohod

potentialContenders.name: Im Si-hyeon

ARC09.blurb:
Korean men have won recurve team gold at three straight Games, and Kim Woojin has been on all of them. He and Kim Soo-nyung are the only archers with three consecutive team golds. This evening, he could be chasing a fourth.

The challengers are growing teeth. France took silver in Paris and lost 5-3 to Korea in the Madrid 2026 World Cup final. The U.S., with Brady Ellison, took silver at the 2025 Worlds. India reached the 2026 Asian Games final.

Quarterfinals through gold fit in under four hours, and the team format means three archers pushing each other through every end.

potentialContenders.name: Dhiraj Bommadevara

ARC10.blurb:
The men's recurve bracket starts to thin on Tuesday morning, and this is the first time the best archers face real danger. A 1/16 match is a long walk from a medal, but also close enough for a shocking exit.

Kim Woojin posted a 695 to top Madrid 2026 qualifying but was still hunting his first individual medal of that season. Lee Woo-seok just won Asian Games gold. India's Dhiraj Bommadevara and Neeraj Chauhan are riding momentum from a breakthrough year.

Men's team medal matches are tonight, so arrive early and stay for the evening.

ARC11.blurb:
Korea's women have a deep tradition at team archery, but the cracks showed in 2026. India beat Korea 5-3 in the Asian Games team final, ending Korea's run of seven straight titles at that event. Korea answered by winning the Madrid World Cup team title, 5-1 over the USA.

The field is more open than at any time in recent memory. Chinese Taipei won 2025 world team gold, and India's women are riding a surge. Korea's squad may not include Paris gold medalists Lim Sihyeon or Nam Su-hyeon.

Medal rounds from the quarterfinals through gold fit into one night, so the pressure builds with every round.

ARC12.blurb:
Mixed team recurve is a sprint: one man, one woman, four arrows each, and no room to hide. The 1/8 round is the first time we see which pairs have chemistry, and this is the quickest format in the sport.

Spain is the benchmark. Elia Canales and Andres Temino won the 2025 world title by beating Korea in Gwangju, and then won the Madrid 2026 World Cup stage. Korea's Kim Woojin and Oh Yejin lost to Spain in the Madrid quarterfinals. That sets up the format's central tension.

Two mixed team events now exist, and this one decides its gold a few days after the compound debut.

ARC13.blurb:
It took 12 arrows to separate Spain from Korea in the 2025 world final, and mixed team has produced some of the sport's best finishes. A quarterfinal can come down to a single arrow, and a gold medal match can be decided by a shoot-off.

Korea won this event in Paris, with Germany second and the U.S. third, but the field has since changed. Spain's Elia Canales and Andres Temino beat Korea's An San and Kim Woojin at the 2025 Worlds, even after the Koreans set a qualification record of 1393.

Revenge and upset live side by side on Wednesday night.

ARC14.blurb:
By the 1/8 round, the draw has done its damage and the men's field starts to feel like a medal race. One bad end sends a favorite home, and the crowd gets to see a short, intense two hours of elimination.

Andres Temino, Spain's 2025 world champion, will be one of the targets everyone aims at. Brady Ellison, ranked world No. 2 in September 2026, would be shooting before a home crowd, and the roar for him could be the loudest of the day. Mete Gazoz and Dhiraj Bommadevara add experience and recent momentum.

The sharp end of the bracket begins here.

ARC15.blurb:
Eight archers, three rounds, and one gold. It all comes down to a night where the nerve of a three-time world champion and the nerve of a home favorite might collide.

Kim Woojin beat Brady Ellison in a shoot-off for Paris gold, the closest finish a final can have. Ellison would love another shot, this time before a home crowd. But Andres Temino is the reigning world champion, Dhiraj Bommadevara won the 2026 World Cup Final, and Junya Nakanishi has finished runner-up in both the World Cup Final and the Asian Games.

One arrow, one target, 27,000 people holding their breath.

ARC16.blurb:
The Paris 2024 triple gold medalist, Im Si-hyeon, finished 10th at Korea's 2026 national team trials and missed the squad. That is how deep the Korean women's program runs, and it is why this morning session is worth your time. Even the sport's best nations could lose a champion before the 2028 Games begin.

The 1/8 round is where the bracket turns brutal. Sixteen archers remain, and a 5-set match can hinge on a single nine that should have been a ten. Arrows thud into the target at 70 meters while the sun climbs over a soccer stadium built for 27,000.

Come early, sit close, and watch the field thin out before the evening crowds arrive.

ARC17.blurb:
The last medal match of archery at the 2028 Games will be decided under the lights in Carson. One arrow from one woman will close the whole program.

The Korean women have owned this event, and Paris 2024 ended in an all-Korean final between Im Si-hyeon and Nam Su-hyeon. Now Kang Chaeyoung is the reigning world champion, while Marie Horackova of Czechia arrives with a 6-0 win in the 2026 World Cup Final. Teenager Kumkum Mohod of India could chase a first archery medal for her country.

The stadium hosted the 2003 FIFA Women's World Cup final and will seat 27,000 for this. When the stands go quiet for a shoot-off arrow, you will hear every breath.

ATH01.blurb:
Four rounds of one race, all on one day, and this is where the climb begins. The women's 100m opens with a preliminary round for lower-ranked sprinters, then Round 1, before the semifinal and final that evening.

Morning at the Coliseum means sun, space to wander and no pressure yet. Pole vault qualifying puts Mondo Duplantis, whose world record now stands at 6.31m, on the runway early, while Camryn Rogers could be swinging in hammer qualifying if she makes the team.

This is the session for spotting names before the stakes rise. Pick a sprinter you've never heard of, and see if she's in the final by dark.

ATH02.blurb:
Melissa Jefferson-Wooden ran 10.61 to win the 2025 world title, a championship record, and now the women's 100m final lands on the first night of athletics. That has never happened at a Games before.

The shot put and the men's 10,000m final share the evening, so the Coliseum gets raw power and long-haul patience in the same sitting. In the circle, Jessica Schilder beat Chase Jackson by eight centimeters at the 2025 worlds, and that rivalry travels well.

With about 77,500 seats around a bowl that has hosted two Games already, the semifinals are the warm-up. The real noise comes at the final.

potentialContenders.name: Chase Jackson
potentialContenders.note: Silver at the 2025 worlds with 20.21m, only eight centimeters short. Named a nominee for 2026 Women's World Athlete of the Year.

ATH03.blurb:
The women's 800m repechage is the safety net, and it punishes complacency. Runners who miss automatic qualification get one more crack at a semifinal place, so a favorite's stumble in Round 1 can turn into a nervy morning.

That makes this a good session for watching big names handle pressure at 9 a.m. Femke Bol, who left the 400m hurdles for the 800m in 2026 with these Games as her stated target, is exactly the kind of name that makes any round worth a look.

Around it, the decathlon opens with the 100m, long jump and shot put. The mixed 4x400m relay begins with heats, where the US set a world record in Paris.
ATH03.potentialContendersIntro: These are projections for the women's 800m, the session's marquee track event. Most of these names would hope to be through before the repechage.

ATH04.blurb:
The men's 100m final is wide open in a way it hasn't been in years. Noah Lyles, the Paris champion, ended 2026 early after a strain at the U.S. Championships, while Kenny Bednarek won the Ultimate Championship in 9.85 and Oblique Seville owns the 2025 world title.

Nothing about the rest of this session lets you breathe. The men's shot put and women's hammer finals fill the infield, and the mixed 4x400m final brings a baton chase that the Netherlands won in Paris after the US set a record in the heats.

It's late Sunday afternoon in the Coliseum, and when the sprinters settle into the blocks, the whole bowl goes still.

ATH05.blurb:
Five centimeters. That was the gap between Leyanis Pérez Hernández and Thea LaFond in the 2025 world triple jump final, 14.94m to 14.89m, with Yulimar Rojas only another 13 back.

A triple jump final in a morning session is a rarity, and the sun already beating down on the Coliseum makes it feel like a different event. Hop, step, jump, and a slow crowd clap that builds with every runway.

The track side has stakes too. The men's 400m hurdles repechage means a fast man who clips a barrier gets a second try, and that's where reputations get a little sweaty.
ATH05.potentialContendersIntro: Focus is on the women's triple jump final. These are projections, and Paris 2024 bronze medalist Jasmine Moore has stepped away to recover, with a return expected in 2027.

ATH06.blurb:
Mondo Duplantis doesn't just win pole vault, he raises the bar on his own record. After 6.31m in 2026, the question here is how high the bar goes in front of a Coliseum crowd that learns the clap-hush-run rhythm in about two jumps.

There's history in the infield and a first on the track. The mixed 4x100m relay debuts at the Games with Round 1 and the final in one session, a short sprint of baton exchanges where one bad handoff ends it.

Women's 800m semifinals bring Audrey Werro's 1:53.70, and the decathlon wraps up with the 1500m, where the points race is decided.
ATH06.potentialContendersIntro: These are projections for the men's pole vault final and the women's 800m semifinals, based on recent form rather than confirmed rosters.

ATH07.blurb:
If you want to see the fastest 110m hurdler alive, here's his first round. Ja'Kobe Tharp ran a world-record 12.75 at the 2026 NCAA Championships and broke 13 seconds six times that year.

Morning heats give you a different kind of Games, with no medals to hand out but hurdles flying and a crowd that's mostly there for the sport itself. Pole vault qualifying lets you see Katie Moon, three-time world champion, find her rhythm.

Men's triple jump qualifying and the first rounds of the women's 400m and men's steeplechase fill out a day for people who like to say they saw it early.

ATH08.blurb:
The women's 800m has become the most fascinating race in the sport. Lilian Odira won the 2025 world title in a championship-record 1:54.62, Audrey Werro followed with a world-leading 1:53.70 in 2026, and Keely Hodgkinson still owns the Paris gold.

Then Femke Bol turns up, a hurdler on a mission, aiming her peak at these Games. Two laps of tactics, with the Coliseum roaring on the final bend.

Beatrice Chebet's 5000m, if she returns from having a baby as expected in 2027, adds a world-record holder to the card. The men's high jump and discus finals fill the infield.
ATH08.potentialContendersIntro: The headline is the women's 800m final, with the women's 5000m also on the card. All 2028 entries are projections, and Chebet's return is expected but not confirmed.

ATH09.blurb:
One medal gets decided at breakfast time, and it's a fun one. The women's 3000m steeplechase mixes tactics, barriers and the water jump, which draws a gasp every time somebody lands a bit short.

It's a session for the curious fan, with repechages that decide who survives and who goes home. Men's and women's 400m and the men's 200m all hand out a second chance, and Busang Collen Kebinatshipi, the 2025 world champion in 43.53, would prefer not to use his.

Women's long jump qualifying shows off Tara Davis-Woodhall, world champion at 7.13m, hunting a clean first jump.
ATH09.potentialContendersIntro: These are projections for the women's steeplechase final and long jump qualifying. Participation in 2028 is not confirmed.

ATH10.blurb:
Two of the best races on the program share one evening. In the men's 400m hurdles, Rai Benjamin beat Karsten Warholm in Paris, took the 2025 world title in 46.52 after an overturned disqualification, and still has Warholm's 45.94 world record to chase.

The men's 1500m is the other one, with Cole Hocker, Josh Kerr and Jakob Ingebrigtsen reuniting. Hocker won in Paris, Kerr set a world mile record of 3:42.66 in 2026, and Ingebrigtsen is back from Achilles surgery.

The women's discus and men's long jump finals fill the stadium's infield, and in a hurdles final you can hear every barrier hit.

ATH11.blurb:
A teenage javelin thrower from China may be the most intriguing name on the card. Yan Ziyi opened her 2026 season with 71.74m, an Asian and world U20 record that sits second on the all-time list, and she followed it with Diamond League and Asian Games titles.

The qualifying morning shows you the thrower close up, run-ups and all, while the men's 3000m steeplechase final is the day's medal race. Soufiane El Bakkali is the Paris champion, and the Coliseum will hear every splash at the water jump.

Men's 800m Round 1 puts Emmanuel Wanyonyi on the track, a 1:41.86 championship record holder from the 2025 worlds.
ATH11.potentialContendersIntro: These are projections for the men's steeplechase and 800m and the women's javelin and high jump qualifying. Nothing is confirmed for 2028.

ATH12.blurb:
Sydney McLaughlin-Levrone set the 400m hurdles world record of 50.37 in Paris, took 2026 off to have her daughter, and is expected back in 2027. Whether she's in the Coliseum for this final is one of the great questions of the Games.

If she isn't, the race still has bite. Anna Cockrell, the Paris silver medalist, led the world in 2026 at 52.13, and Femke Bol has left the hurdles to chase the 800m.

The hammer final, with Ethan Katzberg's 84.70m championship record, and the pole vault final make this a three-medal evening for people who love variety.

ATH13.blurb:
Pedro Pichardo has turned the men's triple jump into a duel of nerves. The Portuguese jumper took Paris silver, then won the 2025 world title, and the Díaz brothers of Spain and Italy are chasing the same pit.

The heptathlon opens in the same morning with the 100m hurdles and high jump, so the stadium sees a two-day grind begin. The 100m hurdles Round 1 includes world record holder Masai Russell, a fast field for a morning.

Men's 5000m Round 1 and the 800m repechage add running to a session where jumpers and multi-eventers get plenty of time in the sun.

ATH14.blurb:
Letsile Tebogo told Kenny Bednarek and Noah Lyles in November 2026 to get used to running behind him. By this evening, the men's 200m final could settle the argument in front of a Coliseum crowd that will have waited a week.

The 110m hurdles final is the other showstopper, with Ja'Kobe Tharp's 12.75 world record. Lyles won his fourth world 200m title in 2025, but his 2026 ended early with injury, so his status is uncertain.

The women's 10,000m final, a 25-lap grind, adds the long-distance drama, and Agnes Ngetich is the name on the lips of distance fans.

ATH15.blurb:
Three sprint finals and a long jump in four hours is the best way to spend a Saturday afternoon. The women's 200m final could belong to Melissa Jefferson-Wooden, whose 21.47 in 2026 sits third on the all-time list.

The 400m finals bring a different edge. Busang Collen Kebinatshipi ran 43.53 to win the 2025 world title and 43.39 at the 2026 Ultimate Championship, and the women's race could feature Marileidy Paulino.

Meanwhile, Tara Davis-Woodhall's long jump final and the heptathlon's closing 800m run alongside the sprints. Bring a hat, sunscreen and a loud voice.
ATH15.potentialContendersIntro: Contenders are for the women's 200m, the 400m finals and the women's long jump. These are projections, and Sydney McLaughlin-Levrone's return from a 2026 break is expected but unconfirmed.

ATH16.blurb:
Nine hundredths of a second. That's all that separated Emmanuel Wanyonyi, Djamel Sedjati and Marco Arop at the 2025 world championships, and the men's 800m final could be decided by even less.

Around it, the medals keep coming: women's high jump, javelin and 1500m, then the men's 4x100m, where Canada, the Paris 2024 champion, could try to defend a gold nobody saw coming. Watch the javelin runway too, where China's Yan Ziyi has thrown 71.74m, second on the all-time list.

The Coliseum is an open bowl, and the late-afternoon sun lingers on the track. A tight 800m homestretch in a stadium that has hosted two earlier Games should be loud.

ATH17.blurb:
Jakob Ingebrigtsen had Achilles surgery in February 2026 and was back by August, beating Cole Hocker in the 5000m at the Ultimate Championship by eight-tenths of a second. The rematch is the story of this afternoon.

This is also the last stadium session of the Games, so it rushes: Masai Russell and the 100m hurdles, the men's javelin, and two 4x400m finals to close. Botswana beat the United States for 2025 world gold in the men's race. The US women could be favorites if Sydney McLaughlin-Levrone is on the anchor leg again.

Stay for the final handoffs. The roar builds around the bowl with every lap.
ATH17.potentialContendersIntro: Contenders are for the men's 5000m, women's 100m hurdles, men's javelin and the 4x400m relays. The 2025 and 2026 results are confirmed, but who actually competes in 2028 is not.

ATH18.blurb:
Maria Perez debuted at the half-marathon walk distance in August 2026 and walked away with a world record of 1:30:06. Now imagine her doing that with a medal on the line, on a morning when two races share one session and neither has a heat to hide behind.

This is the first time the Games have asked walkers to cover 21.1 km instead of 20, and the extra distance rewards patience and punishes anyone who burns early. Judges watch every stride for lifted feet and bent knees, and a single late red card can wreck a podium run. Get a spot along the course at 7:30 a.m. and you will hear the rhythmic scuff of shoes long before the lead pack appears.

The course and venue have not been announced, and the order of the two races is still to be set. But the road events take over after the track program ends, and this is where the walkers get their own stage.
ATH18.potentialContendersIntro: The women's and men's half-marathon walks are both on this card. Paris 2024 20 km medalists set the baseline, but the new distance and the qualifying window running to June 2028 mean the final field is far from settled, so these are projections.

ATH19.blurb:
Two years out, no marathon field is harder to read. Tigst Assefa ran 2:11:04 in Berlin, the third-fastest time ever, then tore her Achilles late in the race and reportedly had surgery the next day. Paris champion Sifan Hassan pulled out of London with an Achilles problem of her own.

That opens the door for Fotyen Tesfay, who ran 2:10:51 in her Barcelona debut, and for Chicago winner Hawi Feysa. Nobody knows yet who will be the favorite.

You stand at the roadside, not in a stadium seat, with the beach, the palms and the Pacific behind you at 7:15 a.m. The finish and full route have not been announced.
ATH19.potentialContendersIntro: Paris 2024 gold, silver and bronze medalists lead the confirmed history, but 2028 rosters are open and injuries cloud the picture. These are projected contenders, not confirmed entries.

ATH20.blurb:
The Games close their athletics program with a question the sport didn't have to ask until recently: how fast is too fast? Sabastian Sawe ran 1:59:30 in London, the first sub-two-hour marathon in a race.

He could meet Tamirat Tola, the Paris champion, on the boardwalk. Tola is 2:02:59 and 2:03:10 fast this year, and he won Paris by pulling away on the course's steepest climb. The 2028 route has not been announced, so nobody knows what kind of race it will be.

The final morning is a roadside party at 7:15 a.m. on Venice's famous boardwalk, the beach and palm trees behind you and no stadium walls. Whoever wins closes the athletics program.
ATH20.potentialContendersIntro: Tola's Paris 2024 gold is confirmed. Everything else here is projection from 2026 form, and none of these runners is confirmed for 2028.
