BDM01.blurb:
Seventy-one wins, one loss. An Se-young's 2026 through the Korea Open reads like a typo, and opening morning at Galen Center is where the Paris 2024 champion could start showing she can carry that form to the Games.

Group play is the sport's soft launch. Nobody is sent home lightly, but the draw starts to take shape, and doubles, mixed and singles all share this block, so one seat lets you sample the whole sport.

The arena holds about 10,000 across two decks, close enough that you hear the shuttle crack off a smash. At 8 AM on a Saturday, that sound is the first real shot of the badminton competition.
BDM01.potentialContendersIntro: This session includes men's and women's singles, so the names to watch are the sport's top singles players. The 2028 field is not set, so all of these are projections.

potentialContenders.name: An Se-young
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 women's singles champion and 2026 world champion. She was 71-1 in 2026 through the Korea Open, with a 55-match winning streak at that point. She is the clear favorite if she is healthy.

potentialContenders.name: Akane Yamaguchi
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world champion and 2026 world runner-up. She lost the 2026 Korea Open final to An, her 11th straight loss to the Korean, so she could be a projected chaser.

potentialContenders.name: Christo Popov
potentialContenders.note: Became the first French men's singles world No. 1 after winning the 2026 French Open. A likely contender if he qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Alex Lanier
potentialContenders.note: 2026 men's singles world champion. With Viktor Axelsen retired, he is projected to be among the favorites for a title that will change hands.

BDM02.blurb:
Nobody has a mixed doubles crown to defend. Zheng Siwei and Huang Yaqiong, who beat Korea 21-8, 21-11 in the Paris 2024 final, retired in December 2025, so every pair walking onto the court in this session is chasing a vacant title.

That makes the afternoon a scouting mission. The rallies are fast and low, with mixed pairs trading drives at the net and the rear court taking turns on the attack. Women's doubles and women's singles share the block.

The Galen Center is small enough that you can follow the footwork, not just the shuttle. Pick a court and watch which partner takes control.
BDM02.potentialContendersIntro: For mixed doubles, the 2026 results point to a handful of pairs that could be ones to watch, though 2028 qualification is still open.

potentialContenders.name: Thom Gicquel / Delphine Delrue
potentialContenders.note: 2026 world champions who also won the Hylo Open in November 2026. They are a likely contender if they keep their partnership.

potentialContenders.name: Feng Yanzhe / Huang Dongping
potentialContenders.note: 2026 world runners-up and French Open champions, so a strong projected medal threat.

potentialContenders.name: Jiang Zhenbang / Wei Yaxin
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 Korea Open as top seeds, beating Gao Jiaxuan and Wu Mengying 21-16, 21-13.

potentialContenders.name: Chen Tang Jie / Toh Ee Wei
potentialContenders.note: Won Malaysia's first mixed doubles world title in 2025. They could be a danger if they qualify.

BDM03.blurb:
The Korean women's doubles team of Baek Ha-na and Lee So-hee became the first Korean pair in 31 years to win a world title. An evening at Galen Center is a good place to see whether that was a breakthrough or the start of a run.

This is the night for doubles purists. Men's and women's pairs attack, defend and rotate at a pace that makes singles look slow, and the singles groups mix in on the other courts.

Stay for the late matches. When the building is full and loud after a long Saturday, a three-game group match can feel like a final.
BDM03.potentialContendersIntro: The headline events here are men's and women's doubles, where 2026 form suggests Korea will be strong. These are projections, not confirmed entries.

potentialContenders.name: Kim Won-ho / Seo Seung-jae
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world champions and 2026 Korea Open winners, beating Hoki and Kobayashi 21-12, 20-22, 21-19. A likely contender if they qualify.

potentialContenders.name: Baek Ha-na / Lee So-hee
potentialContenders.note: 2026 women's doubles world champions, beating Liu Shengshu and Tan Ning 21-15, 21-15 in the final.

potentialContenders.name: Liang Weikeng / Wang Chang
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 men's doubles silver medalists and 2026 world champions. They lost a 21-19 third game to Chinese Taipei in Paris.

potentialContenders.name: Takuro Hoki / Yugo Kobayashi
potentialContenders.note: Lost the 2026 Korea Open final in three games, so they could be a projected dangerous opponent.

BDM04.blurb:
The men's singles draw has lost its anchor. Viktor Axelsen, winner in Tokyo and Paris, retired in April 2026 because of his back, and a field that spent a decade chasing him is now chasing one another.

The early favorite is France. Christo Popov climbed to world No. 1 after winning the 2026 French Open, and Alex Lanier is the reigning world champion. A Sunday morning is a good time to catch the new contenders before the pressure builds.

The seats at Galen Center sit close to the floor, so you will hear the grunts and the squeak of shoes on the court. All five events play in the session.
BDM04.potentialContendersIntro: Because of Axelsen's retirement, the men's singles field is projected to be open. Shi Yuqi's injuries leave his 2028 outlook uncertain.

potentialContenders.name: Christo Popov
potentialContenders.note: World No. 1 since the 2026 French Open, where he came back from losing the 2025 final. A projected favorite.

potentialContenders.name: Alex Lanier
potentialContenders.note: 2026 world champion who dropped only two games on his way to the title.

potentialContenders.name: Kunlavut Vitidsarn
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalist, but he lost in the first round of the 2026 French Open as top seed. Could rebound if his form returns.

potentialContenders.name: Shi Yuqi
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world champion who spent 30 weeks at No. 1 before shoulder and back injuries ended his 2026 season. His 2028 status is uncertain.

BDM05.blurb:
This is the session for discovery, not for stars. Sixteen pairs per doubles event and 38 singles players means the draw is full of players from smaller badminton countries, including a host-country pair or two, who rarely get a stage this big.

Lauren Lam and Allison Quynh Lee, the American pair who reached the 2026 Korea Open semifinals, are the sort of story that could come alive in a home arena. They want to be the first American pair to win a World Tour women's doubles title.

Sit back and enjoy the range of playing styles. Afternoon groups tend to produce the upsets that make the bracket interesting.
BDM05.potentialContendersIntro: For men's and women's singles, the 2026 title winners from Canada and India are the names most likely to be in the field if they qualify.

potentialContenders.name: Victor Lai
potentialContenders.note: World bronze medalist in 2025 and 2026, and the 2026 Korea Open champion after beating Jason Gunawan 21-11, 21-14. A projected medal threat.

potentialContenders.name: Lakshya Sen
potentialContenders.note: Fourth at Paris 2024 and winner of the 2026 Hylo Open as a seventh seed. He could be a dangerous floater in the draw.

potentialContenders.name: P.V. Sindhu
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 Hylo Open and reached the 2026 French Open final. A veteran who could be a threat if she qualifies.

BDM06.blurb:
Five hours of badminton, six to eleven, and a ticket gets you all of it. This is the longest block of the first weekend, with every event on court, and it rewards the fan who settles in and does not look at the clock.

The highlight is the men's doubles race. Liang Weikeng and Wang Chang lost a 21-19 third game in the Paris 2024 final, then won the 2026 world title. Korea's Kim Won-ho and Seo Seung-jae, the 2026 Korea Open champions, are likely to be right behind them.

Galen Center in the evening gets noisy, and the late matches feel like a tournament inside the tournament.
BDM06.potentialContendersIntro: The pairs to watch in men's doubles are projected based on 2026 results. Chinese Taipei cannot defend as a pair because Lee Yang retired in 2024.

potentialContenders.name: Liang Weikeng / Wang Chang
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalists, 21-17, 18-21, 21-19 in the final. They won the 2026 world title as third seeds.

potentialContenders.name: Kim Won-ho / Seo Seung-jae
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 Asia Championships and Korea Open men's doubles as top seeds. A likely contender.

potentialContenders.name: Man Wei Chong / Tee Kai Wun
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 French Open men's doubles over compatriots Goh Sze Fei and Nur Izzuddin.

potentialContenders.name: Aaron Chia / Soh Wooi Yik
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalists and 2026 world silver medalists. They could be hungry for a better medal.

BDM07.blurb:
Eleven titles in a season has been done only three times: Kento Momota in 2019, and An Se-young in 2025 and again in 2026. A Monday morning is a good time to watch the player who makes it look routine.

An beat P.V. Sindhu 16-21, 21-11, 21-12 to win the 2026 French Open, which shows the pattern: lose a game, then take over. If she is on court this session, watch how she manages the pace of a rally.

The early start at Galen Center is a good chance to see singles from the best seats before the crowds grow.
BDM07.potentialContendersIntro: In women's singles, An Se-young leads a short list of likely contenders. These are projections for 2028 and not confirmed entries.

potentialContenders.name: An Se-young
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalist who matched the single-season record of 11 titles again in 2026. She withdrew from one event to manage her workload.

potentialContenders.name: P.V. Sindhu
potentialContenders.note: Lost to An in the 2026 French Open final after taking the first game, and won the Hylo Open. A projected danger.

potentialContenders.name: Wang Zhiyi
potentialContenders.note: Beat An in the 2026 All England final, her only loss of the year through early November. A key rival to watch.

potentialContenders.name: Akane Yamaguchi
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world champion and 2026 world runner-up, a projected medal contender.

BDM08.blurb:
Seeds have not been safe lately. Chou Tien-chen was top seed at the 2026 Korea Open and lost his first match, and Kodai Naraoka, a world silver medalist that year, did the same as third seed. Group play at the Games can be just as tricky.

That gives a Monday afternoon an edge. Veterans like Chou and rising players who are hungry for a breakthrough can both be in the field, and the margin between them can be just a few points.

The small bowl at Galen Center helps. You can watch the body language when a favorite slips behind.
BDM08.potentialContendersIntro: For men's singles, here are several players who could appear, depending on how the 2028 qualifying ranking shakes out. China's Chen Yufei is a projected women's singles name.

potentialContenders.name: Kodai Naraoka
potentialContenders.note: 2026 world silver medalist who reached the final as the 10th seed, but lost in the first round of the Korea Open.

potentialContenders.name: Chou Tien-chen
potentialContenders.note: 2026 world bronze medalist and top seed at the Korea Open, where he lost his first match.

potentialContenders.name: Lakshya Sen
potentialContenders.note: Lost Paris 2024 bronze to Malaysia's Lee Zii Jia, then won the 2026 Hylo Open as seventh seed.

potentialContenders.name: Chen Yufei
potentialContenders.note: Tokyo 2020 women's singles champion and 2025 world silver medalist. A likely contender if she is part of the team.

BDM09.blurb:
France is now a badminton power. Alex Lanier won the 2026 men's world title, Thom Gicquel and Delphine Delrue won the mixed doubles, and Christo Popov became the first French men's singles world No. 1. Monday evening could be a showcase for that rise.

The contrast with the old order is sharp. Viktor Axelsen had back surgery in April 2025 and retired a year later, and the title he held is wide open.

This is a long evening of group play in all five events, so pick a court, watch the French players, and see whether the confidence of 2026 carries over.
BDM09.potentialContendersIntro: Across the singles events, the 2026 world champions are likely names to watch, though 2028 qualification is not settled.

potentialContenders.name: Alex Lanier
potentialContenders.note: 2026 men's singles world champion, who also reached the French Open semifinals as the seventh seed.

potentialContenders.name: Christo Popov
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 French Open, beating Zaki Ubaidillah 21-11, 14-21, 21-13, to reach world No. 1.

potentialContenders.name: An Se-young
potentialContenders.note: 2026 women's world champion and Paris 2024 gold medalist. She won her third Korea Open title in 2026.

potentialContenders.name: Shi Yuqi
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world champion whose 30-week run at No. 1 ended in August 2026 as injuries forced withdrawals. His 2028 outlook is uncertain.

BDM10.blurb:
Two pairs have lost world finals and want a bigger prize. Liu Shengshu and Tan Ning were 2026 runners-up in women's doubles, and Malaysia's Aaron Chia and Soh Wooi Yik, Paris 2024 bronze medalists, took silver in men's doubles. A Tuesday morning gives you a first look at both.

Doubles is the part of badminton that is hardest to follow on television. In person, you see the way partners cover the court and how a defensive lift can set up a smash.

The men's and women's singles groups also play, so there is plenty to watch if a rally ends quickly.
BDM10.potentialContendersIntro: The headline events are men's and women's doubles, where several 2026 finalists are projected to be in the field. These are projections.

potentialContenders.name: Aaron Chia / Soh Wooi Yik
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalists who reached the 2026 world final as fourth seeds. They could be a medal threat.

potentialContenders.name: Liu Shengshu / Tan Ning
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world champions and 2026 runners-up, beaten 21-15, 21-15 by Korea. A likely contender if they remain together.

potentialContenders.name: Baek Ha-na / Lee So-hee
potentialContenders.note: 2026 world champions and the first Korean women's doubles pair to win the title in 31 years.

BDM11.blurb:
The best women's doubles pair of the last Games no longer exists. Chen Qingchen, who won Paris 2024 gold with Jia Yifan, retired in late 2025 and was honored at a ceremony in Hangzhou. The field is wide open.

The pairs filling that space come from several countries. Korea has the world champions, Japan has two pairs that won 2026 titles, and the American pair of Lauren Lam and Allison Quynh Lee are working their way up.

A Tuesday afternoon in the Galen Center is a good time to look for a new favorite. Men's doubles and women's singles also play in this block.
BDM11.potentialContendersIntro: For women's doubles, these pairs are projected contenders based on 2026 results. Qualification is still open.

potentialContenders.name: Baek Ha-na / Lee So-hee
potentialContenders.note: 2026 world champions and world No. 2 as of 6 October 2026. A projected favorite.

potentialContenders.name: Yuki Fukushima / Mayu Matsumoto
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 French Open, and are a likely contender for Japan.

potentialContenders.name: Rui Hirokami / Sayaka Hobara
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 Korea Open, beating Kim Yu-jung and Lee Yu-lim 21-18, 21-18.

potentialContenders.name: Lauren Lam / Allison Quynh Lee
potentialContenders.note: Beat Bulgaria's Stoeva sisters 21-19, 21-10 to reach the 2026 Korea Open semifinals. A home-crowd story if they take part.

BDM12.blurb:
By Tuesday night, group play begins to cut. The doubles groups decide who reaches the quarterfinals, and a pair that has lost twice can find itself in a match it must win.

That gives the men's doubles an edge. Liang Weikeng and Wang Chang, Paris 2024 silver medalists who lost 21-19 in the third game, won the 2026 world title as third seeds, and Korea's Kim Won-ho and Seo Seung-jae were world bronze medalists as top seeds. Neither pair has a free ride.

The Galen Center is at its loudest in the late session. Singles groups share the block, so the noise can follow you from court to court.
BDM12.potentialContendersIntro: Men's doubles is the marquee event here. With Lee Yang retired, the Paris 2024 champions will not defend as a pair, so these projections are open.

potentialContenders.name: Kim Won-ho / Seo Seung-jae
potentialContenders.note: 2026 world bronze medalists who won the Korea Open over Hoki and Kobayashi 21-12, 20-22, 21-19.

potentialContenders.name: Liang Weikeng / Wang Chang
potentialContenders.note: 2026 world champions and Paris 2024 silver medalists. They could be a projected favorite.

potentialContenders.name: Man Wei Chong / Tee Kai Wun
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 French Open. A pair to watch if they hold their ranking.

potentialContenders.name: Takuro Hoki / Yugo Kobayashi
potentialContenders.note: Reached the 2026 Korea Open final, taking a game from the Koreans before losing.

BDM13.blurb:
This is where mixed doubles starts to feel like a medal race. Sixteen pairs have been cut to eight, and from here on a loss ends the run.

The field has no obvious favorite. Zheng Siwei and Huang Yaqiong, the Paris 2024 champions, retired in December 2025, so a new gold medalist is guaranteed. France's Thom Gicquel and Delphine Delrue are the 2026 world champions, while China has several pairs that could take over.

The quarterfinals share the morning with men's and women's singles groups, so the Galen Center runs at full volume from the start.
BDM13.potentialContendersIntro: These are projected mixed doubles contenders based on 2025 and 2026 results. The 2028 field is not decided.

potentialContenders.name: Thom Gicquel / Delphine Delrue
potentialContenders.note: 2026 world champions who also won the 2026 Hylo Open. They are the pair to beat if they remain together.

potentialContenders.name: Feng Yanzhe / Huang Dongping
potentialContenders.note: 2026 world runners-up and French Open winners. A projected medal contender.

potentialContenders.name: Jiang Zhenbang / Wei Yaxin
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world runners-up who won the 2026 Korea Open, beating Gao Jiaxuan and Wu Mengying.

potentialContenders.name: Chen Tang Jie / Toh Ee Wei
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world champions and Malaysia's first mixed doubles title winners. They could be a dark horse.

BDM14.blurb:
Two events, one afternoon, and the answer to who plays in the round of 16. Group play in men's and women's singles is where the favorites show how they handle the Games.

In the women's draw, An Se-young has won 11 titles in both 2025 and 2026, while Akane Yamaguchi has lost to her 11 straight times. In the men's draw, Viktor Axelsen has retired, and France's Alex Lanier and Christo Popov are among those looking to fill his place.

It is a compact session, so the pace is brisk. At Galen Center, you are close enough to see which player sets the tempo.
BDM14.potentialContendersIntro: For singles, these players are projected contenders from 2026 results. None is confirmed for 2028.

potentialContenders.name: An Se-young
potentialContenders.note: Won 11 titles in both 2025 and 2026 and was 71-1 for 2026 after the Korea Open. A projected favorite.

potentialContenders.name: Akane Yamaguchi
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world champion and 2026 runner-up, beaten by An in the Korea Open final 21-12, 15-21, 21-16.

potentialContenders.name: Alex Lanier
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 world title and is a likely contender for gold with Axelsen gone.

potentialContenders.name: Victor Lai
potentialContenders.note: World bronze medalist in 2025 and 2026 and winner of the 2026 Korea Open. A candidate for a surprise medal.

BDM15.blurb:
The last night of group play is when seeds find out whether they are safe. Kunlavut Vitidsarn, the Paris 2024 silver medalist, lost the 2025 world final to Shi Yuqi and then went out in the first round of the 2026 French Open as top seed. Those losses show how thin the margins are.

Expect a few players to play like their season depends on it. If the new best-of-three games to 15 points format applies at the Games, there is less time to recover from a bad start.

This evening block in the Galen Center brings both singles events to a close before the round of 16.
BDM15.potentialContendersIntro: Players in men's and women's singles who could be in the field are listed below. These are projections based on 2025 and 2026 form.

potentialContenders.name: Kunlavut Vitidsarn
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 men's singles silver medalist, but inconsistent in 2026. A comeback could make him a dangerous floater.

potentialContenders.name: Kodai Naraoka
potentialContenders.note: Reached the 2026 world final as the 10th seed. A likely contender if he keeps that form.

potentialContenders.name: Anders Antonsen
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world bronze medalist who reached the 2026 Hylo Open semifinals as top seed. He could be a leading European contender.

potentialContenders.name: Wang Zhiyi
potentialContenders.note: Beat An Se-young in the 2026 All England final, her only loss of the season through early November.

potentialContenders.name: P.V. Sindhu
potentialContenders.note: Reached the 2026 French Open final and won the Hylo Open. A veteran who could be a threat if she qualifies.

BDM16.blurb:
Zheng Siwei and Huang Yaqiong, the Paris 2024 mixed doubles champions, retired in December 2025. That leaves the net wide open, and the semifinals here will show who steps into it.

The field is genuinely unsettled. France's Thom Gicquel and Delphine Delrue arrive as 2026 world champions, with Chinese pairs and Malaysia's Chen Tang Jie and Toh Ee Wei in the mix.

Then the session keeps going: women's doubles quarterfinals and a women's singles round of 16 where An Se-young, if healthy, could start another run. At 8 AM in a roughly 10,000-seat arena, you get three events and a very full morning.
BDM16.potentialContendersIntro: These are projected contenders for the mixed doubles semifinals, based on 2025-26 form. Nothing is confirmed for 2028.

potentialContenders.name: Thom Gicquel/Delphine Delrue
potentialContenders.note: Won France's first mixed doubles world title in 2026 and added the Hylo Open. Could be the pair everyone else has to solve.

potentialContenders.name: Feng Yanzhe/Huang Dongping
potentialContenders.note: 2026 French Open champions. Likely among the Chinese pairs trying to keep the title in the family after Zheng/Huang retired.

potentialContenders.name: Jiang Zhenbang/Wei Yaxin
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 Korea Open and are a second Chinese pair to watch if they hold form.

potentialContenders.name: Chen Tang Jie/Toh Ee Wei
potentialContenders.note: Malaysia's first mixed doubles world champions, in 2025. A real threat to reach the semis if they qualify.

BDM17.blurb:
One loss. That is An Se-young's entire 2026 record through November, set against 71 wins and a 55-match streak. If she walks out for a round of 16 match, the crowd will be watching to see who can take a game off her.

The men's draw is the other draw. With Viktor Axelsen retired, the title is up for grabs and the room is crowded: France's Christo Popov and Alex Lanier, Canada's Victor Lai, and Thailand's Kunlavut Vitidsarn.

This is the first knockout round after group play, so expect brisk matches and the first real eliminations.
BDM17.potentialContendersIntro: These are projected names for the men's and women's singles round of 16, based on 2025-26 form. Qualification for 2028 is still ahead.

potentialContenders.name: An Se-young
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 champion and two-time world champion (2023, 2026), with 11 titles in both 2025 and 2026. The player every draw is built around.

potentialContenders.name: Christo Popov
potentialContenders.note: Became men's singles world No. 1 after winning the 2026 French Open. Could be one of the favorites.

potentialContenders.name: Alex Lanier
potentialContenders.note: The 2026 world champion, who beat Kodai Naraoka 21-11, 21-11 in the final. Gives France two live medal hopes.

potentialContenders.name: Victor Lai
potentialContenders.note: World bronze medalist in 2025 and 2026 and the 2026 Korea Open champion. A dangerous player in this round.

potentialContenders.name: Kunlavut Vitidsarn
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalist and 2025 world runner-up. Likely to be among the contenders if healthy.

BDM18.blurb:
Night session, 8 PM start, and the men's doubles bracket arrives at the quarterfinals with a rare thing: no defending champions. Lee Yang, half of the Chinese Taipei pair that won in Paris, retired in September 2024.

What's left is a loaded field. Liang Weikeng and Wang Chang, Paris silver medalists, won the 2026 world title. Korea's Kim Won-ho and Seo Seung-jae won the 2025 worlds.

Expect the fast, flat exchanges that make doubles so loud in a small arena. The men's singles round of 16 shares the evening, with Popov and Lanier from France possible attractions.
BDM18.potentialContendersIntro: These are projected men's doubles quarterfinalists, based on 2025-26 form. Nothing is set for 2028.

potentialContenders.name: Liang Weikeng/Wang Chang
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalists and 2026 world champions. Could be seeking a gold medal that slipped away in three games in Paris.

potentialContenders.name: Kim Won-ho/Seo Seung-jae
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world champions who won the 2026 Korea Open. Projected to be a top seed.

potentialContenders.name: Aaron Chia/Soh Wooi Yik
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalists and 2026 world silver medalists. Likely contenders.

potentialContenders.name: Man Wei Chong/Tee Kai Wun
potentialContenders.note: 2026 French Open champions over compatriots Goh Sze Fei and Nur Izzuddin. Could give Malaysia a second threat.

BDM19.blurb:
A new mixed doubles champion will be crowned in this session. Zheng Siwei and Huang Yaqiong, who won Paris 2024 gold 21-8, 21-11, retired in December 2025, and nobody has an obvious claim on their spot.

That is why this is worth an early alarm. Gicquel and Delrue could bring France its first mixed doubles medal of this kind, while Chinese pairs and Malaysia's Chen Tang Jie and Toh Ee Wei look to answer.

It's a long morning, too: women's doubles semifinals follow. Medal matches may be played to 15 points under new BWF rules, though a Games-specific confirmation is still pending.
BDM19.potentialContendersIntro: These are projected mixed doubles medal contenders, based on 2025-26 results. Nothing is confirmed for 2028.

potentialContenders.name: Thom Gicquel/Delphine Delrue
potentialContenders.note: 2026 world champions who also won the Hylo Open. A French first, and they could arrive as favorites.

potentialContenders.name: Feng Yanzhe/Huang Dongping
potentialContenders.note: 2026 French Open champions. Could carry China's hopes of keeping the title.

potentialContenders.name: Jiang Zhenbang/Wei Yaxin
potentialContenders.note: 2026 Korea Open champions. A pair on the rise and a contender for the final.

potentialContenders.name: Chen Tang Jie/Toh Ee Wei
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world champions, Malaysia's first in mixed doubles. Could challenge for a medal.

BDM20.blurb:
Viktor Axelsen won the last two men's singles titles, and his back finally ended it in April 2026. So when the quarterfinals start here, no one in the building will be playing for second place behind him.

That changes the feel. Christo Popov, France's first men's singles world No. 1, and 2026 world champion Alex Lanier could set up a French collision. Kunlavut Vitidsarn and Canada's Victor Lai are in that conversation too.

It's a long day, 4 PM into the late night, with men's doubles semifinals closing it. Settle in and bring a jacket for the cold of the arena.
BDM20.potentialContendersIntro: These are projected men's singles quarterfinalists, based on 2025-26 form. Qualification for 2028 is still ahead.

potentialContenders.name: Christo Popov
potentialContenders.note: World No. 1 since October 2026 and the 2026 French Open champion. Likely the highest seed.

potentialContenders.name: Alex Lanier
potentialContenders.note: 2026 world champion and Denmark Open winner. Could face Popov in a French showdown.

potentialContenders.name: Kunlavut Vitidsarn
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalist who took Asian Games gold in 2026. A strong contender.

potentialContenders.name: Kodai Naraoka
potentialContenders.note: Lost the 2026 world final to Lanier 21-11, 21-11. Could be looking for revenge.

potentialContenders.name: Shi Yuqi
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world champion who ended 2026 injured and sought a protected ranking. Only if healthy and qualified.

BDM21.blurb:
The Paris gold-medal pair will not defend. Chen Qingchen retired in October 2025, and she told partner Jia Yifan she would return for 2028 only if needed. No comeback had been announced as of November 2026.

Without them the women's doubles picture is a four-way tangle. China's Liu Shengshu and Tan Ning are world No. 1, but Korea's Baek Ha-na and Lee So-hee beat them in the 2026 world final after losing five times earlier in the year.

Japanese pairs are in the picture too. A morning session with two medals, and neither one is a lock.
BDM21.potentialContendersIntro: These are projected women's doubles medal contenders, based on 2025-26 results. A country can send two pairs only if both are top eight in the qualifying ranking.

potentialContenders.name: Liu Shengshu/Tan Ning
potentialContenders.note: World No. 1 as of October 2026, 2025 world champions and winners of the 2026 China Open. Likely the pair to beat.

potentialContenders.name: Baek Ha-na/Lee So-hee
potentialContenders.note: 2026 world champions who beat Liu/Tan after losing to them five times. Could be the team with the momentum.

potentialContenders.name: Yuki Fukushima/Mayu Matsumoto
potentialContenders.note: 2026 French Open champions and top seeds there. A veteran Japanese pair in the medal hunt.

potentialContenders.name: Pearly Tan/Thinaah Muralitharan
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world silver medalists and 2026 French Open finalists. Could give Malaysia its best women's doubles shot.

potentialContenders.name: Rui Hirokami/Sayaka Hobara
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 Korea Open final 21-18, 21-18 over Kim Yu-jung and Lee Yu-lim. A rising pair worth watching.

BDM22.blurb:
The question hanging over this session is simple: who beats An Se-young? Her 2026 record stood at 71 wins and one loss after the Korea Open, with a 55-match winning streak.

The night session is a women's singles quarterfinal, and the field is stacked to chase her. Akane Yamaguchi has lost 11 straight to her, which may be the toughest rivalry stat in the sport. Chen Yufei, the Tokyo 2020 champion, and Wang Zhiyi, a 2026 world bronze medalist, will each have a shot.

In a roughly 10,000-seat bowl, every rally in an An match feels like a referendum.
BDM22.potentialContendersIntro: These are projected women's singles quarterfinalists, based on 2025-26 form. Nothing is confirmed for 2028.

potentialContenders.name: An Se-young
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 champion and world No. 1, with 11 titles in 2026. The one to beat.

potentialContenders.name: Akane Yamaguchi
potentialContenders.note: World No. 2 and 2025 world champion who has lost 11 straight to An. Could be the closest challenger.

potentialContenders.name: Chen Yufei
potentialContenders.note: Tokyo 2020 champion and 2025 world silver medalist. A proven big-match player if she qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Wang Zhiyi
potentialContenders.note: 2026 world bronze medalist who lost in the second round of the French Open. Streaky and dangerous.

potentialContenders.name: Nozomi Okuhara
potentialContenders.note: Reached the 2026 French Open semifinals before losing to An. A veteran who could be a spoiler.

BDM23.blurb:
Liang Weikeng and Wang Chang lost the Paris 2024 men's doubles final 21-17, 18-21, 21-19, three games and two points from gold. They've since won the 2026 world title, and a gold medal match here could be their chance to finish the job.

Across the net could be Kim Won-ho and Seo Seung-jae, the 2025 world champions, who snapped a seven-month title drought in November 2026. Or Malaysia's Aaron Chia and Soh Wooi Yik. Or someone nobody saw coming.

Morning light, a doubles final, then men's singles semifinals. This is a very good day.
BDM23.potentialContendersIntro: These are projected men's doubles gold medal match contenders, based on 2025-26 form. The pairings for 2028 are still unknown.

potentialContenders.name: Liang Weikeng/Wang Chang
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalists and 2026 world champions. Could be looking for the gold they just missed.

potentialContenders.name: Kim Won-ho/Seo Seung-jae
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world champions and world No. 1 pair, with the 2026 Korea Open. Strong favorites on form.

potentialContenders.name: Aaron Chia/Soh Wooi Yik
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalists and 2026 world silver medalists. They could break through.

potentialContenders.name: Man Wei Chong/Tee Kai Wun
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 French Open 13-21, 21-15, 21-7 over compatriots Goh/Izzuddin. A pair who can be explosive.

BDM24.blurb:
One loss in 72 matches. That was An Se-young's 2026 record after the Korea Open, and if she reaches a semifinal here, it's the match everyone came to see.

Her likeliest semifinal opponents have all had their turns. Akane Yamaguchi has lost 11 straight to her. Nozomi Okuhara pushed her through the French Open semifinals. Wang Zhiyi, a world bronze medalist, can upset anyone on a given day.

The night also holds a men's doubles bronze medal match. A Sunday night in a close, loud arena, with a medal on the line before the main event.
BDM24.potentialContendersIntro: These are projected women's singles semifinalists, based on 2025-26 form. Qualification for 2028 is still ahead.

potentialContenders.name: An Se-young
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 champion, world No. 1 and 71-1 in 2026. The favorite if she stays healthy.

potentialContenders.name: Akane Yamaguchi
potentialContenders.note: World No. 2 who lost the 2026 Korea Open final 21-12, 15-21, 21-16. Likely a semifinalist if she qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Wang Zhiyi
potentialContenders.note: 2026 world bronze medalist and 2025 World Tour Finals runner-up to An. Could be China's best hope.

potentialContenders.name: Nozomi Okuhara
potentialContenders.note: Lost to An in the 2026 French Open semifinals. A veteran who can make matches long.

BDM25.blurb:
For two Games in a row Viktor Axelsen stood on top of this podium. He retired in April 2026 because of his back, so this Monday morning belongs to someone new.

France may have the best claim. Alex Lanier won the 2026 world title 21-11, 21-11 over Kodai Naraoka, and Christo Popov won the French Open at home and holds the No. 1 ranking. Canada's Victor Lai and Thailand's Kunlavut Vitidsarn are not going quietly.

A first-time gold medalist walks out of the Galen Center on the final morning. It's a history-making ticket.
BDM25.potentialContendersIntro: These are projected men's singles medal contenders, based on 2025-26 form. Nothing is confirmed for 2028, and Shi Yuqi's availability depends on recovery.

potentialContenders.name: Alex Lanier
potentialContenders.note: 2026 world champion who also won the Singapore Open, Orléans Masters and Denmark Open. A leading gold medal contender.

potentialContenders.name: Christo Popov
potentialContenders.note: 2026 French Open champion and 2025 World Tour Finals winner. Could meet Lanier in a French final.

potentialContenders.name: Victor Lai
potentialContenders.note: World bronze medalist in 2025 and 2026 and 2026 Korea Open champion. Could break through.

potentialContenders.name: Kunlavut Vitidsarn
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalist and 2026 Asian Games champion. Seeking the gold that slipped away.

potentialContenders.name: Shi Yuqi
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world champion who ended 2026 with shoulder and back injuries. A contender only if he recovers.

BDM26.blurb:
Closing night of badminton at the Galen Center, and the headline act is the player who has made winning look routine. An Se-young took 11 titles in 2025 and again in 2026, the first player to do it in consecutive years.

If she reaches this final, she carries a Paris gold and a lot of weight. Akane Yamaguchi has lost to her 11 straight times, and Chen Yufei and Wang Zhiyi will believe this is the night.

It's a last Monday evening and the end of ten days of racket sound. If the 3x15 format is used, expect matches to move quickly.
BDM26.potentialContendersIntro: These are projected women's singles medal contenders, based on 2025-26 results. Nothing is confirmed for 2028.

potentialContenders.name: An Se-young
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 champion, world No. 1 and two-time world champion. Heavy favorite if she qualifies and stays healthy.

potentialContenders.name: Akane Yamaguchi
potentialContenders.note: World No. 2 and 2025 world champion, beaten by An in the 2026 Asian Games and Korea Open finals. Could be her top rival.

potentialContenders.name: Chen Yufei
potentialContenders.note: Tokyo 2020 champion and 2025 world silver medalist. Experienced enough to push for a medal.

potentialContenders.name: Wang Zhiyi
potentialContenders.note: 2026 world bronze medalist who lost to An in the 2025 World Tour Finals final. A rising threat.

BK301.blurb:
Somebody has to take the first shot at the first Games event the San Fernando Valley has ever hosted, and it happens on a Sunday afternoon in the Sepulveda Basin. Two men's games and two women's games open a 3x3 tournament that has grown to 12 teams a side.

The eight-sided stand wraps one court, so every seat is courtside and no angle is a bad one. Games run ten minutes or to 21, with a 12-second shot clock that punishes slow starts.

Come early for the opening-day buzz and a first look at the defending champions from Paris 2024.
BK301.potentialContendersIntro: Netherlands men and Germany women won gold at Paris 2024, and the 2026 World Cup winners will be chasing them. Who actually opens the tournament depends on qualification, so treat these as likely names.

potentialContenders.name: Netherlands men
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalists, beating France 18-17 in overtime. They slipped to sixth at the 2026 World Cup, so the champions arrive with something to prove.

potentialContenders.name: Germany women
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalists, the first title in their history. They are projected to defend, though a strong 2028 qualifying run is still needed.

potentialContenders.name: Latvia men
potentialContenders.note: Beat Germany 20-15 in the 2026 World Cup final for their first World Cup title. A likely contender if they qualify.

potentialContenders.name: USA women
potentialContenders.note: Host nation, automatically qualified. Paris 2024 bronze medalists and 2026 World Cup champions.

BK302.blurb:
Karlis Lasmanis scored 12 of Latvia's 20 points in the 2026 World Cup final, and the way he sizes up a defender, then drives or shoots, is worth the price of a seat. If Latvia makes it, this early-evening slot is a good chance to see him up close.

The men's field is as deep as it has ever been. Spain, Serbia, Germany and the Dutch all arrive with a recent trophy or a grudge.

Around 5:30 p.m. the Valley heat should be easing off, and the packed octagon should start to hum.
BK302.potentialContendersIntro: These are the men's teams most likely to show up, based on 2025 and 2026 form. Qualification for 2028 is still open, so every name here is a projection.

potentialContenders.name: Latvia men
potentialContenders.note: Tokyo 2020 champions who won the 2026 World Cup and the Europe Cup. They went 7-0 in Paris pool play before losing to France in the semifinals.

potentialContenders.name: Germany men
potentialContenders.note: 2026 World Cup runners-up after finishing fourth in 2025. A strong candidate to be in the mix.

potentialContenders.name: Serbia men
potentialContenders.note: World Cup bronze medalists in both 2025 and 2026, and the 2026 bronze came with Serbian clubs winning multiple World Tour stops.

potentialContenders.name: Spain men
potentialContenders.note: Won their first men's World Cup title in June 2025, beating Switzerland 21-17. Could appear if they qualify.

BK303.blurb:
A 9 p.m. start means this is the first session where the park really belongs to the night crowd. Under the evening sky, the USA women could be playing for the home fans.

They are carrying a strange recent résumé. In 2025 they lost 18-15 to host Mongolia in the World Cup quarterfinals, then bounced back to win their fourth World Cup crown in 2026. Weeks later Canada beat them 21-12 in the AmeriCup final.

That makes every USA game a test of nerve, and the Dutch and German champions keep the stakes high around them.
BK303.potentialContendersIntro: For the women's games, the 2026 form guide points to a handful of favorites. Who arrives in the Valley will not be settled until the 2028 qualifiers finish.

potentialContenders.name: USA women
potentialContenders.note: Host nation, automatically qualified. Paris 2024 bronze medalists and 2026 World Cup champions, but beaten by Canada in the AmeriCup final.

potentialContenders.name: Netherlands women
potentialContenders.note: First World Cup title in 2025, and the 2026 Europe Cup winners with Noortje Driessen named MVP. A strong contender if they qualify.

potentialContenders.name: Germany women
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 champions with Sonja Greinacher as MVP. Their 2026 form is unsteady, so a title defense is a storyline to watch.

potentialContenders.name: Australia women
potentialContenders.note: Runners-up to the USA at the 2026 World Cup and a potential medal threat.

BK304.blurb:
Canada's women are the most dangerous team to catch on an afternoon with nothing yet at stake. They won the 2026 AmeriCup by beating the USA 21-12, and Michelle Plouffe was named tournament MVP.

France is the other name to circle. The 2026 Women's Series Final winners come with Laetitia Guapo's scoring and a confident edge.

It is Monday, the second day of pool play, and the standings are still forming. That is when a team can establish itself or open itself to an upset, all in front of a court-wide crowd.
BK304.potentialContendersIntro: The women's games here should draw from the 2025 and 2026 title winners. These projections are based on recent form, since the 2028 field is not yet set.

potentialContenders.name: Canada women
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 AmeriCup, their third title, and took bronze at the 2025 World Cup. Likely contenders if they qualify.

potentialContenders.name: France women
potentialContenders.note: 2026 Women's Series Final champions, with Laetitia Guapo named MVP. Could be a rising force.

potentialContenders.name: Spain women
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalists, who lost the final 17-16 to Germany. A projected threat if they qualify.

BK305.blurb:
Jimmer Fredette is the face of this session. The USA men won a third straight AmeriCup in 2026 behind his 13 points in the final, but they also lost 22-14 to Germany at the 2025 World Cup. Which version turns up on home turf?

That makes this Monday evening a true test. Latvia, which went 7-0 in Paris pool play, is the standard to measure the hosts against.

With the new play-in round raising the stakes for seeding, every possession counts, even in pool play.
BK305.potentialContendersIntro: These men's teams are the likeliest names for this evening. The USA is already qualified, and the rest are projections based on 2025 and 2026 results.

potentialContenders.name: USA men
potentialContenders.note: Host nation, automatically qualified. Won the 2026 AmeriCup 21-15 over Canada, with Jimmer Fredette named MVP.

potentialContenders.name: Germany men
potentialContenders.note: Beat the USA 22-14 in the 2025 World Cup quarterfinals and reached the 2026 final. Likely to arrive in form.

potentialContenders.name: Latvia men
potentialContenders.note: Tokyo 2020 champions and 2026 World Cup winners. A projected favorite if they qualify.

potentialContenders.name: Canada men
potentialContenders.note: 2026 AmeriCup runners-up, beaten 21-15 by the USA. Could be a danger to the hosts.

BK306.blurb:
Janis Boonstra began 2026 at the top of the women's individual 3x3 ranking, and the Dutch around her have been collecting trophies. They won their first World Cup title in 2025, and a second straight Europe Cup in 2026.

But the late slot rewards the underdog. Latvia's women won the Baku stop in 2025 unbeaten as the No. 6 seed, and France has the momentum of a Series Final title.

At 9 p.m. in the Sepulveda Basin, the night session offers a loose, watch-everything feel, with upsets one hot streak away.
BK306.potentialContendersIntro: For the women's games, the top Europeans are the name brand to watch. These are projections for 2028, based on recent results and rankings.

potentialContenders.name: Netherlands women
potentialContenders.note: 2025 World Cup champions and back-to-back Europe Cup winners. Janis Boonstra topped the individual ranking at the start of 2026.

potentialContenders.name: France women
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 Women's Series Final in Shanghai, with Laetitia Guapo as event MVP. A likely contender.

potentialContenders.name: Latvia women
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2025 Baku stop unbeaten as the No. 6 seed. A dark horse if they qualify.

potentialContenders.name: USA women
potentialContenders.note: Host nation, automatically qualified, and 2026 World Cup champions.

BK307.blurb:
Strahinja Stojacic scored 34 points to win MVP at World Tour Dubai in November 2026, and the Serbian club Ub beat Baskets Bonn 20-19 for its fourth stop title of the season. Serbia is a team that wins close games.

They have not yet climbed the top step at a World Cup, with bronze in both 2025 and 2026, so the gap between very good and best is the story here.

An afternoon men's session is a good place to watch that edge up close, with fans packed around the octagon and little space between court and seats.
BK307.potentialContendersIntro: For the men's games, Serbia is the headline, with its main rivals from Europe. These are projections; the 2028 field is still being decided.

potentialContenders.name: Serbia men
potentialContenders.note: World Cup bronze medalists in 2025 and 2026. Stojacic held the top individual ranking at the start of 2026.

potentialContenders.name: Germany men
potentialContenders.note: 2026 World Cup runners-up to Latvia, after finishing fourth in 2025. A likely force.

potentialContenders.name: Latvia men
potentialContenders.note: 2026 World Cup and Europe Cup champions. Could be the team to beat if they qualify.

potentialContenders.name: Netherlands men
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 champions and 2026 Europe Cup runners-up. Their roster for 2028 is not confirmed.

BK308.blurb:
Mongolia beat the USA 18-15 on home soil in the 2025 World Cup quarterfinals, and then lost the final 15-9 to the Netherlands. The Americans have not forgotten that one.

The USA women rebounded to win the 2026 World Cup, their fourth, but lost to Canada 21-12 in the AmeriCup final. Meanwhile, Germany, the Paris 2024 gold medalists, finished eighth at the 2026 Women's Series Final.

In the 5:30 p.m. session, the champions look vulnerable and the challengers hungry, a combination that makes the sport worth watching.
BK308.potentialContendersIntro: These are the women's teams with the best storylines for this session. Qualification is still open, so treat all of these as projections.

potentialContenders.name: USA women
potentialContenders.note: Host nation, automatically qualified. 2026 World Cup champions who lost the AmeriCup final to Canada.

potentialContenders.name: Mongolia women
potentialContenders.note: Reached the 2025 World Cup final at home and beat the USA in the quarterfinals. Could appear if they qualify.

potentialContenders.name: Germany women
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 champions with MVP Sonja Greinacher, but eighth at the 2026 Series Final. A title defense is far from guaranteed.

potentialContenders.name: Canada women
potentialContenders.note: 2026 AmeriCup champions with a 21-12 win over the USA. A likely contender.

BK309.blurb:
Latvia became the first team to win a Games gold, a Europe Cup and a World Cup when it beat Germany 20-15 in Warsaw in 2026. Spain, meanwhile, claimed its first men's World Cup in 2025.

That sets up a late men's session with real pedigree. France, Paris 2024 silver medalists and fourth at the 2026 World Cup, would like to be in the discussion too.

The 9 p.m. start also gives the club scene a showcase, with Belgian, Serbian and other World Tour winners all feeding the national teams. Expect tight, physical games in the octagon.
BK309.potentialContendersIntro: For the men's games, the best-performing teams of the last two years are the likeliest to appear. Which of them qualify for 2028 is still to be decided.

potentialContenders.name: Latvia men
potentialContenders.note: Tokyo 2020 champions, and the first team to add a Europe Cup and World Cup. Went 7-0 in Paris pool play before the semifinal loss.

potentialContenders.name: Spain men
potentialContenders.note: 2025 World Cup champions, beating Switzerland 21-17 in Ulaanbaatar. Could appear if they qualify.

potentialContenders.name: France men
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalists, who lost the final 18-17 in overtime. Fourth at the 2026 World Cup.

potentialContenders.name: Serbia men
potentialContenders.note: 2025 and 2026 World Cup bronze medalists, with Serbian clubs winning World Tour stops.

BK310.blurb:
Check the trophy cases and nobody owns the sport. Latvia's men took the 2026 World Cup and Europe Cup, the USA men won the AmeriCup, and the USA women won the World Cup.

Then add the Dutch women's back-to-back Europe Cup wins and Canada's 21-12 AmeriCup win over the Americans. A Wednesday afternoon session is a good look at how many teams have a case.

The new play-in round gives the expanded 12-team field extra layers, so even the middle-ranked teams are playing for something. Settle into the shaded seats and let the sport sort itself out.
BK310.potentialContendersIntro: These are the 2026 champions most likely to pop up in this session. Which of them actually reach 2028 is still open.

potentialContenders.name: Latvia men
potentialContenders.note: 2026 World Cup and Europe Cup champions. A projected favorite if they qualify.

potentialContenders.name: USA women
potentialContenders.note: Host nation, automatically qualified. 2026 World Cup champions with a fourth World Cup crown.

potentialContenders.name: Netherlands women
potentialContenders.note: Won back-to-back Europe Cup titles in 2025 and 2026. A likely contender.

potentialContenders.name: Canada women
potentialContenders.note: 2026 AmeriCup champions over the USA. Could be a dangerous team in the pools.

potentialContenders.name: USA men
potentialContenders.note: Host nation, automatically qualified, and three-time defending AmeriCup champions.

BK311.blurb:
The defending champion's best-known name may not even be here. Worthy de Jong, the MVP of the Paris 2024 final, has said he considered retiring after those Games and has not committed to 2028.

That leaves a door open for the hosts. Jimmer Fredette earned MVP honors at the 2026 AmeriCup, with 13 points in the final, and the USA men will be playing in front of their own fans.

It is a Wednesday evening in the Valley, with 12 teams per gender chasing a title. The question of who steps into the champions' shoes is worth watching.
BK311.potentialContendersIntro: For the men's side, the hosts and the continental challengers lead the field of likely names. These are projections only, since qualification is open and de Jong's plans are unconfirmed.

potentialContenders.name: USA men
potentialContenders.note: Host nation, automatically qualified. Beat Canada 21-15 in the 2026 AmeriCup final, with Jimmer Fredette as MVP.

potentialContenders.name: Netherlands men
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalists. Whether de Jong returns is a storyline to watch.

potentialContenders.name: Canada men
potentialContenders.note: 2026 AmeriCup runners-up, and a likely contender to challenge the USA.

potentialContenders.name: USA women
potentialContenders.note: Host nation and 2026 World Cup champions, with a fourth World Cup crown.

BK312.blurb:
The Dutch men have had a rough run since Paris. They finished ninth at the 2025 World Cup and sixth at the 2026 World Cup, though they did reach the 2026 Europe Cup final.

Worthy de Jong still shows flashes. He was MVP of World Tour Bucharest in November 2025, leading Amsterdam to the title, though the same club only finished fourth in Dubai a year later.

On the women's side, Noortje Driessen was Europe Cup MVP, so Wednesday's late session offers the chance to see both Dutch teams searching for form or confirming it.
BK312.potentialContendersIntro: For this late session the Netherlands is the story on both sides of the bracket. Their 2028 rosters and qualification are not yet confirmed, so these are projections.

potentialContenders.name: Netherlands men
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalists, sixth at the 2026 World Cup and Europe Cup runners-up. De Jong's availability is a question.

potentialContenders.name: Netherlands women
potentialContenders.note: 2025 World Cup champions and 2026 Europe Cup winners, with Noortje Driessen as MVP.

potentialContenders.name: USA women
potentialContenders.note: Host nation and 2026 World Cup champions. A likely pool opponent for any contender.

potentialContenders.name: Latvia men
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 Europe Cup over the Netherlands. Could be a pool-play test.

BK313.blurb:
Not every team here has been to the Games before. One of the 2028 qualifying events is a Universality tournament, 12 teams limited to nations that did not play basketball at Tokyo 2020 or Paris 2024.

That means a Thursday afternoon session could introduce you to a first-time Games team, playing in front of a crowd that has never seen it.

Around them are familiar names. Lithuania, the Paris 2024 bronze medalists, lost the European men's title to Latvia in 2026, and Australia won both Asia Cup titles in 2025.
BK313.potentialContendersIntro: These are the sides most likely to be involved, drawn from the 2025 and 2026 results. 2028 qualification is still open, so all of these are projections.

potentialContenders.name: Lithuania men
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalists and 2025 U23 World Cup champions. Lost the European title to Latvia in 2026.

potentialContenders.name: Australia men
potentialContenders.note: 2025 Asia Cup champions. A likely contender if they qualify.

potentialContenders.name: Australia women
potentialContenders.note: 2025 Asia Cup champions and 2026 World Cup runners-up. A projected medal threat.

potentialContenders.name: Puerto Rico men
potentialContenders.note: Took the 2026 AmeriCup bronze behind the USA and Canada. Could appear if they qualify.

BK314.blurb:
Laetitia Guapo took MVP at the 2026 Women's Series Final in Shanghai, and France won its third Series title, tying Canada for the most. The French women look like a team that has figured something out.

On the men's side, the Serbian club Ub rolled through 2026 with World Tour wins in Chengdu, Marseille, Macau and Dubai. The Netherlands, with Alberts, Driessen, de Jong and van der Horst on their 2025 World Cup roster, are the opposition to match.

Thursday evening in the octagon puts all that talent in a space where the crowd is close enough to hear every call.
BK314.potentialContendersIntro: These are the teams with the strongest recent form who could appear on the women's and men's sides. They are projections, since the 2028 fields are still being decided.

potentialContenders.name: France women
potentialContenders.note: 2026 Women's Series Final champions, their third title, with Laetitia Guapo as MVP.

potentialContenders.name: USA women
potentialContenders.note: Host nation and 2026 World Cup champions, with a fourth World Cup crown.

potentialContenders.name: Serbia men
potentialContenders.note: Serbian club Ub won four World Tour stops in 2026, and Serbia took World Cup bronze that year.

potentialContenders.name: Netherlands men
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalists. Their 2025 World Cup roster included Worthy de Jong; 2028 plans are unconfirmed.

BK315.blurb:
This is the last night of pool play, and it ends with the standings sorted. The play-in round begins Friday, July 21, so Thursday's late games decide who gets an easier path and who has to fight for it.

At Paris 2024, with eight teams per gender, the top two pool finishers went straight to the semifinals. How that changes with 12 teams remains to be seen, but the stakes of seeding are the same.

Stay for the 9 p.m. tip and you will watch teams that have been cruising suddenly play every possession like it is the last.
BK315.potentialContendersIntro: For the final pool session, the strongest teams from the 2026 results are the likeliest to be fighting for position. Their 2028 qualification is still to come, so these are projections.

potentialContenders.name: Latvia men
potentialContenders.note: 2026 World Cup champions, with Karlis Lasmanis as MVP. A projected top seed if they qualify.

potentialContenders.name: USA men
potentialContenders.note: Host nation, automatically qualified, and unbeaten at the 2026 AmeriCup with Jimmer Fredette as MVP.

potentialContenders.name: USA women
potentialContenders.note: Host nation and 2026 World Cup champions over Australia.

potentialContenders.name: Serbia men
potentialContenders.note: Ub won four World Tour stops in 2026, most recently Dubai. A likely contender if they qualify.

potentialContenders.name: Netherlands men
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 champions, sixth at the 2026 World Cup and Europe Cup runners-up.

BK316.blurb:
Somebody's tournament ends here, and it ends fast. The play-in is new to 3x3 at the Games, a product of the jump from 8 to 12 teams per gender, and it hands the teams that stumble through pool play one last shot at the quarterfinals. One cold stretch from the arc can end a run.

This is also your first look at the eight-sided stand in the Sepulveda Basin, with fans on every side of a single open-air court. Nobody is hidden behind a baseline.

Four games, two per gender, for a 2 PM start. It's a cheap way to see the sport's depth before the knockout rounds begin.
BK316.potentialContendersIntro: Play-in pairings depend on pool results and qualification, so these are projections based on recent form, not confirmed matchups.

potentialContenders.name: Serbia
potentialContenders.note: Men's bronze medalists at both the 2025 and 2026 World Cups. Likely contenders if they qualify, and a team that could be fighting for a quarterfinal berth.

potentialContenders.name: Netherlands
potentialContenders.note: Defending Paris 2024 men's champions, but 9th at the 2025 World Cup and 6th in 2026. A play-in game is plausible if pool play goes badly.

potentialContenders.name: Canada
potentialContenders.note: Beat the USA women 21-12 to win the 2026 AmeriCup. A dangerous side to meet at any stage, if they qualify.

potentialContenders.name: Australia
potentialContenders.note: Won both the men's and women's titles at the 2025 Asia Cup and were 2026 World Cup women's runners-up. Could appear if pool play leaves them short of a top seed.

BK317.blurb:
Quarterfinals are new to 3x3 at the Games. Paris 2024 went straight from play-in to semifinals. Now one loss in the early evening is the end, and everyone in the stand knows it.

The women's side has a juicy subplot. The USA women lost to Mongolia in the 2025 World Cup quarterfinals, then came back to win the 2026 World Cup. A host-nation team with a point to prove in a knockout game is a good thing to watch.

The men's side could bring Latvia, the 2026 World Cup and Europe Cup champions, into a single-elimination bracket. Come at 5:30 and you get two men's and two women's games, with the late light still on the court.
BK317.potentialContendersIntro: Quarterfinal matchups depend on pool play and qualifying, so these teams are projections based on 2025 and 2026 form, not confirmed pairings.

potentialContenders.name: Latvia
potentialContenders.note: Tokyo 2020 champions and winners of both the 2026 World Cup and Europe Cup. Projected men's favorites if they qualify.

potentialContenders.name: USA
potentialContenders.note: The host team qualifies automatically. The women won the 2026 World Cup after the 2025 quarterfinal loss, and the men won the 2026 AmeriCup.

potentialContenders.name: Netherlands
potentialContenders.note: The women won back-to-back Europe Cup titles in 2025 and 2026. A likely women's contender.

potentialContenders.name: France
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 Women's Series Final, its third title in that series. Could be a tough opponent for anyone.

BK318.blurb:
Nine o'clock at night, in a park in the San Fernando Valley, with a quarterfinal on the line. The late session lets the crowd and the court take over, and nobody can duck a shot.

The women's bracket could bring back last time's finalists. Germany beat Spain 17-16 in Paris, and a rematch of that game, or something close to it, is not hard to picture. Canada's 21-12 win over the USA in the 2026 AmeriCup makes it a field with no obvious favorite.

On the men's side, Serbia and Germany arrive with World Cup medals from 2026. Worthy de Jong, the Paris 2024 hero, hasn't committed to playing in 2028, so his status is the question to watch.
BK318.potentialContendersIntro: Matchups are unconfirmed and depend on qualifying and pool results. These are projections from recent form and Paris 2024 results.

This session is Saturday's first double-header, with the medal games following at night. Four games, two per gender, decide who plays for gold and who goes to the bronze game.

If Latvia's Karlis Lasmanis and Kristaps Gluditis arrive as World Cup and Europe Cup champions, they will be the team everyone is chasing. Fans get to see who can stop them.

Last year's champion was decided by one point in overtime. Paris 2024 gave the Netherlands men gold at 18-17 on a Worthy de Jong two-pointer, and Germany's women beat Spain 17-16. That is how close 3x3 medal games tend to get.

This is the closing night of the 3x3 program. Bronze games come first, then gold, and the eight-sided stand at Valley Complex 3 puts fans on every side of the court, near enough to hear the bounce and the chatter.

Latvia could arrive as the men's team to beat, the first to hold Games, World Cup and Europe Cup titles. The USA women, 2026 World Cup champions, could bring a host crowd along.

BKB01.blurb:
The first basketball tip-off of the 2028 Games comes two days before the Opening Ceremony. That means the Intuit Dome gets to set the tone for the whole fortnight, and it does it at noon with a doubleheader.

Women's basketball arrives with a streak that sounds made up: eight straight golds, with the 67-66 squeaker over France in Paris still fresh. The USA could take the floor in either game here, and Australia, the Paris bronze medalists, is the kind of opponent that tests a favorite early.

Look to the far end of the arena, where The Wall stacks 51 rows of seats. It will be the loudest corner of the building.

This is the first evening game of the women's tournament, 6 p.m. under the Intuit Dome lights, with the crowd settling in before the late game. The matchup is not set, but the field is deep. Spain has a rising star in Iyana Martin, and Belgium has won two straight EuroBasket titles.

It is a good ticket for fans who want to see how a title favorite's challengers actually look.

Iyana Martin, only 20 then, was named to the All-Star Five. Whoever draws the late slot on opening day is going to find a tournament that has no easy nights.

The USA, hosts and eight-time champions, will want to start loud.

Victor Wembanyama said that losing the Paris 2024 final would motivate France to win gold in 2028. The men's tournament begins the day before the Opening Ceremony, and the chase starts here.

The USA is the host and has won five straight titles. Kevin Durant has said he plans to play, and Anthony Edwards and Bam Adebayo look like core pieces, though rosters are not set. Germany arrives as EuroBasket 2025 champion with Dennis Schroder as MVP.

The doubleheader runs through the afternoon, so you can scout one favorite and then see what else is in the group.

The first night is spectacle. The second night is where women's basketball starts to feel like a tournament. By Thursday evening the USA has had its opening test and the field is sorting itself out.

The Americans enter as hosts with one of the younger rosters they have sent to a major event. Their 2026 World Cup team was the second-youngest the USA has ever taken, and it still won the title. Germany is a team to watch too. Leonie Fiebich's All-Star Five run at that World Cup left the host nation in fourth place and angry.

Six o'clock is a good time to arrive. Dinner first, then settle in.

Gabby Williams had the last shot in Paris 2024. It was just inside the arc, so it counted for two instead of three, and France lost 67-66. Two years later she scored 20 in the World Cup final, and France is still searching for the answer.

This is the late Thursday game, a 9:30 p.m. tip with the Intuit Dome at its loudest. France is probably the team most hungry to do something about that single point. With Dominique Malonga scoring 21 in the 2026 final, they have the size to do it.

You can see plenty of what the knockout rounds will look like, before the pressure peaks.

Stephen Curry's late run of threes ended the Paris 2024 final against France. The tournament's late game at 9:30 p.m. is the time of night when that sort of shot gets made.

Caitlin Clark said in November 2026 that women's basketball has a chance to be the premier sport at the 2028 Games. This Sunday doubleheader, midway through group play, is a fair place to test that.

The USA is the host and would be chasing a ninth gold. Breanna Stewart, a four-time World Cup champion and the 2026 MVP, anchors the program. A'ja Wilson won the 2026 WNBA MVP award, which is why selection questions for the 2028 roster are going to be interesting. Rosters are not final.

Nobody can say yet who is playing, and that is the appeal. Qualifying tournaments in early 2028 will fill the field, so this late game could feature a team that just fought its way in.

Canada is already in line for that fight. The Canadians went 5-0 in the August 2026 pre-qualifier in Guadalajara and beat Mexico 83-53 to earn a place in the qualifying tournaments. A team that's hungry just to be here makes for a sharp group-phase game.

The 9:30 PM tip means the night session crowd will be settled in by then. Look for the underdogs first.

BKB22.blurb:
The final day of the women's group phase is when seeding gets settled. A team that slips one place may find a tougher quarterfinal a few days later.

The Americans know that tension. At the 2026 World Cup they beat Italy only 55-52 in the group phase, then crushed Hungary 108-56 in the quarterfinals. One tight game can sit right next to a blowout.

Two games from noon to just after four, and the tournament's shape comes into focus. It's a good session for fans who like their basketball with consequences.

BKB23.blurb:
Germany arrives as the only team since the Soviet Union, Yugoslavia and Spain to hold the World Cup and the EuroBasket titles at the same time. If they qualify, the Intuit Dome gets to see what that looks like.

Dennis Schroder was the EuroBasket 2025 MVP, averaging 20.3 points and 7.2 assists. He plays with the kind of speed that rewards good seats near the baseline.

The 6 PM game tips as Inglewood cools off. Against America, France or Greece, a champion would be a test for the rest of the field.

BKB24.blurb:
Victor Wembanyama is 22 and already France's captain, the youngest since Tony Parker in 2003. Coach Frederic Fauthoux handed him the role in summer 2026, taking over from Rudy Gobert.

He has talked openly about 2028 since the Paris final. If France qualifies, a late-night group game gets a chance to see whether he's bringing something new.

Turkey could be right there with a sharp counterpunch. They finished second at EuroBasket 2025, and Alperen Sengun was an All-Star Five selection. The 9:30 PM start means the arena crowd has had time to warm up.

BKB25.blurb:
Finland made the EuroBasket 2025 semifinals for the first time, the first Nordic country to get that far. A doubleheader like this is where a team like that might sneak up on someone.

Germany beat Turkey 88-83 in that final in a game with 15 lead changes and 11 ties. Isaac Bonga scored 20 points, and Dennis Schroder scored Germany's last six. The Wagner and da Silva generation is tough to read.

Noon to 4:15 PM, two games, and a lot of room for surprises. The groups are still undefined, but the basketball is going to be good.

BKB26.blurb:
Giannis Antetokounmpo had 30 points and 17 rebounds in the EuroBasket 2025 bronze game. That is the kind of line he puts up when he cares, which is why Greece is a team worth a Friday evening.

Greece lost to Turkey in that tournament's semifinals, and both teams could be here if they qualify. Germany and Turkey were each 8-0 going into the final before Germany won 88-83.

The 6 PM tip is a clean start to the night. Inglewood is cooling off, and the arena fills with fans looking for stories.

BKB27.blurb:
This is the last evening of the men's group phase, and France has plenty of reasons to be ready. They lost the final to the USA at Tokyo 2020 and again at Paris 2024, 98-87, with Stephen Curry's late threes doing the damage.

Wembanyama said after Paris that France has every chance in 2028. If they qualify and tip off at 9:30 PM, the crowd will find out whether he meant it.

Germany is the other name to circle, with 2023 and 2025 titles and nine players who were on both rosters. Group play ends tonight, and the knockout bracket takes shape.

BKB28.blurb:
One loss, and it's over. After nine days of group play, the women's bracket gets real.

The afternoon tip is the first of the knockout games, and The Wall is going to be loud for every stop. A team that has coasted through the group phase suddenly finds itself in a 40-minute fight.

With the USA chasing a ninth straight title, someone is going to have to play the game of their life to stop them. France nearly did it at Paris 2024, losing 67-66, and led by 14 in the 2026 World Cup final before losing.

BKB29.blurb:
The American women's World Cup winning streak stands at 36 games, and Saturday night in Inglewood is a good place to see whether it lasts.

A quarterfinal after dark carries a different charge than the afternoon games. The 8 PM tip lets the crowd settle in, and the Dome feels full from the first possession.

The USA beat Spain 76-66 in the 2026 semifinals after leading only 39-36 at halftime. That kind of squeeze is what every opponent hopes to repeat. Nobody has managed it for long.

BKB30.blurb:
The final women's quarterfinal arrives on a Sunday afternoon with the field already thinned. Whatever team is left standing feels like it has a chance.

The pool is deep. Belgium won Group C at the 2026 World Cup, with Australia second, and Japan and Canada are the type of side that can play spoiler. The Americans' 2026 roster was the second-youngest they've sent to a World Cup, which makes the chase for the ninth straight title more interesting.

A 1 PM tip is a good time for families, and The Wall behind the basket gets loud when a team hits a run.

BKB31.blurb:
One bad night and it's over. The women's knockout round starts here, and the United States, chasing a ninth straight gold, can't afford the kind of 14-point first-half hole France dug for them at the 2026 World Cup.

Every team in this bracket knows the margin is thin. At Paris 2024 the Americans beat France by a single point, 67-66.

Sit behind the basket at Intuit Dome and you'll hear the sound of an indoor arena built purely for hoops. The Wall, 51 rows of fans stacked at one end, turns every free throw into a wall of noise. With a prime-time 8 PM tip, this is where the field starts to shrink.

BKB32.blurb:
The post-LeBron, post-Curry era starts to take shape here. LeBron James has said he'll be watching, and Stephen Curry has called playing highly unlikely. Erik Spoelstra's US team will be built from a new generation.

That makes a Monday afternoon quarterfinal a real test. Five straight titles do not guarantee a sixth, and a single-elimination game gives an underdog its best shot.

The 1 PM start means a daytime crowd that has had time to build. At Intuit Dome, the sightlines are steep and close, and the halo board overhead keeps every possession in view.

Victor Wembanyama is 22 and already carries a country. France named him captain in 2026, making him the youngest captain since Tony Parker in 2003, and after Paris 2024 he said the final loss would drive France to go for gold.

In that loss to the US he scored 26 points. Now picture him doing it at night, in front of a loud Inglewood crowd, with a quarterfinal on the line.

If France is here, this is the session to circle for the sheer size of the story. A 7-foot-plus captain who moves like a guard is something you have to see in person.

This is a good session for the fan who likes depth. At 1 PM there is no prime-time glare, just a full arena and a tournament narrowing fast.

Even the qualifying games have been tight. A US team of non-NBA players beat the Dominican Republic 82-81 in July 2026, then Mexico 94-93. That's a reminder that even the biggest favorite wins by inches sometimes.

By Tuesday night of the quarterfinal round, the stars arrive and the stakes sharpen. Erik Spoelstra will coach the US at the 2027 World Cup and in 2028, and no roster has been announced.

BKB36.blurb:
France led the US by 14 in the first half of the 2026 World Cup final, the biggest deficit the Americans had faced at a World Cup since 2006. The Americans won 97-79 anyway.

That's the template for a semifinal: a challenger lands a punch, and the favorite either answers or doesn't. Gabby Williams had 20 points and seven assists in that final, and Breanna Stewart scored 22 on the way to a record second tournament MVP.

Four o'clock is early enough for sunlight outside and a full house inside. The winner books a spot in the gold medal game three days away.

BKB37.blurb:
Late semifinal, late night, and a gold medal game as the prize. That's the kind of setup that makes the 9:30 PM slot special.

The Americans have the youth and the depth. Their 2026 World Cup roster was the second-youngest they've sent, and it still won. Jackie Young added 18 in the final, and Caitlin Clark hit a three just before halftime.

But Spain is no pushover. It beat host Germany 81-58 for bronze at the World Cup behind 20-year-old Iyana Martin, and Spain would love to turn that bronze into a gold-medal-game run.

Here is the first men's semifinal, and it arrives in a new era. LeBron James has ruled himself out. Stephen Curry, who closed Paris 2024 with late threes, said it's highly unlikely he'll play. The torch has to pass.

That opens the door. Victor Wembanyama has said France is aiming for gold after losing the Paris final, and a semifinal is where that ambition could meet the US head-on.

An afternoon tip at Intuit Dome gives you a loud, full arena and a clear view of a sport changing generations. Whoever wins is one game from the final.

The night session carries the weight. The US is going for a sixth straight title, and Wembanyama's France wants to stop it.

With the 9:30 PM tip, the arena will be at full volume. It's a good ticket if you want the best of the knockout bracket under the lights.

BKB40.blurb:
Nobody dreams of this game, and yet it's often the most relaxed, joyful basketball of the tournament. Australia won the Paris 2024 bronze, and Spain took its third World Cup bronze in 2026. Players walk off with a medal around their necks.

The stakes are real, but the pressure is different. Expect looser shooting, bigger smiles, and fans who got in for a fraction of the final's cost.

It's a Friday afternoon at Intuit Dome with the gold game a day away. For the price, it's one of the better values on the schedule.

The afternoon tip at Intuit Dome means a full house and 4,500 people on The Wall. Fans will remember this one for a long time.

A Sunday afternoon final at Intuit Dome, with the halo board overhead and The Wall roaring. Nothing else on the basketball schedule compares.

BMF01.blurb:
Twenty-four riders, twelve spots in each final, and no safety net. Qualification is where a BMX park career can end with one clipped coping or a bailed tailwhip, which is why the morning matters even though no medals get handed out.

This is also the best chance to see the whole field before the pressure peaks. Rimu Nakamura of Japan took 2026 World Cup rounds in Montpellier and Shanghai and won Asian Games gold. Sun Sibei of China, the 2025 women's world champion, has been just as hard to beat. Paris 2024 gold medalist Deng Yawen is a name to watch for if she makes the team.

The setting is a temporary park in the Sepulveda Basin, in the San Fernando Valley, a short drive from where organized BMX racing began in 1969. A 10:30 AM start means riders get a bright Southern California morning for their runs.

BMF02.blurb:
Sixty seconds. Two shots. Only the better run counts. At Paris 2024 the men's podium was separated by barely a point, 94.82 to 93.91 to 93.76. A single clean run can decide a medal, and so can a single crash.

The women's side carries just as much tension. Deng Yawen posted the top score on both of her runs in Paris to win China's first title in the discipline, but Sun Sibei now owns the 2025 world title and has kept winning in 2026. Hannah Roberts, the six-time world champion, missed the podium in Paris and could be back for another chance if she qualifies.

Expect a long morning at a temporary park in the Sepulveda Basin, with riders firing off tricks and the crowd reacting to every landing.

BMX01.blurb:
Brisbane's 2026 world championships lost every Sunday final to wind, a reminder that BMX is eight riders, one gate and a lot of things out of your control. Here the stakes are quieter but just as real: quarterfinal heats and last chance runs decide who earns a semifinal spot.

This is the session for seeing the whole field before the pressure peaks. Short heats, dirt jumps, banked turns and elbows trading into the first corner, all under full mid-July sun in the Sepulveda Basin.

A last chance run is where a favorite learns how thin the margin is. Get there early and watch the stars scramble.
