CLB06.blurb:
Janja Garnbret has 51 World Cup and series wins, 33 of them in Lead, and she still found time in June 2026 to make the first female ascent of Bibliographie, a 9b+ route in France. This is the one discipline where the question is how, not whether.

But Annie Sanders of the USA won the 2026 women's Lead overall title, so the chase now has a face and a home crowd.

The evening semifinal is when the route starts separating the field. Climbers go one at a time, and the stands lean forward with every move.

CLB07.blurb:
At the 2026 Keqiao final, Sorato Anraku finished 14.8 points ahead of Lee Dohyun. In a sport where one missed top can reorder a podium, that is a comfortable cushion, and it is the margin a rival has to erase.

This is the first men's Boulder final to award a medal of its own, not a half of a combined result. Anraku arrives as the reigning world champion and four-time series champion, with Paris silver already on his shelf.

Expect a loud morning: four problems, a crowd that breathes with every attempt, and the Pacific behind it all. A single flash of a top can bring the stands to their feet.

CLB08.blurb:
One boulder. That is all that separated France's Oriane Bertone from the 2025 world title in Seoul, until she failed to top the last problem and Janja Garnbret took the gold. Expect a final that can turn on a single move.

Garnbret has 10 world titles and 18 of her 51 series wins in Boulder, but Zélia Avezou beat her in Keqiao in 2026, and the 2026 standings went into the finale led by Erin McNeice.

It is the first women's Boulder medal ever decided on its own. Friday morning, four problems, and a stadium that learns quickly when to hold its breath.

CLB09.blurb:
One climber could play two of these medal events. Under the qualification rules, an athlete who qualifies in two disciplines counts as one entry, so Sorato Anraku could chase Boulder gold one day and Lead the next, if he qualifies in both.

That sets up a sharp contrast with the specialists. South Korea's Lee Dohyun is the reigning world Lead champion, and Japan's Neo Suzuki won the 2026 series title.

Lead is a single route, a single attempt, and a rope that decides who goes highest. It is a short afternoon session, but a fall in the last metres can flip the podium.
CLB09.potentialContendersIntro: Lee Dohyun is the reigning Lead world champion. The rest are projections based on 2026 standings and Paris 2024 results.

CLB10.blurb:
The final climbing medal of the Games could belong to Janja Garnbret. She has won Lead 33 times at World Cup and series level, and she took four straight at the Koper stop, so she is the favorite for the top rung.

But Annie Sanders won the 2026 Lead overall title, which means a home-crowd rival could be waiting on the wall. Brooke Raboutou and Jessica Pilz, silver and bronze in Paris, add experience to the chase.

Lead finals are one route, one fall, one rope. On a Saturday morning with the Pacific behind the wall, every foothold gets a full-stadium gasp.

CRD01.blurb:
One rider, one clock, no hiding. In Paris, Remco Evenepoel beat Filippo Ganna through rain-soaked streets, and on the women's side Grace Brown won in 39:38.24. Brown has since retired, so this time the women's gold goes to someone new.

This is not a stadium night. You'll stand on a roadside near the zoo entrance in the Griffith Park hills and watch each rider roll down the start ramp alone, a minute or so apart. Then they're gone, up a roughly 35 km course that finishes at Griffith Observatory. You see each of them for a few seconds, so the real drama sits in the splits and the big screens, and in the murmur that builds when someone posts a time nobody can beat.

Both medal events share this one day, a few days before the road races.
CRD01.potentialContendersIntro: Evenepoel won the Paris 2024 men's race and then took the 2025 world title in Kigali, his third straight. Neither he nor Ganna is confirmed for 2028, so the lists below are projections. The women's field is wide open after Brown's retirement.

CRD02.blurb:
Faulkner was a late call-up in Paris, and she won by 58 seconds. Now picture her attacking on home roads, with the Pacific at her back and a hillside finish waiting. If she makes the team, that is the story.

At 150 km, this is shorter than the men's race, so expect less waiting and more fighting. The start is on Venice Beach Boardwalk, where fans can line the roadside with palm trees, skaters and the ocean behind them as the peloton rolls out. It then heads inland through the city to Griffith Observatory.

The finale is a 3.9 km climb at about 4.9 percent, with ramps near 6.7 percent. That is steep enough to break a race open, and Demi Vollering, who still lacks a gold from the Games, is exactly the sort of rider who could do it.
CRD02.potentialContendersIntro: Paris 2024 gold medalist Kristen Faulkner (USA) could defend her title if she makes the team, though she has not confirmed 2028 participation. The rest of the field below is projected from recent form and is not confirmed.

CRD03.blurb:
Two weeks, maybe less, is all the peloton gets between the Tour de France finish on July 16 and this start line. Every rider here has to decide how much of that race is still in the legs.

The field gathers on the Venice Beach Boardwalk for a 250 km run to Griffith Observatory. It starts at the beach and ends on a 3.9 km climb of roughly 4.9 percent, with ramps near 6.7 percent. The full route is not yet published, but the finish is a place to attack, not hide.

The cast is built for drama. Remco Evenepoel arrives as reigning champion and has already ridden an early recon in Los Angeles. Tadej Pogacar says he wants this title and would shape his season around it. And Brandon McNulty is the American world champion, the first elite men's world road champion from the USA since 1993.
CRD03.potentialContendersIntro: Remco Evenepoel (BEL) is the Paris 2024 champion. Everyone else listed is a projection from recent form, since 2028 rosters are not set.

CSL01.blurb:
The first paddle strokes of the 2028 Games come before the Opening Ceremony lights go up in Los Angeles. That makes this a chance to say you saw the sport's first morning.

The field is big, and nobody has a free ride. Every kayaker gets two runs through a 304.8-metre concrete channel, and the best of the two counts. One touched gate or one missed line can ruin a run, so the early heats are tense, not casual.

Sit on the bank with the downtown Oklahoma City skyline behind the whitewater, and watch the favorites feel out the course. Jessica Fox and Jakub Krejci both won world titles on this water in 2026.
CSL01.potentialContendersIntro: Both men's and women's K1 run here. Fox and Krejci won the 2026 world titles in Oklahoma City, so they are the confirmed form guides. Who actually lines up in 2028 is still to be determined.

CSL02.blurb:
Jess Fox missed the entire 2025 season after surgery to remove a tumour from her kidney. Nine months later she was back, and by July 2026 she was world champion on this very channel.

That's the story hanging over this session. Fox clocked 92.06 seconds in that final, and Evy Leibfarth finished 1.31 seconds behind her. If both make the team, the American will have a home crowd cheering her on this course. Semifinal and final are crammed into one morning, so the margin for error is thin.

This is one of the first medal events of the Games. There are no second runs in the final, so each paddler gets one trip down the rapids and must make it count.

CSL03.blurb:
Over one summer in Oklahoma City, Jakub Krejci turned the men's K1 into his own territory. He won the 2026 world title in 83.65 seconds, then added a home World Cup win in Prague.

But the margins here tend to be tight. Michal Pasiut was 0.69 seconds back for silver, and Paris champion Giovanni De Gennaro took bronze at 85.27. The best male paddlers in the world have now seen this channel in anger, which means no one in the final will be unfamiliar with it.

It's a Sunday morning on the banks of the Oklahoma River, and the semifinal and final come back-to-back. Nobody gets to coast, and any slip is punished at once.

CSL04.blurb:
Canoe slalom's less-famous boat is the one where paddlers kneel, use a single blade, and wrestle the current from a very different angle. This is where the C1 field gets sorted.

Men and women both get two runs, and everyone is trying to survive without a gate penalty. Spain's Miquel Trave won the men's world title here in 2026. Women's C1 has Jess Fox, the Paris 2024 champion, and Evy Leibfarth, who won bronze there and hopes to find her best on home soil.

The session is short at about two and a half hours. It's also a good morning to get a first look at both finals fields before the semifinal pressure begins.

CSL05.blurb:
Jess Fox came to Paris and won both K1 and C1, something no woman had done at one Games. Here is a chance to see whether she can defend the C1 half of that double.

But the field has moved on since then. Slovakia took the 2026 women's team title with Zuzana Pankova, Sona Stanovska and Emanuela Luknarova, which suggests depth beyond the usual names. The Czech Republic and France followed. Evy Leibfarth, Paris bronze medalist, was ninth at the 2026 worlds, so she'll want redemption in front of home fans.

Semifinal and final share a morning. By the end, one of those boats is carrying a medal home.
CSL05.potentialContendersIntro: Fox is the Paris 2024 champion, while Slovakia's depth showed in the 2026 team event. Selections are not set, so these are projected contenders for 2028.

CSL06.blurb:
Adam Burgess has been close before. Paris 2024 silver, 2026 world silver on this course, 1.49 seconds behind Miquel Trave. This could be the session where he gets over the top.

Trave, the Spaniard, won the 2026 world title in 88.28 seconds, but the men's C1 is a wide-open field. Nicolas Gestin, the Paris champion, won the Prague World Cup in June 2026. Lukas Kratochvil took world bronze, and Slovenia's Ziga Lin Hocevar has shown up in finals.

The semifinal and final are back to back, so the best of the morning has to survive twice. Wednesday morning, the cheers reward every clean line.

CSL07.blurb:
Kayak cross is chaos with a clock. Several boats leave the start ramp at once, they all want the same line, and the first one through the final gate wins. Nobody can plan for the bump.

The repechage gives paddlers a second chance after a bad first round, so the stakes are higher than a simple prelim. At the 2026 worlds here, 77 men from 40 nations raced, the biggest individual field of the meet. Any of them could take a good lane and get to the next round.

The session runs three hours of heat after heat on the banks of the Oklahoma River. If you like noise and surprise, this is it.

CSL08.blurb:
The crowds have been watching a lot of individual runs, but kayak cross heats feel different. Four boats race through the same gates and only the quickest advance. Contact is part of the show.

This is a short two-hour session, so it moves quickly between rounds. The men's field is big, with 77 from 40 nations at the 2026 worlds, so some of the better-known paddlers can go home early.

Watch for Alena Marx and her brother Dimitri, who both reached the 2026 world podium. They race on instinct and they race aggressively.

potentialContenders.name: Evy Leibfarth
potentialContenders.note: Reached the semifinals and finished 10th at the 2026 World Cup Final. A home-crowd storyline if she lines up.

CSL09.blurb:
Finn Butcher won the first men's kayak cross at the Games, and Noemie Fox won the first women's race. Now both formats get a second chance, with two medals decided in the last slalom session of the Games.

Vit Prindis, 37, won the 2026 world title here by passing Dimitri Marx late. Alena Marx took the women's world title with Noemie Fox second. That means plenty of paddlers have recent proof that this channel rewards quick decisions.

Quarterfinals, semifinals and finals fit into 2 hours and 20 minutes. It's loud and chaotic, and then the slalom program is done.
CSL09.potentialContendersIntro: The 2026 world champions and Paris 2024 winners headline the projected fields for both finals. Selection for 2028 is not confirmed.

potentialContenders.name: Noemie Fox

CSP01.blurb:
One hundredth of a second. That's what separated Katie Vincent's world-record 44.12 from Nevin Harrison's 44.13 in the Paris 2024 women's C1 200m. Harrison, away for more than a year afterward, was back racing in May 2026, and Ukraine's Liudmyla Luzan won that year's world title.

The men's C1 1000m adds a different tension. Czechia's Martin Fuksa and Hungary's Daniel Fejes tied for gold at the 2026 Worlds, so nobody should expect an easy heat.

This is a morning for scouting. You stand on the shoreline of a saltwater channel dredged for the 1932 Games, with Belmont Shore behind you, watching crews fight for finals spots.

potentialContenders.name: Katie Vincent

CSP02.blurb:
Lisa Carrington had her first child in October 2026 and still calls the 2028 Games her goal. If she makes the New Zealand boat, a fifth Games and another run at the women's K2 500m would be among the stories of the week.

She'd have to beat a field that has moved on without her. Australia's Kailey Harlen and Natalia Drobot are the reigning world champions, with China and Germany close behind.

The men's C1 1000m closes the morning. Fuksa, the Paris champion, tied for 2026 world gold, while Brazil's Isaquias Queiroz is chasing redemption after finishing last in that race. Semifinals and finals are packed into one morning along a narrow channel.
CSP02.potentialContendersIntro: The headline events are the women's K2 500m and the men's C1 1000m. Rosters for 2028 are not set, so these names are projections.

potentialContenders.name: Isaquias Queiroz
potentialContenders.note: Paris silver medalist who won the 2026 world C1 500m, his eighth world title, and says 2028 is his focus. He finished last in the 1000m at Worlds after eye surgery and a hip problem.

CSP03.blurb:
Fernando Pimenta won the 2026 world K1 1000m title by 0.22 seconds over Hungary's Balint Kopasz. Add Czechia's Paris champion Josef Dostal and Australia's Thomas Green, and the men's 1000m field looks deep before the heats even start.

The women's K1 500m is just as open. Germany's Pauline Jagsch is the reigning world champion. New Zealand's Aimee Fisher and Australia's Natalia Drobot took the other medals in 2026, and Lisa Carrington's possible return would add another layer.

This is the longest morning of the week, with K4 and C2 crews filling the lanes. You get a look at the contenders in a loose, early-round setting.
CSP03.potentialContendersIntro: The marquee events here are the men's K1 1000m and women's K1 500m. All 2028 entries are projections.

potentialContenders.name: Fernando Pimenta
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 world K1 1000m title in 3:24.39 and also took the K1 5000m, so he's a likely medal contender.

potentialContenders.note: Paris bronze medalist and 2025 world champion who was second to Pimenta in 2026.

potentialContenders.name: Lisa Carrington
potentialContenders.note: Paris K1 500m champion. If she returns after having her first child in October 2026, she'd be the attraction of any heat.

CSP04.blurb:
Lisa Carrington won the Paris 2024 women's K1 500m in a new Games-best time. It was one of three golds that tied the all-time canoeing record at eight. She has said she plans to be in Long Beach.

She'd arrive after a baby and two skipped seasons, and a younger crop has taken over. Jagsch of Germany is the reigning world champion, and Poland's Anna Pulawska won in 2025.

The men's K1 1000m feels a lot like a heavyweight bout over two minutes and fifty seconds or so. Pimenta, Kopasz, Green and Dostal have traded major titles since Paris. Germany, the 2026 world champions in the women's C2 500m, hope to take on China's Paris winners in that event.
CSP04.potentialContendersIntro: Focus is on the women's K1 500m and the men's K1 1000m. These are projections for 2028 rather than confirmed entries.

potentialContenders.name: Lisa Carrington

potentialContenders.name: Balint Kopasz

CSP05.blurb:
Katie Vincent owns a world record, 44.12, and a Paris 2024 gold by one hundredth of a second. At the 2026 Worlds she did not medal in the C1 200m. That's the pressure point for a race over in less time than it takes to tie a shoe.

Luzan of Ukraine won that world title. Canada's Sophia Jensen, a new world champion at 500m, was second in the 200m, and American Nevin Harrison, back after a long break, was third.

The final morning also brings the K4 finals, the loudest boats on the water. Germany won the men's in Paris, and New Zealand won the women's with Carrington. The program ends with whoever finds the final surge down the channel.
CSP05.potentialContendersIntro: The marquee event is the women's C1 200m, and the field below is a projection of who could appear in 2028.

potentialContenders.name: Yarisleidis Cirilo

CTR01.blurb:
Nine in the morning, and the quickest riders on earth are already at the start gate. There is no warm-up lap for the crowd here. Team sprint qualifying is a standing-start burst where one slow launch from the first rider can wreck a whole run.

The Netherlands arrives as Paris 2024 champion in a world-record 40.949 and reigning world champion. China, riding high after a 2026 women's world title, and Great Britain, the Paris women's champion, are the ones to measure them against.

The home angle is quieter but real. The US women qualified in 48.097 at the 2026 Worlds and missed the next round by about half a second. In a 2,450-seat building, you will hear every launch.
CTR01.potentialContendersIntro: Teams to watch in qualifying across both team sprints. Paris 2024 results are confirmed; the 2028 line-ups are projections.

potentialContenders.name: Netherlands (men)
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold in a world-record 40.949 and 2026 world champions with Hoogland, Lavreysen and van den Berg. Likely the benchmark.

potentialContenders.name: Australia (men)
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze and 2026 world silver. Could push the Dutch for the fastest qualifying time.

potentialContenders.name: China (women)
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 world title in 45.578 at home in Shanghai. A rising force heading to Los Angeles.

potentialContenders.name: Great Britain (women)
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 champions in a world-record 45.186 and 2026 world silver. Emma Finucane could anchor again if selected.

potentialContenders.name: United States (women)
potentialContenders.note: Best-ever seventh in 2025, then missed the 2026 cut by about 0.5 seconds. Home soil is the storyline.

CTR02.blurb:
Medals get decided before lunch. The men's and women's team sprint finals share a session, and the house will go from held breath to uproar in under a minute.

The Dutch men set the Paris 2024 bar at 40.949, and Harrie Lavreysen's squad has stayed unbeaten at the Worlds since. On the women's side, China's 2026 world title at home put a new name on the board, while Great Britain's record 45.186 from Paris still stands.

Stay for the afternoon tail. Men's team pursuit qualifying begins, with Denmark, the 2025 and 2026 world champion, bidding to unseat Australia's Paris gold. The compact Carson track puts you a few meters from the speed.
CTR02.potentialContendersIntro: For the team sprint finals, these riders were part of recent medal-winning squads. Who is in the 2028 line-ups is speculative.

potentialContenders.name: Emma Finucane

potentialContenders.name: Yuan Liying

CTR03.blurb:
The flying 200m is the sprinter's naked truth: one rider, one lap of build-up, ten seconds of nothing hidden. Men's sprint qualifying opens the knockout bracket, and the fastest riders are looking for the easiest road to the later rounds.

Matt Richardson holds the world record of 8.857 and beat Harrie Lavreysen at the 2026 Europeans, but he was withdrawn from Britain's 2026 Worlds squad amid a misconduct investigation. His 2028 status is unresolved.

Around the sprints are the women's team pursuit, which has a story of its own. The United States won Paris 2024 gold, then qualified ninth at the 2026 Worlds. Britain's record of 4:02.808 sets the pace now.
CTR03.potentialContendersIntro: For men's sprint qualifying and the women's keirin first round, these are projected names. None have been confirmed for 2028.

potentialContenders.name: Harrie Lavreysen

potentialContenders.name: Matt Richardson

potentialContenders.name: Leigh Hoffman
potentialContenders.note: 2026 world sprint runner-up, beaten 2-0 by Lavreysen. Could hit the fast times in qualifying.

potentialContenders.name: Kaiya Ota

potentialContenders.name: Alina Lysenko
potentialContenders.note: Individual Neutral Athlete and 2026 women's keirin world champion. Her 2028 eligibility is not confirmed.

CTR04.blurb:
The team pursuit final is four minutes of metronomic cruelty. Four riders, one rotating line, and the whole crowd staring at the gap between two jerseys on the opposite straight.

Australia took Paris 2024 gold after a world record in the heats, but Denmark has owned the world titles since, taking 2025 and 2026. Italy, with Filippo Ganna and Jonathan Milan, and Great Britain are very much in the mix.

The session also starts the men's sprint knockouts and has the women's keirin quarterfinals. Sprint rounds are decided in moments, and the keirin is a scrum behind the derny pacing bike. Add the 45-degree banking and a seat close to the rail.
CTR04.potentialContendersIntro: For the men's team pursuit final and the women's keirin, these riders are projected based on recent form. None are confirmed for 2028.

potentialContenders.name: Filippo Ganna

potentialContenders.name: Alina Lysenko

CTR05.blurb:
Thursday is a day of medals. The women's team pursuit final is the headline, and for the home fans, it carries a sting. The United States won Paris 2024 gold, then qualified ninth at the 2026 Worlds in 4:18.810 and failed to advance.

Great Britain's world-record squad is the team to beat, but anything can happen in four minutes.

Around it, the men's omnium is a full day's chess match across four races, with Portugal's Iuri Leitao the reigning world champion. Late in the day, the women's keirin final looks like a sprint behind the derny: elbows, a wooden roar, then silence as the photo-finish result is read.

CTR06.blurb:
Harrie Lavreysen has not lost a world sprint title since 2019. Eight in a row, 23 world titles in all. Then Matt Richardson beat him in the 2026 European final and the story changed.

Men's sprint semifinals are best-of-three duels where tactics matter as much as raw speed. Watch the track stand: the slow circling, the shoulder checks, the sudden launch. It looks like nothing until it looks like everything.

The morning also opens the women's sprint, with qualifying and early rounds. China's Yuan Liying, 21, beat Emma Finucane 2-0 for the 2026 world title. Early heats are where you see the stars before the bracket tightens.
CTR06.potentialContendersIntro: For the men's sprint semifinals and women's sprint opening rounds, these are projected names. 2028 participation is not confirmed.

CTR07.blurb:
Two rides, maybe three, and the men's sprint title is decided. Last year Lavreysen beat Leigh Hoffman by 0.093 and 0.183 seconds. In a sport of hundredths, that is thin margin and total control.

The Dutchman has taken the Paris 2024 sprint gold and the 2026 world title, and he finds himself again at the center. If Richardson is cleared to ride, expect a fierce rematch.

The women's madison final adds another twist. It is chaos by design: relays, sprints for points, a lap gained. Britain's Anna Morris and Erin Boothman won the 2026 world title with 40 points. The crowd will be loud.
CTR07.potentialContendersIntro: For the men's sprint final and women's madison final, these riders are projected based on recent form. The 2028 line-ups remain open.

potentialContenders.name: Harrie Lavreysen

CTR08.blurb:
The men's madison is the sport's most chaotic final, and also its most beautiful. Hand slings, points sprints every ten laps, and a leaderboard that can flip with one lap gained.

Denmark's Carl-Frederik Bevort and Lasse Norman Leth won the 2026 world title with 88 points, well ahead of Portugal's Iuri Leitao and Ivo Oliveira on 67. Portugal won Paris 2024 gold, so the order is up for grabs.

Earlier, the women's sprint reaches the 1/8 and quarterfinals. China's Yuan Liying won the 2026 world title, while Britain's Emma Finucane keeps coming close. The compact Carson Velodrome keeps the two-man relays within touching distance.
CTR08.potentialContendersIntro: For the men's madison final and the women's sprint, these riders are projected. Nothing is confirmed for 2028.

potentialContenders.name: Emma Finucane

CTR09.blurb:
The final morning of track racing starts early and ends loud. Three golds, three very different stories.

The women's sprint pairs Yuan Liying, 21, who won the 2026 world title in Shanghai, against a field that includes Emma Finucane and Paris 2024 champion Ellesse Andrews. The men's keirin is Lavreysen's to lose: he won Paris 2024 gold and the 2026 world title. A derny pacing bike peels off, and eight riders have two and a half laps to settle it.

The women's omnium, held across four races, tests every skill. Anna Morris and Jennifer Valente, two-time Games champion, would be fascinating to see race.
CTR09.potentialContendersIntro: For the women's sprint, men's keirin and women's omnium, these riders are projected. The 2028 entry lists are not confirmed.

potentialContenders.name: Harrie Lavreysen
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 keirin champion and 2026 world keirin champion. A heavy favorite for gold if selected.

potentialContenders.name: Matt Richardson

potentialContenders.name: Yuan Liying

DIV01.blurb:
Ten in the morning, the hills of Brookside Park rising behind the pool, and the springboard is about to get its first real workout of the Games. Nobody collects a medal today, but plenty of people can lose one.

Chen Yiwen, the Paris 2024 champion, is the name to track, and China arrives off a nine-for-nine run at the Montreal World Cup stop. The better subplot sits lower in the order: Britain's Andrea Spendolini-Sirieix, a former platform diver, has retrained on springboard and says she wants a spot.

Prelims are where you see the whole field up close, unhurried, before the pressure arrives.
DIV01.potentialContendersIntro: Chen Yiwen is the reigning champion and won the 2026 Asian Games title; the rest of the field is projected and will depend on qualification through 2027 and 2028.

potentialContenders.name: Chen Yiwen

potentialContenders.name: Andrea Spendolini-Sirieix

DIV02.blurb:
This is the round that breaks hearts quietly. One crooked entry, one early-leaving twist, and a favorite is done before the afternoon crowd ever arrives.

The semifinal trims the springboard field down to the finalists, and the divers know it. Chen Yiwen has been the model of control: gold in Paris, then springboard and synchro titles at the 2026 Asian Games, the synchro win by more than 70 points.

The real tension is behind her. Keeney and the challengers need clean lists here, and in the open air of the Arroyo Seco, the quiet between dives is the loudest part of the morning.
DIV02.potentialContendersIntro: Chen Yiwen and Maddison Keeney are the Paris 2024 gold and silver medalists; who joins them is speculation until qualification is complete.

potentialContenders.name: Chen Yiwen
potentialContenders.note: Defending champion with fresh 2026 Asian Games titles in both individual and synchro.

potentialContenders.name: Maddison Keeney
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalist; if she is on the team, a semifinal safely navigated is her first goal.

potentialContenders.name: Andrea Spendolini-Sirieix

DIV03.blurb:
The first individual diving medals of the Games get decided on a summer afternoon in Pasadena, and the question is a blunt one: can anyone beat China's springboard machine?

Chen Yiwen won in Paris with Maddison Keeney of Australia behind her, and she has kept stacking titles, including the 2026 Asian Games. China won all eight diving golds in Paris, the first clean sweep in the sport's history, and the rest of the world has spent the cycle looking for cracks.

Watch the board at the start of each dive. The hush, the bounce, the tiny splash: a perfect entry is barely a sound, and the crowd will answer it anyway.
DIV03.potentialContendersIntro: Chen Yiwen is the defending champion and the clear favorite; the challengers listed are projections based on Paris 2024 and recent form.

potentialContenders.name: Chen Yiwen
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 champion who won the 2026 Asian Games springboard and synchro titles.

potentialContenders.name: Maddison Keeney
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalist and a likely contender for another podium if she qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Andrea Spendolini-Sirieix
potentialContenders.note: Speculative finalist: a former platform medalist trying to make the Games on springboard, with a fourth-place finish at the 2026 British championships.

DIV04.blurb:
Osmar Olvera is the reigning world champion, and he arrives at a Games on the same continent as home. That alone gives this morning an edge.

The Mexican diver took bronze in Paris behind two Chinese divers, then won the 1m, 3m and 3m synchro at the 2026 Central American and Caribbean Games, scoring 535.30 on springboard. Xie Siyi, born in 1996, owns the last two Games titles and has the calm of a man who has seen every board.

The prelim is the best chance to watch all of them in a relaxed rhythm before finals pressure takes over.
DIV04.potentialContendersIntro: Xie Siyi is the Paris 2024 champion and Osmar Olvera the reigning world champion; others are projected and depend on the 2027 and 2028 qualification path.

potentialContenders.name: Xie Siyi

potentialContenders.name: Wang Zongyuan

potentialContenders.name: Jack Laugher

DIV05.blurb:
Two Chinese divers, one Mexican, and a whole afternoon of arithmetic. That was the Paris podium, and this semifinal is where the 2028 version begins to take shape.

Xie Siyi and Wang Zongyuan are teammates who push each other as hard as any rival could. Osmar Olvera is the wild card: reigning world champion, three-time winner at the 2026 Central American and Caribbean Games, and the diver most likely to crash the Chinese party.

This is the round that sets the final field, so every board is a small trial. Sit near the diving well and you'll hear the board's twang before each takeoff.

potentialContenders.note: Reigning world champion who took three golds at the 2026 Central American and Caribbean Games.

potentialContenders.name: Juan Celaya
potentialContenders.note: Olvera's Paris 2024 synchro partner and 3m bronze medalist at the 2026 Central American and Caribbean Games; a possible semifinalist if he qualifies.

DIV06.blurb:
Of the three men on the Paris springboard podium, only one was not Chinese. Osmar Olvera now holds the world title, and this final is his best chance to turn bronze into something shinier.

Xie Siyi has won this event at the last two Games and would own a historic third if he gets here. Wang Zongyuan, his teammate and Paris silver medalist, knows exactly how thin the margin is.

The session runs barely 75 minutes. That is the whole drama: six rounds, a handful of divers, and a single hard truth, which is that one wobble costs you the medal.
DIV06.potentialContendersIntro: Xie Siyi won in Paris and Osmar Olvera is the reigning world champion; the 2028 field is projected until qualification closes in 2028.

potentialContenders.name: Jack Laugher

DIV07.blurb:
The biggest question in diving has nothing to do with scores. Will Quan Hongchan be here?

She won platform at Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024, then spoke openly in 2026 about the toll that followed. She also missed China's Asian Games trials in June with tibia and ankle injuries. Her presence in Pasadena is a hope, not a given.

If she is missing, Chen Yuxi, the Paris silver medalist and World Aquatics Female Diver of the Year, becomes the face of the event. Either way, this morning's prelim at the Rose Bowl is where the platform story first plays out.
DIV07.potentialContendersIntro: Quan Hongchan and Chen Yuxi went one-two in Paris 2024, but Quan's 2028 participation is uncertain given her injuries and public comments.

potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 champion; injured in 2026 and her 2028 status is unconfirmed, so treat her as a possibility only.

DIV08.blurb:
Ten meters is about three stories up, and the dive takes under two seconds. Do it five times in an afternoon, with a medal final on the line, and you begin to see the weight on these women.

This semifinal feeds the final, and the Chinese contingent carries two of the sport's biggest stories. Chen Yuxi took silver in Paris and competed in both individual and synchro platform at China's 2026 trials while Quan Hongchan sat out injured.

If Quan returns, this is the first chance to see whether her trademark near-silent entries survive the layoff.
DIV08.potentialContendersIntro: Chen Yuxi and Quan Hongchan took the Paris 2024 podium's top two spots; Quan's return is uncertain after her 2026 injuries.

DIV09.blurb:
Cao Yuan finished off China's Paris sweep, and now a bold Australian wants to end it.

Cassiel Rousseau is the reigning world champion on platform, and he will be looking for a Games result to match. Japan's Rikuto Tamai took silver in Paris, and Britain's Noah Williams took bronze. Yang Hao, China's world champion going into Paris, finished 12th, a reminder that platform can bite anyone.

Prelims are loose and watchable, and you can pick a favorite from the first few dives. Sit at the rim of the well and listen to the pool: the splash is the scoreboard.
DIV09.potentialContendersIntro: Cao Yuan, Rikuto Tamai and Noah Williams are the Paris 2024 medalists; whether they return in 2028 is projected, with Cassiel Rousseau the current world champion.

DIV10.blurb:
If Quan Hongchan stands on the platform, this could be the most emotional final of the diving program. She has won two individual Games titles and, in 2026, said she had wanted to retire during a stretch of body-image struggles and online scrutiny.

Her return would be earned the hard way. She also missed the Asian Games trials with tibia and ankle injuries, so nothing here is guaranteed.

Chen Yuxi, the Paris silver medalist, is more than a backup plan. A 3:30 PM start in the Arroyo Seco, five dives, and 10 meters of nerve: this one could be unforgettable.
DIV10.potentialContendersIntro: Quan Hongchan and Chen Yuxi went one-two at Paris 2024, but Quan's 2028 status is uncertain.

DIV11.blurb:
Platform is the one event where China's hold has looked loosest. The men's semifinal, with a final later the same day, is where the next challengers get their shot.

The Paris podium is already a wide net: Cao Yuan, Rikuto Tamai of Japan, Noah Williams of Great Britain. Cassiel Rousseau now holds the world title for Australia. Tom Daley has retired, leaving a hole in the British story, and Canada's Rylan Wiens and Nathan Zsombor-Murray, the Paris synchro bronze medalists, can compete individually too.

Only twelve move on, so the afternoon gets decided by a single clean entry.
DIV11.potentialContendersIntro: Cassiel Rousseau is the reigning world champion and Noah Williams and Rikuto Tamai are Paris 2024 medalists; all 2028 appearances are projections.

DIV12.blurb:
Platform has produced some surprises. Matthew Mitcham took gold for Australia in 2008, and David Boudia won for the United States in 2012, so the idea of a non-Chinese champion is not fantasy.

Cao Yuan has won this event at Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024, and his Paris win completed China's sweep. His 2028 plans have not been confirmed, so do not assume he is here. Cassiel Rousseau, the reigning world champion, is the figure to watch for Australia, with Tamai and Williams chasing their Paris medals.

The final runs just 75 minutes, which means one wobble ends a dream.
DIV12.potentialContendersIntro: Cao Yuan won in Paris, but his 2028 participation is unconfirmed; the others are projected based on Paris 2024 and current world rankings.

DIV13.blurb:
There is no prelim, no semifinal, no second chance. Two women, one board, and five dives that need to look like one.

China's Chen Yiwen won this event in Paris with Chang Yani. Now she has a new partner, Chen Jia, and the pair won the 2026 Asian Games by more than 70 points. The United States took silver in Paris with Sarah Bacon and Kassidy Cook, and as host nation, the Americans will be diving at home in this event.

Synchro rewards a certain kind of attention: watch the splash, then watch the two bodies hit the water together.

DIV14.blurb:
Great Britain's Jack Laugher and Chris Mears won this event at Rio 2016, and no pair from outside China has won it since. That drought is the story here.

China's Wang Zongyuan and Long Daoyi took gold in Paris. Mexico's Osmar Olvera and Juan Celaya took silver, and they added gold in 3m synchro at the 2026 Central American and Caribbean Games. Britain's Laugher and Anthony Harding took Paris bronze and followed it with a world championship bronze.

The afternoon session has a single final, and it is over fast. Sit up high enough to see the two bodies mirror each other all the way down.

DIV15.blurb:
Chen Yuxi and Quan Hongchan won gold in Paris, but Quan's injuries in 2026 reshaped the picture. Chen's new partner Lu Wei has since won the 2026 World Cup Super Final in Beijing and the Asian Games, scoring 347.82 at the latter.

North Korea's Jo Jin-mi and Kim Mi-rae, the Paris silver medalists, chased them to a 317.64 at the Asian Games. That gap of about 30 points is the challenge. Britain's Paris bronze pair will not return, since Andrea Spendolini-Sirieix moved to springboard.

The single-final format is brutal and beautiful. Five dives, perfect timing, and nowhere to hide.

DIV16.blurb:
Ten meters up, two bodies leave the platform as one. Then comes the part nobody can fake: the splash. Synchro is decided in a single final, with no semifinal to recover in and no second chance, so one early-hour mismatch can end a medal run.

China took gold in Paris with Lian Junjie and Yang Hao, part of a sweep of all eight diving titles. But this event has humbled favorites before: Tom Daley and Matty Lee beat China at Tokyo 2020. Daley retired after Paris 2024, so Great Britain's Noah Williams, who took silver there, is likely to be hunting for a fresh partner and a fresh answer.

Sit outdoors in the Arroyo Seco on a July afternoon, with the hills behind the tower. The crowd goes quiet at the top of every dive, then roars when the entries land clean and the water barely breaks.

EQU01.blurb:
The first horse into the ring at the first equestrian session of the Games will carry a long list of questions. The biggest: what does Michael Jung ride now? His champion FischerChipmunk FRH retired in November 2026 at 18, after eight straight championships.

Dressage is the quiet part of eventing, all precision and nerve, and a record-low score here can decide a medal days later. Paris 2024 saw Jung and Laura Collett both set dressage records.

Sit in the old Santa Anita grandstand at 9 AM, with the San Gabriel Mountains beyond the track. You are at the same racetrack that hosted equestrian in 1984, watching the first scores go up.

EQU02.blurb:
Late afternoon light, a long shadow across the track, and a sport that rewards stillness. Dressage numbers in eventing now run absurdly low, and this session is where a rider can post one that everyone else spends three days chasing.

Jung and FischerChipmunk FRH once set a CCI5*-L dressage record of 18.6 at Kentucky in 2025, then went on to win. Those scores are the benchmark, although that horse will not be here. Whoever tops the board in this session will enter cross-country with a real head start.

Bring a sweater for later. After the day's heat, the evening at Santa Anita can cool quickly.

EQU03.blurb:
This is the last dressage session before the standings go into cross-country, so it is the last chance to get a good score on the board. Anyone still behind needs a clean and very accurate test here.

Laura Collett knows how that feels. She and London 52 won the 2025 European title, then took team gold and individual bronze at the 2026 World Championships, the same results as at Paris 2024. Collett has said she may never find another horse like him.

Watch the scoreboard more than the arena. Some riders will leave with a lead worth protecting, and others will already be calculating the risks they must take on Monday.

EQU04.blurb:
Cross-country is the day eventing becomes a different sport. It starts at 8 AM, and nobody is quite sure what the morning will bring.

Collett called her Aachen 2026 round on London 52 the best she had ever had, and that came after a near miss. That is the level of risk riders carry out there. Jung and FischerChipmunk FRH went clear and fastest at those same world championships, but that horse has retired, so he will have to find speed with a new partner.

The racetrack grandstand holds about 26,000 people. When a horse and rider come home clear, you will hear it before you see the time.

EQU05.blurb:
Eventing never ends until the last rail is up. At the 2026 World Championships, Jung went last, needed a clear round inside the time to beat Ros Canter, rattled a pole that stayed up, and won.

That is what to expect on this final night, with both team and individual medals decided in one session that runs until 10 PM. Great Britain won the team title at Aachen by more than 11 penalties, but a rail here can change everything.

The lights, the grandstand, and the hush before each horse turns for the first fence will make this a very long and very tense evening.
EQU05.potentialContendersIntro: For the individual medals, likely contenders include the Paris 2024 podium and the 2026 world medalists. The 2028 horse and rider combinations remain unconfirmed.

EQU06.blurb:
Santa Anita saw Reiner Klimke win team and individual dressage gold on Ahlerich in 1984. Forty-plus years on, dressage returns to the same grounds, and the German tradition faces some real questions.

Jessica von Bredow-Werndl's gold-medal mare TSF Dalera BB retired in August 2024, and her rising horse Diallo BB died in January 2026. She missed the 2026 World Championships after Times Kismet went into quarantine.

So the morning opens with the most open dressage field in years. Germany still won the Aachen team title, with Isabell Werth and Katharina Hemmer posting the decisive scores. Expect the first Grand Prix tests to show who truly is in form.

EQU07.blurb:
Charlotte Fry and Glamourdale are the pair everyone will want to see. They won both the Grand Prix Special and the freestyle at Aachen 2026, and their freestyle score of 91.907% beat the 90.654% they scored at the 2022 world title.

That is a rare and consistent run of form, even though the pair finished ninth in the Grand Prix Special at the 2025 Europeans. The ability to bounce back is part of their story.

The afternoon session at Santa Anita also lets you compare the German, Danish, British and Belgian riders in the same arena. Fine margins in the Grand Prix will separate many of them.

EQU08.blurb:
Cathrine Laudrup-Dufour has been the bridesmaid at consecutive world championships, silver in the Grand Prix Special at Aachen 2026 and again at the previous worlds. She also won the Grand Prix at the 2025 Europeans. This is the rider who might finally close that gap.

Day 2 begins at 9 AM, and the pressure begins to rise. Six nations have already booked team places: Germany, Great Britain, Denmark, Belgium, the Netherlands and Sweden. The Paris 2024 team podium was Germany, Denmark and Great Britain, in that order.

Morning sessions are quieter, so the trade-off is the chance to be close to the arena.
EQU08.potentialContendersIntro: Projected names for Day 2's morning Grand Prix qualifier come from the 2026 world medalists. Start orders and 2028 teams are not confirmed.

EQU09.blurb:
The final Grand Prix session closes the door on qualifying. Whoever is not in the team final or the freestyle by the end of the evening is done.

Isabell Werth has been in this position many times. She won Paris 2024 individual silver, scored 79.876% to clinch Germany's team gold at Aachen 2026, and took freestyle bronze there with Queenparks Wendy de Fontaine.

Then there is von Bredow-Werndl, the reigning champion, who has lost two horses in two years. If Times Kismet is healthy and she is selected, hers is the name to wait for.

A warm evening in Arcadia, and tension in the stands.

EQU10.blurb:
Germany has won the world team title 13 times, most recently at Aachen 2026 by 3.618 points over Great Britain. That is not much margin, and it is the margin everyone in this stadium will be watching.

Germany also won its 26th European team title in 2025, but the 2026 gap was small enough that Britain, Denmark and others can dream. Charlotte Fry, with the Grand Prix Special world title, gives Britain a rider who can swing the result.

The team final is a slow burn. Each rider's score is a piece of the total, so the arithmetic builds all morning.

EQU11.blurb:
The 1984 Games saw Klimke take team gold at this very track, and the host country has come a long way since then. The United States finished eighth at Aachen 2026, so the home crowd has more to hope for than expect.

Still, this is the second half of the team final, and it can be the part where the medals become clear. Sweden, Belgium and the Netherlands all earned quota places at Aachen and could play spoiler.

With the afternoon sun low over the infield, the contrast between the German favorites and the hopeful underdogs makes a good story. Dressage is a team game where one costly mistake can matter a lot.

potentialContenders.note: 2026 double world champion on Glamourdale. Britain's strongest hope to beat Germany.

potentialContenders.name: Patrik Kittel
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2024 World Cup final on Touchdown. Sweden qualified a 2028 team quota, so he could be a key rider.

EQU12.blurb:
Charlotte Fry and Glamourdale rode to 91.907% in the Aachen 2026 freestyle, with artistic marks of 97.200%, in front of more than 40,000 spectators. That is the score everyone must beat.

Freestyle is dressage with music, and it is where riders show their personality. A morning session means a fresh crowd and clean air, and you may hear the music float across the track before you hear the applause.

Von Bredow-Werndl won both of her individual titles on TSF Dalera BB, who retired in August 2024. Whether she can find that same partnership with Times Kismet is one of the biggest questions of the entire Games.
EQU12.potentialContendersIntro: These are likely contenders for the individual freestyle medals, based on Paris 2024 and Aachen 2026. Nothing is confirmed, and several horse partnerships remain uncertain.

potentialContenders.name: Charlotte Fry

potentialContenders.name: Jessica von Bredow-Werndl

potentialContenders.name: Patrik Kittel

EQU13.blurb:
Great Britain is the reigning champion, but Germany arrives with real momentum. Its Aachen 2026 team win was its first world team jumping gold since 2010.

This qualifier decides which nations reach the team final, so it is more than a warm-up. The United States was second going into the Aachen team final, 1.37 penalties behind, and finished fourth. That memory will feel fresh to the home crowd.

Santa Anita's grandstand looks across a racetrack famous for fast horses, and the jumping course should be a very different kind of speed. Santa Anita is also where the 1984 U.S. Dream Team won gold, so the home riders have history behind them.
EQU13.potentialContendersIntro: These are projected leading riders for the jumping team qualifier. Team selection for 2028 is not confirmed, so these are likely names based on world rankings and recent form.

potentialContenders.note: Part of Germany's Aachen 2026 world title team. He could return as an anchor rider.

potentialContenders.name: Marcus Ehning
potentialContenders.note: Rode Coolio for Germany at Aachen 2026. A veteran who could be on the German team again.

EQU14.blurb:
A short session with a lot riding on it. It runs just over two hours, and every fence counts.

Germany's Aachen 2026 victory turned on one moment: Daniel Deusser and Otello de Guldenboom jumped clear to clinch the title before the last German rider, Richard Vogel, even went in. Ehning and Coolio were fault-free as well. That is a very hard standard for Great Britain, the defending champion, to match.

The United States, silver medalist at Paris 2024, finished fourth at Aachen and will want to fix that. In 1984 the U.S. Dream Team won gold at Santa Anita, and a home crowd will bring its own pressure.
EQU14.potentialContendersIntro: For the team final, likely stars come from Germany, Great Britain, the United States and Belgium. Selection for 2028 is still ahead, so these are projections only.

EQU15.blurb:
The defending champion might not defend with his champion horse. Christian Kukuk won at Paris 2024 on Checker 47 in a three-way jump-off, but in August 2026 he asked to have the horse taken off Germany's national championship squad.

Then Kukuk and Checker 47 won the London Grand Prix again, beating Scott Brash by 0.18 seconds, so the pair clearly still have it. It makes the 2028 plan more intriguing.

Meanwhile Steve Guerdat, who finished second in Paris by 0.04 seconds, won the 2026 world title at Aachen without touching a pole all week, after two back surgeries in 2025.

Get there early. This 8 AM qualifier is where the final is decided.
EQU15.potentialContendersIntro: These are likely individual contenders based on Paris 2024 and Aachen 2026. Which horses the riders will use in 2028 is not confirmed.

EQU16.blurb:
Four hundredths of a second. That was all that separated Christian Kukuk from Steve Guerdat in the Paris 2024 jump-off, and the Swiss veteran has spent the time since collecting a measure of revenge: his 2026 world title at Aachen, won after two back surgeries.

This is a Saturday morning at a racetrack, not a stadium, and that suits the sport. Santa Anita's 1934 grandstand faces the San Gabriel Mountains, and the same ground hosted equestrian at the 1984 Los Angeles Games. Riders walk the course, then go one at a time while the crowd holds its breath for every vertical and oxer. A single rail can end a career-defining ride.

If the final turns into another jump-off, you will hear the stands go quiet, then groan or roar with each fence.
EQU16.potentialContendersIntro: Kukuk won Paris 2024 gold and Guerdat is the reigning world champion, but 2028 rosters are not set, so this field is projected from recent form.

FBL01.blurb:
A brand-new stadium, a new tournament and 25,000 seats close enough to the pitch that you can hear the goalkeepers shouting. Etihad Park only opened in July 2027, so the 2028 Games will meet a ground barely a year old.

Getting there is part of the show. You ride the 7 train to Willets Point, pass through The Cube with its programmable LED screens, and walk into a bowl whose transparent roof lets in daylight and keeps the noise from escaping.

With only 12 men's teams in the field, even a group-stage opener carries weight. Mexico, the London 2012 champion, has already booked its place, and the host U.S. side under Steve Cherundolo is in the mix.

FBL02.blurb:
Spain 5, France 3, after extra time. The Paris 2024 men's final was one of the wildest ever played, and every team in this tournament has had two years to think about how to avoid being on the wrong side of a shootout like that.

The field shrinks to 12 this time, which means no padding. A slip on the second group-stage day can decide who goes through. Queens will feel that tension in a bowl designed to keep fans tight to the touchline.

Bring a scarf you can wave. Etihad Park's transparent roof is built to trap noise, and the stands are full of New Yorkers who tend to argue about the offside flag.

FBL03.blurb:
Columbus is not the first city you would pick for a Games, and that is exactly the appeal. This is a soccer town with a ground built for the game, and for one summer it hosts the world's best young players.

Scotts Miracle-Gro Field, called Columbus Stadium during the Games, seats about 20,000 under a canopy that holds the sound in. The Nordecke, the Crew's supporters' end, supplies the drumming, and after the match the Arena District is a short walk to dinner.

The home angle is real: Columbus Crew midfielder Taha Habroune was in the first U.S. U-23 camp of the cycle, so local fans may have someone to cheer.

FBL04.blurb:
Opening day is split across four cities, and Columbus is one of them. This is the first morning of men's football at the 2028 Games, and every team here is still unbeaten and unbothered.

The interesting question is who the home side will rely on. Steve Cherundolo's first U-23 camp had 15 MLS players and eight based in Europe, and six already had senior caps. That blend of league-tested veterans and European prospects is the kind of thing worth watching up close at a 20,000-seat ground.

At this size you can see the coaches' faces on the touchline. It feels more like a big college match than a major tournament.

FBL05.blurb:
Nashville has the biggest soccer-only stadium in the country, and it feels like it. Geodis Park holds more than 30,000, with four stands pressed close to the field and a standing supporters' section making steady noise.

The building has hosted big nights before. Lionel Messi's Inter Miami beat Nashville SC on penalties here in the 2023 Leagues Cup final. The men's group matches open in this park on July 10, which means a crowd that already knows how to be loud.

Plan your trip in. Traffic and parking around the Fairgrounds can back up after big matches, so arrive early.

FBL06.blurb:
The last time Games football was played in St. Louis was 1904, at the first Games on American soil. Now the sport is back, in a downtown stadium that did not exist five years ago.

Energizer Park, called St. Louis Stadium during the Games, seats about 22,400 in a compact bowl that keeps fans close and loud. It opens toward the surrounding district, so the city is part of the setting.

There is a local hook too. St. Louis City SC forward Damion Downs was in the first U.S. U-23 camp and had played for the senior team a month earlier.

FBL07.blurb:
Four months after the defending champions lost 2-0 and then missed a penalty to Spain at Audi Field in October 2026, you could see them again. That is the theme of this tournament: the U.S. women hunting a sixth gold, and a world full of teams who think this is the moment.

Nashville is a good place to test it. Geodis Park seats more than 30,000, the biggest soccer-only stadium in the country, and the standing supporters' section does not stop singing.

With 16 teams for the first time in a generation, there are more places for surprises, and a group-stage match can feel like a final.

FBL08.blurb:
Sixteen women's teams means room for countries that rarely get a stage this big. St. Louis may be where a few of them introduce themselves.

The ground suits an underdog story. Energizer Park seats about 22,400 in a tight bowl, so a loud minority can sound like a majority. This is also a city that last had Games football in 1904, so the novelty runs both ways.

It is the sort of session where you arrive for the name teams and leave talking about the one you had not heard of.

FBL09.blurb:
Brazil and Germany took silver and bronze in Paris, and neither has forgotten how it ended. Both sides could be anywhere in this field, and Columbus is a fine place to meet them.

Scotts Miracle-Gro Field is a tight, soccer-specific ground with a canopy that holds the sound. The Nordecke end drums, and the Arena District around it makes this an easy day out for visitors who are not following the sport closely.

Brazil has qualified. Germany has to win its Nations League group, which also holds the Netherlands, Sweden and Scotland.

FBL10.blurb:
A new stadium in Queens, a host nation with four gold medals' worth of pressure, and a name on the roster list that tells you how much youth is coming through. Emma Hayes's 51-player preliminary list for Concacaf qualifying included Trinity Rodman, Lindsey Heaps, Naomi Girma and Lily Yohannes.

Etihad Park is a 25,000-seat bowl with a transparent roof that lets the daylight in and the noise stay. Gotham FC of the NWSL is also expected to move in from 2028, so this is a ground shaping the women's game here.

If the U.S. is on the card, expect a very loud night in Queens.

FBL11.blurb:
San Diego is the group-stage venue closest to the Rose Bowl, and that makes it the easiest ticket for anyone building a Los Angeles trip around the football. Drive down, watch a match, be home by night.

Snapdragon Stadium seats about 35,000 on natural Bermuda grass, and the women's game has history here. San Diego Wave FC set an NWSL attendance record in its first match in 2022, so the crowd knows how to show up.

This is the biggest bowl of the group-stage venues outside Nashville, so you can expect room for the sort of crowd a major team deserves.

If 16 teams is more than the women's game has had in 20 years, San Diego is where you notice. A bigger field means a bigger first week and a more open race, with groups that will not look like a procession.

Snapdragon Stadium is a 35,000-seat bowl built for soccer, rugby and college football, so the sightlines suit a big match. It is also a place that has already set records for crowds in both the NWSL and MLS.

Go for the football, but keep an eye on the table. Third place can matter more than it used to.

The smallest stadium in the group stage is the one you will remember. PayPal Park seats about 18,000 on steep stands, a bit like a European ground, so nobody is far from the pitch.

There is a roof over much of the seating, a big outdoor bar behind one end, and planes from San Jose International Airport pass overhead during matches. It is a quirky, close, personal place to see a national team.

Bay FC of the NWSL plays here, so the building is used to a women's crowd that is loud and knows the game.

A small ground makes a big match feel bigger. At PayPal Park, the stands climb steeply and the pitch feels close enough to touch, which is exactly what you want when one of the favorites is in town.

Spain is the world champion and England is a perennial challenger, and both are projected to fight for UEFA berths in the 2027 Nations League. If either makes it, San Jose would host a team that can pass a tight room to pieces.

Grab a drink at the outdoor bar behind one end, then find your seat before kickoff.

FBL15.blurb:
By the second matchday the groups start to take shape, and so does the pressure. A team that dropped points on July 10 now has to correct course in front of a New York crowd.

Mexico is a good example of the kind of side that can handle it. It won its place by beating Canada 2-1 after trailing at the break, and the London 2012 champion has never minded a difficult afternoon.

Etihad Park holds about 25,000, a tight bowl under a transparent roof, a short walk from the 7 train. It is a good place to see how the group is going.

Queens gets a brand-new stadium and a world audience in the same breath. Etihad Park is the only venue built from scratch for the 2028 football tournament, and it is slated to open a year earlier, on July 17, 2027.

You walk in through The Cube, a seven-story gateway wrapped in LED screens, a short hop from the 7 train at Willets Point. Inside, the 25,000-seat bowl sits close to the grass, and a transparent roof traps the noise.

The men's field is mostly under-23, so this is a chance to see tomorrow's stars before the knockouts start.

Columbus is a soccer town that sells out and sings. The Crew's supporters' section, the Nordecke, gives one end of this stadium its roar. For a few days the whole bowl may borrow it.

ScottsMiracle-Gro Field holds about 20,000 and sits in the walkable Arena District, so you can eat downtown and stroll to the gate. The stands are tight to the pitch and a canopy covers much of the seating. Crew midfielder Taha Habroune made the first U.S. U-23 camp roster, so a local name could be in the mix.

This is group-stage soccer in a place that knows how to watch it.

FBL18.blurb:
This stadium has already hosted an MLS Cup final. Columbus Crew beat LAFC here in 2023, so a big match on this grass is nothing new.

The 2028 draw is different. Steve Cherundolo, a former MLS Cup-winning LAFC coach, leads the U.S. under-23 side. His first camp had 15 MLS-based players, eight from Europe, and six with senior-team call-ups. If the host plays here, you may be watching a mix of MLS prospects and Europe-based rising stars.

One roster list does not make a team, but it shows where the U.S. is looking.

FBL19.blurb:
St. Louis last hosted Games competition in 1904, the first Games on American soil. This session ends that 124-year wait for the city's soccer fans.

Energizer Park is a compact 22,400-seat bowl built for soccer, opened in 2022, with fans close to the pitch. It sits in an urban campus that opens toward the neighborhood around it.

The home angle is real. St. Louis City SC forward Damion Downs made the first U.S. U-23 camp roster and had just played for the senior team, so a local hero could be on the field.

FBL20.blurb:
Nashville has the biggest soccer-only stadium in the country. Geodis Park holds more than 30,000, and it has hosted a Leagues Cup final where Lionel Messi's Inter Miami beat Nashville SC on penalties.

It is an open-air bowl with stands close to the pitch, canopies over much of the seating, and a standing supporters' section that keeps up a steady noise. Expect a larger crowd than most group matches draw.

The stadium is just south of downtown on the Fairgrounds site, and traffic can back up after big matches, so plan your exit.

FBL21.blurb:
Spain and the United States have been trading blows. In October 2026, Spain won 2-0 in Washington, then took a 2-0 lead in Chester before the Americans pulled back to 2-2 on goals from Ashley Sanchez and Mallory Swanson.

That is the shadow over the host's title defense. Spain is the top-ranked team in the world, about 80 points clear of the U.S. in the October 2026 FIFA ranking, and a Spain-US group meeting would be a preview of something bigger.

Geodis Park's 30,000 seats are close to the pitch, and a standing supporters' section keeps the noise steady.

Sixteen teams instead of twelve. That means more debutants, more surprises, and more matches where the lesser-known side has nothing to lose.

St. Louis gets a taste of that. Energizer Park is a compact bowl of about 22,500 seats, built for soccer in 2022, where fans sit close enough to hear the players.

The field is the largest since 2008, and group games are where the new names show up. Come to see someone you have not heard of play a team you know.

ScottsMiracle-Gro Field seats about 20,000 and sits in the walkable Arena District, with stands tight to the pitch. The U.S. could be a draw if it lands in Columbus, and Emma Hayes has a 51-player preliminary pool including Trinity Rodman, Lindsey Heaps, Naomi Girma and Lily Yohannes.

It is a chance to sample the best of a deeper 16-team field.

FBL24.blurb:

Gotham FC has announced it will play home games here starting in 2028, so this is a ground built for the women's game. The 25,000-seat bowl is tight and the transparent roof keeps the noise in.

If the host is here, you may watch the champions who won gold on a Swanson goal in Paris.

This is the smallest football venue of the Games, about 18,000 seats, and the stands rise steeply enough to feel like a European ground. A roof covers much of the seating and a large outdoor bar sits behind one end. Bay FC plays here, so women's football is familiar.

It may be the best place to see a big name from only a few rows away.

PayPal Park is the smallest venue in the tournament, and it feels like a ground in Europe: steep stands, a roof over much of the seating, and the noise right at pitch level. If a pair of heavyweights are drawn here, the setting could make the match feel like a heavyweight bout in a small room.

Bay Area fans already come out for Bay FC and know how to watch the women's game.

The compact, soccer-friendly bowl has a natural Bermuda grass pitch, and the city hosts 11 football matches in total. That is a lot of chances to see a star, and a crowd that size can swing a match.

It is a good value pick if you want a big stadium with a group-stage ticket.

That could put regional rivals in the same group in San Diego, where the 35,000-seat Snapdragon Stadium can fill with traveling support. The grass is natural Bermuda and the bowl is compact.

A derby-style group match under the lights of a big crowd can feel bigger than the group-stage label suggests.

They have to qualify first. Spain won its U-21 qualifying group with 27 points from 10 matches and France took its group with 26, so both look in good shape for the 2027 U-21 Euros that award three UEFA berths. Nothing is settled.

Etihad Park's tight bowl and LED-lit entrance, The Cube, make a fitting stage for a late group match when the standings tighten.

ScottsMiracle-Gro Field is one of the MLS stadiums outside Los Angeles hosting group and knockout play before the final rounds at the Rose Bowl. The compact bowl and the Nordecke's noise make a close finish feel louder.

The field is mostly under-23, so a late goal can come from a teenager making his name. Morocco, fresh from its first medal in Paris, is a team worth watching if it qualifies.

Scotts Miracle-Gro Field seats about 20,000 in a bowl built close to the touchline, with the Nordecke end supplying the noise. The Arena District is walkable, so the pregame is half the outing.

Group play is where you find the names before the knockout rounds make them expensive to watch. Think of how Fermin Lopez arrived in Paris as a prospect and left with gold.

Make an afternoon of it. The setting and the history are the draw before the first whistle.

Down 2-0 to Spain in October 2026, the United States clawed back to draw 2-2, with Mallory Swanson delivering the late equalizer. It wasn't a trophy, but it reset the pecking order.

That's the backdrop for a Monday in St. Louis, where a 16-team women's field means more heavyweights share groups. The compact bowl at Energizer Park sits close to the pitch, so you can hear the instructions between the players.

The United States are defending champions and hosts, but with Spain ranked first in the world, nothing is simple.

Nashville is the sort of place that suits teams like that. Geodis Park holds 30,109 with stands close to the pitch, canopies over much of the seating, and a standing supporters' section that doesn't sit down. Add a Latin American contingent and a Monday evening can get loud.

The Fairgrounds neighborhood can jam up after matches, so plan your exit.

Nashville's 30,109-seat stadium is a good place for it. Close stands trap the noise, and the supporters' end behind one goal keeps chanting through the quiet stretches.

Group matches reward the early arrival. A Monday in Tennessee could give you a title contender in a stadium that was built to be loud.

You arrive through the Cube, a seven-story gateway covered in programmable LED screens, just off the 7 train. Inside, a transparent roof lets daylight reach the concourse while the 25,000-seat bowl holds the crowd noise close to the pitch.

It is also headed for NWSL use, since Gotham FC will move in from 2028. A women's group match here is a very New York afternoon.

Snapdragon Stadium sits in Mission Valley on a natural Bermuda grass field, and it's the closest group-stage venue to Los Angeles, about 120 miles south. Expect traveling fans from Brazil, Mexico and the American Southwest.

There are no age limits in the women's tournament, so full senior squads appear. The best players in the world are on the pitch.

That adds spice to a Monday at Snapdragon Stadium. The compact bowl, built for soccer, rugby and college football, holds about 35,000, and San Diego's crowds are used to being loud. The sun, the breeze and a natural grass pitch complete the picture.

If you want the sport's world order in one room, this is a safe bet.

FBL44.blurb:
Thirty thousand people can make a quarterfinal feel like a final. At 30,109 seats, Nashville is the second-largest of the venues outside the Rose Bowl.

Geodis Park's close stands, canopies and standing supporters' section mean a crowd that arrives early and stays loud. It's the sort of place where a tight match goes to the last kick and everyone knows it.

This is also where under-23 teams lean on their three overage players. A veteran goalkeeper or striker can decide a 90-minute knockout match.

FBL45.blurb:
One hundred and twenty-four years after football was played at Francis Field in 1904, St. Louis hosts a knockout match with a medal path attached.

Energizer Park keeps things tight. About 22,500 seats sit in a compact bowl on a downtown campus, and the stands lean close to the touchline. A Thursday quarterfinal here will feel more like a club cup tie than a stadium show.

It also offers a chance to see how South American and African teams handle the single-elimination format. Extra time and penalties are possible, and nobody wants to leave early.

FBL46.blurb:
The roof here is transparent, so daylight pours in while the noise stays trapped inside. Etihad Park seats 25,000 in a traditional soccer bowl, right beside Citi Field, and the stands sit close enough to the pitch that a men's knockout tie feels like a street fight.

This is the first round where a bad night ends a tournament in a field cut to 12 teams. The group stage will decide who turns up, and nobody knows yet. Expect under-23 squads with up to three overage veterans, plus a few teenagers hoping to become the name everyone remembers.

You walk in from the 7 train at Willets Point, through the LED gateway known as The Cube.

FBL47.blurb:
In 1999, 90,185 people filled the Rose Bowl to watch the United States beat China on penalties, and American women's soccer never looked the same. Twenty-nine years later, a knockout match returns to that same grass.

This is the first elimination round of a 16-team field, the biggest women's tournament in two decades, so the teams are unknown and the possibilities are wide. If the host side lands here, the old bowl could be close to full, with the San Gabriel Mountains behind the stands.

The seats are bench-style and legroom is short. Bring sunscreen, because the Arroyo Seco can be hot.

FBL48.blurb:
Nashville knows what a big night sounds like here. In August 2023, Lionel Messi's Inter Miami beat Nashville SC on penalties at Geodis Park to win the club's first trophy, and the place roared through all of it.

Now the stakes are higher. With about 30,109 seats, this is the largest soccer-specific stadium in the United States, with four stands close to the pitch and a standing supporters' section that keeps the volume steady. A women's quarterfinal means the first knockout round of a 16-team tournament, with every pass carrying real weight.

The fairgrounds sit just south of downtown, and traffic can back up after big matches. Plan your exit.

FBL49.blurb:
Spain beat the United States 2-0 in October 2026, then the Americans came back from two goals down to draw the rematch 2-2. If the bracket cooperates, a third meeting at Snapdragon Stadium would be the quarterfinal everyone wants.

The compact bowl in Mission Valley was built for soccer, rugby and college football, and the natural Bermuda grass is fast. San Diego Wave FC set an NWSL attendance record in the first match played here, so the crowd knows how to make noise.

It is the first knockout round of a 16-team field, which means newcomers get a real chance to ruin a favorite's week.

FBL50.blurb:
Look up. Planes on approach to San Jose International pass over PayPal Park, and with the smallest capacity in MLS, about 18,000, the stands rise steeply and put every fan almost on top of the pitch.

That makes a women's quarterfinal feel more like a European cup night than a stadium event. There is a big outdoor bar behind one end, a roof over much of the seating, and nowhere for a quiet moment. A knockout match here is intimate, loud and unforgiving.

It is the first knockout round of the 16-team field, and the matchup is a mystery. That is part of the appeal.

FBL51.blurb:
One o'clock on a Monday in Mission Valley, with the sun high and the winner four days from a gold medal match at the Rose Bowl. This is the kind of session where a reputation can crack in 90 minutes.

Spain's under-23 group won gold in Paris by outlasting France 5-3 in extra time, but the men's field is now just 12 teams and the squads turn over completely. Nobody here has an easy path.

Snapdragon Stadium's compact bowl and natural Bermuda grass favor quick passing, and the crowd sits close enough to feel every tackle. Plan for midday sun.

FBL52.blurb:
The Rose Bowl has seen France beat Brazil 2-0 in the 1984 gold medal match in front of 101,799 people, and the stadium keeps that history near the surface. Now it hosts a men's semifinal at 8:30 PM, under evening light with the San Gabriel Mountains fading behind the stands.

Only the winner reaches Friday's gold medal match, in this same bowl. The 12-team field means every team here earned its place through a harder route than in Paris.

The seats are old bench-style with little legroom, but the sunset and the sound system make up for it.

FBL53.blurb:
Emma Hayes won Paris 2024 gold roughly 80 days after officially taking over the United States, and she has said her sights are set on 2027 in Brazil and a home title defense in 2028. A semifinal at Snapdragon Stadium would put that plan under real pressure.

The opponent could be Spain, the reigning world champion, who beat the Americans 2-0 in October 2026 before a 2-2 draw. If the bracket works out, this would be the big one.

The crowd in San Diego knows the Wave, and the compact bowl will show it. Tuesday evening kicks off at 5:30 PM.

FBL54.blurb:
Mallory Swanson's late goal pulled the United States level at 2-2 against Spain in October 2026, after a 2-0 defeat three days earlier. That is the sort of stubborn streak that defines this team, and it could be on display under the Rose Bowl lights.

The 8:30 PM semifinal brings dusk, mountains and a sea of fans in a stadium that hosted the 1999 Women's World Cup final. The winner plays for gold here four days later.

Brazil could be a lurking threat. They have already qualified and were silver medalists in Paris, in what was expected to be Marta's final Games.

FBL55.blurb:
A bronze medal match is a strange, honest kind of football: two teams who have just lost a semifinal, one medal left, and a few hours to forget the heartbreak. It tends to produce open play and a bit of mayhem.

Morocco knows what is possible. Their bronze in Paris 2024 was the country's first medal in the sport, and the reaction showed what it meant. With the men's tournament down to 12 teams, a medal in 2028 will be earned.

The 6:00 PM start at Snapdragon Stadium should bring a cooler San Diego evening and a compact bowl full of fans who came for the football.

FBL56.blurb:
Bronze can be a launchpad. The United States took bronze in Tokyo, then won gold in Paris. Germany took bronze in Paris 2024. Nobody wants this match, but plenty of careers have been turned by it.

It kicks off at 1:00 PM at Snapdragon Stadium, home of San Diego Wave FC, with the sun overhead and a compact bowl that holds the noise. With a 16-team field, this is the first women's tournament in two decades where bronze takes real depth to reach.

Expect two proud teams, a few tired legs and a medal ceremony that matters.

FBL57.blurb:
Spain 5, France 3, after extra time. That was the Paris 2024 men's final, and Fermin Lopez scoring twice in normal time and Sergio Camello adding one in extra time made it one of the wildest finals in the sport's Games history.

Now the final moves to the Rose Bowl, which hosted the 1984 gold medal match and the 1994 men's World Cup final. The 12-team field means the finalists will have beaten stronger opposition than in Paris, and it starts July 10, four days before the opening ceremony.

The setting is huge, the mountains are behind the stands, and the finalists are unknown.

FBL58.blurb:
Eighty days. That is how long Emma Hayes had been in charge when the United States won Paris 2024 gold, beating Brazil 1-0 on Mallory Swanson's early second-half goal. Now she is trying to defend it at the Rose Bowl.

The 12:30 PM kickoff means sun, a huge crowd and no shade for most of the bowl. It is a long way from Paris, closer to the 1999 Women's World Cup final that drew 90,185 here.

The finalists are unknown. Spain, the reigning world champion, drew 2-2 with the Americans in October 2026, and that rematch could be waiting.

FEN01.blurb:
Vivian Kong won women's épée gold for Hong Kong in Paris. Now she is retired and sits on Hong Kong's Legislative Council, so the 2028 bracket opens without a defending champion.

That turns the opening Saturday at the Convention Center into a long hunt. A Table of 64 shrinks to eight between 9 AM and late afternoon, with women's épée and men's sabre bouts running to 15 touches. Sabre is over in a flash; épée grinds you down.

Go for the discovery. Korea's Song Se-ra could arrive as a two-time world champion, and Oh Sang-uk, who won the 2026 Asian Games sabre title despite an ankle injury, could be chasing a repeat.

FEN02.blurb:
The first medals of the 2028 Games get decided under one roof on one Saturday night, and neither title has a settled owner. Women's épée lost its Paris champion to retirement. Men's sabre has a Paris champion who keeps winning but has not said he is coming.

Song Se-ra beat Italy's Giulia Rizzi for the 2026 world title and is the name to circle. In sabre, Korea's Oh Sang-uk and Do Gyeong-dong, the 2026 world silver medalist, could set up a family showdown, with Pavel Graudyn, listed for Russia, the man who beat Do 15-7 at Worlds.

In a hall of roughly 7,000 seats, a 14-14 score sounds like held breath.

FEN03.blurb:
Lee Kiefer has won individual foil gold at Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024, but her 2028 plans are unconfirmed. She sat out the 2026 World Championships while pregnant with her first child. Whether she walks onto a strip Sunday is the question hanging over the women's foil bracket.

If she is not there, the field is open. Italy's Martina Favaretto is the 2026 world champion, and Lauren Scruggs, the Paris silver medalist, reached that event's quarterfinals. Men's épée adds Japan's Koki Kano against Switzerland's Lucas Malcotti, the reigning world champion.

Eight hours of bouts to 15 touches. Settle in and watch favorites vanish.
