A third straight individual foil title would make Lee Kiefer the story of the Games' second night, if she competes. She beat teammate Lauren Scruggs in the Paris final and won the 2025 world title, then pregnancy kept her from the 2026 Worlds. Her 2028 plans are unconfirmed.

The rivals are real. Italy's Martina Favaretto is the 2026 world champion, and Canada's Eleanor Harvey took Paris bronze. On the men's épée side, Japan's Koki Kano is the reigning Games champion and a 2025 world champion, while Switzerland's Lucas Malcotti holds the 2026 world title.

In a hall that usually hosts trade shows, a home foilist in a medal bout fills every seat.

Manon Apithy-Brunet won the French national sabre title six months after giving birth. That is why a Monday prelim is worth watching: the Paris champion could be working her way up a Table of 64 bracket right in front of you.

On the foil strips, Hong Kong's Edgar Cheung is a two-time defending champion who admitted he had barely trained before the November 2025 National Games, where he won bronze. Czechia's Alexander Choupenitch is the 2026 world champion, and Cheung's teammate Ryan Choi was world No. 1 in February 2026.

Early rounds put stars one bad bout from an upset.

FEN06.blurb:
Two Paris champions, two open questions. Manon Apithy-Brunet became a mother after winning sabre gold for France. Edgar Cheung has won foil gold at Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024 and has not confirmed whether he will try for a third.

The field has moved on. Germany's Larissa Eifler is the 2026 women's sabre world champion, Ukraine's Olha Kharlan resumed training in 2025 after taking Paris bronze, and Czechia's Alexander Choupenitch is the 2026 foil world champion.

Monday night pairs sabre's speed with foil's precision, and in the foil semifinals, one right-of-way call can swing everything.

FEN07.blurb:
Team épée turns a solo sport into a relay to 45 touches, and by lunchtime half the field has gone home. Eight teams enter the Table of 8, four reach the medal matches, and the rest fence classification bouts for final placings.

Italy is the one to beat: Paris 2024 gold, then the 2026 world title with Gaia Caforio, Rossella Fiamingo, Giulia Rizzi and Alberta Santuccio. Estonia took 2026 world silver, and Korea took bronze with individual world champion Song Se-ra on the anchor-worthy list.

FFB12.blurb:
The U.S. women failed to score on the last play of the 2026 world final and lost 27-20 to Canada. This semifinal could put them on a path back to that team, or send someone else there first.

The quarterbacks are the story. Sara Parker was the 2026 MVP for Canada, Diana Flores has led Mexico to a World Games title, and the U.S. has leaned on Vanita Krouch for years, though none of these rosters are confirmed.

It's a Friday early afternoon, and the first women's medal games are the next day. These are the teams trying to get there.

FFB13.blurb:
The first men's medal in the Games' history comes with the sport's most dominant team in the mix, and a few teams that have been close. Seven world titles say the U.S. men are the favorite. A 38-32 group loss to American Samoa in 2026 says they can be had.

The session begins with bronze, then moves into the gold medal game. Friday evening should bring the loudest crowd of the tournament so far.

The NFL storyline might matter too, since players under NFL contract can now try out, one per club. Quarterback Darrell 'Housh' Doucette III was 2026 MVP, if he leads again, he'll be the center of the action.

FFB14.blurb:
The final day of the tournament gives women's flag football its first Games medals. Canada is the reigning world champion, and the U.S. women are the hosts who want the title back.

There is also Mexico, which beat the U.S. 26-21 for the 2025 World Games title, and Great Britain, which won the European title in 2025 and lost the 2026 bronze game by a point. That's four teams with a case.

A Saturday afternoon at 12:30 means daylight and a full house. The first women's gold medal gets decided in a stadium built for the biggest goals, and it has to be earned over 40 minutes.

GAR01.blurb:
The first rotation of the first day. The steep seats at DTLA Arena, the building where Kobe Bryant dropped 81, hold a calmer crowd than finals night will, but from the upper rows you can still see every chalk cloud.

This is men's gymnastics before the scores turn into brackets. Daiki Hashimoto, a four-time reigning world all-around champion, could be here chasing Kohei Uchimura's record of six straight world titles. Carlos Yulo, the Paris double gold medalist on floor and vault, is another name to watch if he lines up in this subdivision.

A late-morning start makes this the easy-value ticket of the opening day.

potentialContenders.name: Daiki Hashimoto

potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 all-around and horizontal bar champion. Fell twice in the 2026 world all-around final, so he arrives with something to prove.

potentialContenders.name: Joe Fraser
potentialContenders.note: 2026 world all-around bronze medalist, only Britain's third men's all-around medal at a Worlds.

GAR02.blurb:
Armenia may be the most interesting team of the afternoon. Artur Davtyan finally took the world vault title in 2026 after two straight silvers behind Yulo, and Hamlet Manukyan won pommel horse the same year. Mamikon Khachatryan added a bronze on pommel.

Qualification 2 is the middle of three men's sessions. The afternoon light is gone, the building has filled in, and the scoreboard starts to matter. Some familiar faces won't be here: Britain's James Hall and Italy's Nicola Bartolini both retired in 2026.

Watch the pommel horse, where a single flop ends a medal hope in seconds.

GAR03.blurb:
Late on a Saturday night the last men's gymnasts salute, and by the time the arena empties the bracket is written. The men's team final, the all-around final and the apparatus fields all hang on these two and a half hours.

There's a second story too. The new mixed team event is expected to draw on qualification scores, so every routine could count twice. FIG still hasn't published the format.

If you like specialists, this session carries weight: Zou Jingyuan on parallel bars, Lan Xingyu on rings, and Tang Chia-hung, who beat Oka for the 2026 world high bar title.

GAR04.blurb:
The biggest question in women's gymnastics has no answer yet: will Simone Biles be here? As of late September 2026 she hadn't decided, said she felt she knew which way she was leaning, and has not competed since winning three golds in Paris. She'd be 31.

Whoever walks onto the floor, Sunday morning is when women's competition begins. The U.S. has a ready answer in Skye Blakely, who won the 2026 world all-around title, and Algeria's Kaylia Nemour owns the bars and beam titles.

Get there early. From the steep upper rows the whole floor lies flat below you, and nobody has been tired or nervous yet.

GAR05.blurb:
Rebeca Andrade has retired her best event. After Paris, where she beat Biles on floor, she took 2025 off to protect her health and has said she won't return to floor. Vault and beam are in, and bars follow in 2027.

She won world vault gold in 2026 anyway, her third on the apparatus. A bright Brazil crowd tends to follow her wherever she goes.

This is a compact 100-minute session, a quick look at the afternoon's field. Brazil's women placed fifth at the 2026 Worlds, so the team still has to qualify in Chengdu in 2027.

GAR06.blurb:
Paris made Italy a gymnastics power. Silver in the team final, and Alice D'Amato and Manila Esposito went gold and bronze on beam. The question here is how much of that depth is still standing.

Giorgia Villa retired in May 2026, but Esposito won floor at the 2026 Europeans and reached the world beam final. Nemour is another reason to stay for this evening session: she took the 2026 world beam title on an execution tiebreak over China's Zhang Qingying.

Twelve teams are expected in the field, and the 6:15 PM start means a full house by the second rotation.

GAR07.blurb:
It's past nine at night when this one starts, and it runs until after eleven. By the end, every women's field is set: team final, all-around, apparatus finals, plus mixed team qualifiers if FIG adopts that format.

The nightcap has some of the sport's sharpest storylines. Blakely won the 2026 world all-around without the Cheng vault, on a plan her coach built for 2028. Claire Pease and Reese Esponda went one-two on floor for the U.S. at the 2026 Worlds. Angelina Melnikova, a neutral athlete, has won the 2025 world and 2026 European all-around titles.

And somewhere in the background is Biles, who said she knows which way she's leaning.

GAR08.blurb:
Five gymnasts. No reserves. When one falls, nobody is waiting on the bench.

That's the pressure on a men's team final that opens the gymnastics medals. Japan won the 2026 world title despite misses on parallel bars and a fall on high bar, and Daiki Hashimoto stepped up to take the closing high bar routine himself. China climbed from fourth in qualification to bronze without Zhang Boheng.

A Monday evening crowd at DTLA Arena will watch every counted score swing the standings. Japan beat China in Paris, and the rematch could decide who owns the first medals of these Games.

GAR09.blurb:
Last time the U.S. women won gold. At the 2026 Worlds they lost the title by 0.233 points to China. That margin will hang over this Tuesday evening final.

The U.S. is still a heavy favorite, according to ESPN, because of its depth. Blakely, the 2026 world all-around champion, leads a group with Pease and Esponda, who went one-two on floor in Rotterdam. China, Japan and Italy are the teams most likely to threaten them. And then there's the question of Biles.

Finals sessions have a feel like nothing else: three rotations of gymnasts, ninety minutes of tension.

GAR10.blurb:
1.799 points. That was Hashimoto's winning margin at the 2026 Worlds, the biggest at a Worlds or Games in 13 years. It was his fourth straight world title and seventh overall.

Now he is chasing Kohei Uchimura's record of six straight, and the all-around final is where he can keep climbing. Oka, who won in Paris, fell twice in the 2026 final, and China's Yang Haonan and Zhang Boheng are waiting for any slip.

Six events, one man at a time, on a Wednesday night. At DTLA Arena, with the floor flat beneath you, the whole thing can be a long, quiet duel.

GAR11.blurb:
Women's all-around podiums have featured at least one American at every world and Games championship since 2003, 23 straight going into 2026, and Skye Blakely extended the run with her world title. Nobody in this arena will want to see it end.

The subplot is Biles. She's the Paris champion, will be 31, and has said she hasn't decided. After she posted photos of her childhood gym in August 2026, comeback talk started. Rebeca Andrade has said she plans a fourth Games in 2028, though without floor an all-around bid is unclear.

A Thursday night crowd fills the bowl to the rafters for it.

This is gymnastics with the clutter cleared away: eight athletes, one apparatus, one routine each. A Saturday late-morning start also makes it an easy family ticket.

The sources don't say which apparatus fills this session, so plan for variety. The likeliest stars are the recent world champions: Nemour on bars with 15.333 in 2026, Andrade on vault with 14.466, Fred Richard on floor with 14.633, and Armenia's Hamlet Manukyan on pommel horse.

On an apparatus final, a single wobble costs a medal, and the crowd can feel it.

And Brazil's Flavia Saraiva, who won beam bronze in 2026 for her first world medal there.

Tang Chia-hung won his first world title on high bar in 2026, beating Shinnosuke Oka, the man who won the Games in Paris. That's the freshest rivalry of the apparatus finals, and Monday morning could give it a rematch.

The sources don't say which events fill this session. If floor is here, the American one-two of Claire Pease and Reese Esponda from 2026 is the headline. Rebeca Andrade has said she won't return to floor, and Biles hasn't announced a comeback.

High bar is the best fun of all: long, silent flights, then a gasp.

GAR15.blurb:
Nobody knows exactly how this works yet, and that's part of the draw. The mixed team event is new for 2028, and FIG still hasn't approved the format or the duration.

What we know: a trial at the 2025 European Championships used one man and one woman per nation, with the top 16 qualifying pairs advancing to the final. USA Gymnastics revived the American Cup as a mixed team event in 2026 to prepare.

A Tuesday late-afternoon medal session at DTLA Arena, with a first-ever champion crowned, could be one of those where you can say you were there.

GLF01.blurb:
Sixty men, four days, and a canyon course that has hosted the Los Angeles Open more than 60 times.

Round 1 is the day to wander. There are no big grandstands at Riviera. Fans spread along the fairways off Sunset Boulevard, so you can pick a hole, claim a patch of hillside and watch the whole field come through. Defending champion Scottie Scheffler, who won Paris 2024 with a closing 62, could be among them if he makes the team.

Nobody wins gold on Wednesday, but plenty of players lose a little of it. Come early and see the stars before the pressure bites.

GLF02.blurb:
Scottie Scheffler is a slow starter, and it has been his habit for years. His 2026 opening rounds averaged 69.18, nearly 1.75 strokes worse than his closing rounds.

That makes Thursday the session where a field can get comfortable or get scared. Round 2 is where early scores harden into a leaderboard and the first real separation shows. It's also the best day to learn Riviera properly: the hillside clubhouse looks down on the 18th green, and the slopes around it make a natural amphitheater.

The course is no stranger to local form. Jacob Bridgeman won the 2026 Genesis Invitational here at 18 under.

GLF03.blurb:
In Paris, Jon Rahm and defending champion Xander Schauffele shared the 54-hole lead. Neither made the podium.

That's the lesson of Friday. Round 3 sets the positions, but it rarely decides the winner. Scheffler came from behind to win in Paris. He also did it at the 2026 Tour Championship, where he beat 54-hole leader Viktor Hovland by three with a closing 66.

The afternoon crowds gather around the finishing holes, with the hillside clubhouse looking down on the 18th green. Leaders get a long look from the slopes. Chasers get a long look at the leaders.

GLF04.blurb:
No man has won back-to-back individual golds since golf returned in 2016. Justin Rose, Xander Schauffele and Scottie Scheffler each won once.

Scheffler's chance to break that streak could come in the last round at Riviera. In Paris he shot 62 with a 29 on the back nine, while Tommy Fleetwood answered with a par putt on the final green to finish one shot back. You can see the closing stretch from the hillside around the 18th green, and a statue of Ben Hogan stands near it.

This is the round the whole week funnels into, with medals on the line by evening.
GLF04.potentialContendersIntro: The field is not set until June 2028, so the medal picture below is projection. Only Scheffler, Fleetwood and Matsuyama are confirmed Paris 2024 medalists.

potentialContenders.name: Scottie Scheffler
potentialContenders.note: Confirmed defending champion with four career majors. He is chasing the first back-to-back men's golds if he qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Tommy Fleetwood
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalist, one shot behind. He said he was aiming for world No. 1 in 2026, so a likely contender.

potentialContenders.name: Hideki Matsuyama
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalist. Could return to the podium if he qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Xander Schauffele
potentialContenders.note: Tokyo champion who missed the Paris 2024 podium. Needs to climb back into the US qualifying places.

GLF05.blurb:
Golf's first team medal at the Games since 1904 starts here, and the opening format is the fun one. In four-ball, every player plays her or his own ball and the better score on each hole counts.

That means birdies, bold lines and swings that don't have to be safe. Sixteen national teams, each with one man and one woman, are expected to play 18 holes before the second-day finale.

The event runs between the men's and women's competitions, so Riviera should feel like a changeover day: men's stars still around, women's stars arriving. Watch the hillside and fairways for pairings that click early.
GLF05.potentialContendersIntro: Teams are not yet announced, so every pairing below is speculative. Each country can send one man and one woman who qualify individually.

potentialContenders.name: USA
potentialContenders.note: Speculative pairing of world No. 1s Scottie Scheffler and Nelly Korda. Nelly Korda won the 2026 U.S. Women's Open at Riviera.

potentialContenders.name: Japan
potentialContenders.note: Could pair Hideki Matsuyama, Paris 2024 bronze medalist, with Miyu Yamashita, a top-five woman in late 2026.

potentialContenders.name: South Korea
potentialContenders.note: Women's strength through Ryu Hae-ran and Kim Hyo-joo could make Korea a dangerous team, depending on who qualifies for the men's side.

potentialContenders.name: Thailand
potentialContenders.note: Would lean on Jeeno Thitikul, women's No. 2 in November 2026, if the men's qualifying works out.

GLF06.blurb:
Alternate shot is golf with the safety net removed. One ball, two partners, and one of you has to hit the next shot from wherever the other one left it.

That is the format for the medal round, and it is the first golf team medal at the Games since 1904. A man tees off on some holes, a woman on others, and a single bad drive can swing a hole in a heartbeat.

It all unfolds on a Monday morning, with the sun climbing over the canyon and the field following the pairs hole by hole.
GLF06.potentialContendersIntro: Teams are speculative until qualification ends in June 2028. These are the individual stars who could shape the medal round, assuming they qualify and their countries field teams.

potentialContenders.name: Nelly Korda
potentialContenders.note: Women's world No. 1 as of November 2026. She won the 2026 U.S. Women's Open at Riviera, so she knows the greens.

potentialContenders.name: Scottie Scheffler
potentialContenders.note: Reigning men's champion. A likely partner for Korda if both qualify.

potentialContenders.name: Lydia Ko
potentialContenders.note: Reigning women's champion. Could appear if she qualifies, though New Zealand's men's side is uncertain.

potentialContenders.name: Jeeno Thitikul
potentialContenders.note: Women's world No. 2 as of November 2026. A projected contender for Thailand.

potentialContenders.name: Miyu Yamashita
potentialContenders.note: Top-five woman in late 2026 and a speculative Japan team member.

GLF07.blurb:
Nelly Korda opened the 2026 U.S. Women's Open at Riviera with a 73, tied for 56th. She won it anyway.

That is the reason to be on the grounds for round one. Nothing is settled, and the course has just proven it will give comebacks. This field arrives knowing the layout. Many of these players competed here in 2026, so it will feel familiar rather than new.

Defending champion Lydia Ko tees off with a full set of medals already at home. Walk the fairways, find your player and settle in. The fun is in spotting who plays the first nine as if they know what's coming.
GLF07.potentialContendersIntro: The 60-player field is set from the rankings in June 2028, so these are projections. Ko is the confirmed defending champion.

potentialContenders.name: Nelly Korda
potentialContenders.note: 2020 champion and women's world No. 1 as of November 2026. She won the 2026 U.S. Women's Open at Riviera after a 73 start.

potentialContenders.name: Lydia Ko
potentialContenders.note: Confirmed Paris 2024 gold medalist. Defends her title if she qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Jeeno Thitikul
potentialContenders.note: Women's world No. 2 in late 2026, with wins at Honda LPGA Thailand and the Lotte Championship that year.

potentialContenders.name: Charley Hull
potentialContenders.note: Finished one shot behind Korda at the 2026 U.S. Women's Open at Riviera. Could be a course-form contender.

GLF08.blurb:
Lydia Ko is the only golfer to own all three medals, and she looked like a new player at times in 2026. She shot a career-low 12-under 60 in the first round of the Ford Championship, then finished in the top five.

Round 2 is where reputations get tested. Early momentum meets a course that has been playing for a day, and the players who survive Thursday set up a Friday of real pressure. It's also a day for the flat, steady rhythm of the sport: long walks, quiet putts, small gasps from fairway ropes.

A Riviera Thursday rewards patience. Look for the player who isn't in a hurry.
GLF08.potentialContendersIntro: These are projections, since the women's field is set in June 2028. Ko, Henseleit and Lin are confirmed Paris 2024 medalists.

potentialContenders.name: Lydia Ko
potentialContenders.note: Confirmed Paris 2024 gold medalist with silver and bronze from earlier Games. Her 60 at the 2026 Ford Championship shows her upside.

potentialContenders.name: Jeeno Thitikul
potentialContenders.note: Women's world No. 2 as of November 2026. A projected contender after winning the 2026 Lotte Championship by three strokes.

potentialContenders.name: Esther Henseleit
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalist. Could return to contention if she qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Janet Lin
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalist. Could appear if she makes China's team.

GLF09.blurb:
Moving day at Riviera, and the board starts to show who has the nerve.

Jeeno Thitikul has been world No. 1 without ever winning a major, a distinction she shares with only one other player. A medal would give her something different to hold. She is one of several challengers, from Miyu Yamashita and Ruoning Yin to Lottie Woad, who give the field depth well beyond one or two names.

Some players will already have played the mixed-team event here, so they have a head start on the greens. Watch the crowd gather near the 18th green by late afternoon as positions firm up.
GLF09.potentialContendersIntro: These are projected names based on late-2026 form. The field is not set until June 2028.

potentialContenders.name: Jeeno Thitikul
potentialContenders.note: Women's No. 2 in November 2026 and a former world No. 1 without a major. A projected contender with a title to chase.

potentialContenders.name: Miyu Yamashita
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 Aramco Korea Championship and ranked fourth in the world in November 2026. Likely contender.

potentialContenders.name: Ruoning Yin
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 Buick LPGA Shanghai. Could be China's best medal hope if she qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Lottie Woad
potentialContenders.note: Seventh in the world in November 2026. Speculative contender if she makes the team.

GLF10.blurb:
Nelly Korda won the 2026 U.S. Women's Open at Riviera with a birdie on the par-5 17th, a one-shot win for her fourth career major. She could walk this course again on the final afternoon, with the golf program ending around her.

Lydia Ko, meanwhile, is the defending champion and the most decorated golfer in Games history. She has silver, bronze and gold already, and a hill full of fans would roar at her again.

The slopes above the 18th green turn into an amphitheater as the last groups arrive. Show up for the last putt and stay for the medals.
GLF10.potentialContendersIntro: Qualification ends in June 2028, so these names are projections. Korda is the 2020 champion and Ko the confirmed Paris 2024 gold medalist.

potentialContenders.name: Nelly Korda
potentialContenders.note: 2020 champion and 2026 LPGA Rolex Player of the Year after four wins. She was one point short of Hall of Fame qualification.

potentialContenders.name: Lydia Ko
potentialContenders.note: Confirmed defending champion who completed her set of medals in Paris 2024. Could add another if she qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Jeeno Thitikul
potentialContenders.note: Women's No. 2 in November 2026. A likely contender who is still after a major-level win.

potentialContenders.name: Esther Henseleit
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalist. Could return to the leaderboard if she qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Janet Lin
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalist. Could appear for China if she makes the team.

GRY01.blurb:
Twenty-four gymnasts, four apparatus each, ten tickets to the final. The math is brutal, and it starts at lunchtime.

This is the session for seeing the field before the pressure peaks. Hoop, ball, clubs and ribbon come in rapid rotation, and one dropped apparatus can end a week of work. Watch the home contingent: Rin Keys was eighth and Megan Chu 11th at the 2026 World Championships, and a hometown crowd could push them toward the cut line.

Galen Center is a compact two-deck bowl, so even the upper rows sit close to the carpet. You'll hear the catch, and you'll hear the gasp when one goes wrong.
GRY01.potentialContendersIntro: Qualifiers are split across two sessions, so these gymnasts could appear here or in the evening block. Germany, Bulgaria and Italy have already earned quota places from the 2026 World Championships; the rest of the field is still being decided.

potentialContenders.name: Darja Varfolomeev
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 champion and winner of three straight world all-around titles through 2026. She is the benchmark for everyone else, if she makes Germany's team.

potentialContenders.name: Rin Keys
potentialContenders.note: Eighth in the 2026 world all-around final after seventh in 2025. A possible host-nation storyline if she is selected.

potentialContenders.name: Taisiia Onofriichuk
potentialContenders.note: Fourth in the 2025 world all-around final with 117.400. She is a likely contender to crack the top 10 if Ukraine secures a place.

potentialContenders.name: Takhmina Ikromova
potentialContenders.note: Fifth in the 2025 world all-around final with 114.650. Could be a dark horse for a final spot if she qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Anastasia Simakova
potentialContenders.note: Sixth in the 2025 world all-around final with 114.300. Germany can send up to two, so she is a possible second entry.

GRY02.blurb:
Just 0.050. That was the gap between Stiliana Nikolova and Sofia Raffaeli for 2026 world all-around silver, and both could be on the floor tonight.

Scores from this session merge with the afternoon's into one ranking, so the evening gymnasts know exactly what number they have to beat. Nikolova, the 2026 European champion, has finished second at the World Championships in 2025 and 2026. Raffaeli has all-around bronze from Paris 2024 and both of the last two Worlds. One clean four-apparatus run can reshuffle the leaderboard.

Late-day light fades beyond the north-end windows while the music builds, and the room hushes before every throw.
GRY02.potentialContendersIntro: Entry lists for the two qualification sessions are not set, so these names are projections for the evening block. Bulgaria and Italy have both earned individual quota places from the 2026 World Championships.

potentialContenders.name: Stiliana Nikolova
potentialContenders.note: World all-around silver in 2025 and 2026 and the 2026 European champion. A likely contender for the top qualifying spots, if selected.

potentialContenders.name: Sofia Raffaeli
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalist and 2026 world all-around bronze with 117.550, 0.050 behind Nikolova. A strong candidate for the final.

potentialContenders.name: Boryana Kaleyn
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalist, but she was not in the top eight at the 2025 Worlds. Her 2028 place with Bulgaria is far from certain.

potentialContenders.name: Megan Chu
potentialContenders.note: 11th in the 2026 world all-around final after 12th in 2025. Could be a host-nation entry if selected.

potentialContenders.name: Taisiia Onofriichuk
potentialContenders.note: Fourth at the 2025 Worlds with 117.400. Could appear in either qualification block if Ukraine earns a place.

GRY03.blurb:
Japan, Brazil, Spain. Then Spain, Japan, Brazil. The world group podium has held the same three nations two years running, only reshuffled, and this session is where that streak gets its first real test on the Games stage.

Five gymnasts move as one, flinging apparatus across the floor and catching it without a glance. Qualification brings the five balls routine and the mixed hoops-and-clubs routine. Spain topped both at the 2026 Worlds. Paris 2024 champion China and silver medalist Israel are hunting for a return to the top.

This is the afternoon to see the choreography in its raw form, with eyes on who survives into tomorrow's final.
GRY03.potentialContendersIntro: These are projected groups based on recent world results, since 2028 group qualification is still ahead. Spain has already earned a group quota place.

potentialContenders.name: Spain
potentialContenders.note: 2026 world group all-around champion with 57.450, and top in qualification in both routines at those Worlds. Quota place already secured.

potentialContenders.name: Japan
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world champion and 2026 world silver, plus Asian Games silver in 2026. A likely contender if they qualify.

potentialContenders.name: Brazil
potentialContenders.note: World silver in 2025 on home soil and bronze in 2026. Projected to stay near the podium.

potentialContenders.name: China
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalist, fourth at the 2025 Worlds. Could be a rebound story if they qualify.

potentialContenders.name: Israel
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalist and fifth at the 2025 Worlds with 53.150. A possible challenger if they qualify.

GRY04.blurb:
Darja Varfolomeev walked into Frankfurt in 2026 and left with five of the six individual world titles on offer, including a third straight all-around. Now comes the stage that made her Germany's first gold medalist in the sport.

Ten gymnasts, four routines each, no second chances. The tension is whether anyone can catch her. Stiliana Nikolova has taken world silver in 2025 and 2026. Sofia Raffaeli sits 0.050 behind her for 2026 bronze and owns a Paris 2024 medal as well.

Galen Center on a Friday evening is intimate enough to feel every release and every catch. When the ribbon unfurls in the last rotation, you will not want to blink.
GRY04.potentialContendersIntro: Qualification will set the top 10, so this is a projection based on recent world results. Varfolomeev is the clear favorite if she competes, but none of the 2028 fields are confirmed.

potentialContenders.name: Darja Varfolomeev
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalist and three-time reigning world all-around champion. She won five of six individual world titles in 2026. The favorite if selected.

potentialContenders.name: Stiliana Nikolova
potentialContenders.note: World all-around silver in both 2025 and 2026, and the 2026 European champion. Projected as the main challenger.

potentialContenders.name: Sofia Raffaeli
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalist and all-around bronze at the 2025 and 2026 Worlds. Likely in the medal mix if she qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Taisiia Onofriichuk
potentialContenders.note: Fourth at the 2025 Worlds with 117.400. Could push for a podium spot if she makes the final.

potentialContenders.name: Rin Keys
potentialContenders.note: Eighth at the 2026 Worlds. A possible home-crowd favorite if she earns a place in the top 10.

GRY05.blurb:
The last rhythmic gymnastics medal of the Games gets decided in the middle of a Saturday afternoon, and it will not be quiet.

China arrived in Paris as outsiders and left with the first non-European gold in the sport's history, winning by 0.95. Since then the world has moved. Japan won in 2025, Spain took the title in 2026, and Brazil has been a podium regular for two straight years.

Five gymnasts in perfect sync, apparatus crossing the air in a blur, and a room full of people holding their breath as the last group sets. After the final catch, the sport's 2028 story is done.
GRY05.potentialContendersIntro: Group lineups for 2028 are not set, so these gymnasts are projections based on recent world results and could change with selection and injuries.

potentialContenders.name: Marina Cortelles
potentialContenders.note: Won 2026 world group all-around gold and 2025 world bronze with Spain. A likely contender if she stays in the group.

potentialContenders.name: Megumi Nishimoto
potentialContenders.note: World group all-around gold in 2025 and silver in 2026, plus Asian Games silver in 2026. Projected to anchor a medal push if selected.

potentialContenders.name: Ding Xinyi
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalist who won five balls silver and team bronze at the 2026 Worlds. Could be central to a China comeback if she competes.

GTR01.blurb:
Ivan Litvinovich against Wang Zisai is the rivalry to circle. Litvinovich won Paris 2024 gold, with Wang taking silver, and then beat the defending champion Wang at the 2026 Worlds in Nanjing for his first individual world title. Wang had beaten him at the March 2026 World Cup in Alkmaar. They trade wins, and by 2028 they could still be trading them.

This one is a lunchtime session, not an evening show, so you get a bright, early-afternoon crowd and a full final in under three hours. Qualification and the final come back to back, which means you can watch a field of 20-odd gymnasts shrink to a handful of routines.

From the steep seats at DTLA Arena you look straight down on the bed. Each routine is ten skills in about 20 seconds, and you hear the thump of every landing. A single wobble can decide a medal.
GTR01.potentialContendersIntro: Litvinovich won Paris 2024 gold as a neutral athlete, and the 2026 world podium repeated the Paris order. Who actually competes in 2028 is not yet settled, including eligibility terms for Belarusian athletes, so treat this list as a projection.

potentialContenders.name: Ivan Litvinovich
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 champion (as AIN) and Tokyo champion, plus 2026 world champion. Eligibility for 2028 had not been confirmed in available information.

potentialContenders.name: Wang Zisai
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalist and 2025 world champion. Went undefeated in the 2026 World Cup series through Riccione, so he is a likely top contender.

potentialContenders.name: Yan Langyu
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalist and 2026 Asian Games champion. His landing error in the 2026 team final cost China, so he may be looking to answer that.

potentialContenders.name: Hayato Miyano
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world bronze medalist who performed what the federation called the first 10-triple routine at Riccione in 2026. A high-difficulty threat if he makes the team.

potentialContenders.name: Ruben Padilla
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world silver medalist. If he makes the US team, a home crowd could be a lift.

GTR02.blurb:
Bryony Page has a full set: Rio silver, Tokyo bronze, Paris gold. She would be 37 in 2028, and she has not publicly confirmed her plans, but if she is on the bed in Los Angeles, watching her would be a treat.

The field she faces is deep and shifting. China's Hu Yicheng won the 2025 world title, a Chinese gymnast took home gold in Nanjing in 2026, and Viyaleta Bardzilouskaya, Paris silver medalist, took the 2026 world silver. Japan keeps producing medalists too.

This is the evening session, and DTLA Arena at night is the place for it. The seats rise steeply, so even the upper rows look straight down on the bed, and the room goes still before each routine. Ten skills later it exhales together. The margins here are often tenths of a point.
GTR02.potentialContendersIntro: Page won Paris 2024 gold and Bardzilouskaya (then AIN) took silver. Who is in the 2028 field, including Page and any Belarusian or Russian athletes, is not settled, so these names are projections.

potentialContenders.name: Bryony Page
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 champion and the only woman with a full set of trampoline medals. Selected for the 2026 Worlds at age 35, but her 2028 plans were not confirmed.

potentialContenders.name: Viyaleta Bardzilouskaya
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalist (as AIN) and 2026 world silver medalist. Could return if eligibility allows.

potentialContenders.name: Hu Yicheng
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world champion, the first Chinese woman to win it in a decade. Likely part of a strong Chinese challenge.

potentialContenders.name: Hikaru Mori
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world silver medalist. A consistent medal contender if she makes Japan's team.

potentialContenders.name: Sophiane Méthot
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalist. Could contend again if she qualifies.

HBL01.blurb:
Handball gets going before the Opening Ceremony. Two days ahead of it, Long Beach Arena opens the men's tournament, and the sport's top team walks in with a question: how good is Denmark without Mikkel Hansen and Niklas Landin Jacobsen?

So far, the answer is frightening. The Danes took the 2025 world title, beating Croatia 32-26, and then won EHF EURO 2026 over Germany, with Mathias Gidsel scoring 68 goals.

Get there early. The drum-shaped 1962 arena has a giant gray whale mural wrapped around its outer wall. Inside, you can watch the whole sport's first morning from the seats.
HBL01.potentialContendersIntro: Denmark is the reigning Paris 2024 champion, and the other teams below are projected contenders, since no 2028 berths beyond the host's are confirmed yet.

potentialContenders.name: Denmark
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalist and 2025 world champion. Gidsel, a three-time IHF World Player of the Year, leads a team that has already shown it can win without its retired legends.

potentialContenders.name: Germany
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalist and EHF EURO 2026 runner-up, losing the final 34-27. A likely contender if they qualify, and hosts of the 2027 World Championship.

potentialContenders.name: Croatia
potentialContenders.note: Lost the 2025 World Championship final 32-26 to Denmark. Could appear if they qualify.

potentialContenders.name: USA
potentialContenders.note: Automatic host qualifier, with a best Games finish of sixth, in 1936. A home crowd could make them a nuisance for anyone.

HBL02.blurb:
Revenge has a long memory in handball, and Germany has been carrying one around since Paris. The Germans lost the gold medal match 39-26, then lost the EHF EURO 2026 final to Denmark 34-27 in Herning.

If the draw puts Germany or Spain on court this afternoon, watch the pace. Handball is sixty minutes of fast breaks, wing jumps that hang in the air and goalkeepers spreading themselves across the net, and the best teams squeeze it all into long runs. Spain, the Paris bronze medalist, specializes in the grinding kind.

This is the early-afternoon slot, so you get the same quality as the evening but with room to get a seat close to the court.
HBL02.potentialContendersIntro: The teams below are projected contenders based on Paris 2024 results and recent form. None except the United States has a confirmed 2028 berth, so treat this as informed speculation.

potentialContenders.name: Germany
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalists with a score to settle with Denmark. The 2027 World Championship in six German cities could even earn them a direct berth.

potentialContenders.name: Spain
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalists. They sat third in the November 2026 EHF EURO Cup, so they could be a quiet threat.

potentialContenders.name: Denmark
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 champions and EURO 2026 winners over Germany. The favorite if they qualify, as expected.

potentialContenders.name: Hungary
potentialContenders.note: Leading their EURO 2028 Qualifiers group with two wins under new coach László Sótonyi. A dark horse if they reach Long Beach.

HBL03.blurb:
Mathias Gidsel is the sort of player you want to see under evening lights. He is the first man to win the IHF World Player of the Year three years running, and he plays a game of angles that makes defenders look flat-footed.

This is the first prime-time men's session of the Games, and the arena should be fuller and louder. If the host American team lands in this slot, the noise could climb. The U.S. men have never finished better than sixth, in 1936, so every goal against a European powerhouse would be a story.

Bring a jacket for the walk back along the Long Beach waterfront. The harbor breeze is real after dark.
HBL03.potentialContendersIntro: These are projected teams for the evening slot. The United States is confirmed as host, and the rest are speculation based on form.

potentialContenders.name: Denmark
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 champions and four-time defending world champions after the 2025 title. Gidsel's three straight World Player of the Year awards make this a must-watch team.

potentialContenders.name: USA
potentialContenders.note: Host qualifier. Handball's rare American appearance, with a best finish of sixth in 1936.

potentialContenders.name: Croatia
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world silver medalists and in Group C of the 2027 World Championship with Spain. Could appear if they qualify.

potentialContenders.name: Hungary
potentialContenders.note: Perfect start to EURO 2028 qualifying with big wins over Montenegro and Kosovo. A possible European qualifier.

HBL04.blurb:
Norway arrives as the team everyone is chasing, and in handball that means they are chased hard. Paris 2024 gold, EHF EURO 2024 and the 2025 World Championship came in a row.

Henny Reistad is the engine. She scored eight goals in the Paris final, was MVP and top scorer (55 goals) at the 2025 Worlds, and has been named the IHF's top female player three years running. Watching a left-handed shot like hers from a few rows back is the best argument for buying a ticket.

The women's tournament opens at 9 AM, so you are among the first to see which team looks sharpest.
HBL04.potentialContendersIntro: Norway won gold in Paris and is projected to be back, but 2028 berths are not settled. The others below are speculative contenders.

potentialContenders.name: Norway
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalists and 2025 world champions, beating Germany 23-20 in Rotterdam. Reistad is the star to watch if they qualify.

potentialContenders.name: France
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalists, who took bronze at the 2025 Worlds. A likely contender for the podium.

potentialContenders.name: Germany
potentialContenders.note: 2025 World Championship runners-up, losing 23-20 to Norway. A rising force if they qualify.

potentialContenders.name: USA
potentialContenders.note: Host qualifier. Coached by Sarah Gascon and captained by Julia Taylor, they have a best Games finish of fifth, in 1984.

HBL05.blurb:
Norway and France do not need an excuse to be rivals. France beat Norway 31-28 in the 2023 world final, and Norway answered with Paris gold, EHF EURO 2024 and the 2025 world title.

So a Thursday afternoon women's session may turn into a preview of the medal rounds. Reistad set the EHF Champions League scoring record, 154 goals for Team Esbjerg in 2024/25, while goalkeeper Katrine Lunde, if she is still in net, remains a wall that shooters respect.

The afternoon slot gets a mixed crowd of families, handball obsessives and locals who just wandered over from the waterfront. By the second match they all know the rules.
HBL05.potentialContendersIntro: The teams below are projected from Paris 2024 and recent world results. No 2028 field is set beyond the United States as host.

potentialContenders.name: Norway
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 champions with Reistad, 2025 World Championship MVP, if she is in the squad. Lunde, third in the 2025 Player of the Year vote, could be in goal if she plays on.

potentialContenders.name: France
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalists and 2023 world champions. Bronze at the 2025 Worlds after losing to Germany in the semifinals.

potentialContenders.name: Denmark
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalists and fifth at the 2025 Worlds. A projected contender again.

potentialContenders.name: Brazil
potentialContenders.note: Sixth at the 2025 Worlds, the best non-European finish, with Bruna de Paula runner-up for 2025 Player of the Year. Could earn the Pan American berth.

HBL06.blurb:
The most interesting storyline in women's handball right now is Germany. A team that had gone 32 years without a world final reached one in 2025, knocking out defending champion France in the semifinals on the way.

Viola Leuchter, the best young player of that tournament, is the sort of name to learn before you sit down. If she stays healthy, she could be one of the Games' break-out athletes in Long Beach.

This evening session is where the new challengers and old powers collide. Hungary hosts the 2027 World Championship in the winter before, and the champions there qualify directly, so form could change by the time these teams hit the court.
HBL06.potentialContendersIntro: These are projected contenders for this evening session, based on the 2025 World Championship. None of these berths is confirmed except for the United States as host.

potentialContenders.name: Germany
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world silver medalists, their first world final in 32 years. Leuchter, named best young player, could be a headline name if she makes the team.

potentialContenders.name: Netherlands
potentialContenders.note: Co-hosts and fourth at the 2025 World Championship. A projected contender if they qualify.

potentialContenders.name: Hungary
potentialContenders.note: Seventh at the 2025 Worlds, per the finishing order, and 2027 World Championship hosts. Could earn a Europe berth.

potentialContenders.name: USA
potentialContenders.note: Host qualifier, with a fifth-place finish in 1984. A local favorite regardless of the result.

HBL07.blurb:
Saturday morning, the day after the Opening Ceremony, and the Games' first big weekend is underway. For American handball fans, a small but very passionate group, this could be the day the host men's team gets to play.

The U.S. qualifies automatically as host, which makes its place in the field a rarity: a country outside Europe's heartland in a sport where Denmark, Germany and Spain traditionally decide the podium. Sixth place in 1936 is the best Games result.

Keep an eye on pace and noise. Handball's hardest shots come at the wings and the line, and a drum-shaped arena sends every thud of ball against post straight back to the stands.
HBL07.potentialContendersIntro: The United States is confirmed as host. The others are projected contenders based on Paris 2024 and recent results.

potentialContenders.note: Host qualifier with a best Games finish of sixth, in 1936. Played Canada in the August 2026 series in Sioux City to start the Americas path.

potentialContenders.name: Germany
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalists and EURO 2026 runners-up. They host the 2027 World Championship and could qualify directly.

potentialContenders.name: Denmark
potentialContenders.note: Reigning Games champions and 2025 world champions. Likely to travel as favorites.

potentialContenders.name: Spain
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalists. A seasoned team that could be dangerous in a group.

HBL08.blurb:
Qualifying for Europe's spots is a tournament in itself. Thirty-two teams in eight groups are fighting for berths, and the stories behind them could decide who is in Long Beach.

Hungary has opened with two wins under new coach László Sótonyi. Croatia and Spain, meanwhile, share Group C at the 2027 World Championship in Munich, a dress rehearsal that might send one straight to the Games.

The afternoon session is a good pick for anyone who likes the tactical side. The 6-0 defensive wall, the pivot battling for position, the goalkeeper reading a wing shot: watch them from the upper rows for the patterns.
HBL08.potentialContendersIntro: Which European sides arrive is still being decided, so these are projected contenders and not confirmed entries.

potentialContenders.name: Croatia
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world runners-up, placed in Group C of the 2027 Worlds. A likely European contender.

potentialContenders.name: Spain
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalists, in the same 2027 World Championship group as Croatia. Could appear if they qualify.

potentialContenders.name: Hungary
potentialContenders.note: Maximum points in their EURO 2028 qualifying group so far. A dark horse if they come through the next rounds in March 2027.

potentialContenders.name: Germany

HBL09.blurb:
Saturday night at Long Beach Arena is the best seat in the first week for the men's tournament. The matches are in prime time, and the favorites tend to be on court.

If Denmark and Germany end up in the same group, this is the match to circle. The Danes took the 2024 gold 39-26 and beat the Germans again, 34-27, for the EHF EURO 2026 title, with Mathias Gidsel scoring 68 goals. Germany knows what it needs to change.

The IHF says tickets are sold through a fully digital process managed by AXS and Eventim, so have your phone charged. Then get in, find your seat and let the noise build.
HBL09.potentialContendersIntro: The teams below are projected contenders based on recent finals. No 2028 berths besides the host's are confirmed.

potentialContenders.name: Denmark
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 champions, 2025 world champions and EURO 2026 winners, led by Gidsel. Favorites if they qualify.

potentialContenders.name: Germany
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 and EURO 2026 runners-up. Their rematch with Denmark is the one to watch.

potentialContenders.name: Spain
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalists. Played in the November 2026 EHF EURO Cup and could be a quiet threat.

potentialContenders.name: USA
potentialContenders.note: Host qualifier. Could stage a Saturday-night upset if the home crowd gets involved.

HBL10.blurb:
A Sunday morning can belong to one player. Henny Reistad scored 154 goals for Team Esbjerg in 2024/25, an EHF Champions League single-season record, then led the 2025 World Championship with 55.

If she lines up for Norway, watch how defenses try to take away her shot and how often she beats them anyway. Then check the other end: Katrine Lunde, third in the 2025 Player of the Year vote, is the goalkeeper who might stop her teammates' rivals, if she plays on.

Sunday mornings are a bargain. You get a high-level game and a calmer crowd, with plenty of time afterward to walk around the harbor and look at the whale mural.

potentialContenders.name: Norway

potentialContenders.name: Denmark

HBL11.blurb:
In 1984, the American women finished fifth, the sport's best U.S. result at a Games, in the last Summer Games in Los Angeles. Forty-four years later, the host team plays in Long Beach, a short drive from where that fifth place was earned.

That tradition makes a Sunday afternoon session the one for families and for anyone curious about the sport. Women's handball is physical, fast and usually close, and the home team gets noise at every goal.

Also watch for Brazil. The Brazilians were the top non-European finisher at the 2025 Worlds, and a team from the Americas can make this feel like a regional derby.
HBL11.potentialContendersIntro: The United States is the only confirmed team. The rest are projected contenders based on the 2025 World Championship.

potentialContenders.name: USA
potentialContenders.note: Host qualifier with a best Games finish of fifth in 1984. Their place is guaranteed, though the results are not.

potentialContenders.name: Brazil

potentialContenders.name: France

potentialContenders.name: Netherlands

HBL12.blurb:
Twenty-nine to twenty-one. That was the Paris 2024 final, and Norway still thinks about how clean it was. Henny Reistad scored eight goals as the Norwegians took gold from France.

France has not gone away. It won bronze at the 2025 Worlds, and a Sunday night session in Long Beach is where a rematch would feel biggest. The crowd is up late, the building is full, and the final whistle comes close to 10:30.

Keep your tickets handy and be ready for the digital entry system the IHF has confirmed, run by AXS and Eventim. Then settle in for a night that could shape the women's bracket.
HBL12.potentialContendersIntro: The teams below are projected contenders based on Paris 2024 and the 2025 World Championship. None is confirmed except the United States as host.

potentialContenders.name: Norway
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 champions, 29-21 over France, and 2025 world champions. Reistad and goalkeeper Katrine Lunde were their key players, if they are both in the squad.

potentialContenders.name: France
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalists and 2025 world bronze medalists. A natural rival for Norway in the medal rounds.

potentialContenders.name: Germany
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world silver medalists, beating France in the semifinals. Leuchter, best young player in 2025, is a name to watch if selected.

potentialContenders.name: Denmark
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalists and fifth at the 2025 Worlds. A projected contender again.

HBL13.blurb:
A Monday morning at 9 AM is where handball rewards the curious. Not every team in a twelve-team field is a title threat, and the early session is the best place to see who the surprises might be.

Hungary is an easy one to circle. The Hungarians won their first two EURO 2028 qualifying games by 32-21 and 34-20 under new coach László Sótonyi, and a team with momentum can make life hard for bigger names.

The arena is quiet early, which means you hear everything: sneakers squeaking on the floor, the thump of seven-meter throws and the goalkeepers shouting at their defenders.
HBL13.potentialContendersIntro: The field is not set, so these are projected contenders for the men's morning session. Nothing here is confirmed beyond the United States as host.

potentialContenders.name: Denmark
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 champions and 2025 world champions. Projected favorites, though Hansen and Landin Jacobsen have retired.

potentialContenders.name: Germany

potentialContenders.name: USA

HBL14.blurb:
Spain is the team that does not make noise until it has to. Bronze in Paris, third in the November 2026 EHF EURO Cup with two points, and a seat in 2027 World Championship Group C in Munich, next to Croatia.

That is why this Monday afternoon feels like an experienced fan's session. Look for the patient build-up, the precise screens and a defense that gives away little. Croatia, 2025 world silver medalists, are the type of opponent who can punish a slow start.

Bring a program, or at least a plan, because this is the middle of the Long Beach week. There will be time to explore the harbor before the next set of matches.

potentialContenders.name: Spain

potentialContenders.name: Croatia

potentialContenders.name: Germany

potentialContenders.name: USA

HBL15.blurb:
Denmark's challengers keep waiting for the dynasty to crack, and it keeps not happening. The Danes won in Paris, then won two more titles without Mikkel Hansen or Niklas Landin Jacobsen.

So a Monday night at Long Beach Arena belongs to anyone with a chance to test them. Slovenia shares a 2027 World Championship group with Denmark in Kiel, and that meeting could give a hint of what's coming.

This is the last session in the batch, so expect a loud finish to the first men's week. Watch Mathias Gidsel's footwork: he is quick enough to change direction in the air, and the crowd will gasp.
HBL15.potentialContendersIntro: These are projected contenders based on 2027 World Championship groups and recent form. Nothing beyond the United States as host is confirmed.

HBL16.blurb:
Handball at nine in the morning has its own texture: fresh legs, a crowd still holding coffee, and a hall quiet enough that you hear everything. Shoes squeal, resin-sticky balls slap into palms, and a goalkeeper barks at her defense.

The women's field is built around Norway, the Paris 2024 champion and 2025 world champion. If Henny Reistad is healthy, the captain who scored 55 goals in the world title run is the player to track.

Group-stage mornings are where the pecking order starts to form, and you get a close look at it from inside a drum-shaped arena.
HBL16.potentialContendersIntro: Group draws and rosters for 2028 aren't set, so these are the teams most likely to shape the women's field, based on Paris 2024 and the 2025 World Championship.

potentialContenders.name: France

potentialContenders.name: Brazil

HBL17.blurb:
Germany spent 32 years waiting for a world final, then reached one in Rotterdam in 2025. The route went through France, the defending champion, in the semifinals. Viola Leuchter, named best young player at that tournament, gives the story a face.

That is why a mid-group afternoon in Long Beach is worth your time. The top four of six teams advance, so each result moves the quarterfinal picture and every goal difference can matter.

Expect handball's quick, physical rhythm: wings sprinting into space, a pivot wrestling for position, and goalkeepers making saves from point-blank range.

HBL18.blurb:
Evening sessions bring Long Beach's best look. The harbor goes dark outside, the arena lights hit the floor, and the whale mural on the rounded exterior wall is the last thing you pass on the way in.

France is the kind of team this slot suits. The Paris 2024 silver medalists took bronze at the 2025 Worlds after Germany knocked them out in the semifinals, and they are still a side nobody wants to face in a group.

Night handball is loud and quick, with fast breaks, big saves and a final five minutes that can swing a quarterfinal place.

HBL19.blurb:
Thirty-nine to twenty-six. That was the score when Denmark beat Germany for gold in Paris, and it is the margin every other men's team is trying to close.

The men's tournament opens just before the Opening Ceremony, so this is a morning to see how the field looks while the scoreboard is still fresh. Mathias Gidsel, the three-time IHF World Player of the Year, is the player who can change a match with one spin and one shot.

With a 12,000-seat hall holding handball's biggest names, the early starts offer a good look at the sport's top talent.
HBL19.potentialContendersIntro: No team has a confirmed 2028 berth yet beyond the U.S. as host. These are projected contenders based on Paris 2024 and recent form.

HBL20.blurb:
The United States is in the men's tournament as host, and for a country with little handball tradition, that makes this a notable week. The best U.S. men's finish at the Games is sixth, back in 1936.

If the Americans take the floor in this afternoon block, the crowd could make it feel like a home event for the sport. Even if they don't, the afternoon offers a view of the established powers. Croatia and Spain, grouped together at the 2027 Worlds, are the kind of sides that push each other to the final minute.

It is a good session to learn why this sport is a European obsession.

HBL21.blurb:
Thirty-seven to thirty-seven. That is what Portugal and Spain, the Paris 2024 bronze medalists, produced in a November 2026 qualifier. It is the kind of score that tells you what a handball night can become.

This evening block is built for goals. Denmark's own recent games included a 28-28 draw with Spain and a 33-24 win in Switzerland, with Mathias Gidsel scoring nine in one and Simon Pytlick ten in the other.

Two matches, a loud arena and a fast, high-scoring sport make this a strong pick if you want to see handball at its quickest.

HBL22.blurb:
In August 2026, Henny Reistad took a hard fall in a pre-season friendly and was hospitalized, and for a moment there were fears of something serious. The three-time IHF World Player of the Year, who captained Norway to the 2025 world title, has since moved on to a new chapter with Brest in France.

That makes a Thursday morning in Long Beach a chance to see the best centre back in the women's game. If she is on Norway's roster, she'll be the one dictating tempo from the middle.

Even if the details change, the setting stays the same: a drum-shaped arena and a hall full of fans.

HBL23.blurb:
The Netherlands lost two pillars when Lois Abbingh and Estavana Polman retired from the national team after the 2025 World Championship. The team had finished fourth, one match from a medal.

That gives an afternoon in Long Beach a rebuilding story. Will a new generation of Dutch players hold the standard, or will others take the space? Pay attention to who steps up in the back court and who handles the pressure in close finishes.

It is also a daylight session at a harbor-side arena, and the sport's changing of the guard is easy to follow from the seats.

HBL24.blurb:
Europe has dominated women's handball for generations, and the 2025 World Championship table made that clear. Brazil in sixth and Angola in tenth were the only non-European teams in the top ten.

That gives this Thursday evening a different kind of interest. Watch for the teams that have to travel and fight for every possession against opponents who see each other every season. If an outsider pushes a favorite, the late-evening crowd in Long Beach will find out first.

And the home team, the United States, has a quota place and a best Games finish of fifth in 1984 to improve on.

HBL25.blurb:
Mathias Gidsel scored a record 68 goals at the 2026 European Championship, and his team still looked deeper than its scorer. Simon Pytlick put up ten goals in a qualifier in Switzerland just months later.

That is the kind of Denmark you could see on a Friday morning in Long Beach: a four-time reigning world champion through 2025, with a 2026 European title added. The Danes are the team everyone has to solve.

Even for neutral fans, an early start is a good chance to watch the world's best team without waiting for the knockout rounds.

potentialContenders.name: France

HBL26.blurb:
France finished seventh at the 2026 European Championship. For a program that has built so much of men's handball's history, that is a result that stings, and it makes the Games a stage for a response.

Croatia comes from the other direction. The 2025 world silver was its first world podium since 2013, and the squad could still be on the rise.

An afternoon session with a fallen giant, a returning contender and, if they appear, the host Americans offers plenty to watch. The hall holds about 12,000, and it can get loud in a hurry when a team makes a comeback.

HBL27.blurb:
Germany has lost to Denmark in the Paris 2024 final, 39-26, and again in the 2026 European final, 34-27. Two big defeats to the same opponent can sour a team, or sharpen it.

If the rematch comes in the group stage, a Friday night in Long Beach is the place for it. Gidsel, 27 and the IHF World Player of the Year for three straight years, against a German defense determined to slow him.

Even without that pairing, the evening gives you a late, loud session with Spain and Croatia in the mix as well.
HBL27.potentialContendersIntro: The 2028 field isn't confirmed, so this rivalry is a projection based on the last two major finals.

potentialContenders.name: Croatia

HBL28.blurb:
Gold at Paris 2024, two world titles, three European titles. Henny Reistad's Norway résumé already reads like a veteran's, and she is a Saturday-morning ticket for anyone who wants to see how a centre back can control an entire game.

She will have moved from Esbjerg to Brest by then, and the 2026 scare after a hard fall in a friendly will be history, if she is fit. Reistad's career Champions League total stood at 869 goals in October 2026.

Watch how she draws two defenders and finds the pivot. It is a lesson in handball, played in a harbor-side arena.

HBL29.blurb:
Three teams skipped the qualifying scramble for the 2026 Women's Euro: Norway, Denmark and Hungary, the top three from 2024. Saturday afternoon in Long Beach could show how well that elite group holds up on a bigger stage.

Hungary is the one to watch for an upset. It finished just behind Brazil at the 2025 Worlds and hosts the 2027 World Championship, with momentum that could carry into 2028.

This is a daylight session with the whole weekend crowd in the building, a good one for newcomers who want to learn the sport's flow.
