HBL30.blurb:
Norway beat Denmark 31-23 in the 2024 European final, the kind of margin that makes a rematch worth circling. Add Henny Reistad, who holds the record for goals at the Women's EHF FINAL4 with 93, and you have a Saturday-night draw.

Big-stage scoring is her specialty. If she is fit and on the roster, it could be a night of long shots from the back court and quick Danish counters.

Saturday night in Long Beach, with the whales on the wall outside and a full 12,000-seat arena inside, is when this tournament is likely to feel its loudest.
HBL30.potentialContendersIntro: These are projected contenders. None of these teams other than the U.S. host has a confirmed 2028 place yet, and Reistad's participation depends on health and selection.

potentialContenders.name: Norway
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalist and 2025 world champion, with a 31-23 win over Denmark in the 2024 European final.

potentialContenders.name: Denmark
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalist, beaten by Norway in the 2024 Euro final. A likely contender for a rematch.

potentialContenders.name: Germany
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world silver medalist after reaching its first world final in 32 years.

potentialContenders.name: France
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalist and 2025 world bronze medalist.

HBL31.blurb:
Nine in the morning, a drum-shaped arena on the Long Beach waterfront, and the bracket finally bites: lose and your tournament is over. That is the first men's quarterfinal.

If Denmark finishes near the top of its group, a game like this could be its first real test. The Danes hold Paris 2024 gold, four straight world titles and the 2026 European crown, and Mathias Gidsel scored a record 68 goals at that Euro.

Handball up close is thudding shots, squeaking soles and a crowd learning the rules in real time. About 12,000 seats are planned.
HBL31.potentialContendersIntro: The quarterfinal pairings depend on group results, so these are projections based on recent form rather than confirmed matchups.

potentialContenders.name: Denmark
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalist (39-26 over Germany) and 2025 world champion. Could appear here if it finishes high in its group, with Gidsel as the headline act.

potentialContenders.name: Croatia
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world silver medalist, its first world podium since 2013. A likely contender if it qualifies, and a team that already pushed Denmark to a final.

HBL32.blurb:
Thirty-seven all. That was the score when Spain and Portugal met in the November 2026 European qualifiers, a 74-goal draw that shows what an Iberian handball afternoon can look like.

Spain arrives as Paris 2024 bronze medalist and also drew 28-28 with Denmark in the same window. If these two meet again in the second quarterfinal, expect a fast, goal-heavy game where one six-minute run swings everything.

The midday start gives the arena its first full-house buzz of the day. The crowd will be loud, and the goalkeepers will be busy.
HBL32.potentialContendersIntro: Matchups are not set. These teams are projections drawn from recent results, including the 2026 European qualifiers, and none has a 2028 berth confirmed.

potentialContenders.name: Spain
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalist that drew with both Denmark (28-28) and Portugal (37-37) in November 2026. A likely contender if it qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Portugal
potentialContenders.note: Beat Switzerland 33-28 and held Spain to a 37-37 draw in the qualifiers. Could be the dark horse of the knockout bracket if it books a place.

potentialContenders.name: France
potentialContenders.note: Finished seventh at the 2026 Euro after a main-round exit. Speculative: a proud handball nation looking to bounce back if it qualifies.

HBL33.blurb:
Mathias Gidsel is the name on the posters, but Denmark's real edge may be who comes next. Simon Pytlick scored ten goals in a 33-24 win over Switzerland in Zurich in the November 2026 qualifiers, and Gidsel put nine into a 28-28 draw with Spain.

When a team has two shooters like that, a late-afternoon quarterfinal can turn on which one the defense chooses to ignore.

Settle in around four o'clock. Handball's rhythm of long attacks, sudden fast breaks and a 12,000-seat arena inhaling on every shot is best tasted live.
HBL33.potentialContendersIntro: Quarterfinal matchups depend on group play. These projections come from current form, and nothing about 2028 rosters is confirmed.

potentialContenders.name: Denmark
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalist, 2025 world champion and 2026 European champion. Could appear here, with Gidsel and Pytlick leading a deep back court.

potentialContenders.name: Germany
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalist beaten 34-27 by Denmark in the 2026 Euro final. A likely contender, and the 2027 World Championship will be on home soil.

potentialContenders.name: Croatia
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world runner-up. Projected to be in the mix if it qualifies for 2028.

HBL34.blurb:
The last men's quarterfinal is the late one, and it fills the final two semifinal places before the arena empties into a Long Beach night. By 9:30 PM, half of the day's losers will have already flown home in their heads.

This is also where France could try to make up for a seventh-place finish at the 2026 Euro, when the defending European champions went out in the main round.

The U.S. men, who hold the host place and won the 2026 North America and Caribbean title, would love to be in the building for this one. A home crowd would help them.
HBL34.potentialContendersIntro: Pairings are not set, so these are projections. The host place is the only men's 2028 berth confirmed so far.

potentialContenders.name: France
potentialContenders.note: Seventh at the 2026 Euro after a main-round exit. Speculative: could be a dangerous knockout team if it qualifies and rediscovers its form.

potentialContenders.name: USA
potentialContenders.note: Holds the automatic host place. Beat Canada 40-18 and 40-23 in August 2026 to reach the 2027 Pan American Games. A quarterfinal would be a big step up.

HBL35.blurb:
Henny Reistad went to hospital after a hard fall in an August 2026 friendly. Norway's whole story is a reminder of how much rides on the three-time world player of the year, who scored eight goals in the Paris 2024 final.

If she is healthy, Norway has plenty to protect. It is the reigning Games champion and 2025 world champion, the only nation with five women's world titles.

The first women's knockout session starts at nine in the morning. Challengers get an early look at the team they all have to beat.
HBL35.potentialContendersIntro: Pairings depend on group results, and the field is still being filled through the 2026 Euro and qualifying events. These are projections.

potentialContenders.name: Norway
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 champion (29-21 over France) and 2025 world champion. Could appear here if it qualifies and tops its group, with Reistad's fitness a storyline.

potentialContenders.name: Netherlands
potentialContenders.note: Lost the 2025 world semifinal 35-25 to Norway. Dione Housheer made the All-Star team; a likely contender if it qualifies.

HBL36.blurb:
Denmark has been the bridesmaid for a decade. Bronze at Paris 2024 gave the country medals in both handball tournaments, but the Danes lost the 2024 European final to Norway 31-23 in Vienna.

The gap to the top is the whole story of this early-afternoon quarterfinal. Henny Reistad is set to leave Team Esbjerg for Brest after the 2026-27 season, which puts a Danish club-turned-rival star on the other side of the net in a different way.

The lunchtime slot belongs to travelers and regulars. Bring a hat for the walk along the Long Beach waterfront.
HBL36.potentialContendersIntro: Matchups are not set. These are projections from recent form, and no 2028 berth beyond the host place is confirmed.

potentialContenders.name: Denmark
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalist and 2024 European runner-up. Likely contender if it qualifies, but the 2026 Euro result could change its outlook.

potentialContenders.name: Brazil
potentialContenders.note: Finished sixth at the 2025 world championship, the best result by a non-European team. Could be the non-European side to watch if it qualifies.

HBL37.blurb:
France won the 2023 world title and reached the Paris 2024 final, where it lost 29-21 to Norway. The Bleues then ran into Germany in the 2025 world semifinals and went out.

That makes this late-afternoon quarterfinal a test of whether a team can reset after a fall. For the French, the Games might be the last chance for a generation that has done almost everything but win the gold.

The four o'clock slot has the best light on the waterfront, and the arena should be warm by the second half.
HBL37.potentialContendersIntro: Pairings depend on group results. These are projections, and the women's field is still being finalized through the 2026 Euro and later qualifiers.

potentialContenders.name: France
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalist and 2023 world champion, knocked out by Germany in the 2025 semifinals. Likely contender if it qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Angola
potentialContenders.note: Finished 10th at the 2025 worlds, one of only two non-European teams in the top 10. Speculative: could be a surprise knockout team if it qualifies.

HBL38.blurb:
Germany lost the 2025 world final 23-20, a three-goal margin against Norway after knocking out defending champion France in the semifinals. That is not a bad place to start a tournament.

If Germany makes it to Long Beach, this evening quarterfinal could be its coming-out party at the Games, with Viola Leuchter, the 2025 best young player, in a leading role.

The night session closes out the women's quarterfinals. Expect the hardest-working crowd of the day to be in the seats.
HBL38.potentialContendersIntro: Pairings depend on group results and qualifying, so these are projections. The U.S. host place is the only women's berth confirmed so far.

potentialContenders.name: Germany
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world runner-up, projected as a contender if it qualifies for 2028. Leuchter, Vogel and Döll were standouts in 2025.

potentialContenders.name: USA
potentialContenders.note: Automatic host place, its first women's handball appearance at the Games since 1996. Built through a Florida residency program under Sarah Gascon, with many recruits new to the sport. A quarterfinal would be a major step.

HBL39.blurb:
Denmark has beaten Germany in two straight major finals, 39-26 in Paris and 34-27 at the 2026 Euro. A semifinal is a different kind of fight, because a loss here means a bronze match, not a final.

Denmark's case is easy to make. The Danes won the 2025 world title 32-26 over Croatia, and Mathias Gidsel was MVP of both that tournament and the 2026 Euro.

The morning semifinal in Long Beach is a measuring stick for everyone else. The rest of the field will want to prove the Danes can be hurt.
HBL39.potentialContendersIntro: Semifinal participants are not known. These players are projections based on form, and none is confirmed for 2028.

potentialContenders.name: Mathias Gidsel
potentialContenders.note: Three-time IHF World Player of the Year and MVP of the 2025 Worlds and 2026 Euro. Will be 29 in 2028 and is a likely headliner if Denmark qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Simon Pytlick
potentialContenders.note: Scored ten goals in a 33-24 win over Switzerland in November 2026. Could be the second option who breaks a semifinal open.

potentialContenders.name: Juri Knorr
potentialContenders.note: Speculative: a leading playmaker for a Germany side that has lost two straight finals to Denmark, if he is in the squad.

HBL40.blurb:
The second men's semifinal is the one where the favorite may not be the Danes. Croatia reached the 2025 world final and lost 32-26 to Denmark, its first world podium since 2013.

Spain, the Paris 2024 bronze medalist, drew with both Denmark and Portugal in the November 2026 qualifiers. France finished seventh at the Euro but has the talent to go on a run.

The afternoon start gets the arena at its liveliest, as winners dream of a final and losers still have a medal on the line.
HBL40.potentialContendersIntro: Semifinal pairings are not set. These are projections from recent results, and none of them is confirmed for 2028.

potentialContenders.name: Luka Cindrić
potentialContenders.note: Speculative: a key back-court threat for a Croatia side that reached the 2025 world final, if he is in the squad.

potentialContenders.name: Aleix Gómez
potentialContenders.note: Speculative: a winger who could lead Spain's push to defend its Paris 2024 bronze, if Spain qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Dika Mem
potentialContenders.note: Speculative: could drive a French rebound after a seventh-place finish at the 2026 Euro, if France qualifies.

HBL41.blurb:
Henny Reistad was MVP and top scorer at the 2025 Women's World Championship with 55 goals, her second straight world MVP award. If she and Norway reach Long Beach, a semifinal is where the pressure peaks.

Norway beat the Netherlands 35-25 in the 2025 semifinals, and the 2025 title was its fifth, a record. Reistad will play for Brest in 2027-28.

The morning session puts a world-class opponent in front of a first women's semifinal crowd at Long Beach Arena. Look for the goalkeepers and watch Norway's fast breaks.
HBL41.potentialContendersIntro: Semifinal pairings are not set. These players are projections based on 2025 form and are not confirmed for 2028.

potentialContenders.name: Henny Reistad
potentialContenders.note: Three-time IHF World Player of the Year and 2025 world MVP. Likely headliner if Norway qualifies, though her fitness after the August 2026 fall is worth watching.

potentialContenders.name: Katrine Lunde
potentialContenders.note: All-Star goalkeeper at the 2025 Worlds. Speculative: she could still be in goal if she keeps playing and Norway qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Dione Housheer
potentialContenders.note: Made the 2025 world All-Star team as the Netherlands reached the semifinals. Projected to be a key figure if the Dutch qualify.

HBL42.blurb:
Germany went to the 2025 world final and lost 23-20 to Norway. France had won the 2023 world title, then lost to Germany in the 2025 semifinals. That kind of history gives a semifinal an edge.

Viola Leuchter was named best young player at the 2025 Worlds, and Emily Vogel and Antje Döll joined her on the world All-Star team. If those names reach Long Beach, this could be a changing of the guard.

The afternoon slot is built for a game that comes down to the last two minutes. A nervous crowd is a loud one.
HBL42.potentialContendersIntro: Semifinal pairings are not set. These players are projections from 2025 form, and none is confirmed for 2028.

potentialContenders.name: Viola Leuchter
potentialContenders.note: Best young player at the 2025 Worlds. Likely to be a leading figure if Germany qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Antje Döll
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world All-Star. Could be one of Germany's most reliable scorers if the team reaches a semifinal.

potentialContenders.name: Sarah Bouktit
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world All-Star. Could lead a French response after the semifinal loss to Germany, if France qualifies.

HBL43.blurb:
Nobody wants to be here on a Thursday morning, and everybody who is plays like it matters. A bronze medal match is a heartbreak and a second chance sharing one court.

Spain won this match at Paris 2024. Germany lost the 2026 Euro final 34-27, Croatia was the 2025 world runner-up and France fell in the main round of the Euro, so the candidates for a bronze match have all sorts of motive.

The U.S. men, who hold the host place, would love a medal at home. It would take a huge run, but a Long Beach crowd can make that feel possible.
HBL43.potentialContendersIntro: The bronze match pits the two semifinal losers, so these players are projections and nothing about 2028 rosters is confirmed.

potentialContenders.name: Aleix Gómez
potentialContenders.note: Speculative: a winger who could lead Spain's bid to repeat as bronze medalist, if Spain qualifies and loses a semifinal.

potentialContenders.name: Juri Knorr
potentialContenders.note: Speculative: could be the playmaker for a Germany side stung by finals losses to Denmark, if he is in the squad.

potentialContenders.name: Luka Cindrić
potentialContenders.note: Speculative: could be a key piece of a Croatia team that reached the 2025 world final, if the team qualifies.

HBL44.blurb:
Mathias Gidsel will be 29 at the 2028 Games and in his prime, and before the 2026 Euro he said it would be wrong not to call Denmark the biggest favorites. He backed it up with a record 68 goals.

Denmark beat Germany 39-26 in the Paris 2024 final and 34-27 in the 2026 Euro final, and has four straight world titles. The question is whether anyone can stop a team that keeps getting better.

By mid-afternoon in Long Beach, the whole arena should be on its feet. Gold is the only thing left to play for.
HBL44.potentialContendersIntro: Finalists are not known. These players are projections from recent form, and nothing about 2028 participation is confirmed.

potentialContenders.name: Mathias Gidsel
potentialContenders.note: Three-time IHF World Player of the Year, 2025 world MVP with a ten-goal final, and 2026 Euro MVP. A likely headliner if Denmark qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Simon Pytlick
potentialContenders.note: Scored ten in a 33-24 win over Switzerland in November 2026. Could be the second scorer who decides a final.

potentialContenders.name: Juri Knorr
potentialContenders.note: Speculative: playmaker for a Germany side that has lost two straight major finals to Denmark, if he makes the squad.

HBL45.blurb:
For the winner, this is a medal. For the loser, a long flight. Women's bronze comes with the sharpest contrast in the tournament, since both teams had a final in their sights 48 hours earlier.

Denmark won this match at Paris 2024, and it gave the country medals in both tournaments. Whoever lands here, whether it is France, Germany, the Netherlands or Brazil, will have a reason to play loose.

The morning start means a lighter crowd with plenty of die-hard fans. You will hear every coach and every shot.
HBL45.potentialContendersIntro: The bronze match pits the two semifinal losers. These players are projections from 2025 form, and no 2028 rosters are confirmed.

potentialContenders.name: Dione Housheer
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world All-Star. Could lead a Dutch push for a first medal if the Netherlands qualifies and loses a semifinal.

potentialContenders.name: Sarah Bouktit
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world All-Star. Speculative: could help France rebound after the 2025 semifinal exit, if it qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Antje Döll
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world All-Star. Could be a leader for Germany, runner-up in 2025, if it qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Bruna de Paula
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world All-Star as Brazil finished sixth. Speculative: a non-European threat if Brazil qualifies.

HBL46.blurb:
Eight goals from Henny Reistad turned the Paris 2024 final into a Norwegian coronation, 29-21 over France. Now comes the sequel, and it closes the handball program at the 2028 Games. Norway arrive as the team everyone else is built to stop: Paris champions, then 2025 world champions after a 23-20 win over Germany in Rotterdam.

Reistad, the IHF world player of the year in 2023, 2024 and 2025, will be 29 by then and, if she is in the squad, should be at her peak. Katrine Lunde, an All-Star goalkeeper at the 2025 worlds, could still be the wall at the other end of every shot. Whoever lines up opposite will have to solve both.

Inside a round, drum-shaped arena on the Long Beach waterfront, about 12,000 fans will sit close to a fast, physical, loud sport. Handball finals feel like a collision. Expect the noise to jump on every steal and every goalkeeper save.
HBL46.potentialContendersIntro: Norway won Paris 2024 and the 2025 world title, which makes them the projected favorite to reach this final. The challengers below are likely contenders based on recent form, and none of the 2028 rosters are confirmed.

potentialContenders.name: Henny Reistad
potentialContenders.note: Scored eight goals in the Paris 2024 final and was MVP and top scorer (55 goals) at the 2025 worlds. Named IHF world player of the year in 2023, 2024 and 2025. She would be 29 in 2028 if she makes the team.

potentialContenders.name: Katrine Lunde
potentialContenders.note: Made the 2025 world championship All-Star team in goal. Her place in 2028 is not confirmed, so watch Norway's goalkeeping plans.

potentialContenders.name: France
potentialContenders.note: Silver medalists at Paris 2024 and the Tokyo champions. They lost to Germany in the 2025 world semifinals and could be a contender to avenge the Paris final.

potentialContenders.name: Germany
potentialContenders.note: Reached the 2025 world final after knocking out France in the semifinals, then lost 23-20 to Norway. A likely contender if they qualify and keep their form.

potentialContenders.name: Denmark
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalists. A projected medal contender, though a final berth is speculation.

HOC01.blurb:
Germany arrive as world champions, the Netherlands as Paris 2024 gold medalists, and Belgium as Pro League winners. Nobody has played a minute at these Games yet, and that is the whole appeal of opening day.

The Paris final ended 1-1 and the Dutch won the shoot-out 3-1. Germany then beat Spain 1-0 for the 2026 World Cup, so the pecking order is anything but settled.

Carson Field is a training ground turned stadium, with temporary stands built around the pitch. Settle in for a morning double-header, and note which teams look sharp first.
HOC01.potentialContendersIntro: The draw is not set, so these are projected teams for the men's pool. Belgium and the United States are confirmed for 2028; the rest are likely entrants based on recent form.

potentialContenders.name: Germany
potentialContenders.note: Likely contender. Paris 2024 silver medalists and winners of the 2026 World Cup, 1-0 over Spain in the final.

potentialContenders.name: Netherlands
potentialContenders.note: Defending champions after the Paris shoot-out win over Germany, but they finished fourth at the 2026 World Cup.

potentialContenders.name: Belgium
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2025-26 Pro League and secured a direct place for 2028.

potentialContenders.name: India
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalists, and 2026 Asian Games champions who qualified directly.

potentialContenders.name: United States
potentialContenders.note: Confirmed as hosts, and back in the men's tournament for the first time in about three decades.

HOC02.blurb:
India come to California with a Paris bronze, a fifth men's Asian Games gold, and a captain who knows where the goals are. Harmanpreet Singh scored twice in the 5-1 win over Malaysia in the 2026 final.

The World Cup was a sterner lesson. India finished eighth after a 3-3 draw with Belgium ended in a shoot-out loss. They are still the highest-ranked Asian side, and a team with something to prove is worth watching.

This session runs into the night, so the second match is played under the lights beside the Galaxy's stadium. Pool placings now decide who skips the new play-in round.
HOC02.potentialContendersIntro: Pairings are not confirmed, so these are teams that could appear in the evening men's pool matches.

potentialContenders.name: India
potentialContenders.note: Qualified directly. Captain Harmanpreet Singh scored twice in the 2026 Asian Games final, and the team ranked eighth after the World Cup.

potentialContenders.name: Germany
potentialContenders.note: Likely contender. 2026 World Cup winners and 2025 European champions.

potentialContenders.name: Belgium
potentialContenders.note: Confirmed for 2028 as Pro League winners, and beat India in a shoot-out at the 2026 World Cup.

potentialContenders.name: Spain
potentialContenders.note: Projected to qualify. Lost the 2026 World Cup final 1-0 to Germany.

HOC03.blurb:
On August 29, 2026, Argentina beat the Netherlands in a shoot-out and ended a run of three straight Dutch world titles. If the two meet in Carson, expect that final to be on everyone's mind.

The Dutch women had gone through the 2025-26 Pro League without a defeat in regulation time. That is the standard Argentina has to match, and it makes any early meeting between them worth watching.

This is the first day of women's hockey at the Games, and the pitch is still new to everyone. A morning start gives you a first look at the field before the pool table tightens.
HOC03.potentialContendersIntro: The women's draw is not confirmed. The Netherlands, India and the United States have qualified, and the others are projected from recent form.

potentialContenders.name: Netherlands
potentialContenders.note: Qualified. Paris 2024 gold medalists and 2025-26 Pro League winners, with Yibbi Jansen as the league's top scorer on 15 goals.

potentialContenders.name: Argentina
potentialContenders.note: Likely contender. Paris 2024 bronze medalists and 2026 World Cup winners.

potentialContenders.name: India
potentialContenders.note: Qualified by winning the 2026 Asian Games, 1-0 over China in the final.

potentialContenders.name: Belgium
potentialContenders.note: Projected contender. Third in both recent Pro League seasons.

potentialContenders.name: United States
potentialContenders.note: Confirmed as hosts, so they could be on court in front of a home crowd.

HOC04.blurb:
Lalremsiami's 200th international match produced the only goal of the 2026 Asian Games final, and India's women had their first title at that event since 1982. In Carson they could be looking at a very different level of opposition.

That team finished fifth at the 2026 World Cup, their best finish in 52 years, and rose to eighth in the world rankings. Deepika Sehrawat scored 21 goals at the Asian Games.

The evening session runs until 10 PM, so expect the pitch lit up beside the Galaxy's stadium. China, the Paris silver medalists, must still qualify, so their place here is not guaranteed.
HOC04.potentialContendersIntro: The evening pool pairings are not confirmed. India is qualified, and the other teams are projected contenders.

potentialContenders.name: India
potentialContenders.note: Qualified. Asian Games champions, and fifth at the 2026 World Cup.

potentialContenders.name: Argentina
potentialContenders.note: Likely contender. 2026 World Cup winners who beat the Netherlands in the final shoot-out.

potentialContenders.name: China
potentialContenders.note: Only if they qualify. Paris 2024 silver medalists who lost the Asian Games final and missed the direct place.

potentialContenders.name: Netherlands
potentialContenders.note: Qualified. Defending champions with a record five women's golds.

HOC05.blurb:
Spain keep arriving at the edge of the podium. They lost the Paris bronze match to India, then lost the 2026 World Cup final 1-0 to Germany. The question is whether a Saturday morning in Carson is where that changes.

Around them sit teams with similar ambitions. Australia ranked third in the world after the World Cup and beat England in the fifth-place match. Belgium won the Pro League by beating the Netherlands 2-1 on the final weekend.

This is the middle of the pool stage, when ranking points turn into real pressure. Pool position will decide who goes straight to the quarterfinals and who must play in.
HOC05.potentialContendersIntro: Pairings are not set. These teams are likely to be in the men's mix, and only Belgium and India are confirmed so far.

potentialContenders.name: Spain

potentialContenders.name: Australia

potentialContenders.name: Belgium

potentialContenders.name: India
potentialContenders.note: Qualified. Paris 2024 bronze medalists who beat Spain for the medal.

HOC06.blurb:
Belgium's women waited 48 years for a World Cup podium and finally got one in 2026. They have since held third in the world rankings, and the Saturday night crowd in Carson will get to see them in this field.

They have history with Argentina, too. At Paris 2024 the two drew 2-2 for bronze, and Argentina won the shoot-out 3-1. Belgium finished third behind the Netherlands and Argentina in both recent Pro League seasons.

The session starts at 5:30 PM and runs late, so the second match plays well into the night. Pool results here feed straight into the new play-in structure.
HOC06.potentialContendersIntro: The pairings are not confirmed. The Netherlands, India and the United States have qualified, and the others are likely contenders.

potentialContenders.name: Belgium
potentialContenders.note: Likely contender. Won a medal at the 2026 World Cup, their first podium in 48 years.

potentialContenders.name: Argentina
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalists, who beat Belgium in that shoot-out.

potentialContenders.name: Germany
potentialContenders.note: Could appear. Runner-up at the 2025 EuroHockey Championship.

potentialContenders.name: India
potentialContenders.note: Qualified by winning the 2026 Asian Games.

HOC07.blurb:
Two finals, two 1-1 draws, two shoot-outs, one win each. The Netherlands beat Germany in Paris, and Germany won the rematch at the 2025 EuroHockey final.

Then Germany took the 2026 World Cup, with Michel Struthoff's 44th-minute goal beating Spain, while the Dutch finished fourth after losing the bronze match to Argentina. That makes this the rivalry to watch, and any meeting would feel like a final.

A Sunday morning start is a good fit for a first-time visit. The United States men are back in the Games after about three decades, so the home crowd has its own story to follow.
HOC07.potentialContendersIntro: The pool draw is not confirmed. The United States and India have qualified, and the rest are projected from recent results.

potentialContenders.name: Germany
potentialContenders.note: Likely contender. 2026 World Cup winners with a fourth world title, level with Pakistan's record.

potentialContenders.name: Netherlands
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalists who finished fourth at the 2026 World Cup.

potentialContenders.name: India
potentialContenders.note: Qualified. Manpreet Singh became the first Indian player with three Asian Games golds.

potentialContenders.name: United States
potentialContenders.note: Confirmed as hosts, in the men's tournament for the first time in about three decades.

HOC08.blurb:
The Netherlands won Paris gold, then won the 2024-25 Pro League, and have slipped since. They finished fourth in the 2025-26 Pro League and again at the 2026 World Cup.

Belgium's 2-1 win in Wavre on June 27, 2026 helped them claim the Pro League title, and that is the kind of team the Dutch must now beat. India, who beat Pakistan 5-3 in the pool stage of that World Cup, are another dangerous side.

This Sunday evening session runs to 10 PM, which should make for a charged finish to the second match. Pool position decides who skips the play-in round.
HOC08.potentialContendersIntro: The pairings are not confirmed. Belgium, India and the United States are qualified, and the rest are likely contenders.

potentialContenders.name: Belgium
potentialContenders.note: Qualified as 2025-26 Pro League winners, with a 2-1 win over the Netherlands on the final weekend.

potentialContenders.name: Netherlands
potentialContenders.note: Defending champions. Won the 2024-25 Pro League but finished fourth in 2025-26.

potentialContenders.name: Germany
potentialContenders.note: Likely contender. 2025 European champions and 2026 World Cup winners.

HOC09.blurb:
Pool placings matter more in 2028 than they did in Paris. Where the top four of six teams once went straight to the quarterfinals, a play-in round now makes every pool result count.

That gives a Monday morning a different edge. Teams outside the headline names, such as England (second in the 2025-26 Pro League), New Zealand (ninth at the 2026 World Cup) and South Africa (the top African side, 13th), have a real shot at taking points off a favorite.

It is a good session for seeing the depth of the field. Look for the teams who treat every match like a knockout.

HOC10.blurb:
The Netherlands have won the Pro League six times, they hold a record five women's golds, and they lost the 2026 World Cup final on penalties. Expect a team with something to settle.

Yibbi Jansen led the 2025-26 Pro League with 15 goals, and the Dutch were the first team other than the hosts to qualify. China lost the Asian Games final 1-0 to India and missed the direct place, so their presence here is not a given.

This Monday night session runs until 10 PM, so the second match plays well after dark. For anyone who wants the favorites under pressure, this is a good slot.

HOC11.blurb:
Most of the year this is where the LA Galaxy train. For two weeks it is a hockey stadium, with temporary stands and a 15,000-seat primary field, and the women's tournament is now well under way.

Argentina's 3-1 shoot-out win over the Netherlands at the 2026 World Cup was their first world title since 2010. Belgium reached that podium for the first time in 48 years, and India took the Asian Games title. All three are real threats in a pool.

A Tuesday morning start is quiet by stadium standards, but the pitch is where the stakes sit.
HOC11.potentialContendersIntro: The pairings are not confirmed. The United States, Netherlands and India are confirmed for the women's tournament, and the others are projected contenders.

HOC12.blurb:
Eight teams will fight for four quarterfinal places in the new play-in round, so a bad pool finish now has a real price. Tuesday night is when teams start to feel it.

The Netherlands and Argentina have been trading blows for years. Argentina won 3-2 in Santiago del Estero in December 2024 and then won the World Cup final shoot-out, even though the Dutch finished ahead of them in both recent Pro League seasons.

The session runs until 10:30 PM, so the second match finishes late. Australia, ninth in the world rankings, could be one of the sides looking to cause an upset.

One men's place in this field was handed out a year earlier at the 2027 Pan American Games in Lima, and every continent will have a team in Carson. Wednesday morning is a good time to see how wide the field really is.

The heavyweights are well known. The Netherlands won the 2024-25 Pro League, Belgium followed with the 2025-26 title, and Germany took the 2026 World Cup. India are qualified as Asian champions.

This is the second week of hockey, and pool tables are starting to show who looks like a contender.

Spain had more of the ball and more penalty corners in the 2026 World Cup final. They even pulled their goalkeeper for an extra outfield player late on, and still lost 1-0. Now they have a chance to prove it was only a bad day.

Spain also finished third in the 2024-25 Pro League and third at the 2025 European Championship. England, runners-up in the 2025-26 Pro League, will want something to say too.

A Wednesday night session runs to 10 PM at a temporary stadium beside the Galaxy's. Teams that miss the quarterfinals directly go into the July 22 play-in round.

This is the last men's pool session at Carson Field. After it, the table is final, and the play-in round on July 22 sorts out who goes through.

By now the contenders should be clear. Germany arrive as world champions, Australia are third in the world rankings, and the Netherlands are still trying to rebuild after finishing fourth at the World Cup. India, ranked eighth, took bronze in Paris and beat Spain for it.

A Thursday morning start is a calm setting for what could be the most pressured matches of the pool.

Argentina beat the Netherlands in a shoot-out to win the 2026 World Cup, the Dutch side's first World Cup defeat since 2010. The Netherlands still hold the Games title and six of the seven Pro League crowns.

Which of them takes the pitch on this Thursday evening depends on the pool draw. Both will be chasing a straight route to the quarterfinals and a way around the new play-in round. Watch the Dutch penalty corners: Yibbi Jansen topped the Pro League scoring charts in each of the last two seasons.

HOC17.blurb:
A saved penalty stroke from Savita Punia sealed India's 1-0 win over China in the 2026 Asian Games final. It flipped the pecking order in Asian women's hockey, and China, Paris 2024 silver medalists, now need another route to these Games.

By Friday morning, the pool table is starting to bite. Results here decide who goes straight to the quarterfinals and who has to survive Sunday's play-in. That makes a morning match in the open-air stands feel less like a warm-up and more like a pressure test, with a Pro League heavyweight or two still sorting out their positions.

HOC18.blurb:
Finish high and you slide into the quarterfinals. Slip, and you're back at Carson on Sunday, fighting with seven other teams for four remaining places. The last pool whistle on a Friday night is where that gets decided.

The pecking order says Argentina and the Netherlands, but only just. Argentina were Pro League runners-up in both 2024-25 and 2025-26 before winning the World Cup on a shoot-out in Amstelveen. The Dutch won both of those Pro League titles.

It's the final women's pool night, so expect every scoreboard to matter.

HOC19.blurb:
This is hockey with a trapdoor. The play-in round is new for 2028, and on this Saturday morning the men's teams that missed a direct quarterfinal berth play for just four spots. Lose and you're out of medal contention before you've reached the last eight.

The teams aren't known yet, but the possibilities are juicy. India won bronze at Paris 2024 and the 2026 Asian Games, yet finished eighth at the 2026 World Cup. The Dutch were fourth at that tournament, and Germany and Spain filled the final.

The stands are temporary and the stakes aren't.

HOC20.blurb:
A World Cup finalist or a Pro League runner-up could be playing for its life tonight. The four winners advance to the men's quarterfinals, and the four losers go home with no medal chance left.

It's the second pair of play-ins on a Saturday, so the early session has already shown how this new round feels. Spain lost the 2026 World Cup final 1-0 to Germany, having controlled possession and corners. England finished second in the Pro League behind Belgium. Either could be forced into a knockout.

Evening hockey in the open air, with a loser-out edge.

HOC21.blurb:
Germany lost the fifth-place match at the 2026 World Cup to an Indian side that scored three times. India finished fifth, their best World Cup result in 52 years, and lifted themselves to eighth in the world rankings.

That result is a reminder of how thin the margins are in the women's play-in. Eight teams that missed a straight route to the quarterfinals play for four places, and the morning session sets up the first two. Australia also arrive with scars after losing both the World Cup semifinal and bronze match.

The new round brings knockout nerves to a Sunday morning.

Four of the eight play-in teams go through to Tuesday's quarterfinals, and four go home. By Sunday evening, the tension will be obvious in the way teams play the final quarter.

Australia know the feeling of near misses. They reached the 2026 World Cup semifinal, lost 1-0 to Argentina, then lost the bronze match 1-0 to Belgium. India's Navneet Kaur scored twice in a 3-1 win over Germany at that World Cup to deliver fifth place.

That's the kind of finisher you want to see when the clock is running down.

Belgium clinched the 2026 Pro League in June, then finished seventh at the World Cup that summer. That's the lesson of knockout hockey: one off quarter and the favorite goes home.

On this Monday morning, the men's bracket starts to thin. Pool winners join four play-in survivors, and the rankings, with Germany, Belgium and Australia at the top after the World Cup, count for very little. Germany bring the 2026 world title and a 1-0 win over Spain in the final.

Be in your seat early: the two matches run through the morning in the open air.

Spain beat the Netherlands 4-3 in the 2026 World Cup semifinal, in the Dutch home stadium, then lost 1-0 to Germany in the final. The Dutch were left with a bronze-medal defeat to Argentina.

Now the Dutch are back to defend the Games title they won on a shoot-out in Paris, where they drew 1-1 with Germany and won 3-1 from the spot. This Monday evening quarterfinal session is where any of the big names could be ambushed.

India's captain Harmanpreet Singh scored twice in the Asian Games final, and a drag-flick from him can swing a match in an instant.

Argentina's women beat the Netherlands in a shoot-out in Amstelveen to win the 2026 World Cup. It was the Dutch side's first World Cup defeat since 2010, and the rematch could be waiting right here.

The quarterfinal draw blends pool winners with the four play-in survivors, so the field is part heavyweight, part survivor. The Netherlands remain No. 1 in the FIH rankings with 4083 points, with Belgium third.

The morning session means two knockout matches in daytime open-air conditions, at a venue that was built for training and has been converted into a hockey stadium.

China led the Paris 2024 final for most of the match, and lost it only in the shoot-out to the Netherlands. For China, the 2026 Asian Games final felt like the opposite: Savita Punia saved a penalty stroke from Zhang Ying, India won 1-0, and China missed the direct route to 2028.

If China make it back through qualifying, a quarterfinal here would be a measure of how far their progress goes.

The evening session also has Argentina, Belgium and the Netherlands within reach, and Belgium's first World Cup medal since 1978 will have them hungry for more.

HOC27.blurb:
One goal. Michel Struthoff scored late in the third quarter of the 2026 World Cup final, and that was enough for Germany, even as Spain had more of the ball and more penalty corners.

That's the German blueprint: absorb pressure, take the moment. They've won four men's World Cups, the most of any nation, and beat the Netherlands in a shoot-out in the 2025 EuroHockey final.

On a Wednesday morning, at the first of two men's semifinals, someone will try to knock them off. Matches at this stage are often decided by a single moment.

Belgium locked up the 2026 Pro League on June 27, beating the Netherlands 2-1 with a match to spare, and goalkeeper Vincent Vanasch took player of the match. Two months later, they were seventh at the World Cup.

Which Belgium turns up here, if they reach the last four, is the question. At full tilt they have Hendrickx and Boon in front of one of the best goalkeepers in the game.

This is the second men's semifinal, the 8:00 PM start under a Los Angeles evening sky, with a gold medal match at stake.

HOC29.blurb:
Yibbi Jansen scored in the 2026 World Cup final, and it wasn't enough. María José Granatto cancelled it out for 1-1, and Argentina took the shoot-out 3-1. The Dutch have won the World Cup nine times, a record, and rarely lose a final.

The Netherlands are also reigning champions, and Jansen was the top scorer and best player at the 2025 EuroHockey Championship, which the Dutch won. Frédérique Matla scored the only goal in their 2026 semifinal against Belgium.

A semifinal this tight on a Thursday morning can come down to a single penalty corner.

HOC30.blurb:
Belgium waited 48 years for a World Cup medal. Charlotte Englebert's goal against Australia in the 2026 bronze match ended it, and made them third in the world.

A semifinal berth in 2028 would take them a step beyond that, to a medal match at the Games. Standing in the way might be Argentina, World Cup winners, or the Netherlands, still No. 1 in the rankings.

India's women, ranked eighth after the 2026 World Cup, could be a wildcard here. Savita Punia's penalty save against China is the kind of play that changes a tournament.

HOC31.blurb:
Bronze medal matches in hockey rarely play like consolation prizes. This is the match where a team's tournament either gets a medal or a long flight home, and the stakes show in every tackle in the circle.

India is the story to watch if they get here. They took bronze in Paris 2024 and have since won back-to-back Asian Games titles, but they finished eighth at the 2026 World Cup and sit eighth in the rankings, so another podium would take real work. Spain, Argentina and Belgium are the kind of sides who can make it a proper scrap.

Get there for the morning start at Carson Field. It's a temporary stadium with around 15,000 seats, and the noise from a loyal section of fans can fill a pitch this size. Penalty corners are the moments to watch for.

HOC32.blurb:
Germany and the Netherlands played Paris 2024 to a 1-1 draw and the Dutch won the shoot-out 3-1. It was a gold medal decided from the penalty spot, and the rematch is the one people will want.

The field has moved on since. Germany won the 2025 EuroHockey title and the 2026 World Cup, beating Spain 1-0 with Michel Struthoff's late third-quarter goal. They are the top-ranked side, ahead of Belgium. The Dutch finished fourth at that World Cup, so they arrive as defending champions with something to prove.

This is the late-night match at Carson Field, 9 PM under the lights, with the temporary stands full. Hockey at this level is fast, tactical and tense, with 1-0 finals common. Keep an eye on the goalkeepers, and expect any shoot-out to be unbearable.
HOC32.potentialContendersIntro: No team has qualified for this match yet, so these projected finalists are speculation based on 2026 form and rankings.

potentialContenders.name: Germany
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalists and the 2026 World Cup winners, the nation's fourth men's World Cup title. Top of the FIH rankings and the likely favorites.

potentialContenders.name: Netherlands
potentialContenders.note: Defending champions who won Paris 2024 gold in a shoot-out. They finished fourth at the 2026 World Cup, so 2028 could be about proving they are still the best.

potentialContenders.name: Belgium
potentialContenders.note: Qualified by winning the 2025-26 Pro League, beating the Netherlands 2-1 in the process. Second in the rankings, they are a contender for gold.

potentialContenders.name: Spain
potentialContenders.note: Reached the 2026 World Cup final and lost 1-0 to Germany after pulling the goalkeeper late. Could be a threat in the knockout rounds.

HOC33.blurb:
Belgium went more than four decades without a World Cup medal in women's hockey. In 2026 Charlotte Englebert's goal against Australia ended that wait, and a bronze medal match in Carson would be another chance for the Red Panthers to prove they belong on the podium.

The opponents are not easy to pick out. Australia lost both of their last matches at the 2026 World Cup by a single goal. Argentina and India, both of whom beat strong sides in 2026, could also end up here. Indeed, Argentina won bronze in Paris 2024 on a shoot-out.

It's a 10:30 AM start, which means a quieter crowd than the evening final but also a closer look at the details. Watch the penalty corner routines closely. In a one-goal match, they often decide everything.
HOC33.potentialContendersIntro: The field for this match is not set, so the following are projected based on 2026 form and are speculative.

potentialContenders.name: Belgium
potentialContenders.note: Won bronze at the 2026 World Cup with a 1-0 win over Australia, their first World Cup medal since 1978. Third in the FIH rankings and the Pro League table.

potentialContenders.name: Australia
potentialContenders.note: Finished fourth at the 2026 World Cup after consecutive 1-0 losses. A strong team that could return to the medal rounds.

potentialContenders.name: India
potentialContenders.note: Fifth at the 2026 World Cup after beating Germany 3-1, and qualified as Asian Games champions. Could be a surprise contender for a medal.

potentialContenders.name: Argentina
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalists, who drew 2-2 with Belgium and won the shoot-out 3-1. Likely to be a title contender, but could end up here after a semifinal loss.

HOC34.blurb:
Argentina beat the Netherlands in a shoot-out at the 2026 World Cup in Amstelveen, the Dutch team's first World Cup defeat since 2010. Yibbi Jansen scored for the Netherlands, María José Granatto equalised for Argentina, and the Dutch run of world titles ended at three. If the same teams meet again in Carson, they will have a reason to care.

The Dutch have won a record five women's gold medals, including Paris 2024 against China. They qualified for 2028 by winning the Pro League for the sixth time and are still ranked No.1, but Argentina finished as runners-up in that competition too.

This is the Saturday-night final, 9 PM start at Carson Field. A temporary stadium of around 15,000 should be loud. Hockey finals are often tight, and shoot-outs are not rare.
HOC34.potentialContendersIntro: No team has yet reached this match, so the contenders below are projections based on 2026 form and rankings, and the players are speculative.

potentialContenders.name: Netherlands
potentialContenders.note: Defending champions with a record five women's golds, Pro League winners and No.1 in the rankings. Yibbi Jansen scored in the 2026 World Cup final, and the Dutch will want revenge.

potentialContenders.name: Argentina
potentialContenders.note: 2026 World Cup winners, their third world title and first since 2010, and Pro League runners-up. Granatto scored the equaliser in the final, and they are a likely finalist.

potentialContenders.name: Belgium
potentialContenders.note: Won bronze at the 2026 World Cup and ranked third in the world. Could challenge for gold if they get past the favorites.

potentialContenders.name: China
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalists who led most of the final. Not yet qualified for 2028 after losing the 2026 Asian Games final to India, so a return to the final is a long shot.

JUD01.blurb:
The first mat bouts of the 2028 Games happen before lunch, and the draw is the drama. A top-ranked name can meet a dangerous unseeded rival in the opening hour, and one of them is out.

Women's -48kg is the lightest class, all speed and scrambles. Japan's Wakana Koga won the 2026 world title in Baku, and Italy's Assunta Scutto has reached three straight world finals. Men's -60kg has crowned a different world champion every year since 2024.

The temporary stands at Hall 2 put you close to the mats. Pick a bout, watch the grips fight for ten seconds before anyone throws, and see the favorites work through the field before evening pressure sets in.
JUD01.potentialContendersIntro: Projected names for women's -48kg and men's -60kg, based on recent world results. None is confirmed for 2028.

potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 women's -48kg champion. If she makes the Japanese team, she starts as the defending title holder.

potentialContenders.name: Wakana Koga
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 world title in Baku over Scutto. Japanese selection could pit her against Tsunoda.

potentialContenders.name: Assunta Scutto
potentialContenders.note: World champion in 2025 and runner-up in 2024 and 2026. Her three straight finals make her a likely contender.

potentialContenders.name: Ahmad Yusifov
potentialContenders.note: 2026 world -60kg champion on home soil in Baku, after coming from behind to beat Sherzod Davlatov.

potentialContenders.name: Ryuju Nagayama
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world -60kg champion and a 2026 bronze medalist. Could be Japan's man at the weight.

JUD02.blurb:
Somebody leaves Hall 2 tonight as the first judo medalist of the 2028 Games. That ippon will be replayed all week.

Scutto is the story to follow in women's -48kg. She took world silver in 2024, gold in 2025 and silver in 2026, and a Games gold is the one thing missing. Japan's Natsumi Tsunoda arrives as Paris champion, and Wakana Koga is the new world champion, so Japan's selection is a storyline of its own.

In men's -60kg, Azerbaijan's Ahmad Yusifov won last year's Worlds after coming from behind. In a class with a new world champion every year, expect scrambling, golden score and a loud late-afternoon crowd.
JUD02.potentialContendersIntro: Medal contenders for women's -48kg and men's -60kg. Entries are projections based on 2024 to 2026 form.

potentialContenders.name: Assunta Scutto
potentialContenders.note: Three straight world finals at -48kg (silver 2024, gold 2025, silver 2026). Likely contender if she qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Wakana Koga

potentialContenders.name: Ahmad Yusifov

potentialContenders.name: Giorgi Sardalashvili

JUD03.blurb:
In Paris, Uta Abe lost her opening bout to Diyora Keldiyorova, who then won Uzbekistan's first women's judo gold at -52kg. That result is the thread running through Sunday morning.

Keldiyorova spent more than two years away after becoming a mother, then won the Asian Open in Aktau in October 2026. Abe has won six world titles since.

The men's -66kg draw has its own tension. Hifumi Abe, Takeshi Takeoka and Ryoma Tanaka have each won a world title since 2024, so Japan may have its hardest selection call here. In the early rounds, stars can still fall to an upset.
JUD03.potentialContendersIntro: Names to watch in men's -66kg and women's -52kg. 2028 spots are unconfirmed, so these are projections.

potentialContenders.name: Hifumi Abe
potentialContenders.note: Gold in Tokyo and Paris 2024, plus a fifth world title in Baku in 2026. Could go for a third straight Games title if selected.

potentialContenders.name: Takeshi Takeoka
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world champion and world No. 1 entering Baku in 2026. Took bronze, and could challenge for the Japanese spot.

potentialContenders.name: Uta Abe
potentialContenders.note: Won her sixth world -52kg title in 2026. A possible first-round name for opponents dreading the draw.

potentialContenders.name: Diyora Keldiyorova
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 champion. Won the Asian Open in October 2026 after returning from motherhood, if she qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: David Garcia Torne
potentialContenders.note: 2026 world -66kg silver medalist, a likely contender.

JUD04.blurb:
Siblings on one card. Hifumi and Uta Abe both won world titles in Baku in 2026, and if both make Japan's team they would fight on this evening, a rare double.

Hifumi has won gold in Tokyo and Paris, then took a fifth world title in 2026 with an ippon over Spain's David Garcia Torne. He says he is looking toward another Games. Uta's challenge could come from Keldiyorova, who beat her in her opening Paris bout and has since returned from motherhood.

With repechage, semifinals and finals packed into three hours, the late-afternoon Hall 2 crowd gets a medal rhythm that never lets up.
JUD04.potentialContendersIntro: Contenders for men's -66kg and women's -52kg. Nobody is confirmed for 2028, so treat these as projections.

potentialContenders.name: Hifumi Abe
potentialContenders.note: Two-time Games champion who won the 2026 world title by ippon. Could chase a third straight gold if selected.

potentialContenders.name: Uta Abe
potentialContenders.note: Six-time world champion at -52kg, including 2026. Her only high-profile loss in Paris came in the opening round.

potentialContenders.name: Diyora Keldiyorova

potentialContenders.name: David Garcia Torne

potentialContenders.name: Odette Giuffrida
potentialContenders.note: 2024 world champion and a 2026 world bronze medalist at -52kg. Could be a medal threat.

JUD05.blurb:
Fifty entries in men's -73kg at the 2026 Worlds, one of the largest fields in Baku. That is a lot of upset potential for a Monday morning.

The champion there was Japan's Ryuga Tanaka, a 22-year-old former junior world champion, who won in golden score. France's Joan-Benjamin Gaba, the 2025 world champion, lost his first bout in Baku, so reputations only go so far. Hidayat Heydarov, Paris gold medalist, adds a bigger name.

Women's -57kg is just as loose. Canada's Christa Deguchi won Paris gold, and Japan's Akari Omori took the 2026 world title. Sit close and look for the early round shocks.

potentialContenders.name: Akari Omori

potentialContenders.name: Hidayat Heydarov

potentialContenders.name: Ryuga Tanaka

potentialContenders.name: Joan-Benjamin Gaba
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world champion who lost his first bout in Baku in 2026. A comeback storyline, if he qualifies.

JUD06.blurb:
Akari Omori finished the 2026 world final the hard way: golden score, a turnover, a hold-down. Eteri Liparteliani had won gold in 2025 and was one hold-down from another. That is the sort of finish tonight's fans will watch for in women's -57kg.

Christa Deguchi, Canada's Paris champion, adds an extra layer. A Canadian judo champion in a Los Angeles crowd, with both countries' fans nearby, could add some noise.

Men's -73kg is a lottery of champions: Heydarov in 2024, Gaba in 2025, Ryuga Tanaka in 2026. Three hours, four medal bouts and no obvious favorite.

JUD07.blurb:
Tato Grigalashvili has four world titles and a Paris silver. Takanori Nagase has two straight Games golds at -81kg. Tuesday's elimination rounds could see two of the weight's biggest names circling the same bracket.

There are 48 entries in each class, so this is a day for volume and discovery. Japan's Sanshiro Murao was the top seed in the -81kg field in Baku, and Timur Arbuzov was the 2025 world champion.

In women's -63kg, Japan's Haruka Kaju has dominated, defending her world title in 2026 over Israel's Kerem Primo. Arrive early, because the early rounds are where reputations get tested.

JUD08.blurb:
Haruka Kaju has won nine straight international tournaments since December 2024. In women's -63kg she walks in as world No. 1, and the pressure is entirely on whoever draws her.

The men's -81kg could bring a rematch of the Paris final, where Takanori Nagase beat Tato Grigalashvili. Grigalashvili then lost the 2025 world final to Timur Arbuzov and won his fourth title in 2026, in a long golden-score battle with Zelim Tckaev.

Tuesday evening has revenge, streaks and one-point margins. Hall 2's compact stands are close enough to hear every grip break.

JUD09.blurb:
Lasha Bekauri won Paris gold at -90kg. Two years later in Baku he was unseeded and drew Sanshiro Murao in the round of 16, and Murao beat him. Imagine that bracket landing on a Wednesday morning in LA.

The field of 49 men's -90kg entries means you will see other contenders go out early as well. Women's -70kg adds another unpredictable field. Croatia's Barbara Matic won Paris, Japan's Shiho Tanaka won 2025 Worlds and lost in round three in Baku, and Spain's Ai Tsunoda Roustant took the 2026 title.

These are the rounds where a heavyweight name can fall, and where you spot the next one.

Bekauri against Murao, round three. In Paris, Bekauri beat Murao in the final. In Baku, Murao beat him in the round of 16. If both reach the 2028 final, it will be the rubber match nobody has to invent a storyline for.

There is a wrinkle: Japan's Goki Tajima has reached three straight world finals at -90kg, so Japanese selection is no formality.

Women's -70kg has produced a different world champion in each of the last three years, so the other half of the night is unpredictable. Wednesday evening is the one session that could deliver both a rematch and a surprise.

potentialContenders.name: Ai Tsunoda Roustant

JUD11.blurb:
Men's -100kg is the biggest field in judo. Fifty-six competitors showed up in Baku in 2026, and the 2028 bracket will likely be as crowded. Expect a long morning of bouts you did not see coming.

Paris gold medalist Zelym Kotsoiev of Azerbaijan is the name on the posters. Georgia's Ilia Sulamanidze, the Paris silver medalist, is the listed 2026 world champion. The 2025 champion, Matvey Kanikovskiy, missed Baku while an anti-doping case is ongoing.

Women's -78kg has its own mystery. Alice Bellandi, Paris and 2025 world champion, missed 2026 with a shoulder injury while the UAE's Lytvynenko took the world title.

JUD12.blurb:
Alice Bellandi has Paris gold and the 2025 world title, but she missed the 2026 Worlds with a shoulder injury. Her health will be the question when women's -78kg finals begin Thursday evening.

She may face the UAE's Lytvynenko, who won the world final by scoring two waza-ari within three minutes, and Germany's Anna Monta Olek, who has taken silver and bronze at the last two Worlds.

The men's -100kg final could be just as tense. Kotsoiev's Paris gold and Sulamanidze's Paris silver both belong to a division with a new world champion and a missing 2025 winner. Three hours, four medals, one very busy Hall 2.

JUD13.blurb:
Is Teddy Riner coming back? He won his third individual heavyweight gold in Paris and has said he is aiming for another title, but his 2028 entry is not confirmed. If he appears, a Friday-morning elimination bout will have every phone in the stands out.

The field he would face is good. Inal Tasoev has three world +100kg titles, and Korea's Kim Min-jong beat Tasoev twice before the 2026 Worlds. Czech two-time Games champion Lukas Krpalek won a sixth world medal in Baku.

Women's +78kg brings Brazil's Paris gold medalist Beatriz Souza and 19-year-old Lee Hyeon-ji, who scored ippon in every contest on her way to the 2026 world title.

The heaviest classes close the individual program, and it takes a certain kind of crowd to love them. Tonight that crowd gets ippons that shake the mat.

Teddy Riner owns three individual heavyweight golds. He says he is aiming for another, but his 2028 participation is unconfirmed. If he is not there, Inal Tasoev may be the man to beat, after throwing home favorite Ushangi Kokauri for ippon in the 2026 world final. Kokauri, 34, has two world silvers, 2018 and 2026.

Women's +78kg has gone to Korea at the last two Worlds, with Kim Ha-yun in 2025 and Lee Hyeon-ji in 2026. Brazil's Beatriz Souza owns the Paris gold.
JUD14.potentialContendersIntro: Projected contenders for women's +78kg and men's +100kg. Riner is not confirmed for 2028.

JUD15.blurb:
France has won the mixed team title at every Games it has been contested, and both finals came against Japan. The question for the final morning is whether anyone can break that run, and who makes the cut for the final.

The field is deeper than that record suggests. Georgia won the 2025 world title, the first nation other than Japan to do so. In 2026 Uzbekistan beat the defending champions and took bronze, and Japan beat Russia 4-1 in the final.

Teams fight across six weight categories, with women's and men's bouts alternating. Elimination rounds, repechage and semifinals fill an eight o'clock start in Hall 2.

JUD16.blurb:
One bout can decide everything. In Paris, it was Teddy Riner against Tatsuru Saito with France trailing Japan, and Riner won it to give France a second straight mixed team title. Both times the victim was Japan.

This is the last session of the 2028 judo program, and the format keeps it tense. Teammates crowd the edge of the mat, momentum swings from one bout to the next, and a lead can disappear in a single throw.

The stands are temporary and built close around the mats, inside a downtown convention hall. When a team needs one more win, the noise has nowhere to go.

LAC01.blurb:
The first lacrosse game at a Summer Games in 120 years kicks off at midday in Exposition Park, and the sport has changed shape since 1908. Six players a side, a smaller field, shorter games. Nobody gets to breathe.

Sixes moves end to end and piles up goals, and a three-goal lead can vanish in a couple of possessions. The United States is in as host, fresh off a 12-11 win over Canada in the 2026 Pan-American final that was decided in the last minute.

The stands here are steep and close to the field, so you will hear the ball hit sticks. Opening day of a sport this old and this new is a story you can say you saw.
LAC01.potentialContendersIntro: Only the United States is locked in as host; every other men's team is still to be decided, so these are projections based on current rankings and 2026 continental results.

LAC02.blurb:
Sixteen straight wins. That is the length of the U.S. women's sixes streak as of October 2026, and the 2028 tournament opens with the whole world trying to end it.

This is the first time women's lacrosse is played for medals at a Summer Games, and the opening-night session lands in the evening, when the stadium shifts from daytime sun to something louder and warmer. The favorite is clear. The nerves are not: Canada took the 2022 World Games final and the U.S. needed a Emma LoPinto goal with 38 seconds left to win the 2026 Pan-American final 15-14.

Come for a debut, stay to see whether the champions look as untouchable as the streak suggests.
LAC02.potentialContendersIntro: The United States is the only confirmed team as host. The rest of the field is unknown, so these are likely contenders based on 2025 and 2026 results.

LAC03.blurb:
Everyone in this session got here by a long road. Continental championships, a 16-team world event in Colorado Springs, then a last qualifying tournament in early 2028 for the stragglers. By Tuesday, the men's field is a mix of favorites and teams who fought for a seat.

That makes day two interesting. The opening-day nerves are gone, the underdogs have a game of film on everyone, and the bracket pressure starts to build in a six-team round robin where every result counts.

Watch Canada, the top-ranked men's sixes team and a double gold winner at the 2025 Super Sixes in Oshawa, to see if it plays like a team that knows what it is.
LAC03.potentialContendersIntro: Outside of the host United States, the men's field is not yet set, so these are projected contenders based on rankings and 2026 results.

LAC04.blurb:
The scores tell the story of what the field is up against: 25-13 over Australia, 32-8 over Czechia, 24-10 over Japan. The U.S. women went unbeaten at the 2025 World Games, and nobody has really stopped them since.

So the question on Tuesday night is simple: who can make it uncomfortable? Maybe it is Canada, a one-goal loss away from the title in 2026. Maybe it is a European side like Great Britain or Israel, or a team nobody has noticed yet.

The evening session has a different feel from the afternoon. The crowd is looser, louder, and quicker to roar at a goalkeeper's save or a long run down the field.
LAC04.potentialContendersIntro: Only the United States is confirmed as host. These other teams are projected contenders based on 2025 and 2026 results, if they qualify.

LAC05.blurb:
Lacrosse began as a Native American game, and the Haudenosaunee men are the sport's living link to that. Whether they will be in Exposition Park Stadium is the biggest open question in the tournament.

The U.S. and Canadian governments asked the IOC in January 2025 to let them compete. The IOC said in February 2025 that the Haudenosaunee would not play as their own team without a recognized national committee. As of November 2026, they are still optimistic but have no decision date.

If they play, this session could carry more weight than any other in the round robin. If they don't, it will still feel like a story unfinished.

LAC06.blurb:
Goalkeepers decide sixes games, and this session could show it. Japan's Mao Kawamura made nine saves in the 2026 Asia-Pacific final, and her team beat Australia 9-8. In a game this fast, one stopped shot can swing a whole night.

Midweek is when a round robin starts to separate the contenders from the teams hoping for a miracle. Margins here tend to be tiny: Israel beat Czechia 15-14 on a goal with 40 seconds left in a 2026 European semifinal, and the U.S. needed a 38-second winner against Canada.

Bring your attention span. At an evening game in this tight stadium, the final minute is often the best part.

LAC07.blurb:
Australia and Japan played the 2026 Asia-Pacific final to a one-goal margin, and that is how most of this session could go: tight, fast and quickly decided.

Thursday is the point of the round robin where qualifiers start to feel real. Great Britain, ranked No. 4 in men's sixes, is the kind of team that can unsettle a favorite, and Australia, ranked No. 6, won its Asia-Pacific title after a 26-6 win over New Zealand early on.

The afternoon crowd arrives in sun and caps. With the stands this close to the pitch, you will be able to hear every shout from the bench.

LAC08.blurb:
Nobody has ever won a women's lacrosse medal at a Summer Games, which makes this evening a first draft of history. By Thursday, the round robin is deep enough to show which teams are really in the hunt.

The women's depth chart is wider than the headlines suggest. Australia beat Japan 13-12 in overtime for 2025 World Games bronze, and Japan came back to beat the Aussies in the 2026 Asia-Pacific final. Europe sent five teams to the 2027 worlds, and Israel and Great Britain are climbing.

Sixes was invented for this stage. Settle in, watch the pace, and enjoy being early to the story.

LAC09.blurb:
By Friday afternoon, the men's table has teeth. This is the last day of the round robin, and the standings decide who plays for medals on Saturday.

If the top two seeds are in the mix, the stakes will be obvious. Canada and the U.S. have traded results in recent years: Canada won the 2022 World Games sixes final, the U.S. won the 2023 world field championship, and then the U.S. won twice in the final minute in Oshawa in 2026.

Someone will have to win, and someone will go home. In a stadium holding about 22,000, that tension is easy to feel.

LAC10.blurb:
Friday night is when the round robin stops being a warm-up. Medal spots are on the line, and a single loss can turn a comfortable table into a scramble.

The U.S. women will arrive carrying a long winning streak, which was 16 straight sixes games as of October 2026. Canada has proven it can hurt them, and the rest of the field has had a week to study how.

Expect one tight finish. Sixes produces them. You will be seated in an evening crowd that knows what is at stake, with the medal games one night away.

LAC11.blurb:
One match could settle the best rivalry in the men's game. Canada beat the U.S. in the 2022 World Games sixes final. The U.S. won the 2023 world field title, then beat Canada 12-11 in Oshawa in 2026 on a final-minute goal.

Now imagine that with a medal on the line and about 22,000 people packed into a steep soccer stadium next to the Coliseum. The bronze game comes first, a warm-up with its own pride at stake, and then the gold game closes the tournament.

If the Haudenosaunee get cleared to play, the story gets bigger. Either way, you will remember who held the stick at the end.

LAC12.blurb:
The first women's lacrosse medals at a Summer Games will be handed out late Saturday night, and the story could write itself. The U.S. beat Canada 16-8 for 2025 World Games gold after losing 14-12 to them in 2022. In 2026, the Americans won 15-14 when Emma LoPinto scored with 38 seconds left.

The bronze game opens the night, and the gold game closes the whole tournament.

By now the stadium is full, loud and ready, with the roar of the supporters' terrace behind one goal. Whoever wins, they will be the first name on a list that never existed before.

MPN01.blurb:
Whether Michelle Gulyás, the Paris 2024 champion with a world-record 1,461, lines up here is an open question. She missed the 2025 and 2026 World Championships with injury, and the women's field has been reshuffled without her.

Blanka Guzi is the reigning world champion, and Egypt's Farida Khalil took 2026 world silver at 15. A semifinal is the first look at that rivalry: head-to-head fencing, a 70m, eight-obstacle sprint that replaced riding, then the swim and the laser run.

The sport opens its four days at 9 AM in a San Fernando Valley park. Watch who survives the cut.

MPN02.blurb:
Two points. That separated Czechia's Matej Lukes and Egypt's Mohamed El-Ashqar in a 2026 world semifinal, 1,557 to 1,555, and the men's field is tight everywhere you look.

El-Ashqar also posted the fastest obstacle time of that day, 18.39 seconds, which shows how much the new 70m, eight-obstacle sprint rewards raw speed. Egypt is deep, with Paris 2024 champion Ahmed El-Gendy and 2025 world champion Moutaz Mohamed both possible entries.

Fencing bouts, a swim and a laser run, all before lunch in a Sepulveda Basin park. Only those who advance get to race again on Tuesday.

MPN03.blurb:
Halfway through the 2026 world final, Blanka Guzi was behind. Egypt's Farida Khalil, then 15, led. Guzi caught her late in the laser run and took the title with 1,485 points.

That is the template for this final: 18 athletes, two hours, and a laser run where the first person across the line wins. There is no calculator and no waiting for judges. The gap on the screen is the gap on the course, and shooting nerves can scramble it.

Guzi, Khalil, Britain's Kerenza Bryson and, if healthy, Paris champion Michelle Gulyás could all be in the hunt on a Monday morning.

MPN04.blurb:
Matej Lukes ran the fastest laser run of the 2026 world final, 10:24.81, and turned a deficit into gold with 1,586 points. Egor Gromadskii finished five seconds behind him.

Moutaz Mohamed shows the other side of the format. He placed last in fencing in that final and still ran his way to fourth. In a sport where the first one across the line wins, no deficit feels safe.

Tuesday morning closes the sport's four days at Valley Complex 2, with Ahmed El-Gendy's Paris 2024 world record of 1,555 as the mark to chase.

MTB01.blurb:
Tom Pidcock punctured in Paris, lost about 40 seconds, and still won. He finished with a final-lap pass on Victor Koretzky that drew boos from the home crowd. If he lines up in 2028 chasing a third straight gold, expect the same trick: fall behind, then make everyone pay.

A one-day final with no heats leaves nothing banked. At the 2026 worlds Pidcock started on the fifth row and needed four of eight laps to reach the lead. Alan Hatherly punctured and finished 27th.

The Industry Hills course is brand new, hillside terrain with drops and jumps. The loop lets you move between viewing areas as riders pass again and again. Pick a technical spot and wait.
MTB01.potentialContendersIntro: Pidcock won Paris 2024 and the 2026 world title, but he said he will step away from mountain biking in 2027 for road racing, so his 2028 start is a hope rather than a certainty. The rest of this list is projection based on recent form.

potentialContenders.name: Tom Pidcock
potentialContenders.note: Gold at Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024, and 2026 world champion after rallying from the fifth row. He has said he hopes to race for a third straight gold, if the road schedule allows.

potentialContenders.name: Luca Martin
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 World Cup overall in both cross-country and short track, and a likely contender for 2028. He moves to Decathlon Ford Racing Team in 2027.

potentialContenders.name: Alan Hatherly
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalist and world champion in 2024 and 2025. A puncture dropped him to 27th at the 2026 worlds, which shows how fragile this race is.

potentialContenders.name: Charlie Aldridge
potentialContenders.note: Second to Pidcock at the 2026 worlds and winner of the Lake Placid World Cup finale in a sprint. A rising threat, and a possible British teammate or rival for Pidcock.

potentialContenders.name: Christopher Blevins
