potentialContenders.note: Massimo Fabbrizi and Alessia Iezzi won the 2025 world title after topping qualification with 145. Italy also won mixed skeet at Paris 2024 with a different pairing.

potentialContenders.name: San Marino
potentialContenders.note: Gian Marco Berti and Alessandra Perilli took 2025 world silver after a four-way shoot-off. A strong pairing if they qualify.

potentialContenders.name: USA
potentialContenders.note: Walton Eller and Ava Downs won 2025 world bronze, with Downs medaling at 20. The U.S. also took silver in mixed skeet at Paris 2024, and a home crowd could make them a threat.

potentialContenders.name: Egypt
potentialContenders.note: Ahmed Zahar and Maggy Ashmawy lost the 2025 bronze match to the U.S. A possible dark horse if they qualify.

SKB01.blurb:
Twenty-two skaters, one final, and no safety net. Rayssa Leal, the Paris 2024 bronze medalist, finished seventh at the 2026 world championships after missing all three best-trick attempts, and she reportedly called that event a testing ground for 2028. This is where she could start answering.

The Japanese depth is the other story. Ibuki Matsumoto won her first tour title at 13, and Yumeka Oda is the reigning world champion.

Settle in at Valley Complex 1 in the late afternoon, with open sky over the Sepulveda Basin and a freeway hum in the distance. You see the stars up close before the pressure peaks.
SKB01.potentialContendersIntro: Japan has won both 2026 world titles in this event, but Paris 2024 bronze medalist Rayssa Leal and Australia's Chloe Covell give the field real range. Who qualifies for 2028 is still to be decided.

potentialContenders.name: Yumeka Oda
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 world title in Asuncion, her second after Tokyo 2023, following runner-up finishes at Kitakyushu 2025 and Rome 2026.

potentialContenders.name: Ibuki Matsumoto
potentialContenders.note: Won the March 2026 world title in Sao Paulo and took her first tour title at 13; a likely contender if she makes the team.

potentialContenders.name: Rayssa Leal
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalist and four-time SLS Super Crown champion who had a rough Asuncion final. Her bounce-back is a storyline to watch.

potentialContenders.name: Chloe Covell
potentialContenders.note: Won the Rome World Cup in 2025 and 2026, scoring 177.01 in the 2026 final. A projected medal threat.

potentialContenders.name: Coco Yoshizawa
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalist who was still scoring in the Asuncion final. She could be a title defender in 2028.

SKB02.blurb:
Nyjah Huston fractured his skull and eye socket in a crash in January 2026, and he says he is still aiming for 2028, when he will be 33. If he makes the team, a morning prelim could be the first real test of that comeback.

Around him, street skating has gotten young and fast. Ginwoo Onodera won the 2025 SLS Super Crown at 15, then clinched the 2026 world title on his final attempt. Sora Shirai has won Rome two years running. Two-time champion Yuto Horigome went out in the quarterfinals at the last worlds.

Expect sunshine, an open-air course and 22 skaters you can watch up close.
SKB02.potentialContendersIntro: These are projections for 2028 based on current form and rankings. Japan's teenagers lead the pack, while Paris 2024 gold medalist Yuto Horigome and bronze medalist Nyjah Huston are the veterans trying to hold them off.

potentialContenders.name: Ginwoo Onodera
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 world title in Asuncion with his final attempt and the 2025 SLS Super Crown at 15. A likely favorite.

potentialContenders.name: Sora Shirai
potentialContenders.note: Won the Rome World Cup in 2025 and 2026 and finished ahead of or near the top in several major events. A consistent contender.

potentialContenders.name: Toa Sasaki
potentialContenders.note: Won the March 2026 world title in Sao Paulo with 174.10 and was on the Rome 2026 podium.

potentialContenders.name: Yuto Horigome
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalist and two-time champion who exited in the quarterfinals at the 2026 Sao Paulo worlds. Could still bounce back.

potentialContenders.name: Nyjah Huston
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalist recovering from a serious January 2026 skull fracture. He has said he is aiming for 2028.

SKB03.blurb:
Street finals tend to be settled on the last trick. Ibuki Matsumoto beat Yumeka Oda by 0.22 at Kitakyushu in 2025 with her final trick, and Rayssa Leal edged Momiji Nishiya by 0.02 in Rio in 2026. That's the margin you may be watching for.

Japan owns the recent form: two different women won 2026 world titles, and Coco Yoshizawa and Liz Akama went gold and silver in Paris 2024. Chloe Covell of Australia won Rome by more than 20 points, and Leal has four SLS Super Crowns.

The 8:30 pm start in the Sepulveda Basin puts the final under the lights, with a short, high-pressure program ahead.
SKB03.potentialContendersIntro: Japan has the deepest recent record, but the 2028 field is not set. These are projected contenders based on current form and Paris 2024 results.

potentialContenders.name: Yumeka Oda
potentialContenders.note: Reigning world champion after winning in Asuncion in October 2026. She was runner-up at Kitakyushu 2025 and Rome 2026.

potentialContenders.name: Ibuki Matsumoto
potentialContenders.note: Won the March 2026 world title in Sao Paulo and a 2025 tour event on her last trick; a likely threat if she makes the team.

potentialContenders.name: Coco Yoshizawa
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalist who won bronze in Sao Paulo and posted a 75-point run in Asuncion. A defending champion to watch.

potentialContenders.name: Rayssa Leal
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalist who won SLS Sydney and SLS Rio in 2026. She could rebound from her seventh in Asuncion.

potentialContenders.name: Chloe Covell
potentialContenders.note: Rome World Cup winner in 2025 and 2026, with a 177.01 in the 2026 final. A projected medal threat.

SKB04.blurb:
Last time, Yuto Horigome sat fourth with one trick left and won gold with a nollie 270 bluntslide. That is the standard for this format: the final trick can still flip the whole podium, so nobody is safe until the last board lands.

The favorites could well be Japanese. Japan swept the Rome 2026 podium, with Sora Shirai on top, and Sasaki Toa has twice been world champion. Horigome, who lives in California, would arrive as the defending champion and a skater who has done this before. The Americans, Jagger Eaton and Nyjah Huston, took silver and bronze in Paris.

The setting is a temporary park in the Sepulveda Basin, with an 8:30 pm start. The sun should be gone, the lights should be on, and the crowd will be roaring for every run.
SKB04.potentialContendersIntro: Paris 2024 gold went to Yuto Horigome, with Jagger Eaton and Nyjah Huston behind him. Japan dominated the 2026 season so far, though 2028 rosters are not set and all of these skaters still have to qualify.

potentialContenders.name: Yuto Horigome
potentialContenders.note: Won gold at Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024, the latter with a last-trick comeback from fourth. Based in California, and a likely contender if he qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Sora Shirai
potentialContenders.note: World No. 1 going into WST Rome in June 2026, where he won with 177.92. Projected to be a leading favorite if that form holds.

potentialContenders.name: Sasaki Toa
potentialContenders.note: Two-time defending world champion who missed Paris 2024. He has said he definitely wants to compete in 2028.

potentialContenders.name: Ginwoo Onodera
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 World Championships in Asuncion, his first WST event win. Worth watching as a rising threat.

potentialContenders.name: Nyjah Huston
potentialContenders.note: Bronze medalist in Paris 2024. Could appear as a home-crowd hope if he makes the US team.

SKB05.blurb:
Keegan Palmer owns two golds, yet at the 2026 worlds in Asuncion his 81.40 came in a pre-final round, and his name is absent from the final scores. Nobody gets to coast in this field.

Twenty-two skaters, no more than three per nation, start dropping in at 10:30 AM. Spain's Egoitz Bijueska arrives as reigning world champion. Japan's Issei Sakurai landed three runs over 90 in the Rome final.

This is an open-air temporary park inside the Sepulveda Basin, in morning light. It's the session where you see the whole field at once, including names you'll hear again on Wednesday night.
SKB05.potentialContendersIntro: Paris 2024 gold went to Keegan Palmer, but the 2026 form book belongs to a new wave. Who actually shows up in 2028 depends on the June 2028 World Skateboarding Ranking, so these are projections.

potentialContenders.name: Keegan Palmer
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalist and Tokyo 2020 champion. He moved to San Diego at 14, so this is close to a home event. He was only 81.40 in a pre-final round at Asuncion 2026, so expect him to want a statement run.

potentialContenders.name: Egoitz Bijueska
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 world title in Asuncion with 94.50 and the 2025 title in Sao Paulo. Likely a top seed if he qualifies, and he has called the Games his childhood dream.

potentialContenders.name: Tom Schaar
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalist and Asuncion 2026 silver medalist with 93.07. A projected contender who could draw a loud home crowd.

potentialContenders.name: Issei Sakurai
potentialContenders.note: Ranked 20th before the 2026 Rome World Cup, then landed three runs over 90 in the final. A likely sign of how deep this field has become.

potentialContenders.name: Gui Khury
potentialContenders.note: Bronze at the 2026 Asuncion worlds with 92.15. A projected contender if he qualifies.

SKB06.blurb:
Mizuho Hasegawa threw down a 96.33 in Rome, which World Skate called the highest women's park score in World Skateboarding Tour history. And Japan can send only three women. That cap makes the sport's deepest nation a fascinating puzzle to watch.

Under the night sky, 22 skaters take their runs and the field starts to separate. Sky Brown, a two-time Games bronze medalist, has finished second to Hasegawa on the biggest recent stages in Rome and Asuncion. Paris champion Arisa Trew, who won at X Games Sacramento 2026, is the wild card.

Come for the depth: you see the whole field in one sitting.
SKB06.potentialContendersIntro: Paris 2024 gold went to Australia's Arisa Trew, but Japan's Mizuho Hasegawa has led the 2026 form. Which three Japanese skaters get through qualification is still to be decided, so this list is a projection.

potentialContenders.name: Mizuho Hasegawa
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 world title in Asuncion and the 2026 Rome World Cup with a 96.33 run. A likely favorite if she makes Japan's team.

potentialContenders.name: Sky Brown
potentialContenders.note: Bronze at Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024, 2025 world champion, and runner-up in both Rome and Asuncion in 2026. She is working toward a third Games.

potentialContenders.name: Cocona Hiraki
potentialContenders.note: Silver medalist at Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024, still chasing a first gold. She took third at the 2026 Rome World Cup, four points behind Brown.

potentialContenders.name: Arisa Trew
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalist at 14, Australia's youngest-ever gold medalist, and X Games Sacramento 2026 winner. A projected contender if she qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Hikari Satake
potentialContenders.note: Posted the top score of 82.00 in an early round at Asuncion 2026. A possible depth name, and a reminder of how crowded Japan's list is.

SKB07.blurb:
Keegan Palmer has won every men's park gold ever awarded, and a third would make it three straight. The skater most likely to spoil that scored 95.83 at the 2025 worlds in Sao Paulo, exactly Palmer's winning score at Tokyo 2020.

That's Spain's Egoitz Bijueska, who was 15 when he took back-to-back world titles and calls the Games his childhood dream. Add Tom Schaar, Gui Khury and California's Gavin Bottger, and the Wednesday night final could be wild.

At Paris, only two of eight finalists landed their opening runs, and Palmer's 93.11 first run held up. One clean run could end the night.
SKB07.potentialContendersIntro: Palmer won Paris 2024 and has the titles, while Bijueska won the last two world championships. The final field depends on the June 2028 World Skateboarding Ranking, so these are projected contenders.

potentialContenders.name: Keegan Palmer
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 and Tokyo 2020 champion, going for a three-peat. His 2026 X Games results were silver, bronze and fourth, so he is strong but not untouchable.

potentialContenders.name: Egoitz Bijueska
potentialContenders.note: 2026 world champion with 94.50 and 2025 champion with 95.83. A likely favorite if he qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Tom Schaar
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalist. Silver at the 2026 Asuncion worlds with 93.07, after bronze at Sao Paulo.

potentialContenders.name: Gui Khury
potentialContenders.note: Bronze at Asuncion 2026 with 92.15, a projected final-round threat.

potentialContenders.name: Gavin Bottger
potentialContenders.note: 2023 world champion from Oceanside, California, and X Games park gold medalist in 2025 and 2026. He is a possible home favorite if he qualifies.

SKB08.blurb:
Eighty-seven hundredths of a point. That was the gap from gold to bronze in the Paris 2024 women's park final, and it is the best argument for a ticket to this one.

Three skaters from that podium could be back. Arisa Trew won at 14 and just took X Games Sacramento 2026. Cocona Hiraki has two Games silvers and no gold. Sky Brown has two bronzes, two world titles and a runner-up finish at the 2026 worlds.

Then there's Mizuho Hasegawa, who owns the 2026 world title and the tour's highest score. A Thursday-night final in the Valley could be settled by a single landed run.
SKB08.potentialContendersIntro: Paris 2024 gold went to Arisa Trew, but Mizuho Hasegawa took the 2026 world title. The final field will be set by the June 2028 ranking after the Qualification Series, so these are projected contenders.

potentialContenders.name: Mizuho Hasegawa
potentialContenders.note: 2026 world champion who scored 96.33 in Rome, the highest-ever women's park score on the tour. Silver at X Games Chiba and New Orleans in 2026.

potentialContenders.name: Sky Brown
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2023 and 2025 world titles and took bronze at Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024. Likely contender if she makes her third Games.

potentialContenders.name: Cocona Hiraki
potentialContenders.note: Silver at Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024, still seeking a first gold. A projected medal threat if selected.

potentialContenders.name: Arisa Trew
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalist with 93.18 and Australia's youngest-ever gold medalist. Won X Games Sacramento 2026.

SQU01.blurb:
Somebody has to hit the first ball. Tonight, on a working studio backlot in Universal City, squash plays its first match as a Summer Games sport, and the debut belongs to the Round of 16.

Temporary stands wrap the courts, the Back to the Future courthouse facade looms behind them, and the lights come up as the evening cools. Single elimination means every match is a cliff edge: lose once and the tournament is over.

Malaysia's Ng Eain Yow and Sivasangari Subramaniam already hold quota places as 2026 Asian Games champions. Top-ranked names could also open their campaigns tonight.
SQU01.potentialContendersIntro: Round of 16 pairings by night aren't set, so these are likely names rather than confirmed matchups, and only Malaysia's two champions are confirmed qualifiers so far.

potentialContenders.name: Ng Eain Yow
potentialContenders.note: Confirmed qualifier after winning his second straight Asian Games gold in September 2026, beating India's Abhay Singh 3-0 in the final.

potentialContenders.name: Sivasangari Subramaniam
potentialContenders.note: Confirmed qualifier as 2026 Asian Games champion, beating India's Anahat Singh in the final.

potentialContenders.name: Mostafa Asal
potentialContenders.note: Men's world No. 1 as of October 2026 and a two-time reigning world champion. Likely top seed if he qualifies, though his night in the Round of 16 is not set.

potentialContenders.name: Amina Orfi
potentialContenders.note: Became the youngest women's world No. 1 in September 2026, at 19. A likely top-of-the-draw presence if she qualifies.

SQU02.blurb:
Here is how a favorite gets knocked out in squash: an 18-year-old with nothing to lose. India's Anahat Singh beat eight-time world champion Nour El Sherbini 3-0 in October 2026, and a knockout draw is built for that kind of upset.

Night two of the Round of 16 carries that edge. Every loser goes home after one match, and universality places in the draw could also produce some lopsided early pairings, so watch the court for sharp shifts in momentum.

Sit close to the glass if you can. The rallies here are short on mercy and long on movement, and the open-air backlot setting makes the whole thing feel like a film premiere with a scoreboard.
SQU02.potentialContendersIntro: Who plays on this particular night isn't known, and Egypt can send only two players per gender, so these are projected names who could appear.

potentialContenders.name: Anahat Singh
potentialContenders.note: Ranked 15th at 18, she beat El Sherbini 3-0 at the 2026 Silicon Valley Open. A potential giant-killer if she qualifies, and she lost to Subramaniam in the Asian Games final.

potentialContenders.name: Nour El Sherbini
potentialContenders.note: Eight-time world champion and world No. 3 in October 2026. Could appear if she is one of Egypt's two women.

potentialContenders.name: Olivia Weaver
potentialContenders.note: World No. 4 in June 2026 and a likely American contender, though she withdrew from the 2025-26 Tour Finals injured, so her form and fitness are worth tracking.

potentialContenders.name: Youssef Ibrahim
potentialContenders.note: Men's world No. 7 in October 2026 and runner-up at the 2026 world championship. He could appear if he is one of Egypt's two men.

SQU03.blurb:
Brothers can end up in the same draw, and the ElShorbagys are the reason to think about it. Marwan and Mohamed, both representing England and ranked ninth and 10th in October 2026, could each take one of the two places England is allowed.

This is night three of four in the Round of 16, and by now the bracket's shape is clear. The last place in each draw will already have been settled in Seattle in June, on an all-glass court, so some players here will have arrived via a tournament that few fans watched.

Expect a mix of established stars and qualification-route stories, played under studio lights on a film set.
SQU03.potentialContendersIntro: Match assignments for this night aren't set. These are projected players, and qualification isn't confirmed for anyone other than the Asian Games winners.

potentialContenders.name: Marwan ElShorbagy
potentialContenders.note: Ranked ninth in the October 2026 PSA men's list and a likely contender if England's two places go to the brothers.

potentialContenders.name: Mohamed ElShorbagy
potentialContenders.note: Ranked 10th in October 2026. A possible bracket-mate for his brother's country quota, if both qualify.

potentialContenders.name: Juan Vargas
potentialContenders.note: Ranked 29th in October 2026, so the continental route could be his best path to the draw.

potentialContenders.name: Nele Gilis
potentialContenders.note: Ranked 13th among women in October 2026 and a potential dangerous early-round opponent if she qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Ng Eain Yow
potentialContenders.note: Confirmed qualifier as two-time Asian Games champion, ranked 17th in October 2026.

SQU04.blurb:
Ali Farag won't be here. The four-time world champion retired in May 2025, so the first Games draw belongs to the players who stepped into the space he left.

Tonight is the last Round of 16 session, and by 11:15 pm the quarterfinal lineups are set in both brackets. That makes every match a gate: lose and you're gone, win and you're eight players from the podium.

New Zealand's Paul Coll and Peru's Diego Elias, the 2026 US Open finalists, are the sort of names who could close out the night. The host quota also guarantees American players a place in the draws, which could add some home volume.
SQU04.potentialContendersIntro: These are projected players for the final Round of 16 night, not confirmed pairings, and 2028 qualification is still open for most of them.

potentialContenders.name: Paul Coll
potentialContenders.note: World No. 2 in October 2026 and winner of the 2026 British Open and US Open, beating Elias 3-1 in Philadelphia. A leading contender if he qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Diego Elias
potentialContenders.note: 2024 world champion, beating Asal in the final, and world No. 3 in October 2026. Likely to be in the field if he qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Hania El Hammamy
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world championship runner-up and 2026 US Open defending champion. Could appear if she is one of Egypt's two women.

SQU05.blurb:
Lose and you go home with nothing. Win and you are one match from a medal. That is the whole quarterfinal in a sentence, and it makes this the first night in which the stakes feel physically heavy.

Mostafa Asal arrives as back-to-back world champion, winning in Chicago in 2025 over Ali Farag and in Giza in 2026 over Youssef Ibrahim. On the women's side, Hania El Hammamy saved a match ball at the 2026 US Open to beat fellow Egyptian Fayrouz Aboelkheir, then faced four-time champion Nouran Gohar. That kind of resilience is what this round tests.

Egypt can send only two per gender, so the draws are tougher than the rankings suggest.
SQU05.potentialContendersIntro: Quarterfinal pairings aren't known, so these are projected names, and any Egyptians depend on which two per gender are selected.

potentialContenders.name: Mostafa Asal
potentialContenders.note: Two-time reigning world champion and men's world No. 1 as of October 2026. He is the projected man to beat if he qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Amina Orfi
potentialContenders.note: Took the women's world No. 1 spot in September 2026 by beating El Hammamy 3-2 in the Qatar Classic final.

potentialContenders.name: Nouran Gohar
potentialContenders.note: Won her first world title in 2024, beating El Sherbini in their fourth straight world final. A possible quarterfinalist if she is in Egypt's two.

potentialContenders.name: Hania El Hammamy
potentialContenders.note: Saved a match ball at the 2026 US Open and has been a repeated finalist, so she could be dangerous in a knockout.

potentialContenders.name: Victor Crouin
potentialContenders.note: Men's world No. 6 in October 2026 and a likely contender to disrupt the Egyptian side of the draw.

SQU06.blurb:
By the last ball tonight, the semifinal lineups are finished, and every player left is guaranteed at least a shot at a bronze medal match. Nobody here has ever won a squash medal at a Summer Games, because the sport has never been on the program.

The men's story could be Paul Coll against Diego Elias again, the pair who met in the 2026 US Open final, which Coll won 3-1. Elias also beat Mostafa Asal for the 2024 world title.

On the women's side, a quarterfinal could test Olivia Weaver's home hopes if she qualifies and recovers fully, or Orfi's youth against anyone willing to take her on.
SQU06.potentialContendersIntro: Projected names only: quarterfinal pairings, qualification and fitness are all open, and Weaver's injury recovery is something to watch.

potentialContenders.name: Paul Coll
potentialContenders.note: Ranked No. 2 in October 2026, with the 2026 British Open and US Open titles. Highest-ranked non-Egyptian in the men's list alongside Elias.

potentialContenders.name: Diego Elias
potentialContenders.note: 2024 world champion and world No. 3. Could be a key semifinal-run name if he qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Olivia Weaver
potentialContenders.note: World championship semifinalist in 2024 and 2025 and USA No. 1 in June 2026. A potential home favorite, subject to her recovery from injury.

potentialContenders.name: Amina Orfi
potentialContenders.note: 2026 women's world champion and youngest women's world No. 1 at 19.

potentialContenders.name: Sivasangari Subramaniam
potentialContenders.note: Confirmed qualifier as 2026 Asian Games champion, with a chance at a deep run.

SQU07.blurb:
Three straight world titles, three different Egyptians: Nouran Gohar in 2024, Nour El Sherbini in 2025, Amina Orfi in 2026. The women's semifinals are where that depth could run straight into the two-per-country limit.

Orfi, at 19 years and two months in September 2026, broke a record Susan Devoy set in 1984 to become the youngest women's world No. 1. If she is on court tonight, she could be playing either a rival or a compatriot.

Two matches, a hush between points, a late start under the studio lights. The winners play for gold on Sunday. The losers still get a bronze match, so nobody walks off empty-handed.
SQU07.potentialContendersIntro: These are projected semifinalists, not confirmed ones, and at most two Egyptian women can be in the draw.

potentialContenders.name: Amina Orfi
potentialContenders.note: Reigning world champion and women's world No. 1, who beat El Hammamy 3-2 in the Qatar Classic final for her first Platinum title.

potentialContenders.name: Nour El Sherbini
potentialContenders.note: Eight-time world champion and 2025 titlist, though she lost 3-0 to Anahat Singh in October 2026, so form is a question.

potentialContenders.name: Nouran Gohar
potentialContenders.note: 2024 world champion and a four-time US Open champion, a likely semifinal threat if she is one of Egypt's two.

potentialContenders.name: Sivasangari Subramaniam
potentialContenders.note: Confirmed qualifier after beating Anahat Singh in the 2026 Asian Games final.

potentialContenders.name: Olivia Weaver
potentialContenders.note: Two-time world championship semifinalist who could be a home contender, depending on qualification and recovery from a June 2026 injury.

SQU08.blurb:
Diego Elias beat Mostafa Asal in the 2024 world final. Since then, Asal has won two straight world titles, which sets up the men's semifinals as a question of who owns the sport right now.

Paul Coll lingers in that argument too. The New Zealander won the 2026 British Open and the US Open, then topped Elias 3-1 in Philadelphia, so any of those three could be the obstacle for the other two.

Ali Farag, who beat Asal in the 2022 and 2023 world semifinals, is gone. Egypt's four top-seven men can't all be here either, which opens space for a surprise on a late summer night.
SQU08.potentialContendersIntro: These are the likely semifinalists if form holds. Draws and qualification for 2028 are not settled, and only two Egyptian men can qualify.

potentialContenders.name: Mostafa Asal
potentialContenders.note: Back-to-back world champion in 2025 and 2026 and world No. 1 in October 2026.

potentialContenders.name: Paul Coll
potentialContenders.note: World No. 2 and the 2026 British Open and US Open champion. A likely podium threat if he qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Diego Elias
potentialContenders.note: Beat Asal for the 2024 world title, was world No. 3 in October 2026, and is a possible semifinalist.

potentialContenders.name: Youssef Ibrahim
potentialContenders.note: 2026 world final runner-up and world No. 7. Could take one of Egypt's two spots.

potentialContenders.name: Ng Eain Yow
potentialContenders.note: Confirmed qualifier as Asian Games champion, a possible underdog.

SQU09.blurb:
Every medal in this sport is a first, and tonight the women get theirs. Whoever wins the bronze match opens the evening by stepping onto a podium that has never existed before, and then the gold match gives the name that goes first on the list.

The recent history points to Egypt. Gohar, El Sherbini and Orfi have won the last three world titles, with Orfi the reigning senior and junior champion at 19. But with only two Egyptians per event, the medal matches could include a visitor.

Watch the Courthouse Square court, the backlot facade, the quiet before a serve. This is a coronation night with no precedent.
SQU09.potentialContendersIntro: These are projected medal-match players. Qualification and semifinal results are not settled, and no more than two Egyptians can be in the draw.

potentialContenders.name: Amina Orfi
potentialContenders.note: Reigning world champion and youngest women's world No. 1, a projected favorite if she qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Nour El Sherbini
potentialContenders.note: Eight-time world champion who beat El Hammamy in the 2025 final in Chicago, and a likely medal threat if she makes Egypt's two.

potentialContenders.name: Nouran Gohar
potentialContenders.note: 2024 world champion and a four-time US Open champion, a possible podium name.

potentialContenders.name: Hania El Hammamy
potentialContenders.note: Defending US Open champion and 2025 world runner-up, in contention if she is selected.

potentialContenders.name: Sivasangari Subramaniam
potentialContenders.note: Confirmed qualifier as 2026 Asian Games champion, and the sort of non-Egyptian who could break up the podium.

SQU10.blurb:
The last squash match of the Games is also the one everyone has been waiting for: the first men's gold medal in the sport's history. It starts at 8:30 pm and could end close to midnight.

Mostafa Asal could be in the box seat, a two-time reigning world champion who beat Ali Farag in Chicago in 2025, only for Farag to retire less than two weeks later. Paul Coll and Diego Elias have both beaten him on big stages and could be waiting.

With no more than two Egyptians in the draw, at least one non-Egyptian will finish on the podium. Bronze comes first, gold last, and then the sport has its first men's champion.
SQU10.potentialContendersIntro: These are projected medal-match contenders based on October 2026 form. Qualification and results are not confirmed, and the two-per-country cap shapes the field.

potentialContenders.name: Mostafa Asal
potentialContenders.note: Two-time reigning world champion (2025, 2026) and men's world No. 1 as of October 2026.

potentialContenders.name: Paul Coll
potentialContenders.note: World No. 2 with the 2026 British Open and a 3-1 US Open final win over Elias for his 35th PSA title.

potentialContenders.name: Diego Elias
potentialContenders.note: 2024 world champion, beating Asal in the final, and a likely threat if he qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Youssef Ibrahim
potentialContenders.note: 2026 world final runner-up and world No. 7, a possible second Egyptian in the field.

potentialContenders.name: Victor Crouin
potentialContenders.note: World No. 6 in October 2026 and a potential dark horse for a bronze-medal run.

SRF01.blurb:
The first heat paddles out at 7:30 AM, when the marine layer still hangs over San Clemente and the cobblestones at Lower Trestles are wet and cold underfoot. Nobody on the sand knows yet who will be in the water.

That's the appeal. Round 1 is where you meet the field, and with 24 men and 24 women, the places include universality spots for smaller surfing nations. Expect a few names you've never heard alongside veterans such as Carissa Moore, if she makes the team.

There are no permanent grandstands here, just the shoreline close to the lineup. Attendance will be capped well below a normal pro event, so you're likely to be among the few who saw these surfers before the pressure built.
SRF01.potentialContendersIntro: The full Round 1 field won't be known until shortly before the Games, so these names are projections based on recent form and the 2026 World Surfing Games.

potentialContenders.name: Carissa Moore
potentialContenders.note: Tokyo 2020 gold medalist who returned to the tour; she could appear if she earns a place through the published selection procedures.

potentialContenders.name: Griffin Colapinto
potentialContenders.note: On Team USA's six-surfer squad at the 2026 World Surfing Games and a regular at Trestles. A likely contender for a 2028 place.

potentialContenders.name: Crosby Colapinto
potentialContenders.note: Also on the 2026 World Surfing Games squad. A San Clemente local who could be a home-break dark horse if he qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Lucca Mesinas
potentialContenders.note: Posted an event-high score on Day 3 of the 2026 World Surfing Games in front of the home crowd in Peru. Could be a name to watch if Peru qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Catalina Zariquiey
potentialContenders.note: Also posted an event-high score at the 2026 World Surfing Games; a possible early-round surprise if she makes the field.

SRF02.blurb:
A 34-year-old and a 19-year-old walked away from Lower Trestles in September 2026 as the most recent winners at this wave. If both qualify, you could be watching them in the water together.

Miguel Pupo of Brazil edged Kanoa Igarashi 14.77 to 14.40 for his first Trestles title. Canada's Erin Brooks beat Gabriela Bryan 13.00 to 11.90, her third straight tour win, after a requalification scare earlier in the year.

Round 2 is where reputations get tested. The field has settled in, the surfers know the cobblestone point, and one bad exchange can end a campaign. Because each pathway caps nations at one surfer, countries are sending whoever earned the places, not necessarily their biggest names.
SRF02.potentialContendersIntro: Nothing is settled for 2028, but the 2026 Lexus Trestles Pro results are a good guide to who could do well at this wave.

potentialContenders.name: Erin Brooks
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 Trestles Pro final at 19 for her third straight tour win. Could be a title threat if Canada qualifies her.

potentialContenders.name: Miguel Pupo
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 Trestles Pro at 34, beating Kanoa Igarashi in the final. His age and the Brazilian selection path are both open questions for 2028.

potentialContenders.name: Gabriela Bryan
potentialContenders.note: Runner-up to Brooks at Trestles in 2026 and on Team USA's 2026 World Surfing Games squad; a likely American contender.

potentialContenders.name: Kanoa Igarashi
potentialContenders.note: Lost the 2026 Trestles final to Pupo by 0.37. His 2028 place is not confirmed, but he could be a danger if he qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Yago Dora
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2025 Trestles Pro and the 2025 world title. Projected to be among Brazil's strongest men.

SRF03.blurb:
Gabriel Medina has a bronze from Paris and three runner-up finishes in 2026, but no tour win since April 2023. That drought is the subtext of Round 3, where the field narrows toward the quarterfinals.

He ran into Griffin Colapinto in Portugal and lost 17.60 to 16.77, a San Clemente surfer who has grown up on waves like this one. If both are here, a Trestles meeting would be all about home knowledge.

The women's side has its own weight. Molly Picklum, the 2025 world champion, and Carissa Moore, the Tokyo gold medalist who returned to the tour, sat at Nos. 1 and 2 in late October 2026. Several nations could have three surfers per gender in the draw, so countrymen may face each other.
SRF03.potentialContendersIntro: These are projections based on late-October 2026 form, not confirmed 2028 entries.

potentialContenders.name: Gabriel Medina
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalist and No. 4 in the men's rankings in late October 2026. Winless on tour since April 2023 despite three runner-up finishes in 2026.

potentialContenders.name: Griffin Colapinto
potentialContenders.note: Beat Medina in the 2026 Portugal final for his third win there. A likely contender for a US place, with deep Trestles experience.

potentialContenders.name: Yago Dora
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world champion and No. 1 in the men's rankings in late October 2026. A projected Brazilian contender.

potentialContenders.name: Molly Picklum
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world champion, won the 2026 Portugal event and led the women's rankings in late October 2026. Could be the woman to beat if she qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Carissa Moore
potentialContenders.note: Tokyo 2020 gold medalist, No. 2 in the women's rankings in late October 2026 after returning to the tour. Her place is not confirmed.

SRF04.blurb:
Caroline Marks won gold in Paris by 0.17, 10.50 to 10.33, over Tatiana Weston-Webb. That one-wave margin is what a single day of quarterfinals, semifinals, and medal matches is built around.

The format has no second chances. Nothing carries over from earlier rounds, and the schedule depends on wave conditions. The WSL dropped its own winner-takes-all finals at Lower Trestles starting in 2026, so the medal day here is now the one that matters most.

The contenders could be the Colapintos, Marks, or Filipe Toledo, who live in San Clemente or grew up on this wave. Attendance on the temporary beachfront setup will be capped, with off-site viewing parties in town, so being on the shore for a medal match will be rare.
SRF04.potentialContendersIntro: The defending champions are confirmed from Paris 2024. Who actually reaches the 2028 final is open, so the others here are projections.

potentialContenders.name: Caroline Marks
potentialContenders.note: Defending women's gold medalist who won at Paris 2024 by 0.17 and grew up surfing Trestles. She is projected to be a contender if she qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Kauli Vaast
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 men's gold medalist, who opened that final with a 9.50. He is a defending champion, but Trestles is a very different wave from Teahupo'o.

potentialContenders.name: Griffin Colapinto
potentialContenders.note: San Clemente local who won the 2026 Portugal final. A likely US men's contender if he makes the team.

potentialContenders.name: Carissa Moore
potentialContenders.note: Tokyo 2020 gold medalist and one of two Americans to win women's gold. Could return to the medal stage if she qualifies.

potentialContenders.name: Gabriel Medina
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalist who finished runner-up three times on tour in 2026. A projected Brazilian threat.

SWA01.blurb:
China broke up a twin act. After Lin Yanjun and Lin Yanhan took silver at the 2025 worlds, Yanjun teamed with Xu Huiyan, and the new pair won the technical duet at Xi'an and again at the Toronto Super Final in their debut season.

That sets up a first-morning test against Austria's Alexandri twins, the reigning world technical champions, and Britain's Kate Shortman and Isabelle Thorpe, who reunited in 2026 after Shortman's long break. If Russian swimmers return, the field gets deeper still.

The technical routine is the strict one, with required elements and nowhere to hide. You'll watch it in the open air beside the Long Beach waterfront, at the start of the sport's first Games back in Southern California since its 1984 debut.
SWA01.potentialContendersIntro: These are the duets to watch in the technical routine, based on 2025 and 2026 results. Who qualifies for 2028 is not yet settled.

potentialContenders.name: Lin Yanjun / Xu Huiyan
potentialContenders.note: Won the technical and free duet at the 2026 World Cup Super Final in their first season together. They are a likely favorite if China keeps the pairing.

potentialContenders.name: Anna-Maria Alexandri / Eirini-Marina Alexandri
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2025 world duet technical title ahead of China's Lin sisters. They could be the biggest threat to a Chinese opening lead.

potentialContenders.name: Kate Shortman / Isabelle Thorpe
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalists, back together in 2026. Shortman has said she is targeting the 2028 Games.

potentialContenders.name: Mayya Doroshko / Tatiana Gayday
potentialContenders.note: Took 2025 world technical bronze. Russia's 2028 status is unresolved, so their presence is a question mark.

SWA02.blurb:
Whatever happened in the technical routine the day before is now banked. The duet medals go to whoever combines it best with the free routine, and the free routine is where the artistry lives: music, theme, choreography and risk.

China's Lin Yanjun and Xu Huiyan scored 315.0224 with a shadow-of-the-moon routine in Toronto, a double over the field. Spain's Iris Tio Casas, the first swimmer to win world titles in all four disciplines, and Lilou Lluis Valette own the 2025 world free title.

Shortman and Thorpe won Britain's first medal in the sport at Paris 2024, silver behind the Wang twins. A gold would finish that story. Wednesday late morning in Long Beach, the pool turns into a stage.
SWA02.potentialContendersIntro: Medals here depend on combined technical and free scores. Based on recent form, these duets look like the main contenders if they qualify for 2028.

potentialContenders.name: Lin Yanjun / Xu Huiyan
potentialContenders.note: Swept both duet events at the 2026 Super Final, scoring 315.0224 in free. They are a projected favorite for gold.

potentialContenders.name: Iris Tio Casas / Lilou Lluis Valette
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2025 world duet free title. Tio Casas has world titles in solo, duet, mixed duet and team.

potentialContenders.name: Kate Shortman / Isabelle Thorpe
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalists who reunited in 2026. They are chasing Britain's first gold in the sport.

potentialContenders.name: Anna-Maria Alexandri / Eirini-Marina Alexandri
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2025 duet technical world title. Their free routine will decide whether they hold a medal position.

potentialContenders.name: Wang Liuyi / Wang Qianyi
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalists. China has not confirmed whether they will defend the title, so this is speculative.

SWA03.blurb:
Eight swimmers, up to two of them men, move as a single organism. That is the team technical routine, and it opens the team event with the sport's strictest test of synchronization.

China is the team everyone is chasing. It won the 2025 world technical by more than seven points over Neutral Athletes B, then won again at the 2026 Super Final in Toronto. Its lineup features Lin Yanjun and Xu Huiyan, who also swim as a duet.

The Russian question hangs over the pool. Restrictions were lifted in 2026, but participation at the Games is not settled.

Thursday's session is short, so get there early. The first routine scores matter all the way to Saturday.
SWA03.potentialContendersIntro: These are the teams to watch in the technical routine, based on 2025 and 2026 results. Who qualifies, and in what form, is still to be decided.

potentialContenders.name: China
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2025 world team technical with 307.8001 points and the 2026 Super Final technical. They are the projected leader.

potentialContenders.name: Neutral Athletes B
potentialContenders.note: Second at the 2025 worlds and winners at the 2026 European Championships. A Russian return in 2028 is unresolved.

potentialContenders.name: Spain
potentialContenders.note: Took 2025 world technical bronze and Paris 2024 team bronze. Iris Tio Casas gives them a world-title pedigree.

potentialContenders.name: USA
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 team silver medalists. They entered all 11 events at the 2026 Super Final and named a 2026-2028 training squad.

SWA04.blurb:
China has not lost a world team free title since 2022. In Toronto, it did not even enter the event. Was that a rest or a signal? The 2028 team free is where rivals will try to find out.

This is the middle chapter of three routines, and it is the longest on pool-deck storytelling: themes, formations and eight bodies underwater and in the air. Japan, second at Singapore 2025 (334.7232), and Spain, third, want to cut into China's 348.4779.

The United States, silver in Paris, finished just off the podium in the 2025 team free. Expect them to push for more.

At Long Beach, the best routines show that artistic swimming is as much theater as sport.
SWA04.potentialContendersIntro: These are the teams likely to feature in the free routine, based on recent worlds. 2028 qualification is not yet decided.

potentialContenders.name: China
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2025 world team free title with 348.4779 points. They have won it at every worlds from 2022 through 2025.

potentialContenders.name: Japan
potentialContenders.note: Second in the 2025 world team free with 334.7232. They could be China's most direct challenger in this routine.

potentialContenders.name: Spain
potentialContenders.note: Third in the 2025 world team free and Paris 2024 team bronze medalists.

potentialContenders.name: USA
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalists. Their 2025 world team free finished just off the podium, so they are chasing a rebound.

SWA05.blurb:
Throws, lifts and flips. The acrobatic routine is the sport's boldest, and at Paris 2024 it was where China sealed its first team gold. It is also the last artistic swimming session of the Games.

China swept all three team routines at the 2025 worlds, with the acrobatic title at 229.0186. It scored 243.3207 in Toronto in 2026 with duet stars Lin Yanjun and Xu Huiyan in the lineup. The United States, silver in Paris, raised its difficulty at the 2025 worlds in a push for a medal and still left without one.

Saturday morning in Long Beach, the whole pool watches the air. One missed catch can undo three days of work.
SWA05.potentialContendersIntro: Team medals here combine technical, free and acrobatic scores. These teams look like the strongest bets, pending 2028 qualification.

potentialContenders.name: China
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalists and 2025 world acrobatic champions. They won the 2026 Super Final acrobatic with 243.3207 points.

potentialContenders.name: USA
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalists. They bring a history of bold acrobatic difficulty and a medal bid to prove.

potentialContenders.name: Spain
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalists and 2025 world acrobatic bronze. They are a steady podium threat.

potentialContenders.name: Neutral Athletes B
potentialContenders.note: Silver in the 2025 world acrobatic and winners at the 2026 European Championships. Russia's 2028 status is unresolved.

SWM01.blurb:
Doors open on the pool at 9:30 in the morning, and the first thing you see is a 50-meter pool laid across an NFL field under a translucent roof. Coastal air drifts in through the open sides.

The field has questions. Gretchen Walsh swam the second-fastest 100m butterfly in history at the 2025 World Championships, and she needs to get through this heat first. Ariarne Titmus has retired, so the women's 400m freestyle has no defending champion. Summer McIntosh beat Katie Ledecky in that event at Worlds.

The new men's 50m butterfly and women's 50m backstroke also swim their first Games heats. This session is cheap, early and full of firsts.
SWM01.potentialContendersIntro: Focus is on the women's 100m butterfly and women's 400m freestyle heats, plus the men's 400m freestyle. Who actually swims in 2028 is still to be decided, so these are projections.

potentialContenders.name: Gretchen Walsh
potentialContenders.note: World record holder in the 100m butterfly and the 2025 world champion in 54.73, the second-fastest swim ever. She took silver in Paris 2024 behind teammate Torri Huske.

potentialContenders.name: Torri Huske
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 100m butterfly champion. A likely contender to fight Walsh for the American spots if she makes the team.

potentialContenders.name: Summer McIntosh
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalist in the 400m freestyle who beat Ledecky for the 2025 world title. With Titmus retired, she is a projected favorite.

potentialContenders.name: Katie Ledecky
potentialContenders.note: Bronze in the 400m freestyle at Paris 2024 and winner of the 800m and 1500m at the 2025 World Championships. She could still appear here if she chases the 400m too.

potentialContenders.name: Lukas Märtens
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 men's 400m freestyle champion, who took bronze in the 800m at the 2025 World Championships. A likely contender to defend his title.

SWM02.blurb:
Night one, and nobody is hiding. The first medals of the pool program go out in four races, and two of them are relays.

The women's 400m freestyle is the one to circle. Titmus won it in Paris and has since retired, so a new champion will be crowned. McIntosh and Ledecky are the names everyone is watching, and McIntosh won their most recent world title meeting.

Then come the 4x100m freestyle relays, where Australia's women beat the United States in Paris. That rivalry is still tight: at the 2025 Worlds, Australia beat the US by 0.66 seconds in the women's 4x200m relay. Under the lights, with 38,000 seats in the stadium, those four-person sprints can feel like a punch fight.
SWM02.potentialContendersIntro: Focus is on the women's 400m freestyle final and the women's 100m butterfly semifinal. Who qualifies is not yet known, so these are projections.

potentialContenders.name: Summer McIntosh
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalist who beat Ledecky for the 2025 world title in Singapore. A projected favorite with Titmus gone.

potentialContenders.name: Katie Ledecky
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalist in the 400m and the 2025 world champion in the 800m and 1500m. She could provide the main challenge to McIntosh.

potentialContenders.name: Gretchen Walsh
potentialContenders.note: Reigning 100m butterfly world champion in a championship-record 54.73, and a semifinalist in this session if she makes the team.

potentialContenders.name: Lukas Märtens
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 men's 400m freestyle winner ahead of Elijah Winnington. A likely contender to defend his title.

potentialContenders.name: Elijah Winnington
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalist in the men's 400m freestyle, projected to challenge Märtens again if he qualifies.

SWM03.blurb:
Tatjana Smith retired after Paris, came back, and has now announced she will swim for the Netherlands. Her heat in the women's 100m breaststroke is the best subplot of the morning: a defending champion in a new cap, trying to make the 2028 field.

Down the card, the men's 400m IM goes straight from heats to the final, so only eight swimmers survive. Léon Marchand has won this event at Paris 2024 and the 2025 Worlds, and he will ease through the morning in front of the home crowd.

The women's 100m freestyle and men's 100m backstroke add depth, so you get a spread of sprinters without the pressure of a final.
SWM03.potentialContendersIntro: Focus is on the women's 100m breaststroke and men's 400m IM. Entries are projections until the teams are named, and Marchand had an adductor injury in June 2026.

potentialContenders.name: Tatjana Smith

SWM04.blurb:
Two events are making their Games debut tonight: the men's 50m butterfly and women's 50m backstroke. Both are over in about 25 seconds, so do not blink or look at your phone.

The women's 100m butterfly is the headliner. Huske and Walsh went one-two in Paris, and Walsh has since won Worlds in a championship-record 54.73, the second-fastest ever. Two Americans, one world record, and a rematch where each swimmer knows what the other has.

Add the men's 400m IM, with Marchand's pull-and-kick finish, and a men's 100m breaststroke where Nicolò Martinenghi defends the title that Adam Peaty tied for silver behind. That is five finals in two hours.

SWM05.blurb:
Morning heats are where you can see who is actually fit. McIntosh's 400m IM goes straight to a final, so a single heat decides whether she gets another crack at gold. She won it at Paris 2024 and again in 2025.

Men's 200m freestyle is also stacked. David Popovici won at Paris and at Worlds in 1:43.53, with Luke Hobson 0.31 seconds behind, and every swimmer in the heat knows it.

The men's 1500m freestyle also swims its single heat, and the new 50m breaststroke gets its first Games prelims. Few sessions let you see so many distances and so many future finalists in the same two hours.

SWM06.blurb:
Tatjana Smith's story lands in a medal race tonight. She won the 100m breaststroke in Paris, retired, and is now trying to come back for the Netherlands while still training at home in South Africa. If she makes the final, you will see the fastest comeback in the sport.

McIntosh's 400m IM is the distance event in the session. Four medley strokes over eight lengths, and her turn speed is what separates her from the rest.

Set that against a women's 100m freestyle final that follows Sarah Sjöström's Paris win, plus the men's 100m backstroke, and you have an evening that goes by in a blur.

Katie Ledecky's 1500m freestyle is a straight-to-final race, so her morning heat is the only time you can see her swim that distance before the medals are on the line. She won the 2025 world title in 15:26.44.

The women's 200m freestyle has a hole where Ariarne Titmus used to be. She retired in October 2025, and defending champion Mollie O'Callaghan has disclosed spinal stress fractures, so it is not clear who will be swimming.

The men's 50m freestyle is a flat-out burst. Cameron McEvoy won in Paris and at Worlds, and Caeleb Dressel's recent form has the crowd wondering if he is back.

SWM08.blurb:
The first Games medal in the men's 50m breaststroke goes out tonight, and the event's biggest name might not be in it. Adam Peaty holds the world record at 25.95, set in 2017, and he failed to reach the 2026 European semifinals.

That opens things up for a field that has never raced this for a medal. It is a quick, chaotic dash that rewards reaction time.

Stay for the men's 200m freestyle and 200m butterfly. Popovici carries the 2025 world title in 1:43.53, and Marchand won the butterfly in Paris. McKeown's 100m backstroke final sits on the card too, along with the men's 1500m.

SWM09.blurb:
The men's 4x200m freestyle relay goes straight from heats to the final, which makes this morning a sorting hat. Three nations that finished on the podium in Paris, plus Japan and Romania, will fight for eight spots.

Britain won it in Paris with the United States second. Popovici and Hobson went one-two in the 2025 world 200m freestyle, and Japan's Tatsuya Murasa set a national record for bronze, so the relay is less predictable than it used to be.

Individually, Marchand could be in the 200m IM, and the new women's 50m butterfly makes its Games debut.

SWM10.blurb:
Ledecky's 1500m freestyle final is a slow-burn drama. Thirty lengths, a crowd that rises with each lap, and a champion who tends to pull away in the middle of the race. She won in Paris and at the 2025 Worlds in 15:26.44.

Then the relay, with Britain trying to hold off the United States and Australia in the men's 4x200m. The women's 200m breaststroke has Kate Douglass against Tatjana Smith, the Paris silver medalist, who is coming out of retirement to swim for the Netherlands.

Cameron McEvoy's 50m freestyle is the shortest race, over before the crowd finishes its first breath.

Australia's women hold the 4x200m freestyle relay world record at 7:37.50 from 2023, and they beat the United States by 0.66 seconds at the 2025 Worlds. This morning's heat decides the lanes for that evening.

The individual events are the real appetizers. Kaylee McKeown is the reigning world and Games champion in the 200m backstroke, with Regan Smith a step behind. Men's 100m freestyle is another to watch, with Pan Zhanle's world-record gold in Paris and David Popovici and Kyle Chalmers on the podium.

Go early, find a seat near the turn, and watch the swimmers explode off the wall.

At the 2025 World Championships, Léon Marchand took 1.31 seconds off Ryan Lochte's 200m IM world record, a mark that had stood since 2011. Tonight, he is back in the pool for the final, with a semifinal-to-final transition that rewards his fast finishing.

The women's 50m butterfly makes its Games debut. Gretchen Walsh won the world title in 24.83, almost half a second clear of the field, so the new event may come down to who can chase her.

Also on the card: Hubert Kós in the 200m backstroke and the Australia-United States relay rivalry in the women's 4x200m freestyle.

The mixed 4x100m medley relay does the same. The United States won in Paris, and coaches must decide who swims which leg, so the heat itself is part of the puzzle.

In the men's 100m butterfly, Maxime Grousset won the 2025 world title, and Kristóf Milák is the Paris champion. New 50m backstroke and breaststroke heats add a sprint flavor to the session.

Pan Zhanle blew the field away in the 100m freestyle at Paris 2024 with a world record, and tonight's final is the most anticipated race of the evening. Kyle Chalmers and David Popovici, the Paris silver and bronze medalists, are still looking for gold.

Kaylee McKeown and Regan Smith stage the women's 200m backstroke rematch. McKeown won by 0.96 seconds at the 2025 Worlds, and Smith has been second to her each time.

The women's 200m IM brings McIntosh and Douglass back together, while semifinals in the new 50m backstroke and breaststroke events give a sprinter's preview.

Sarah Sjöström won the event in Paris, and a star of her era trying to hold off a young generation is a story in itself.

The medley relay heats go straight to finals, so the coaches' choices are the secret of the morning. Walsh won the 2025 world 100m and 50m butterfly, and she looks like the likely US butterfly leg.

SWM16.blurb:
Someone will become the first Games champion in the men's 50m backstroke, and someone else will own the same distinction in the women's 50m breaststroke. Both events are new for 2028, and both finals land tonight.

Around them sits a men's 100m butterfly final with real stakes. Kristóf Milák won Paris gold, Maxime Grousset took the 2025 world title in 49.62, and Caeleb Dressel holds the world record at 49.45. Add Daniel Wiffen's 800m free title defense and a mixed medley relay where the US is the Paris champion.

Look down on a pool built on an NFL stadium floor, with the ring-shaped video board overhead and a coastal breeze through the open sides. The 50s are over before you finish inhaling.

Then the program stretches out. Summer McIntosh could defend her 200m butterfly title against Regan Smith, and Katie Ledecky, who set a championship-record 8:05.62 at the 2025 Worlds, could chase another 800m freestyle crown if she makes the team.

Two medley relays close the afternoon on the final weekend, with China's men and the US women both carrying Paris gold into the water beneath the translucent canopy.

TEN01.blurb:
The first tennis ball of the 2028 Games gets struck in Carson on a Wednesday morning, and the Wimbledon trophies are barely three days old. Mixed doubles used to sit near the end of the schedule. Now it opens the show.

Three first-round matches fill the 8,000-seat Center Court, where open sky and hard courts feel a long way from Roland Garros clay. Sixteen pairs start, eight survive, and the winners are back on court that evening.

Czechia's Katerina Siniakova and Tomas Machac, the Paris 2024 gold medalists, are the names to circle if they return to defend.

TEN02.blurb:
Court 1 is where you go to hear the squeak of shoes. It's a smaller, tighter stadium than Center Court, with fans seated close enough to catch a muttered word between partners.

Three first-round mixed matches run here while Center Court and Court 2 play simultaneously, eight in all across the complex. That makes it a good place for a scouting day: one loss and a pair is gone from a 16-team field.

The clock is the hidden opponent. Anyone who went deep at Wimbledon, which ends July 16, has had only a few days to switch surfaces.

TEN03.blurb:
Two matches, one outer court, and a front-row view of the sport's most compressed tournament. Court 2 is the quietest of the three first-round venues, and that is the appeal.

With only 16 pairs, nobody gets a warm-up round. Lose here and you're out before dinner; win and you're back for a quarterfinal that same evening. The format rewards teams who find chemistry in a hurry.

The surface is also a story. Paris 2024 was played on clay. Carson is open-air hard court, with the faster, flatter bounce that suits big servers.

TEN04.blurb:
Some of these players will already have won a match this afternoon. By 6:30 p.m. the legs are heavy and the quarterfinals begin, which is exactly the point of the new one-day-and-a-half format.

Center Court hosts two of the four quarterfinals, and the winners come back for a semifinal at 11 a.m. the next day. Tactics matter less than stamina, and every long deciding set exacts a price.

If Wimbledon regulars arrive in Carson three days after their own finals, expect tired, tough, experienced players trying to stay sharp in the evening air.

TEN05.blurb:
By the time this session starts, every pair on Court 1 has already earned its place the hard way: a first-round win earlier the same day.

Two quarterfinals play here while two more run on Center Court. Winners go to a semifinal in the morning, and medals are decided that night. Nobody here has time to be tentative.

The event used to be a late-week curiosity. Moving it to the start follows the US Open's lead, and the pace feels like a sprint. China's Wang Xinyu and Zhang Zhizhen made Paris 2024 silver. Could they build on it here?

TEN06.blurb:
Eleven a.m. on Thursday and four pairs are one win from a gold-medal match. Lose and there's still a bronze match tonight, but the gap in feeling between the two is huge.

The day has a second layer. Singles begins on the same date, so anyone entered in both events could be juggling a semifinal with a first-round draw.

That tension is the story: tennis stars, a few days removed from Wimbledon, trying to turn a rushed partnership into a medal. Center Court will be loud, bright, and still warming up.

Czechia's Siniakova and Machac are the Paris champions. China's Wang and Zhang were silver. Does either pair come back, or does a new team crash the podium?

TEN29.blurb:
Mixed doubles medals are already decided by the time Monday arrives. The mixed event runs first, on July 19 and 20, so the outer courts now belong to the main draws.

That shifts the mood. With the bracket narrowing, you can wander Courts 3-10 and catch men's third-round matches, women's quarterfinals and doubles rounds with little crowd noise except applause.

It is a day for the tennis enthusiast who likes to find a match before the stadium crowd does. Pick a court and settle in.

TEN30.blurb:
Gauff opened the 2026 WTA Finals by beating Jessica Pegula 6-4, 6-7(5), 6-2 in three hours of American tennis. A Monday-night quarterfinal in Carson could stage something similar with more at stake.

This is the most dramatic slot of the early week. The women's quarterfinals decide who plays for medals, and the evening air gives the stadium of 8,000 a late-summer feel under the lights.

Men's third-round matches share the bill, and with Djokovic, Zverev and Alcaraz in the potential field, the late match could be the one fans remember.

TEN31.blurb:
Wimbledon ends, and days later the world's best are trying to win on a hard court in Carson. That scramble is the subplot of this Tuesday: tired legs, short turnarounds, and a bill of quarterfinals and semifinals with no easy minutes.

The women's bracket could be loaded. Mirra Andreeva won the 2026 French Open, Elena Rybakina reached No. 1 after beating Aryna Sabalenka in the US Open final, and Coco Gauff has said she plans to play. On the men's side, Alexander Zverev finished 2026 as year-end No. 1.

About 8,000 seats surround an open-air court in the midday sun, close enough that you'll hear every grunt and every line call.

TEN32.blurb:
This is the long-haul ticket. Nine hours on Carson Court 1 means men's doubles semifinals, women's doubles quarterfinals and men's singles quarterfinals, all in one sitting.

Smaller than the main stadium and closer to the action, Court 1 puts you near enough to hear doubles teams whispering signals at the net. Doubles is where this tournament gets chatty and quick, and the match tiebreak that decided the Paris 2024 men's final can decide a semifinal here too.

If Marcel Granollers and Horacio Zeballos, Wimbledon champions Harri Heliovaara and Henry Patten, or Paris gold medalists Matthew Ebden and John Peers show up, the doubles alone are worth the seat.

TEN33.blurb:
Court 2 is where you go to feel like you've found something. It holds far fewer fans than the main stadium, and with an all-day ticket you can watch the draw thin out from a seat close to the baseline.

Men's doubles semifinals share the day with men's singles and women's doubles quarterfinals. The women's doubles bracket has a built-in storyline: Sara Errani and Jasmine Paolini, the Paris 2024 gold medalists, reached the 2026 WTA Finals doubles semifinals for the first time after a comeback win in a 10-point tiebreak.

Players must be on a nominated Davis Cup or Billie Jean King Cup team at least twice across 2027 and 2028 to qualify, so who shows up is an open question.

TEN35.blurb:
The night session gets the women's semifinals, and the stakes are plain: win and you play for gold on Thursday, lose and you play for bronze.

Zheng Qinwen won gold at Paris 2024 on clay by beating Donna Vekic, and she's the reigning champion. The field chasing her has changed. Rybakina took the 2026 US Open over Sabalenka. Andreeva opened her WTA Finals debut with a 6-4, 6-0 win. Gauff has said she plans to play in her home country.

The men's quarterfinals share the bill, so it's a long evening of hard-court tennis with real consequences.

TEN36.blurb:
At Paris 2024, Novak Djokovic beat Carlos Alcaraz 7-6(3), 7-6(2) for the one title missing from his career. A rematch could build here, two days before the final.

Djokovic said in October 2026 that he sees no reason he can't make 2028 once his health issues are resolved. He will be 41. Alcaraz beat him in the 2026 Australian Open final to complete the career Grand Slam.

The women's doubles semifinals share the session, and Errani and Paolini, the Paris gold medalists, could be among them. Come for the semifinals, stay for the doubles. It's an afternoon where everything is on the line.

TEN37.blurb:
Wednesday night is the last time the crowd gets to breathe before the medal matches. Two men's singles semifinals decide who plays for gold on Friday, and the stakes show in the way points are played.

It's hard to imagine a bigger draw for a Southern California night. Zverev, the 2026 year-end No. 1, could meet Alcaraz, who became the youngest man to complete the career Grand Slam in Melbourne. Add Djokovic at 41, chasing another medal, and there's a story on every court.

The women's doubles semifinals may also appear, and Errani and Paolini, the Paris 2024 gold medalists, would be worth the early arrival.

TEN38.blurb:
Two matches, two medals, one afternoon. The bronze match opens the day, and the gold-medal match follows with the Carson sun still high.

Zheng Qinwen won gold at Paris 2024 by beating Donna Vekic, and Iga Swiatek took bronze. Four years on, the rankings look different. Rybakina is No. 1, Andreeva won the 2026 French Open, Linda Noskova won Wimbledon, and Gauff has said she wants to play in front of a home crowd.

The women's final can be a collision of styles: Rybakina's serve against Andreeva's counterpunching, with 8,000 fans close enough to feel each rally.

Doubles medals get decided late, and this one runs until midnight. It's the sort of session where you buy a ticket for the match tiebreak and end up remembering the volleys.

The Paris 2024 men's final ended 10-8 in a match tiebreak, with Matthew Ebden and John Peers beating Rajeev Ram and Austin Krajicek for Australia's first tennis gold in 28 years. This one could finish just as tight.

The field could include recent major champions: Granollers and Zeballos at Roland Garros, Heliovaara and Patten at Wimbledon, Harrison and Skupski in Melbourne. A night final under the Carson lights, with a bronze match first.

TEN40.blurb:
Everything in the tournament has been aimed at this afternoon. Men's singles is the only event still alive on the last day, and the bronze match leads into the gold-medal match.

The story everyone wants is the Paris rematch. Novak Djokovic beat Carlos Alcaraz 7-6(3), 7-6(2) in France, and Alcaraz then completed the career Grand Slam by beating Djokovic in Melbourne in 2026. If both make it, and Djokovic's health holds up at 41, the finals could carry that history.

Zverev is a threat too, and Sinner may return from a knee injury. It's a final-day afternoon in the sun, with the whole sport watching.

TEN41.blurb:
The tennis tournament ends late on a Friday night with a women's doubles final. It could be the best way to close.

Sara Errani and Jasmine Paolini beat Mirra Andreeva and Diana Shnaider at Paris 2024 for gold, winning a final-set tiebreak. If the Italians return, they'd bring a French Open title, a 2026 WTA Finals semifinal run and a reputation for coming back from behind.

Andreeva is now a major champion in singles, and Shnaider has risen too, so the field could look much stronger than the one that played in Paris. Bronze goes first, then the gold match, the final points of the tennis event, and it all happens under the lights in Carson.

TKW01.blurb:
Sixty-eight fighters from 66 nations packed the men's -58kg draw at the 2025 World Championships, and that is the kind of crowded bracket that opens the taekwondo program here. Morning sessions are where you meet the field before the pressure peaks.

The women's -49kg has no defending champion at all. Thailand's Panipak Wongpattanakit retired after Paris 2024, so every fighter on the mat is chasing a vacant throne.

In a converted exhibition hall with about 7,000 temporary seats, you sit close enough to hear the kicks land on the chest protectors. Come early and watch a future medalist work through a Round of 32.

Park Tae-joon won Paris 2024 gold, then ran into the same wall three times in a row. The wall has a name: Abolfazl Zandi. If both reach the quarterfinals and semifinals here, this is where the Korean's slump either ends or deepens.

The women's -49kg bracket is just as unsettled. Fu Xiaolu showed her nerve at the Muju 2026 Grand Prix, dropping the first round of a semifinal to a teammate and then storming back.

Afternoon sessions are when brackets narrow fast. Every win sends a fighter to the medal contests, and every loss to a finalist sends one to the repechage.

The men's -58kg carries a different tension. Park Tae-joon beat Gashim Magomedov for gold in Paris, then slid. Iran's Abolfazl Zandi, the reigning world champion, has beaten him three straight times, and Bae Jun-seo has beaten him too.

Repechages and bronze contests build toward the late finals. By then, the hall is full of flags and the fighters are in their final rounds.

Ulugbek Rashitov is the first man to win two taekwondo titles at the Games, and he has not fought since May 2025. His two-year suspension for whereabouts failures ends May 12, 2027, which leaves him more than a year to get back in form. Whether he turns up in this Round of 32 is one of the great unknowns of the week.

The women's -57kg has its own question. Brazil's Maria Clara Pacheco beat Paris champion Kim Yu-jin in the 2025 world final.

The early rounds are your chance to see teenage prospects like Jordan's Fadia Khirfan before the afternoon crowd arrives.

TKW08.blurb:
Belarus had never won a World Taekwondo Grand Prix until Raman Turavinau took the -80kg title at Muju in 2026. He is the kind of fighter you might see for the first time here and remember by the final.

Brazil's Henrique Marques wears the world crown at -80kg after beating China's Xiang Qizhang in Wuxi. Xiang had beaten South Korea's Seo Geon-woo in the semifinals. Their rematch could be here.

The women's -67kg has two Hungarian names and one Brazilian name in the conversation. Luana Marton's age and Milena Titoneli's experience should make for an intriguing quarterfinal.
TKW08.potentialContendersIntro: Contenders for the women's -67kg and men's -80kg quarterfinals and semifinals. All are projected, and 2028 selection is not confirmed.

TKW09.blurb:
Hungary could walk in with both the Games champion and the world champion in the same weight class. Viviana Marton took gold in Paris, Luana Marton won the 2025 world title, and they could be on the same side of the draw. In a hall with about 7,000 seats, that rivalry would be a headline.

The men's -80kg could be a three-continent argument. Firas Katoussi of Tunisia won Paris gold over Iran's Mehran Barkhordari, Brazil's Henrique Marques is the world champion, and Belarus's Raman Turavinau is the new Grand Prix winner.

Brazil's recent run at these weights points to a growing contender in the late rounds.

TKW10.blurb:
The heavyweights get the last morning of taekwondo, and the biggest question isn't who is entered but who is allowed. France's Althea Laurin, the Paris champion, was handed a 20-month suspension for missed tests, and reports have not said whether she can return in time for the 2028 Games.

The men's field has other stories. South Korea's Kang Sang-hyun won the 2025 world title at +87kg, a division not on the Games program, so watching how he handles the +80kg weight is part of the draw. Iran's Arian Salimi is the Paris champion, and the USA's Jonathan Healy won world bronze.

Home fans should look for Healy's name early.

potentialContenders.name: Svetlana Osipova
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 +67kg silver medalist, ranked No. 2 by World Taekwondo in November 2024.

TKW11.blurb:
Heavyweight taekwondo is where a single kick can end a match, and this afternoon can be the last chance for big names to survive before the bronze and gold medal contests. Semifinal losers fall straight into the bronze medal fights, and fighters beaten by the finalists go to the repechage.

In Paris, both heavyweight medal events were held on one Saturday at the Grand Palais. Here the same final day is in downtown Los Angeles, a few minutes from L.A. Live.

Cheick Sallah Cisse won gold at Rio 2016 in the -80kg division, then moved up and took bronze in Paris. Watching a veteran like him in a quarterfinal is a lesson in how heavyweights adapt.

TKW12.blurb:
Althea Laurin won Paris gold with a high kick in the final seconds of a 2-0 final over Svetlana Osipova. It was France's first taekwondo gold. Whether Laurin or any of the Paris heavyweights come back to defend is the open question of the final night.

The men's +80kg has an equally rich past. Arian Salimi beat Great Britain's Caden Cunningham for gold in Paris, and Cheick Sallah Cisse of Cote d'Ivoire, a Rio gold medalist at -80kg, took bronze in the heavier division.

Repechages build the drama toward the late gold medal fights. When the last taekwondo champion is decided, this hall will have its final roar.
