TRI01.blurb:
Before any other event at the 2028 Games hands out a medal, someone will win one here, at 7:30 on a Saturday morning with sand still on their feet. Triathlon hasn't opened the medal schedule since Sydney 2000.

The swim starts from the beach itself: a 1,000m lap, a 25m dash across the sand, then a 500m second lap. Eight bike laps with two tight turnarounds follow, then four laps of running through the Venice canals area, finishing where Venice Boulevard meets the sand.

If form holds, Cassandre Beaugrand arrives as the Paris champion who went unbeaten through the 2026 WTCS season. Whoever wants her title has to survive the bike first.
TRI01.potentialContendersIntro: Beaugrand won Paris 2024 gold and the 2026 world title, but the 2025 world champion and several podium regulars could push the pace. The 2028 field is still projected until the May 2028 qualification ranking settles it.

potentialContenders.name: Cassandre Beaugrand
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 champion who went unbeaten in the 2026 WTCS season and won the Pontevedra Grand Final for her second world title. The clear favorite if she keeps this form.

potentialContenders.name: Lisa Tertsch
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2025 world title in Wollongong and finished five seconds behind Beaugrand in London in 2026. A likely contender for the podium.

potentialContenders.name: Beth Potter
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalist and third in the final 2025 WTCS standings. A strong runner who could be in the mix if she makes the team.

potentialContenders.name: Léonie Périault
potentialContenders.note: Second in the final 2025 WTCS standings. Could give France two serious medal threats if she qualifies alongside Beaugrand.

potentialContenders.name: Taylor Knibb
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 Ironman World Championship in Kona and is collecting 2028 qualification points at standard distance. Her bike strength could shake up a home race if she makes the team.

TRI02.blurb:
Matthew Hauser beat Vasco Vilaça by 0.08 seconds at the 2026 Pontevedra Grand Final. He had already outsprinted him in Hamburg and London that season. If both are in the pack coming off the last canal lap in Venice, that rivalry could decide the Games title.

Then there's Alex Yee, the Paris champion, who ran 2:06:38 for the marathon and 13:27.79 for 5000m, and still finished third in Pontevedra after starting the run 50 seconds down. Give him a gap anywhere near that and nobody is safe.

The men race on Sunday at 7:30, a day after the women, on the same surf start and the same four-lap run.
TRI02.potentialContendersIntro: The men's field is projected from recent form, and the 2028 rosters are not set. The 2025 and 2026 world champions and the Paris 2024 gold medalist look like the strongest names.

potentialContenders.name: Matthew Hauser
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world champion who beat Vilaça by 0.08 seconds in Pontevedra and won Hamburg three years running. A likely contender with one of the best finishing kicks in the sport.

potentialContenders.name: Vasco Vilaça
potentialContenders.note: 2026 world champion who has lost several close sprints to Hauser. Could be a first-time Games medal threat for Portugal.

potentialContenders.name: Alex Yee
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalist who overtook Hayden Wilde in the final minute. He says he is fully focused on triathlon for 2028, and his run speed makes him dangerous from any deficit.

potentialContenders.name: Hayden Wilde
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalist who won the 2025 T100 world title and the 2026 Ironman 70.3 World Championship. Whether he targets the 2028 short-course race is unconfirmed.

potentialContenders.name: Morgan Pearson
potentialContenders.note: Won the World Triathlon Cup in San Pedro de la Paz in November 2026 and finished fourth at WTCS London. A possible home-team medal hope if he is selected.

TRI03.blurb:
Four athletes, each racing for barely twenty minutes, and one tag at a time decides everything. In 2028 the order flips to woman-man-woman-man, so the anchor leg now belongs to a man.

Each leg is a 350m swim from the shoreline, a 6.6km bike over two laps and a 1.6km run over two laps. There is almost no room to recover from a bad transition.

Paris ended in a three-way sprint, with Germany edging the United States and Great Britain. In Hamburg in 2026, Hungary's Csongor Lehmann pushed France's Dorian Coninx to the line. This is the last triathlon medal of the Games, and the crowd will have seen all of it before 10 a.m.
TRI03.potentialContendersIntro: Relay teams are built from individual stars, and the 2028 lineups are not set. France and the United States already hold places, and the remaining spots depend on the May 2028 relay ranking.

potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 Mixed Relay World Championships in Hamburg with Périault, Richard, Lombardi and Coninx, earning direct qualification. Beaugrand could strengthen the lineup if she's selected.

potentialContenders.name: Australia
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world champions by three seconds over France, with Sophie Linn, Luke Willian, Emma Jeffcoat and Matthew Hauser. If they qualify, a Hauser anchor is a threat.

potentialContenders.name: Germany

potentialContenders.name: Great Britain
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalist and bronze again at the 2026 world championships in Hamburg. Alex Yee could be a possible anchor if he is selected.

potentialContenders.name: United States
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalists and already guaranteed a place as host. Finished fourth in Hamburg in 2026 with Sereno, Rider, Spivey and Pearson, and will chase a home medal.

TTE01.blurb:
A world No. 1 who reached the summit at 19, and a mixed doubles bracket where China keeps more than one weapon in reserve. That is the opening morning.

Japan's Sora Matsushima became the first non-Chinese man atop the rankings since Timo Boll in 2018. If he makes the team, his round of 64 match is the first public test of that status. In the mixed doubles round of 16, three-time world champions Wang Chuqin and Sun Yingsha could be on the table.

Hall 3 is a converted exhibit hall, so you sit close enough to hear the ball snap off the table. Early rounds like this reward anyone who wants to see stars before the pressure peaks.

TTE02.blurb:
Doubles has been gone from the table tennis program for two decades, and this is the session where it comes back. Nobody in the building has seen a Games doubles match since 2004.

The round of 16 is a fast, cooperative game of rotating partners and tight timing. Pairs with years together tend to beat superior individuals who don't mesh. France's Alexis and Félix Lebrun, brothers who took world bronze in Doha in 2025, could bring a home-away-from-home crowd with them. On the women's side, Japan's Satsuki Odo and Sakura Yokoi are the kind of pair that can make a seeded team nervous.

Sit close and watch the footwork, because nothing here is slow.

TTE03.blurb:
Fan Zhendong won men's singles gold in Paris, and Chen Meng won the women's title, but both are far from certain to be back. That leaves this night session as a look at who might take the crown.

Watch the men's draw. Japan's Sora Matsushima led the 2026 World Cup final 3-2 before losing 4-3 to Wang Chuqin, a result that sums up the current gap between China and everybody else: one game. The women's field is just as crowded, with Sun Yingsha and Miwa Harimoto near the top.

It is a late start under indoor lights, and a round of 64 session is the best place to spot a dark horse.

TTE04.blurb:
Three straight world titles, and then a loss. Wang Chuqin and Sun Yingsha have owned mixed doubles, but at the 2026 Asian Games their teammates Lin Shidong and Kuai Man beat them for gold.

That makes this quarterfinal a window into a Chinese selection question, not just a bracket. Whoever China sends, South Korea's Lim Jong-hoon and Shin Yu-bin, world bronze medalists in 2025, and Japan's Yoshimura and Odo, the 2025 world finalists, will line up for the upset.

It's a morning session in a close hall, with best-of-five matches that can turn in two rallies. Stay for the singles round of 64 that fills out the rest of the session.

TTE05.blurb:
Truls Möregårdh knocked out the top seed in Paris and rode the upset all the way to a final. That's what an afternoon round of 64 can offer: a name nobody circled who changes the bracket.

The Swede is a good example of the risk and the reward. He won WTT Champions Macao in September 2026, then pulled out of Frankfurt with an injury, so his health will matter. The women's side has its own surge in Japan's Miwa Harimoto, who won the 2026 titles in Yokohama and Macao.

There is no cushion in single elimination. One bad set, and a top-five player can be on the way out before the evening crowd arrives.

TTE06.blurb:
This is the first night when the mixed doubles draw narrows to four pairs, and the first time a table tennis medal match feels close.

China has two leading pairs and has been switching between them. Wang Chuqin and Sun Yingsha won three straight world titles, including a 3-1 win over Japan in the 2025 Doha final. Then Lin Shidong and Kuai Man beat them at the 2026 Asian Games. If either gets through, South Korea's Lim Jong-hoon and Shin Yu-bin, the Asian Games top seeds, are waiting.

The hall is small and the finish is after 11 PM, so expect a loud, tight crowd that knows every point matters. A round of 64 singles session runs alongside.

TTE07.blurb:
Men's and women's doubles quarterfinals mean two sets of pairs fighting for the first doubles medals in 24 years, and the stakes show in every long rally.

The Lebrun brothers are the story for many fans. Alexis and Félix, the world bronze medalists in 2025, play a fast, shared style that sometimes looks like one player in two bodies. On the women's side, China's Wang Manyu and Sun Yingsha were world No. 1 in 2026 and carry the weight of a program that wants every gold.

It's a morning session at close quarters, with a round of 64 singles card mixed in. Doubles is quick, and you may miss a turning point if you blink.

TTE08.blurb:
Félix Lebrun was the 17-year-old who turned a Paris crowd into a wall of noise on the way to singles bronze. In Los Angeles, he'd be the visitor, and this afternoon round of 64 is a good place to see what that looks like.

His 2026 was uneven. He won WTT Champions Chongqing, beating Wen Ruibo 4-1, but lost in the Yokohama quarterfinals as second seed. He sits at No. 2 in the world, behind Japan's Sora Matsushima.

Locals can look for the USA's Kanak Jha, ranked No. 24 in October 2026. A home-table underdog in a tiny hall is a real draw.

TTE09.blurb:
The first table tennis medals of the 2028 Games are decided here, and the room will know it.

China took every gold in Paris, including mixed doubles, and the question for the whole tournament starts right here. Wang Chuqin and Sun Yingsha are the Paris gold medalists and three-time world champions, but they lost the 2026 Asian Games final to teammates Lin Shidong and Kuai Man. Japan's Yoshimura and Odo, beaten 3-1 in the 2025 Doha final, and South Korea's Lim Jong-hoon and Shin Yu-bin are the obvious pairs to break the streak.

The bronze match comes first, then the gold match, after 9 PM in a small hall where every point is loud.

TTE10.blurb:
The men's doubles semifinals are the best argument for bringing the event back. Two years of results show it's the least predictable doubles draw in the sport.

Japan's Hiroto Shinozuka and Shunsuke Togami won the 2025 world title as the second seeds. The Lebrun brothers, Alexis and Félix, took bronze in Doha and have a fast, instinctive style. Togami also beat South Korea's Oh Jun-sung 3-2 in Frankfurt in November 2026, which shows how close Japan's depth is.

A singles round of 32 session runs alongside. You will see the world's top ten at close range as the draw begins to separate real threats from the rest.

TTE11.blurb:
The reigning women's singles champion isn't expected to be here. Chen Meng indicated after Paris that it would be her last Games, so the women's draw is more open than it has been in a decade.

Sun Yingsha, the 2025 world champion and No. 2 in October 2026, is the obvious favorite. Japan's Miwa Harimoto and China's Wang Yidi follow her in the rankings. On the men's side, Sora Matsushima, who reached No. 1 at 19, leads a field that includes Félix Lebrun, Tomokazu Harimoto, Truls Möregårdh, and Wang Chuqin.

The round of 32 is when the seeds start meeting real opposition, and the hall is still small enough to lean over a rail.

TTE12.blurb:
China may not be the favorite here. No men's doubles title was won by a Chinese pair at the 2025 Worlds, so this is one of the sport's least certain gold medals.

Japan's Hiroto Shinozuka and Shunsuke Togami won in Doha as second seeds. Chinese Taipei's Lin Yun-ju and Kao Cheng-jui took silver, and two French pairs shared bronze: the Lebrun brothers and Esteban Dorr with Florian Bourrassaud. With no defending champion, a new name goes on the list tonight.

Bronze first, then gold, in a small hall after 9 PM. The first men's doubles gold in 24 years will be awarded about two feet from the front row.

China's Wang Manyu is in a good spot for a puzzle. She won the 2025 world women's doubles title with Kuai Man, but was the No. 1 pair in mid-2026 with Sun Yingsha. Whom she plays with could be one of the more interesting decisions in the draw.

The semifinals look for answers. Japan's Miwa Harimoto and Miyuu Kihara and South Korea's Shin Yu-bin and Ryu Han-na both took world bronze in 2025, and either could unsettle China.

The session also includes round-of-32 singles, so you can watch a doubles semifinal then walk up to a table where Sora Matsushima or Hina Hayata might be playing.

TTE14.blurb:
The last round of 32 is when the bracket tells you what you've been hoping to see: either a favorite survives, or a swing player takes advantage.

Truls Möregårdh, the Paris silver medalist, is the one to watch. He beat Lin Shidong 4-3 in the 2025 Malmö final and Hugo Calderano in Macao in September 2026, then pulled out of Frankfurt with an injury. His health is the question mark in any singles draw.

Tomokazu Harimoto, the Frankfurt champion after beating Patrick Franziska 4-2, will be hoping to keep winning. Wang Chuqin, the 2025 world champion, is China's best chance of denying them.

TTE15.blurb:
Women's doubles hasn't had a medal ceremony at the Games since 2004, and the first one in 24 years is tonight. There is no defending champion, which makes the room feel strangely open.

China's Wang Manyu and Kuai Man won the 2025 world title in straight games over Austria's Sofia Polcanova and Romania's Bernadette Szocs, a cross-national pair who tend to play like they've known each other for years. Wang Manyu and Sun Yingsha were world No. 1 by mid-2026, and Sun could also be entered in singles and mixed doubles.

Bronze first, then gold, starting after 9 PM in a hall that is small enough for every cheer to be heard from the first row to the last.

TTE16.blurb:
Odd sight for this sport: the top of the men's world rankings is Japanese, and China's best man sits fifth. Sora Matsushima reached No. 1 in October 2026 and was still there at the end of the month, so the first round-of-16 session could show a shifting balance of power before lunch.

Hall 3 is an exhibit hall turned arena, so fans sit close to the tables. A morning crowd in a room this size hears every ball clack off the rubber.

The women's draw runs alongside, and Sun Yingsha, the 2025 world champion, is the name to find on the order of play if she makes the team.

TTE17.blurb:
Paris fell for Félix Lebrun, who took bronze in front of a home crowd. The 2028 Games could bring him back as one of the favorites, ranked world No. 2 in October 2026 and winner of WTT Champions Chongqing that year.

His brother Alexis, ranked No. 8, could be across the draw. Few sessions in the round of 16 offer a family storyline like that.

The afternoon block also lines up deep Japanese and Chinese fields in both draws. In a hall where you sit a few rows from the table, a Lebrun rally at full speed is something to see up close. Watch his fitness, since he was listed as withdrawn from WTT Champions Frankfurt in November 2026.

TTE18.blurb:
Truls Möregårdh already knows what a Paris surprise feels like. He knocked out the top seed there and reached the final, and a late night in Hall 3 is where he could try to do it again. He won WTT Champions Macao in September 2026 and was ranked No. 4, though an injury forced him out of Frankfurt that November.

This evening block closes the round of 16 and sets the quarterfinals, so the stakes feel different from the morning matches. Hugo Calderano, the 2025 world runner-up, is the type of player who can wreck a bracket.

Home fans may be looking for Kanak Jha, ranked 24th in October 2026, if he is on the team.

TTE19.blurb:
The throne is empty, or at least unclaimed. Chen Meng has said Paris would be her last Games, and Fan Zhendong has not said whether he will return. The first quarterfinal session could be the first look at a singles field without either champion.

With eight players left in each draw and a limit of two per country, a quarterfinal can turn on one hot streak. Wang Chuqin, the 2025 world champion, and Sun Yingsha, ranked world No. 2 in October 2026, are the names the draw is built around.

In Hall 3, a fifth-game decider is close enough that you can watch players read the spin.

TTE20.blurb:
Last four spots, and two Japanese siblings who could be sitting in the same hall. Tomokazu Harimoto won WTT Champions Frankfurt in November 2026, and his sister Miwa won both Yokohama and Macao that year. If both qualify, this session could put them in quarterfinals on the same afternoon.

The men's draw has other threats. Félix Lebrun, the Paris bronze medalist, was ranked No. 2 in October 2026, and Truls Möregårdh, the Paris silver medalist, is a veteran of big matches.

With semifinal places at stake, the crowd noise in Hall 3 bounces off the walls of a closed room.

TTE21.blurb:
The last quarterfinal session of the Friday block runs late, with eight players left in each draw and a room that has been loud all day. This is where upsets tend to cluster, and 2026 gave plenty of reasons to expect them.

Jang Woojin won his first WTT Champions title in Montpellier. Simon Gauzy beat Tomokazu Harimoto 3-0 there. Patrick Franziska came back from 2-0 down against Alexis Lebrun and saved four match points.

Then there is the two-player limit per country, which keeps the draw from becoming a Chinese or Japanese procession. Hall 3 is small enough that every scream carries.

TTE22.blurb:
Four women are left, and Sun Yingsha is the one the other three will be thinking about. She won back-to-back world titles, passed 200 consecutive weeks at No. 1 in March 2026, and then saved two match points against Hana Goda in a seven-game World Cup quarterfinal.

That match shows both sides of her. She has the cushion of a champion, but she can be taken the distance. Kuai Man beat her in Chongqing, and an ankle injury cost her a December 2025 semifinal.

With a two-player cap per country, only so many Chinese players can get this far. Hall 3 should hold its breath at 10-all.

TTE23.blurb:
China has won every women's singles gold from 1988 through Paris 2024. That is the number hanging over this final, and it is what makes a night of table tennis feel like a siege.

Chen Meng has said Paris was her last Games, so a new champion is coming no matter what. The favorite is probably Sun Yingsha, who beat Wang Manyu in a seven-game world final in 2025 and again at the 2026 World Cup, though Kuai Man proved she can beat her.

The bronze match opens the session, then the gold. In a small hall, a 4-3 final means everyone around the table feels each point.

TTE24.blurb:
Hugo Calderano has beaten Wang Chuqin when it counted, in the 2025 World Cup semifinals. Wang Chuqin then beat him 4-1 in the world final. A men's semifinal could bring them back together, and the story keeps turning.

Wang Chuqin holds world titles in singles, men's doubles and mixed doubles, and he won the 2026 World Cup after trailing Sora Matsushima 3-2. Truls Möregårdh, the Paris silver medalist, and Liang Jingkun both took bronze at the 2025 Worlds.

In the afternoon, with only four men left, every rally runs long. Rows near the tables hear grunts and shoes squeaking on the floor.

TTE25.blurb:
Fan Zhendong has not said whether he is coming back. That uncertainty sits over the whole men's final, because the Paris 2024 gold medalist left the world rankings in December 2024, said he was not retiring, and beat Wang Chuqin twice in 2025.

If he makes it, he would be the champion against the field. If he doesn't, Wang Chuqin, the 2025 world champion and 2026 World Cup winner, is the favorite to carry China's hopes.

The bronze match comes first, then the gold. A crowd packed into Hall 3 for the final match won't be long on silence.

TTE26.blurb:
Table tennis has never had a mixed team medal at the Games, and this is where the new event begins. At the World Cup format, the lower-ranked captain gets to choose whether men's or women's doubles is played first in the closing doubles, so tactics start before the first serve.

Ties are a series of doubles and singles matches with games counted cumulatively, which means a team can lose a match and still be fine. China has won every Mixed Team World Cup since 2023, and the rest of the groups are playing to catch up.

In Hall 3, the long day session is a chance to find out which teams have real balance.

TTE27.blurb:
Eleven-four, eleven-four, eleven-six. That was the score when Wang Chuqin and Sun Yingsha opened the 2025 Mixed Team World Cup final against Japan's Sora Matsushima and Satsuki Odo. It shows how fast a tie can be set up in this format.

Groups 3 and 4 take the floor for the first time at night. Teams will be trying to avoid an early hole, because the leading teams move on to the quarterfinals.

The evening session in Hall 3 is long, and the crowd should be close enough to feel each small swing in a doubles match.

TTE28.blurb:
By the second round, the group tables stop being theoretical. A team that lost an opener now needs wins, and a team that won can start worrying about seeding.

China arrives with the biggest reputation after taking both team golds at Paris 2024 and winning the 2025 Mixed Team World Cup. Wang Manyu said that final showed the Chinese team's strength, and Chinese association president Wang Liqin called the format transformative.

The mixed event replaces the men's and women's team events of 2008 to 2024. Hall 3 is cozy for that kind of change, and the day runs from morning into afternoon.

TTE29.blurb:
Depth is the whole point here. A mixed team needs men and women who can both play doubles and singles, and a country with one superstar can still be stuck.

Brazil could be the test case. Hugo Calderano, the 2025 world runner-up, is a possible singles anchor, but only if a mixed team qualifies around him. Japan shows the other side. Hina Hayata won a singles bronze and the women's team silver at Paris 2024, and Japan reached the 2025 Mixed Team World Cup final.

In Hall 3 at night, a team with two strong halves gets to play like it.

TTE30.blurb:
This is the last day of group play, and the knockout bracket is the prize. If the 2028 event follows the World Cup model, group standings decide seeding, with first facing fourth and second facing third in the semifinals.

That adds tension to ties that might otherwise be quiet. A team that thinks it has already qualified may still fight for position.

China has won every Mixed Team World Cup since 2023. Wang Chuqin and Sun Yingsha, the 2025 world mixed doubles champions, won the opening doubles of the 2025 final 11-4, 11-4, 11-6. Hall 3 should be loud through the afternoon.

TTE31.blurb:
Nobody gets a medal on this night, but plenty of teams can lose their path to one. Round 3 of group play is where seeding gets settled, and the quarterfinals start the next morning.

The format rewards depth. Every tie is a race to eight games across five three-game sets, opening with mixed doubles and closing with women's doubles. A team with one cold singles player can still survive if its pairs click.

Hall 3 is an exhibit hall converted to an arena, so you sit close to the tables. You hear every ball clip the edge and every coach bark between points. With two groups playing, you can pick a table and watch a bracket spot get won.

TTE32.blurb:
China has won every Mixed Team World Cup since the format began in 2023, and that unbeaten run is the weight sitting on every other team in the hall. This morning session is where the quarterfinals begin and the chasers get their first real swing.

The cracks are small but real. China's men dropped group-stage ties to South Korea and Sweden at the 2026 World Team Championships, ending a 26-year team-match winning streak, then won the title anyway. That tells you the margin is thin, and also that China recovers fast.

Two ties, five sets each, one table in your sightline. Mixed doubles opens, and the first 11 points can swing a whole afternoon.

potentialContenders.note: Projected quarterfinalist. Dang Qiu and Annette Kaufmann won the opening mixed doubles in an 8-5 win over Hong Kong, China in 2025.

potentialContenders.name: France
potentialContenders.note: Could appear. Beat Japan in Stage 2 of the 2025 event, with Felix Lebrun and Prithika Pavade among the key performers.

TTE33.blurb:
Evening session, one loss from elimination, and the Hall 3 crowd has time to settle in. This is the second set of quarterfinals, and the winners go to Friday's semifinals.

The Japan-Germany rivalry is the one to watch if the draw delivers it. Japan beat Germany 8-3 in the 2025 group stage, but Germany's Dang Qiu, Patrick Franziska and Benedikt Duda have all sat in the world top 10, and Annette Kaufmann and Nina Mittelham are the kind of women's players who produce upsets.

Then there are the Lebrun brothers, Sweden's Truls Möregårdh and Korea's grinders. Any of them can turn a quiet Thursday night into a long one.
TTE33.potentialContendersIntro: Pairings are unconfirmed, so these are teams that could appear in the evening quarterfinals.

potentialContenders.name: Japan
potentialContenders.note: Likely contender. Beat Germany 8-3 in the 2025 group stage and were runners-up to China in both team events at the 2026 World Team Championships.

potentialContenders.name: Germany
potentialContenders.note: Projected threat. Depth in the men's draw (Dang Qiu, Franziska, Duda) and upset potential from Kaufmann and Mittelham.

potentialContenders.name: France
potentialContenders.note: Could appear. The Lebrun-led men's team won bronze at the 2026 World Team Championships, and Felix and Alexis Lebrun were in the 2025 mixed lineup.

potentialContenders.name: Korea Republic
potentialContenders.note: Reached the 2025 semifinals and lost 8-3 to China. Their men beat China in the group stage at the 2026 World Team Championships.

potentialContenders.name: Sweden
potentialContenders.note: Possible contender if they qualify. Truls Möregårdh won men's singles silver at Paris 2024, and Sweden were runners-up in the men's team event.

TTE34.blurb:
In 2025, China beat Korea Republic 8-3 in a semifinal that was closer than the score. The Koreans took more games than they had in their earlier group meeting and still could not find a way through.

That is the sort of tie you might see here: one team that has already seen China's pairings and adjusted, and one that adjusts back. Wang Chuqin and Sun Yingsha, the world No. 1 mixed doubles pair at the end of 2025, can set the tone in the first three games.

Midday on a Friday, with a gold medal match one day away. The losers still get a bronze match the next afternoon, but everyone in this hall wants Saturday night.
TTE34.potentialContendersIntro: Semifinal lineups aren't known, so these are projected players based on 2025 and 2026 form. Likely to appear if China reaches this semifinal.

potentialContenders.name: Wang Chuqin
potentialContenders.note: Projected starter. Part of the world No. 1 mixed doubles pair with Sun Yingsha at the end of 2025, and won the 2026 Men's World Cup final 4-3 over Sora Matsushima.

potentialContenders.name: Sun Yingsha
potentialContenders.note: Likely starter. Finished the 2025 Mixed Team World Cup without losing a game, winning 21 games across seven matches.

potentialContenders.name: Kuai Man
potentialContenders.note: Could appear. Took her deciding game 11-6 in the 2025 semifinal against Korea Republic to put China up 5-1.

potentialContenders.name: Dang Qiu
potentialContenders.note: Could appear if Germany advances. The doubles specialist won the opening mixed doubles with Annette Kaufmann in Germany's 2025 quarterfinal win.

TTE35.blurb:
Last time out, Japan lost the final 8-1, and the loss took a lot of the shine off getting there. Here they could get another try, and a semifinal is the chance to arrive at the final in better shape.

Japan is the team with the clearest path to challenging China. They were runners-up in both team events at the 2026 World Team Championships, their first men's world team final since 2016, and Sora Matsushima lost the 2026 Men's World Cup final in seven games. Germany beat them for nothing, but they did stay competitive in group play and have the depth to make a tie messy.

This is a late Friday night session, which means the loudest crowd of the week so far.
TTE35.potentialContendersIntro: Pairings are unconfirmed, but Japan and Germany met in this slot at the 2025 Mixed Team World Cup, so these are projected players if either team reaches the semifinal.

potentialContenders.name: Sora Matsushima
potentialContenders.note: Likely starter. Played mixed doubles in the 2025 final and was runner-up at the 2026 Men's World Cup, losing 4-3 to Wang Chuqin.

potentialContenders.name: Satsuki Odo
potentialContenders.note: Projected mixed doubles partner for Matsushima, as in the 2025 final.

potentialContenders.name: Tomokazu Harimoto
potentialContenders.note: Could appear. Seeded higher than any German man at the 2025 Mixed Team World Cup and on Japan's 2026 world team roster.

potentialContenders.name: Hina Hayata
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 women's singles bronze medalist. Lost to Wang Manyu in the 2026 women's world team final decider.

potentialContenders.name: Dang Qiu
potentialContenders.note: Could appear if Germany advances. A former world top-10 player and Germany's key doubles piece.

TTE36.blurb:
Nobody dreams of the bronze match, and yet this one will be different. It is the first mixed team bronze match ever played at the Games, and for whichever team wins, a medal around the neck on the final Saturday.

The feelings are raw. These are the two teams who lost semifinals less than a day earlier and have to reset in time for a midday start. France could bring Felix Lebrun, who won men's singles bronze at Paris 2024 and beat Tomokazu Harimoto 3-0 in the 2025 event. Germany's pairs have the kind of chemistry that can steal a tie.

Hall 3 is small, and in a bronze match you can watch players hurting and fighting from a few rows away.
TTE36.potentialContendersIntro: The semifinal losers are unknown, so these are projected players based on recent form, flagged as speculation.

potentialContenders.name: Felix Lebrun
potentialContenders.note: Could appear if France is here. Won men's singles bronze at Paris 2024 and beat Tomokazu Harimoto 3-0 at the 2025 Mixed Team World Cup.

potentialContenders.name: Dang Qiu
potentialContenders.note: Possible contender. A former world top-10 player who won the opening mixed doubles with Annette Kaufmann at the 2025 event.

potentialContenders.name: Annette Kaufmann
potentialContenders.note: Likely to appear if Germany lands in this match. Her doubles chemistry with Dang Qiu has already produced results.

potentialContenders.name: Shin Yu-bin
potentialContenders.note: Could appear if Korea reaches the bronze match. Part of South Korea's mixed doubles bronze at Paris 2024, and Korea won women's team bronze there too.

TTE37.blurb:
Eight games decide it, and the first three belong to the mixed doubles. In the 2025 final, Wang Chuqin and Sun Yingsha beat Japan's Sora Matsushima and Satsuki Odo 11-4, 11-4, 11-6, and the result of the tie was clear before the second set began.

That is the pressure on everyone else. China has won every Mixed Team World Cup, including a third straight title in Chengdu, and won all five table tennis golds at Paris 2024. The question for the first mixed team gold medal match at the Games is whether anyone can stretch China to a deciding set.

Saturday night in a tight Hall 3, with the crowd probably on its feet by the second point.
TTE37.potentialContendersIntro: The final is unconfirmed, but China is the projected favorite and Japan the most likely challenger based on 2025 and 2026 results. Ma Long, Fan Zhendong and Chen Meng left the world rankings in 2024, so their 2028 status is unclear.

potentialContenders.name: Wang Chuqin
potentialContenders.note: Projected starter. World No. 1 mixed doubles pair with Sun Yingsha at the end of 2025, and 2026 Men's World Cup champion.

potentialContenders.name: Sun Yingsha
potentialContenders.note: Likely starter. Did not lose a game at the 2025 Mixed Team World Cup, winning 21 straight across mixed doubles and women's singles.

potentialContenders.name: Wang Manyu
potentialContenders.note: Could appear. Beat Hina Hayata 11-7, 11-7, 11-5 in the deciding rubber of the 2026 women's world team final.

potentialContenders.name: Sora Matsushima
potentialContenders.note: Likely starter if Japan reaches the final. Runner-up at the 2026 Men's World Cup and mixed doubles player in the 2025 final.

potentialContenders.name: Hina Hayata
potentialContenders.note: Could appear. Paris 2024 women's singles bronze medalist and a key player on Japan's runner-up women's team in London.

VBV01.blurb:
Somebody has to hit the first serve of the tournament, and it happens at nine in the morning on a wide public beach in Long Beach. The sport grew up in Southern California, and this is the first time it gets a Games stage in its home region.

The morning light is soft, the Pacific sits behind the court, and the stands fill with the people who actually play on sand like this. Nobody has seen the pool draws yet, which is part of the pull. Early pool play is where you spot a pair before the bracket makes them a headline.

Three matches, no pressure to wait for a final. Get there early.
VBV01.potentialContendersIntro: No 2028 rosters or pool draws are set, but several continental champions have already earned quota places for their countries. If their national committees send them, these pairs could appear.

potentialContenders.name: Melissa Humana-Paredes / Brandie Wilkerson
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalists who won the 2026 NORCECA title, which earned Canada a women's quota place. Whether they are the pair Canada sends is a committee decision.

potentialContenders.name: Trevor Crabb / Chase Budinger
potentialContenders.note: 2026 NORCECA men's champions, who gave the host nation its maximum two men's places. Budinger also competed at Paris 2024.

potentialContenders.name: Katja Stam / Raisa Schoon
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 European women's title unbeaten in six matches and earned the Netherlands a quota place. Likely contenders if they stay together.

potentialContenders.name: Mark Nicolaidis / Izac Carracher
potentialContenders.note: 2026 Asian champions who came back from a set down in the semifinals. Could be a dangerous pool opponent.

VBV02.blurb:
Thirteen Tour golds, a world title, and a fourth straight run at the top of the sport: Sweden's David Ahman and Jonatan Hellvig arrive as the pair everyone else is chasing. They were 22 when they won Paris 2024, and they have not slowed down.

Afternoon sessions at Alamitos Beach are long and bright, with sun on the sand and wind that can change a rally from one side to the other. Pool play is where depth shows. A favorite can be tested by a sharp serving team on a gusty day.

Four matches over four hours, with plenty of time to settle in and watch the real contenders work.
VBV02.potentialContendersIntro: This looks like a men's-heavy window, and the picks below are projections only, since no pool draws or rosters are confirmed. Sweden can send at most two men's teams.

potentialContenders.name: David Ahman / Jonatan Hellvig
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalists and 2025 world champions. They won the 2026 Joao Pessoa and Ostrava Elites. If Sweden selects them, they would be the team to beat.

potentialContenders.name: Jacob Holting Nilsson / Elmer Andersson
potentialContenders.note: 2026 European champions who earned Sweden a men's quota place and were described as FIVB World Ranking leaders in August 2026. They lost the 2025 world final to Ahman and Hellvig.

potentialContenders.name: Andre Stein / Renato Lima
potentialContenders.note: 2026 South American champions who beat Ahman and Hellvig in an Ostrava pool match. They are a likely spoiler.

VBV03.blurb:
The best women's final in the sport's Games history went three sets, and the question here is whether its two sides can do it again. Brazil's Ana Patricia and Duda beat Canada's Brandie Wilkerson and Melissa Humana-Paredes 26-24, 12-21, 15-10 in Paris. It was Brazil's first title in the event since 1996.

The backdrop has shifted since. Duda announced a break from competition until November 2026 to prepare for this race, and Ana Patricia partnered with Carolina Horta Maximo in the meantime. Canada won the 2026 NORCECA title.

After 8 PM, Long Beach cools off and the lights take over. The court glows against a dark ocean, and the crowd settles in for three matches.
VBV03.potentialContendersIntro: These are projections for the women's matches, since pool draws are not out and no rosters are confirmed.

potentialContenders.name: Ana Patricia / Duda
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalists. They lost the March 2026 Joao Pessoa final in straight sets to Cruz and Brasher, and Duda's break is a storyline. They are likely contenders if they reunite.

potentialContenders.name: Melissa Humana-Paredes / Brandie Wilkerson
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalists who won the 2026 NORCECA title. Canada's only women's medal in the sport.

potentialContenders.name: Kristen Cruz / Taryn Brasher
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world silver medalists who beat Ana Patricia and Duda for the 2026 Joao Pessoa title. A home-crowd threat if they are selected.

potentialContenders.name: Katja Stam / Raisa Schoon
potentialContenders.note: 2026 European champions and a potential dark horse.

VBV04.blurb:
Sunday morning in Long Beach, and the home crowd gets its first real look at the American hopes. Beach volleyball was born in these communities, so a lot of these seats will be filled by people who learned the game on nearby sand.

Trevor Crabb and Chase Budinger came through the 2026 NORCECA final in three sets against Mexico, 17-21, 21-16, 19-17, to give the USA its maximum two men's places. On the women's side, Southern California natives Kelly Cheng and Megan Kraft reached the NORCECA final unbeaten before losing to Canada. That loss left the second U.S. women's spot open.

A 9 AM start means sunshine, a morning chill, and a lot of noise.
VBV04.potentialContendersIntro: U.S. teams for 2028 are not named, since national committees choose them. These pairs are the likeliest to appear if they are picked.

potentialContenders.name: Trevor Crabb / Chase Budinger
potentialContenders.note: 2026 NORCECA champions who beat Canada's Schachter and Pickett in the semifinals. A likely U.S. men's pair.

potentialContenders.name: Kelly Cheng / Megan Kraft
potentialContenders.note: Partners since January 2026, they took bronze in their first event together at Joao Pessoa. They lost the NORCECA final 21-16, 27-25. Their 2028 spot is not secured.

potentialContenders.name: Kristen Cruz / Taryn Brasher
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world silver medalists who won the March 2026 Joao Pessoa Elite. They could be the other U.S. women's entry.

VBV05.blurb:
The men's final in Paris ended 21-10, 21-13, which tells you how far Germany's Nils Ehlers was from the top. Since then, he has found a new partner and a new path. Ehlers and Lui Wust won the 2026 Hamburg Elite over Norway's Anders Mol and Christian Sorum, the first Tour gold for both.

That is the thread through an afternoon where past medalists look for a second act. Mol and Sorum, the 2020 Games champions, took bronze in Paris. Canada's Wilkerson and Humana-Paredes hold the only women's medal in the sport for their country.

Four matches fill the long, bright afternoon. Bring a hat.
VBV05.potentialContendersIntro: These men's pairs are projections for the afternoon, since neither pool draws nor rosters have been announced. Norway has not yet earned a men's quota place.

potentialContenders.name: Nils Ehlers / Lui Wust
potentialContenders.note: Ehlers won Paris 2024 silver with Clemens Wickler. This pairing won the 2026 Hamburg Elite, 22-20, 21-9 in the final. They could be Germany's team if they qualify.

potentialContenders.name: Anders Mol / Christian Sorum
potentialContenders.note: 2020 Games champions and Paris 2024 bronze medalists. Mol plans to try to qualify with Sorum for a third Games, so they are likely contenders if they qualify.

potentialContenders.name: Brandie Wilkerson / Melissa Humana-Paredes
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalists who won the 2026 NORCECA title for Canada's women's quota place.

VBV06.blurb:
A loss in pool play does not usually mean much to a champion. It did make Sweden's Ahman and Hellvig pay attention at the 2026 Ostrava Elite, when Brazil's Andre Stein and Renato Lima beat them in the pool before Sweden went on to win the tournament for a third straight year.

That is the kind of match this session can offer. Sweden's golden pair against Brazil's South American champions is the sort of contest the pool format makes possible.

Night sessions bring cooler air and a lit court against a black Pacific, with the crowd leaning in on every serve. It ends close to 11 PM and feels like a final.
VBV06.potentialContendersIntro: No pool draws are set, so this is a projection for the men's matches only.

potentialContenders.name: David Ahman / Jonatan Hellvig
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalists. They won the 2026 Ostrava Elite for a third straight year, though they dropped a pool match there to Stein and Lima. They are likely title contenders if Sweden selects them.

potentialContenders.name: Andre Stein / Renato Lima
potentialContenders.note: 2026 South American champions who secured a men's quota place for Brazil. They beat Sweden's top pair in pool play at Ostrava.

potentialContenders.name: Jacob Holting Nilsson / Elmer Andersson
potentialContenders.note: 2026 European champions and a second Swedish pair in the mix. Sweden's national committee decides who fills its places.

VBV07.blurb:
Australia swept both Asian titles in 2026, and Monday morning is a chance to see why. Mark Nicolaidis and Izac Carracher won an all-Australian men's final and, in the semifinals, came back from a set down against Qatar, 14-21, 24-22, 15-11.

That comeback instinct is what a pool-play crowd wants to see. The women's champions Stefanie Fejes and Taliqua Clancy closed their final with a 21-16 second set.

A 9 AM start on a Monday suits people who like seeing a pair they have not heard of play with nothing to lose. The marine layer may still be rolling off the beach, and the court is yours before the afternoon heat.
VBV07.potentialContendersIntro: Australia has earned one quota place per gender, but its committee will choose the athletes. Qatar has not been confirmed in the field.

potentialContenders.name: Mark Nicolaidis / Izac Carracher
potentialContenders.note: 2026 Asian men's champions who beat Thomas Hodges and Ben Hood in the final. They won a three-set semifinal against Qatar.

potentialContenders.name: Stefanie Fejes / Taliqua Clancy
potentialContenders.note: 2026 Asian women's champions who earned Australia's women's quota place. A likely pool-play threat if selected.

potentialContenders.name: Cherif Younousse / Ahmed Tijan
potentialContenders.note: The Qatari pair pushed Australia to three sets at the 2026 Asian championships. They could appear only if they qualify.

VBV08.blurb:
Ahman and Hellvig were 22 when they won Sweden's first beach volleyball gold in Paris, which tells you something about how long this partnership could run. Their 2026 started with the Joao Pessoa Elite in March. It was their first event back since winning the world title.

Sometimes titles come easy. At Ostrava, Qatar's Younousse and Tijan withdrew injured at 10-10 in the third set of a semifinal, which gave Sweden the win. It was a reminder that luck matters too.

The afternoon at Alamitos gives you four matches and the sun on the sand. Look for the pairs that grind.
VBV08.potentialContendersIntro: These are projections, since pool draws and rosters have not been announced.

potentialContenders.name: David Ahman / Jonatan Hellvig
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalists and 2025 world champions who returned in March 2026 to win Joao Pessoa. If Sweden selects them, they are a top contender.

potentialContenders.name: Cherif Younousse / Ahmed Tijan
potentialContenders.note: Reached the 2026 Ostrava semifinals and the 2026 Asian semifinals. Could appear if they qualify.

potentialContenders.name: Ana Patricia / Duda
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalists. Duda paused competition until November 2026 to prepare for the qualifying race, so their 2028 status is not confirmed.

VBV09.blurb:
By Monday night, pool tables start to matter. A loss can force a team into a tougher road, and the Round of 16 line is close enough to see.

The matchups here could come from the best recent results. Canada's Humana-Paredes and Wilkerson beat Americans Cheng and Kraft 21-16, 27-25 to win the NORCECA title. Germany's Ehlers and Wust beat Norway's Mol and Sorum in Hamburg, a match Mol and Sorum entered after a 16-21, 24-22, 19-17 semifinal comeback.

The lights are on, the temperature has dropped, and the stands should be loud. Late in pool play, it is never casual.
VBV09.potentialContendersIntro: Pool draws are not out, so these are projected contenders, not announced matchups.

potentialContenders.name: Melissa Humana-Paredes / Brandie Wilkerson
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalists who beat the Americans in the 2026 NORCECA final.

potentialContenders.name: Kelly Cheng / Megan Kraft
potentialContenders.note: 2026 NORCECA runners-up who are still working for the second U.S. women's place. The home crowd would be behind them if selected.

potentialContenders.name: Nils Ehlers / Lui Wust
potentialContenders.note: 2026 Hamburg Elite champions who could represent Germany if they qualify.

potentialContenders.name: Anders Mol / Christian Sorum
potentialContenders.note: 2020 Games champions who reached the Hamburg final. Likely contenders if they qualify.

VBV10.blurb:
Anders Mol has said he plans to come back. After winning the 2026 Montreal Elite without dropping a set, which was their third straight win there, Mol stepped away from the Tour for many months. His plan is to chase a third Games with Christian Sorum.

If they get here, it is a veteran pair among the favorites. They already lost the 2026 European title match to Sweden's Holting Nilsson and Andersson, who also dropped a quarterfinal to Canada's Sam Schachter and Jake Pickett in Montreal.

That is the beauty of a morning at Alamitos: the lesser-known teams can ruin a famous name before lunch.
VBV10.potentialContendersIntro: Norway has not earned a men's quota place yet, so Mol and Sorum are projections. All of the pairs below are possibilities, not confirmed entries.

potentialContenders.name: Anders Mol / Christian Sorum
potentialContenders.note: 2020 Games champions and Paris 2024 bronze medalists. Mol plans to return and try to qualify for a third Games.

potentialContenders.name: Jacob Holting Nilsson / Elmer Andersson
potentialContenders.note: 2026 European champions who beat Mol and Sorum in the final. They earned Sweden a men's quota place.

potentialContenders.name: Sam Schachter / Jake Pickett
potentialContenders.note: Took bronze at the 2026 NORCECA championship and at Montreal, their first Tour medal in 16 events together. They could be a spoiler.

VBV11.blurb:
Kelly Cheng and Megan Kraft grew up with this sand under their feet. Both are Southern California natives who teamed up in January 2026, and this is the kind of crowd they have wanted all their lives.

They already have a Tour bronze from their first event together and a NORCECA final behind them. They still need a second U.S. women's place, which will come through the 2027 World Championships, the ranking, or the 2028 qualifier series.

The afternoon also offers the men. Chase Budinger and Trevor Crabb won NORCECA in a 17-21, 21-16, 19-17 thriller, which gave the host two men's spots. Four matches, long shadows, and a crowd with a stake.
VBV11.potentialContendersIntro: U.S. teams are not set, and pool draws are not out. Sweden's pair is included as a possible opponent for the home teams.

potentialContenders.name: Kelly Cheng / Megan Kraft
potentialContenders.note: Southern California natives and 2026 NORCECA runners-up. Cheng is a 2023 world champion. The pair would need to earn the second U.S. women's place.

potentialContenders.name: Trevor Crabb / Chase Budinger
potentialContenders.note: 2026 NORCECA champions. Budinger competed at Paris 2024. Likely U.S. men's team if selected.

potentialContenders.name: David Ahman / Jonatan Hellvig
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalists and 2025 world champions who opened 2026 with the Joao Pessoa title. They would be a heavy test for any host pair.

VBV12.blurb:
This beach was not the first choice. Organizers moved beach volleyball to Long Beach's Alamitos Beach after negotiations with Santa Monica broke down. What they built is a temporary stadium on a public beach, with the ocean behind the court.

The men's draw comes with an all-Swedish storyline. Holting Nilsson and Andersson lost the 2025 world final to their countrymen Ahman and Hellvig, then beat everyone at the 2026 Europeans. Sweden can only send two teams, so a pool match like this one gives you a close look at who the committee might choose.

Night play means lights, sea air, and a quiet that falls before each serve.
VBV12.potentialContendersIntro: No pool draws or rosters are confirmed. These are projected contenders for men's and women's matches.

potentialContenders.name: Jacob Holting Nilsson / Elmer Andersson
potentialContenders.note: 2026 European champions and FIVB World Ranking leaders as of August 2026. They earned Sweden a men's quota place.

potentialContenders.name: David Ahman / Jonatan Hellvig
potentialContenders.note: Beat their countrymen in the 2025 world final and won Joao Pessoa and Ostrava in 2026. Sweden's committee decides who fills its places.

potentialContenders.name: Katja Stam / Raisa Schoon
potentialContenders.note: Ranked fifth in the world at the time of their unbeaten 2026 European title run. Likely women's contenders if they stay together.

VBV13.blurb:
Eleven days into the tournament window, the field is still taking shape. The 2026 continental championships handed out five quota places per gender, and by Wednesday morning you can see how that map plays out on the sand.

Europe sent the Netherlands' Stam and Schoon and Sweden's Holting Nilsson and Andersson. Australia swept Asia, Brazil's Stein and Lima took South America, and Canada and the USA split NORCECA. Each team carries a continental title into the match.

The 9 AM start is a calm, bright slot with a chance to see a new face before the field narrows. Go for the geography lesson.
VBV13.potentialContendersIntro: Quota places belong to national committees, so these champions are projections, not confirmed entries.

potentialContenders.name: Katja Stam / Raisa Schoon
potentialContenders.note: 2026 European women's champions who earned the first European women's quota place.

potentialContenders.name: Jacob Holting Nilsson / Elmer Andersson
potentialContenders.note: 2026 European men's champions who beat Norway in the final.

potentialContenders.name: Andre Stein / Renato Lima
potentialContenders.note: 2026 South American champions and a men's quota place for Brazil.

potentialContenders.name: Stefanie Fejes / Taliqua Clancy
potentialContenders.note: 2026 Asian women's champions who earned a quota place.

VBV14.blurb:
One American women's spot is still open as far as these inputs show, and the contenders are in the building. Kristen Cruz and Taryn Brasher are 2025 world silver medalists who beat Paris 2024 champions Ana Patricia and Duda in the March 2026 Joao Pessoa final.

Cheng and Kraft are also in the race. Kraft won three Tour medals in 2025 with Terese Cannon, and Cheng is a 2023 world champion. The 2027 World Championships, the FIVB ranking, or the 2028 qualifier series will decide the second place.

Four matches, afternoon sun, and a sport on its home sand. If you want the rivalry, this is the window.
VBV14.potentialContendersIntro: The USA's second women's place is not decided, so these women's pairs are projections, not announced entries.

potentialContenders.name: Kristen Cruz / Taryn Brasher
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world silver medalists who won the March 2026 Joao Pessoa Elite over Ana Patricia and Duda.

potentialContenders.name: Kelly Cheng / Megan Kraft
potentialContenders.note: Cheng is a 2023 world champion. They lost the 2026 NORCECA final 21-16, 27-25 to Canada and took bronze in their debut event together.

potentialContenders.name: Ana Patricia / Duda
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalists. Duda's break until November 2026 makes their 2028 line-up an open question.

potentialContenders.name: Melissa Humana-Paredes / Brandie Wilkerson
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalists and 2026 NORCECA champions.

VBV15.blurb:
Three nations that stood on the Paris men's podium could all show up on this night. Sweden won gold, Germany took silver, and Norway took bronze, and they have been busy since.

Germany's Nils Ehlers, now with Lui Wust, won the 2026 Hamburg Elite over Norway's Mol and Sorum, 22-20, 21-9. Mol and Sorum recovered to win Montreal, their 38th win in 105 events together, before Mol began a break. Sweden's Ahman and Hellvig won Joao Pessoa without losing a match.

It is the last night of pool play for this stretch. The ocean goes dark, the lights hold the court, and the crowd knows it is looking at a possible Round of 16 preview.
VBV15.potentialContendersIntro: These men's pairs are projections only. No pool draws are announced, and Germany and Norway have not confirmed their teams.

potentialContenders.name: David Ahman / Jonatan Hellvig
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalists and 2025 world champions who won the 2026 Joao Pessoa Elite without losing a match.

potentialContenders.name: Nils Ehlers / Lui Wust
potentialContenders.note: Ehlers won Paris 2024 silver with Clemens Wickler. This pair won the 2026 Hamburg Elite. If they qualify, they are a podium threat.

potentialContenders.name: Anders Mol / Christian Sorum
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalists and 2020 Games champions. Mol plans a return after his break, so they are likely contenders if they qualify.

VBV16.blurb:
Duda walked away from competition for three months in 2026 for one reason: to arrive at 2028 sharp. If she and Ana Patricia are back together here, the Paris champions could open the Thursday morning card in front of a Long Beach crowd still settling into its seats.

This is the discovery slot. Pool play at 9 AM means fresh legs, a wide beach, and the Pacific sitting right behind the end line. Nobody is under knockout pressure yet, so you get to watch big names find their rhythm.

Bring sunscreen and arrive early. Seeing a gold medalist on a half-empty stand is a rare treat.
VBV16.potentialContendersIntro: Women's pairs are likely to headline, though the session may include men's matches. No 2028 rosters or pool draws are confirmed, so these are projections.

potentialContenders.name: Ana Patricia / Duda
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalists, with Brazil's first women's title since 1996. Duda paused competition from August to November 2026 to prepare for the qualification race, so whether they qualify together is still an open question.

potentialContenders.name: Kristen Cruz / Taryn Brasher

VBV17.blurb:
Forty-eight teams. No more than two per country in each gender. And right now, nobody can say for sure who gets to walk onto this sand on a Thursday afternoon.

That is what makes this session interesting. Qualification is still playing out through the 2027 World Championships in the Netherlands, the ranking list, and a 2028 qualifier series, and national committees pick the actual pairs. Some of the teams you see here may not have been obvious picks today.

Four matches spread across the afternoon give you room to wander in, find a seat, and scout a field that is still taking shape. Sunset is closer than it looks.

VBV18.blurb:
Imagine a Swedish civil war on the sand. At the 2025 World Championship in Adelaide, Ahman and Hellvig beat their own countrymen, Holting Nilsson and Andersson, for the title, and the 2026 European final then sent Holting Nilsson and Andersson to the front of the queue for Sweden's first men's quota place.

By 8 PM the beach is cooling and the stadium is loud. Night pool play has a looser feel than the knockouts, with plenty of room to see the Paris gold medalists and the Norwegians chasing a third Games.

The session runs to 11 PM. It's a late one, but worth it.

VBV19.blurb:
Canada's only loss at the 2026 NORCECA Championship came from Kelly Cheng and Megan Kraft, a pair that had only been together since January. They then lost the final to the same Canadians, 21-16, 27-25, and the question lingers: who has the edge now?

Friday morning pool play is where these stories simmer. It is among the last preliminary sessions before the Round of 16, so points and pride are starting to matter, though losing still isn't the end of the road.

The pairs here include Latvia's reigning world champions, the Dutch, and the Americans, and a crowd that gets going on the first long rally.

VBV20.blurb:
This is the last night of group stage, and the afternoon matters more than it looks. When these four matches finish at 6 PM, pool play is done and the single-elimination bracket takes over.

Expect pairs who are safely through to play with some freedom, and those on the bubble to play like they're in a final. The stands in Long Beach tend to know the difference before the scoreboard does.

Swedish star Ahman and Hellvig, the first men's pair to reach two straight World Championship finals, could be among those sorting out seeding. The sun is still high at 2 PM. By the last point it will have started to drop.

VBV21.blurb:
The home crowd gets its Friday night here. If Kristen Cruz and Taryn Brasher qualify, an American pair that has beaten Brazil's Paris champions in a final could take the sand under the lights in Southern California.

Cruz, who competed as Kristen Nuss until recently, lost in the Round of 16 at Paris 2024. A crowd on the beach where the sport grew up could carry her differently.

Three matches, eight to eleven at night. Expect noise: American flags in the stands, Canadian ones across the aisle, and cool ocean air whenever the wind shifts.
VBV21.potentialContendersIntro: U.S. teams are guaranteed one women's place as hosts, and the men also won a quota at the 2026 NORCECA Championship. No 2028 rosters are confirmed, so these are projections.

VBV22.blurb:
The United States can send at most two women's pairs, and the list of serious candidates is longer than that. A Saturday morning pool session is a chance to see why the selection debate is going to be tough.

Brasher and Cruz have reached the podium in 11 of their last 13 international events as of March 2026. Cheng and Kraft, partners since January that year, are chasing them. Both have beaten Canada this year.

Only two matches fill the 9 to 11 AM window, so the morning feels unhurried. Coffee in hand, ocean at your back, you can follow every ball.

VBV23.blurb:
American men's beach volleyball has a crowded room and not enough chairs. At the 2025 Worlds, Schalk and Shaw beat Evans and Budinger 16-21, 21-19, 15-9 in the same pool, and since then partnerships have shifted.

That is the draw of this Saturday night session. Four matches from 7 to 11 PM mean you could see the home pairs, a Canadian duo ranked 19th in the world, and Brazilians who won their continent.

As the temperature drops and the lights come up on a beach that has no stadium on it most days, the sport feels like it has come home.

VBV24.blurb:
Taryn Brasher and Kristen Cruz know what a Round of 16 exit feels like. They lost at this stage at Paris 2024, their first Games, and then spent a cycle making sure it would not happen again.

The first single-elimination session of the tournament has a different pulse from pool play. One bad set and you go home. In Adelaide in 2025, the Americans fell behind Stam and Schoon in a Round of 16 match, then won 20-22, 21-19, 15-6 and rode that momentum to a silver medal.

The Sunday morning light is soft and the nerves are real. Two matches, two ends to a run.

VBV25.blurb:
Ana Patricia and Duda won Paris in a 26-24, 12-21, 15-10 thriller, the first women's final at the Games to go three sets. But being champions guarantees nothing on a knockout afternoon.

At the 2025 Worlds they lost in straight sets to Americans Donlin and Denaburg in the Round of 16. In 2026 they fell to Brasher and Cruz in a final. Duda stepped away for three months, and Ana Patricia played Hamburg with Carolina Horta Maximo.

If the Brazilians arrive in Long Beach together and healthy, a 1 PM Sunday knockout is a test of whether the champion's form has held.

VBV26.blurb:
Sweden's David Ahman and Jonatan Hellvig beat Germany 21-10, 21-13 in the Paris final. It was barely a contest, and the result handed Sweden its first beach volleyball gold.

Here is what's remarkable: they were not always dominant. They lost the 2023 World final, and Ahman said he had been injured before they won the 2025 title in Adelaide. Getting back to the top took work.

A late-afternoon Round of 16 match in Long Beach, with the sun low and the sand still warm, is a chance to see them chase a second straight gold. Two matches, 5 to 7 PM.

VBV27.blurb:
Brandie Wilkerson and Melissa Humana-Paredes lost Paris by five points in a third set. Then, in 2026, they got back to work with the same coaches who helped them reach that podium, Marcio Sicoli and Guilherme Tenius.

The results arrived fast. They won the Ostrava Elite16, beat Latvia's Graudina and Samoilova in a 23-21 second set, and on November 8 took the NORCECA title over Kraft and Cheng, securing Canada's women's quota place.

A Sunday night knockout under the lights, the ocean dark behind the court, is exactly the setting where a pair with unfinished business can do real damage.
VBV27.potentialContendersIntro: Women's matches could headline this night session, with Canada's Paris silver medalists the main story. Quota places belong to the country, and Canada's 2028 roster has not been named.

VBV28.blurb:
Latvia has a world title and no guaranteed ticket to this beach. That is the quirk of this qualification cycle, and it makes a Monday morning knockout interesting.

Tina Graudina and Anastasija Samoilova won the 2025 Worlds in Adelaide, Latvia's first, by coming back after losing the first set to Cruz and Brasher, 21-15, 15-21, 15-11. But bronze at the 2026 Europeans sent the continental quota to the Netherlands instead.

They still have the ranking list, the 2027 World Championships, and the 2028 qualifier series. If they get here, a 9 AM match on a quiet beach could be a contender's showcase.

VBV29.blurb:
Depth is the theme at lunchtime on Monday. France's Rotar and Gauthier-Rat took men's bronze at the 2025 Worlds. Sweden's second pair, Holting Nilsson and Andersson, won silver and a European title. Brazil sent two women's pairs to the world semifinals.

That is a lot of contenders for two matches. Any of them could be on this sand, and some may not survive the afternoon.

Alamitos Beach sits right in downtown Long Beach, so you can wander out for lunch and be back for a 1 PM knockout. The ocean breeze may be a factor too.

VBV30.blurb:
Two matches remain, and then the quarterfinal field is set. That makes the last Round of 16 session of the tournament the end of the line for some well-known names.

Watch for the women's side. Brazil won gold in Paris for the first time since 1996, but Ana Patricia and Duda lost in the 2025 Worlds Round of 16. Switzerland took bronze. Kelly Cheng, a 2022 world champion, and Megan Kraft are looking to improve on a 2026 NORCECA final loss.

Early evening on a Monday, with the light turning gold, is when a long run of knockouts can feel suddenly final.

VBV31.blurb:
One loss and you go home. The Round of 16 is where the 48-team field gets cut in half, and nobody gets a second chance.

The matchups are a mystery. Most quota places will be settled by a ranking list that closes March 31, 2028. What is certain is the setting: a temporary stadium on Alamitos Beach, about 12,000 seats on open sand, with the Pacific behind the court.

This is the session for discovery. Two matches, the first knockout nerves of the tournament, and a few pairs you've never heard of trying to take down the names you have.

VBV32.blurb:
Two o'clock sun, bright sand, and eight teams left in each draw. The best pairs in the world now play one match from a medal round.

At this stage the reigning champions start to feel hunted. Sweden's Ahman and Hellvig followed Paris gold with the 2025 world title in Adelaide, and everyone left in the bracket has spent months studying them. On the women's side, Latvia's Graudina and Samoilova beat the Americans in the 2025 world final and carry the same target.

The afternoon slot is the daylight session, so you'll see every serve and block against the Pacific backdrop.

VBV33.blurb:
Sweden has two men's pairs good enough to cause trouble for everyone else, and a night quarterfinal is where that depth could show.

Ahman and Hellvig have won three straight Ostrava Elite16 titles, and their career Tour tally stands at 13 gold, five silver and two bronze. Their countrymen Nilsson and Andersson beat Norway's Anders Mol and Christian Sorum in the 2026 European final, so even the Paris bronze medalists have work to do.

Settle in for evening beach volleyball by the Pacific. Every point goes a bit tighter once the knockouts start.

VBV34.blurb:
The biggest question in women's beach volleyball may still be whether Ana Patricia and Duda are playing together at all.

They won Paris gold, a three-set classic that returned Brazil to the top for the first time since 1996. Since then there have been medical withdrawals, mental-health breaks and a partner switch for Ana Patricia in Hamburg. Duda is aiming to be in top condition for the 2028 qualification race, and a reunion in Long Beach is not confirmed.

If they are here, the pairing to watch is Americans Taryn Brasher and Kristen Cruz, who beat them 21-16, 21-19 in the Joao Pessoa final.

VBV35.blurb:
This is the last quarterfinal session. By the end of it, the semifinal fields in both draws are set.

The pairs at the net will have come from everywhere. Quota places have gone to Australia in both genders, to the Netherlands' Schoon and Stam, to Brazil's men, and to Morocco and Nigeria through the 2026 African titles. The 2027 Worlds and a ranking list closing March 31, 2028 still have places to give.

An evening quarterfinal on Alamitos Beach means a standing crowd and a lot of one-point swings. Somebody's tournament ends in front of 12,000 people.

VBV36.blurb:
Afternoon semifinals are where beach volleyball turns into a series of long rallies. One win reaches a medal match, and one loss leaves only bronze.

Canada's Melissa Humana-Paredes and Brandie Wilkerson would arrive with a point to prove. They lost the Paris final in three sets, then won the 2026 Ostrava Elite16 by beating Switzerland's Mader and Kernen in the semifinals and the Dutch pair in the final.

On the men's side, Sweden's Ahman and Hellvig are the standard. The matchups are unknown, and the ranking list is still the main route into the draw.
