VBV37.blurb:
Sweden beat Norway in the 2026 European men's final, and it was Nilsson and Andersson, not Ahman and Hellvig, who did it. The best men's pair in the world might not even be the best pair in Sweden.

The evening semifinals decide who plays for gold and who plays for bronze. Germany's Ehlers and Wickler lost a bronze match at the 2025 Worlds and may arrive with unfinished business.

The Americans add a home-sand storyline. Crabb and Benesh are on the men's side, and Brasher and Cruz, who took 2025 world silver, are on the women's.
VBV37.potentialContendersIntro: Semifinal lineups are not known, so these are projected contenders based on 2025 and 2026 form, across both draws.

potentialContenders.name: Jacob Holting Nilsson / Elmer Andersson
potentialContenders.note: 2026 European champions over Norway and 2025 world silver medalists. A projected men's semifinalist if they qualify.

potentialContenders.name: Anders Mol / Christian Sorum
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalists and 2026 European runners-up. Could be a veteran threat in the late rounds.

potentialContenders.name: Nils Ehlers / Clemens Wickler
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalists who lost the 2025 Worlds bronze match. Likely contenders if they qualify.

potentialContenders.name: Taryn Brasher / Kristen Cruz
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world silver medalists and 2026 Joao Pessoa winners. They could bring the biggest home-crowd noise of the session.

potentialContenders.name: Melissa Humana-Paredes / Brandie Wilkerson
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalists who beat Americans Kraft and Cheng 21-16, 27-25 in the November 2026 NORCECA final.

VBV38.blurb:
The Paris final went three sets, 26-24, 12-21, 15-10, and it was the first women's final at the Games to go the distance. Now picture a rematch.

Brazil's Ana Patricia and Duda took gold, Canada's Brandie Wilkerson and Melissa Humana-Paredes took silver, and both have held places in 2028 conversations. Canada has the quota. Brazil's duo has had medical withdrawals and breaks, and their joint 2028 plans are unconfirmed.

The broader field is just as open. Latvia's Graudina and Samoilova are reigning world champions, and Americans Brasher and Cruz beat Ana Patricia and Duda in 2026. A bronze match opens the session, then the gold.
VBV38.potentialContendersIntro: No 2028 finalists are set. These are projections based on Paris 2024 and recent form. Whether Ana Patricia and Duda will play together has not been confirmed.

potentialContenders.name: Ana Patricia / Duda
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalists. A reunion at 2028 is unconfirmed, but a title defense would be one of the stories of the Games.

potentialContenders.name: Melissa Humana-Paredes / Brandie Wilkerson
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalists who secured Canada's quota by winning the 2026 NORCECA title. A likely finals contender.

potentialContenders.name: Taryn Brasher / Kristen Cruz
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world silver medalists who beat Ana Patricia and Duda 21-16, 21-19 in Joao Pessoa. They'd have a home crowd behind them.

potentialContenders.name: Alina Graudina / Tina Samoilova
potentialContenders.note: Reigning world champions after the 2025 final over the USA. Projected to be in the medal conversation if they qualify.

VBV39.blurb:
This session closes the beach volleyball program at Alamitos Beach Stadium, with a bronze match and then a gold-medal match in the evening.

Sweden's Ahman and Hellvig beat Germany 21-10, 21-13 in Paris for Sweden's first gold in the sport, then added the 2025 world title. Their career Tour tally is 13 gold, five silver and two bronze. They have been so dominant that the question is who can stay with them.

A few candidates stand out. Nilsson and Andersson, their countrymen, took 2025 world silver and the 2026 European title. Norway's Mol and Sorum are Paris bronze medalists, and Crabb and Benesh would give the home crowd a reason to roar.
VBV39.potentialContendersIntro: The men's final field is unknown, so these are projected contenders based on 2025 and 2026 form. A country can send at most two pairs.

potentialContenders.name: David Ahman / Jonatan Hellvig
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalists and 2025 world champions. Projected as the pair to beat if they qualify and stay together.

potentialContenders.name: Jacob Holting Nilsson / Elmer Andersson
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world silver medalists and 2026 European champions. Could make it a Swedish final.

potentialContenders.name: Anders Mol / Christian Sorum
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalists who finished second at the 2026 Europeans. A likely podium threat.

potentialContenders.name: Taylor Crabb / Andrew Benesh
potentialContenders.note: Won bronze at the 2026 Ostrava Elite16. If they earn the U.S. place, they could deliver a home-crowd medal run.

potentialContenders.name: Nils Ehlers / Clemens Wickler
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalists and fourth at the 2025 Worlds. A projected contender seeking revenge for 21-10, 21-13.

VVO01.blurb:
The first serve of the 2028 volleyball tournament goes up at 9 AM in a building made for hockey. Honda Center, still called The Pond by longtime locals, has hosted Stanley Cup Finals. Now it gets a net and a crowd that can say it was there for the start.

Morning matches on opening day reward early risers. Nobody is tired, nobody has lost, and the field is still a puzzle you get to start solving. Japan, the Asian champion, has said a medal is the goal, and teams like that do not ease into anything.

The arena is air-conditioned against July in Orange County, so the only heat is on the court.
VVO01.potentialContendersIntro: Six men's teams have qualified so far: the United States, Japan, Cuba, Brazil, Tunisia and Poland. Any of them could open the tournament in this slot, and the remaining six berths are still to be decided.

potentialContenders.name: Poland
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 silver medalist, and winner of the 2026 Nations League and EuroVolley, so a likely headliner wherever it is scheduled.

potentialContenders.name: Japan
potentialContenders.note: Beat Iran 3-0 in the 2026 Asian Championship final and finished fourth in the 2026 Nations League; Ran Takahashi says the goal is a medal.

potentialContenders.name: Brazil
potentialContenders.note: Three-time men's champion (1992, 2004, 2016) that won the 2026 South American Championship without dropping a set.

potentialContenders.name: Cuba
potentialContenders.note: Back at the Games for the first time since Rio 2016, after winning the 2026 NORCECA qualification tournament.

VVO02.blurb:
Sooner or later the home crowd gets its turn, and an early-afternoon slot on opening day is a fine place to find it. The United States men arrive as Paris 2024 bronze medalists and 2026 Nations League runners-up, having lost a five-set final to Poland that went 15-10 in the decider.

That sting is the story. Veterans such as Matt Anderson, Jeff Jendryk, Micah Ma'a and Erik Shoji were part of the Paris bronze and the 2026 NORCECA title, and could still be around if they make the roster.

In a hockey arena with an enclosed bowl, every kill sounds twice as loud.
VVO02.potentialContendersIntro: The host United States is the one men's team guaranteed a spot, and it could appear in any early session. Other qualified teams are projected opponents.

potentialContenders.name: USA
potentialContenders.note: Host nation and Paris 2024 bronze medalist; silver at the 2026 Nations League after beating Italy and Japan on the way to the final.

potentialContenders.name: Poland
potentialContenders.note: Beat the U.S. 3-2 in the 2026 Nations League final in Ningbo and tops the world ranking.

potentialContenders.name: Japan
potentialContenders.note: Edged by the U.S. 3-2 in the 2026 Nations League semifinal; Takahashi was Asian Championship MVP.

potentialContenders.name: Cuba
potentialContenders.note: Lost 3-1 to the U.S. in pool play at the 2026 NORCECA championship, so any rematch carries history.

VVO03.blurb:
Cuba has been gone for a decade. The last time its men's team played at the Games was Rio 2016, and after beating Canada 3-1 in the 2026 NORCECA qualification final in Moncton, it is back.

Marlon Yant scored 25 in that final and Miguel Lopez added 22, and that kind of power hitting is exactly what plays well in an evening session. The sun is down, the building is filling up, and a team with a long volleyball tradition gets to walk back onto the biggest floor in the sport.

If you like your matches with a comeback story attached, circle this one.
VVO03.potentialContendersIntro: Cuba is already qualified, so this evening slot is a natural place to see it, though the schedule decides the matchups. Other likely participants are among the six teams that have qualified so far.

potentialContenders.name: Cuba
potentialContenders.note: Returning after missing 2020 and 2024; Yant and Lopez powered the NORCECA qualification final win over Canada.

potentialContenders.name: Poland
potentialContenders.note: World ranking leader that won both the 2026 Nations League and EuroVolley; Wilfredo Leon and Tomasz Fornal were the MVPs.

potentialContenders.name: USA
potentialContenders.note: Host and Paris 2024 bronze medalist, and a 3-1 winner over Cuba at the 2026 NORCECA championship.

potentialContenders.name: Brazil
potentialContenders.note: 2026 South American champion and three-time Games winner, projected to be one of the toughest tests in the pool.

VVO04.blurb:
The last match of opening day starts at 9 PM and finishes near midnight. This is the session for people who like their volleyball with a night-owl edge, when the arena looks different and the late crowd is the loudest.

Tunisia is the kind of team that can make it special. It won its 12th African title in 2026 with an unbeaten run, then a 3-0 final over Cameroon, and returns for its eighth Games after missing Paris 2024.

Brazil, a three-time champion, is the sort of opponent that turns a late slot into a headline. When the last rally ends, you are still in Anaheim, grinning.
VVO04.potentialContendersIntro: Tunisia, Brazil and Poland have all qualified, and any of them could land in this late slot. Final pool draws and matchups are still to be set.

potentialContenders.name: Tunisia
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 African Championship with a 3-0 final over Cameroon; returning for an eighth Games appearance.

potentialContenders.name: Brazil
potentialContenders.note: Champion in 1992, 2004 and 2016, and winner of the 2026 South American Championship without losing a set.

potentialContenders.name: Poland
potentialContenders.note: Captain Aleksander Sliwka led the team to the 2026 European title in a rematch of the Paris 2024 final.

VVO05.blurb:
Ran Takahashi served 22 aces at the 2026 Asian Championship, the best in the tournament, and Japan rode that serve to a 3-0 final over Iran. If you want to see why a quick, precise team can beat bigger ones, watch what happens when the ball leaves his hand.

Japan qualified two years early, a gift captain Yuki Ishikawa says gives the team time to prepare, and opposite Yuji Nishida gives it a hitter who can finish. Sunday morning, second day of the tournament, the arena settles into a rhythm.

This is a good session for fans who like skill over size.
VVO05.potentialContendersIntro: Japan has qualified and is a likely participant in a session like this. The other qualified teams could appear as opponents, and the schedule will decide.

potentialContenders.name: Japan
potentialContenders.note: 2026 Asian champion and Nations League fourth-place team; Takahashi, Nishida and Ishikawa lead a team that says it wants a medal.

potentialContenders.name: Poland
potentialContenders.note: World ranking leader that won the 2026 Nations League and EuroVolley.

potentialContenders.name: Tunisia
potentialContenders.note: 2026 African champion with an unbeaten run; a physical team that could test any opponent.

potentialContenders.name: Brazil
potentialContenders.note: Three-time men's champion that dominated the 2026 South American Championship.

VVO06.blurb:
Poland keeps winning everything around the Games. The Paris 2024 silver medalists took the 2026 Nations League, then the 2026 European title, and the team's only men's gold came nearly 50 years before Paris.

That is the question hanging over this Sunday afternoon session: can the sport's current benchmark turn that run into the one result that has eluded it? Tomasz Fornal, the Nations League MVP, and Wilfredo Leon, the EuroVolley MVP, give it two ways to win a rally.

Expect scouts, coaches and rival fans to be watching as closely as the neighbors in your row.
VVO06.potentialContendersIntro: Poland is qualified. France and Italy have not yet qualified, so their presence in 2028 is a projection, but both could reach the Games through the 2027 World Cup or the world ranking.

potentialContenders.name: Poland
potentialContenders.note: Qualified after beating France 3-1 in EuroVolley 2026; second straight Nations League title.

potentialContenders.name: France
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 champion chasing a third straight title, if it qualifies; still has the World Cup and ranking routes.

potentialContenders.name: Italy
potentialContenders.note: 2025 world champion that has not yet qualified; lost 3-0 to the U.S. in the 2026 Nations League quarterfinals.

potentialContenders.name: USA
potentialContenders.note: Host and Paris 2024 bronze medalist that lost the 2026 Nations League final to Poland in five sets.

VVO07.blurb:
Melissa Vargas and Paola Egonu each scored 28 points in the EuroVolley 2026 final in Istanbul, and the match still went to a deciding set that Turkiye won 15-10. If the women's tournament has a defining duel, that is it.

The women's competition opens at 5 PM on Sunday, an hour when fans file in from the parking lots and the arena fills quickly. Turkiye, the 2026 Nations League champion, and the Paris 2024 champions from Italy carry the sport's best rivalry. Italy has not yet qualified, so seeing both would take a successful run through the 2027 World Cup or the ranking.

But even without them, the first women's night has a lot to offer.
VVO07.potentialContendersIntro: Six women's teams have qualified: the United States, Canada, Thailand, Egypt, Turkiye and Brazil. Italy, the Paris 2024 champion, still needs a berth, so any appearance would be a projection.

potentialContenders.name: Turkiye
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 Nations League and EuroVolley; fourth at Paris 2024, its best Games result.

potentialContenders.name: USA
potentialContenders.note: Host nation and Paris 2024 silver medalist, always a draw in front of a home crowd.

potentialContenders.name: Brazil

potentialContenders.name: Italy

VVO08.blurb:
Canada's women have waited 32 years. The team last played at the Games in Atlanta 1996, and a 3-1 win over the Dominican Republic in the 2026 NORCECA qualification final ended that gap.

Now the Canadians show up in Orange County, a short flight and a long road from home, with Giovanni Guidetti on the bench and Kiera Van Ryk, the 2026 Nations League best scorer, swinging at the net. Alexa Gray scored 22 alongside Van Ryk in that qualification final.

This late Sunday slot is the kind of match that grows as the night goes on. Bring the energy of a homecoming.
VVO08.potentialContendersIntro: Canada is qualified and could appear in this late slot. The other qualified women's teams are projected opponents; the schedule decides.

potentialContenders.name: Canada
potentialContenders.note: Back at the Games for the first time since 1996; ranked eighth in the FIVB world ranking in October 2026.

potentialContenders.name: USA
potentialContenders.note: Host nation and Paris 2024 silver medalist, with a neighbor-versus-neighbor angle if it meets Canada.

potentialContenders.name: Turkiye

potentialContenders.name: Brazil
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 bronze medalist that won the 2026 South American Championship.

VVO09.blurb:
Two teams will be doing something they have never done at the Games. Thailand qualified for the first time by coming back to beat China in the 2026 Asian Championship final, and Egypt will play women's volleyball at the Games for the first time too.

This Monday morning session is about discovery. Thailand's Pornpun was the Asian Championship MVP, and Mariam Metwally earned the same honor in Africa. Neither team carries the weight of a medal favorite, which is exactly when volleyball gets loose and fun.

Debuts are special, and the crowd can smell that. Show up early and meet the teams everybody will be talking about next week.
VVO09.potentialContendersIntro: Thailand and Egypt are qualified, and a debut-heavy session like this could feature one or both. Other qualified teams are possible opponents; China and Japan could still reach the Games.

potentialContenders.name: Thailand

potentialContenders.name: Egypt
potentialContenders.note: Fourth African title in 2026 and a first Games appearance in women's volleyball; Metwally was MVP.

potentialContenders.name: Canada

potentialContenders.name: China

VVO10.blurb:
Brazil has been to the final of the Women's Nations League five times as runner-up, and twice in a row it has come up just short, in 2025 against Italy and in 2026 against Turkiye. That is a lot of silver for a team that wants gold.

In the 2026 final in Macao, Ana Cristina scored 25, Rosamaria Montibeller had 19 and Julia Bergmann 15, but it was not enough. Brazil also owns the Paris 2024 bronze, and a team that keeps getting this close has a reason to be dangerous.

Catch it on a Monday afternoon in Anaheim, when the players are fresh and the crowd is full of fans who know Brazilian volleyball.
VVO10.potentialContendersIntro: Brazil is qualified and is a likely participant in a marquee-style session like this. Turkiye, the United States and Italy are possible rivals, though Italy still needs to qualify.

potentialContenders.note: Beat Brazil in the 2025 Nations League final; has not yet qualified, so any 2028 appearance is a projection.

potentialContenders.name: USA
potentialContenders.note: Host and Paris 2024 silver medalist, always a test for Brazil in the NORCECA-South America mix.

VVO11.blurb:
Paola Egonu was the MVP of the Paris 2024 final, with 22 points, as Italy won its first women's gold. She will be 29 in 2028, and the stage is hers again if Italy gets there.

That is the catch. Italy lost the EuroVolley 2026 final 3-2 after leading, and it has not yet qualified. The route is open through the 2027 World Cup in Canada and the United States, where Italy is the defending champion, or through the world ranking.

If the champions show up in this Monday evening slot, it will be because they earned it. Come hoping, and be ready if they do.
VVO11.potentialContendersIntro: Italy has not yet qualified, so its appearance here is a projection rather than a fact. The teams listed could appear if they qualify for the Games.

potentialContenders.name: Poland

VVO12.blurb:
Melissa Vargas scored 33 points in the 2026 Nations League final. She scored 28 in the EuroVolley 2026 final. She was the MVP of both. If you want a single hitter who can take over a night, this is your one.

She is Cuban-born, plays for Turkiye, and Turkiye has risen from a fourth-place finish in Paris 2024 to the top of the sport, even if the 2025 world championship final went 3-2 to Italy. The next step is a medal at the Games.

Late Monday night, 9 PM, is a fine time to be in the seats. The building is loud, the floor is bright, and an attacker is warming up.
VVO12.potentialContendersIntro: Turkiye is qualified, and the host United States, Brazil and Canada are among the other qualified teams that could share a late slot.

potentialContenders.name: USA

potentialContenders.name: Brazil

potentialContenders.name: Canada

VVO13.blurb:
France won in Tokyo and again in Paris, the first men's team to repeat since the United States in 1984 and 1988. It was a 3-0 sweep of Poland in the Paris 2024 final, with Jean Patry and Trevor Clevenot leading the way.

The question for Tuesday morning is whether France can make it three. It has not yet qualified, and Poland beat it 3-1 in the EuroVolley 2026 final in Milan, 31-29 in the first set. So for now the champions are chasing.

Open the program on a weekday morning and look for the team in blue. If it makes it, it will be worth the early alarm.
VVO13.potentialContendersIntro: France has not yet qualified, so its place in this session is a projection. Poland, the United States and Japan are already in the field.

potentialContenders.name: Poland

potentialContenders.name: USA
potentialContenders.note: Host nation and Paris 2024 bronze medalist, runner-up in the 2026 Nations League.

potentialContenders.name: Japan
potentialContenders.note: 2026 Asian champion and Nations League semifinalist.

VVO14.blurb:
This is the third time the United States has hosted volleyball at the Games, after Los Angeles 1984 and Atlanta 1996. The American men won gold in 1984 and again in 1988, and that history gives a Tuesday afternoon match some weight.

The 2026 version of the team is good enough to carry it. It won the NORCECA championship in Moncton, beating Cuba 3-1 and the Dominican Republic 3-0 in pool play, and then took Nations League silver, a five-set loss to Poland. The Paris 2024 bronze medalists are close.

A home crowd at Honda Center can change a rally. If you want to watch the Americans turn that closeness into something bigger, this is your afternoon.
VVO14.potentialContendersIntro: The host United States is guaranteed a place in the tournament and could appear in this slot. The qualified teams below are possible opponents.

VVO15.blurb:
Half the fun of a Tuesday evening match is not knowing who will be on the floor. Six men's places are still open: three go to the 2027 World Cup in Poland, and three go by world ranking after the 2028 Nations League preliminary phase.

That means the strongest names may arrive late. France, the Paris 2024 champion, lost the EuroVolley 2026 final to Poland. Italy, the 2025 world champion, was swept 3-0 by the United States in the Nations League quarterfinals. Slovenia finished third in the 2026 Nations League. None of them has qualified yet.

So this slot is a bet on the bracket coming together. Come see who made it.

VVO16.blurb:
Honda Center is a hockey barn, and at 9:00 PM on a July Tuesday it turns into a late-night volleyball room. The air conditioning hums and the rallies echo off the bowl.

Poland is the name that hangs over the men's field. The Paris 2024 silver medalist won the 2026 VNL for the third time and took the 2026 European title, and if it's on court tonight you'll see why everyone is chasing it.

A night match stretches long when sets go to extra points, so this is a good ticket for fans who like their volleyball with a late finish.

VVO17.blurb:
Twelve years is a long time to wait for a Games. Cuba's men get to end the wait in Anaheim if they land on this morning card.

The Cubans earned their return by beating Canada 3-1 in Moncton, and a 9:00 AM crowd tends to reward the underdog with early noise. Morning sessions are quieter and looser, a chance to sit close and see players warm into the tournament.

Behind it all runs the bigger question: with three places still decided by the World Ranking after the 2028 VNL, every team in the building arrives with something to prove.

VVO18.blurb:
The United States men have spent the last year trading blows with Japan and Poland, and an afternoon at Honda Center could bring another chapter.

Japan beat the U.S. 3-2 in Orleans during the 2026 VNL preliminary round. The Americans answered by rallying past the unbeaten Japanese 3-2 in the semifinals, then lost the final to Poland in five sets. This is a rivalry with real recent history.

A 1:00 PM start puts the sun outside and the crowd inside, with a Paris 2024 bronze medalist playing at home trying to turn that medal into gold.
VVO18.potentialContendersIntro: Pairings aren't set, so these are the teams most likely to supply the drama, drawn from the six men's teams qualified so far.

VVO19.blurb:
Brazil's women know how to lose a final and come back angrier. They took a first set off Turkiye in the 2026 VNL final in Macao, then dropped the next three.

That is the edge you could see here on Wednesday evening, with Paris 2024 bronze medalists carrying a grudge into the 5:00 PM slot. Brazilian volleyball has a particular feel: fast tempo, big blocks (Julia Kudiess was named best blocker at the 2026 VNL) and a bench that never sits still.

Canada, newly qualified and eager, makes the field stranger and more fun.

VVO20.blurb:
The reigning champions might not even be here. That is the strange tension hanging over this late-night women's card.

Italy won Paris 2024 gold and the 2025 world title, yet lost the 2026 European final 3-2 to Turkiye, despite 28 points from Paola Egonu, and still has to qualify. If Italy gets through, a 9:00 PM match with Egonu on court is the kind of ticket you buy early.

If not, the late slot still offers a deep field and the hum of a full arena past dinner.

VVO21.blurb:
Thursday morning, 9:00 AM, and the room is still waking up. This is the session where you find out who made it here.

The road to 2028 runs through a 32-team World Cup in the United States and Canada in August 2027, plus a ranking race after the 2028 VNL. Whoever clears that gauntlet arrives with nerves and adrenaline, and nothing sharpens a first-set serve like it.

The U.S. will host women's volleyball at the Games for the third time, after 1984 and 1996, and a morning match is a chance to soak in that history before the crowds peak.

VVO22.blurb:
Canada's women haven't played Games volleyball since 1996. That's the story at 1:00 PM Thursday.

Giovanni Guidetti's team earned the trip by beating the Dominican Republic 3-1 in Santo Domingo (25-15, 20-25, 25-23, 25-14). Even better for the neutral fan, Canada swept the United States 3-0 in Quebec City during the 2026 VNL, so a rematch with the hosts would need no extra promotion.

The afternoon slot is built for exactly this: a team new to the stage, an arena full of curious fans, and a match that might not go the way the rankings say.

Italy against Turkiye is the best women's rivalry in the sport right now. Italy won the 2025 world title in a five-set final in Bangkok over Turkey. A year later, Turkiye beat Italy 3-2 in the 2026 European final in Istanbul.

One of those teams, though, is already qualified, and the other has to earn its ticket. Melissa Vargas, named best opposite at the 2025 worlds, and Paola Egonu, the Paris 2024 MVP, could meet across the net.

The 5:00 PM slot is prime time before the dinner rush, with a bowl that should be buzzing.

VVO24.blurb:
The final preliminary slot for the women is when seeding gets personal. A win here can mean a softer quarterfinal draw, and the home team knows it.

The U.S. women have shown both sides. In 2026 they went 7-1 early in the VNL and clinched the top seed with a 3-0 win over Brazil in Osaka, then lost a five-set quarterfinal to host China 3-2 in Macao, including a 17-25 fourth set.

That swing from dominance to heartbreak is the kind of drama you'll want to see at 9:00 PM, when a Thursday-night crowd has settled in and the volume rises with every point.

Two-time defending champions usually walk in like they own the building. France, though, is still trying to find the door.

The Paris 2024 gold medalists swept Poland and became the first men's team since the United States in 1984 and 1988 to win back-to-back titles. But Poland beat France in the 2026 European final, and France hasn't qualified for 2028. Its route runs through the 2027 World Cup in Poland or the World Ranking.

If France arrives, this 9:00 AM Friday slot is a chance to see a dynasty start the final chapter.

Wilfredo Leon was named MVP of the 2026 European Championship, and Poland, the ranking leader when it qualified, wants gold more than any team. France, which lost the Paris 2024 final to... no, won it, 3-0 over Poland, is trying to qualify to get the revenge.

A 1:00 PM match carries a quieter intensity. Every rally gets attention, and the Poland-France grudge may produce the best one.

Friday at 5:00 PM is the home-team session. The American men have a Paris 2024 bronze, a 2026 VNL silver, and a head coach, Karch Kiraly, who knows what a gold-medal team looks like.

The final in Ningbo was a heartbreaker: a 3-2 loss to Poland in a fifth set that ended 15-10. Before that came the comeback of the tournament, a 3-2 rally past previously unbeaten Japan in the semifinals. This team plays with its chin up.

With the U.S. ranked fourth in the FIVB World Ranking as of October 2026, the crowd will believe gold is possible.

They beat Morocco 3-1 in the semifinals, then swept Cameroon 3-0 (25-22, 25-18, 25-19) in the Tunis final. That kind of unbeaten run is the reason to circle a 1:00 PM Saturday slot: a team with nothing to lose can turn a favorite's afternoon into a long one.

This is the session for fans who like underdogs, close sets and a crowd that leans toward whoever is fighting.

Inside Honda Center, the air conditioning hums against the July heat and some 18,000 seats curl around a single court.

It could be the group you catch under Saturday's late lights. Melissa Vargas, named best opposite at the 2025 Worlds, swings from the right side, and Turkiye has gone from silver in 2025, its first world medal, to Nations League champion in 2026.

Anaheim has been the U.S. national teams' training base since 2006. A late first-round match here carries a home-gym familiarity for the Americans, and a stern test for any visitor.

Thailand has never played a women's volleyball match at a Summer Games. On Sunday morning, it may get to.

The path was dramatic: a comeback over China in the 2026 Asian final in Tianjin, under coach Kiattipong Radchatagriengkai, who is on his second stint with the team. Japan, fourth at the 2025 Worlds and Asia's top-ranked side, took bronze and still has to qualify, so the field around Thailand may look different by then.

A 9 a.m. start means fresh legs, a crowd arriving with coffee, and a chance to watch a debut nation before the pressure peaks.

Africa's rise has depth: Cameroon took bronze and earned the continent's third place at the 2027 Women's World Cup. For Egypt, the job against an established power is simple: take a set and let the building lean in.

If the United States is on this card, it's worth watching Erik Sullivan's team. It beat France 3-2 and Germany 3-0 in week one of the 2026 Nations League, with Karch Kiraly now coaching the men.

VVO45.blurb:
Japan swept Iran 3-0 in the 2026 Asian final, and Ran Takahashi was named MVP. Put him across the net from Wilfredo Leon, Poland's 2026 European MVP, and the semifinal sells itself.

Poland took Paris silver, losing 3-0 to France. Brazil, a three-time Games champion, won the 2026 South American Championship without dropping a set, and Cuba returns for the first time since Rio 2016.

Wednesday's 11 a.m. winners go to Saturday's gold medal match; losers play for bronze on Friday. France and Italy still need to qualify, but a semifinal without them is hard to imagine.

VVO46.blurb:
Poland walked into the Paris 2024 final as the world No. 1 and walked out after a 3-0 loss to France. Now the Poles hold the 2026 European title and the 2026 Nations League crown, and a semifinal here could be the rematch they have waited four years for.

Wilfredo Leon, the 2026 European MVP, hits with a snap you hear before you see the ball land. Tomasz Fornal, the Nations League MVP, answers from the other side of the net.

The 4 PM start puts a hungry crowd under the roof at Honda Center, the building locals still call The Pond. One win means gold on Saturday. A loss means bronze on Friday night.

VVO47.blurb:
Paola Egonu scored 28 points in a European final last year and still lost. That is the kind of sentence that explains Italy and Turkey, two teams that have traded five-set finals back to back.

Italy won the 2025 world title 3-2 under Julio Velasco. Turkey took the 2026 European crown 3-2 in Istanbul. If either lands in this bracket, the rivalry is already loaded before the first serve.

This is an 11 AM start, with a morning crowd and a bowl of seats pitched steeply around the floor. The winners play for gold, and the losers play for bronze. Setter Alessia Orro's quick hands will keep the rallies fast.

VVO48.blurb:
Turkey has been climbing for years. Fourth in Paris was its best Games finish. A world final lost 3-2 followed, and then the 2026 Nations League and European titles arrived within weeks of each other.

Now the question is whether the Turks can turn that run into a Games final. Melissa Vargas, the VNL MVP, can end a rally from the back row at any moment. Hande Baladin and Ilkin Aydin gave Turkey 19 and 15 points in last year's VNL final.

The 4 PM semifinal is the afternoon peak at Honda Center. Expect a lot of red flags in a building where a mid-match momentum shift is felt instantly.

VVO49.blurb:
Nobody wants to be here on Friday night, and everybody here wants to leave with a medal. That tension is the whole appeal of a bronze match.

The United States men took bronze in Paris and now host. They also lost a five-set VNL final to Poland in 2026, so American fans know how thin the gap can be. If the U.S. ends up here, the building will be loud and a little tense.

The 8:30 PM start means a late-night crowd under the arena lights. Players in this match will be racing through the disappointment of Wednesday's semifinal. Expect fast, loose volleyball with no one holding back.

VVO50.blurb:
France is trying to win a third straight men's gold. Only the United States in 1984 and 1988 has done two in a row in recent history, and no team has gone three.

Standing in the way could be Poland, the world No. 1 and the team France beat 3-0 in Paris. Poland won the 2026 Nations League and beat France in the European final. Add Italy, 2025 world champions, and Brazil, three-time Games winners, and the field looks deep.

The 10 AM start means a gold-medal match at brunch time in Anaheim. Expect a lot of noise early in the first set at Honda Center.

VVO51.blurb:
Brazil keeps reaching big matches and keeps finishing second or third. Bronze in Paris. Bronze at the 2025 worlds. Losses in the 2025 and 2026 VNL finals. A bronze match is where that story could finally get a happy ending, or one more shrug.

Brazil has qualified as South American champion, so a trip to Anaheim is likely. If the Brazilians play here, fans in yellow will be hard to miss.

The 2:45 PM start gives this match a relaxed afternoon feel. Both teams will be tired, and both will want a medal. That makes for a loose, emotional finish.

VVO52.blurb:
Italy beat Turkey 3-2 in the 2025 world final. Turkey beat Italy 3-2 in the 2026 European final. A third meeting with gold at stake would be hard to resist.

Paola Egonu and Melissa Vargas each scored 28 in Istanbul. Alessia Orro sets Italy's rhythm, and Julio Velasco's team defends the first Games title it won in Paris. Turkey, under Daniele Santarelli, has been closing the gap steadily.

The 10 AM start gives the final a bright, early feel at Honda Center. If the United States or Brazil crash the party, expect the noise to go up another notch.

WLF01.blurb:
One kilogram. That is all that separated Pak Myong-jin from Turkey's Muhammed Furkan Ozbek at the 2026 Worlds, where Pak's 331kg total set a world record and Hampton Morris of the USA sat only three kilos back.

Morris, the Paris 2024 featherweight bronze medalist, set a clean and jerk world record in that same meet. If he makes the team, an American will be chasing gold on the opening night of weightlifting at the 2028 Games.

The Peacock Theater puts every seat in front of a single raised platform, so you watch each attempt head-on, like a stage show where the bar is the star. In a division this tight, one missed jerk reshuffles the podium.

WLF02.blurb:
Zhang Haiqin beat Miranda Ulrey 221kg to 220kg at the 2026 Worlds. Those are the margins a late-night final in Los Angeles is built on.

Ulrey is American, which means a hometown lifter could be chasing the lightest women's title of the Games. A one-kilo gap is a single clean and jerk attempt, and every lifter in the field knows it.

The session starts at 8:50 PM, and the finish comes under the lights of a theater built for award-show finales. Expect the room to hold its breath on each lift and then roar when the bar locks out.

WLF03.blurb:
Record watch applies to both finals in this long afternoon. Pei Xinyi of China won 61kg at the 2026 Worlds with a world-record 254kg, and the IWF called it the best women's performance of 2026.

Then comes 69kg, where North Korea's Song Kuk Hyang lifted 275kg and set a world-record 122kg snatch. Olivia Reeves, the Paris 2024 middleweight champion, is recovering from a stress fracture, and her 2028 category is unconfirmed. If she lands in one of these two classes, the American crowd will have a lifter to follow.

Two medal finals in one session means almost five hours of platform action, with plenty of time to watch the nerves change from lifter to lifter.

WLF04.blurb:
The most interesting lifter in this 75kg final might be the one who may not be allowed to lift. Indonesia's Rizki Juniansyah won Paris 2024 gold at 73kg, the closest division to this new weight class. In fall 2026 he was under an IWF provisional suspension over alleged whereabouts failures, and the Court of Arbitration for Sport declined to lift it. The main case had not been decided in the latest reports.

Without him, North Korea's Ri Ryong-hyon already looks formidable after a 365kg world title in Ningbo. Six kilos back was Indonesia's Rahmat Erwin Abdullah, and Thailand's Weeraphon Wichuma was only four further behind. It is a final worth watching from the first snatch.

WLF05.blurb:
Karlos Nasar put 230kg overhead in Ningbo. That clean and jerk, a world record, helped him to a 415kg total at 95kg, also a world record. The Paris 2024 champion at 89kg is carrying real momentum into this session.

The 85kg final may be wilder. At the 2026 Worlds, Egypt's Abdo Younes and Colombia's Yeison Lopez traded world-record totals back and forth until Younes finished on 390kg. Lopez took silver with 387kg and a 178kg snatch record, so don't expect a quiet rematch.

That is two finals in one long afternoon, with plenty of time between flights to settle in for the next big lift.

WLF06.blurb:
China's Peng Cuiting broke Olivia Reeves's snatch world record twice at the 2026 Worlds, finishing at 126kg, and still came away with silver. That is how deep women's 77kg has become.

Yang Qiuxia took gold with 265kg, and Egypt's Sara Samir, a two-time Games medalist, sealed bronze on her last clean and jerk. Reeves, the Paris 2024 champion and 2025 world champion at 77kg, withdrew from the 2026 meet with a stress fracture. Her 2028 category is not confirmed, which leaves a big question over the home crowd.

The session runs from 8:50 PM, so settle in for a long Thursday night.

WLF07.blurb:
Nineteen kilograms. That is the gap between Liao Guifang's 291kg world-record total in Ningbo and Bahrain's Alina Marushchak, who took silver with 272kg. The IWF called Liao's win a landmark, and it makes her the one to catch at 86kg.

The field has a wild card in Norway's Solfrid Koanda. The Paris 2024 heavyweight champion won the 2025 world title at 86kg despite a back injury, sat out the 2026 Worlds with back problems, and starts her 2028 qualifying in Qatar in December 2026.

It's a late-afternoon session, and the theater's tiered seats should give a clear view of each of Liao's lifts. If Koanda is healthy, the chase is on.

WLF08.blurb:
Akbar Djuraev missed one lift in Ningbo, a 238kg clean and jerk that would have been another world record, and still won by 14kg. His 198kg snatch and 432kg total are already world records, and it was his fourth world title.

Chasing him is a pack that includes Iran's Alireza Nassiri (418kg) and Turkmenistan's Sahzadbek Matyakubow (417kg). The Paris 2024 heavyweight champion, China's Liu Huanhua, finished sixth at 110kg, 27kg behind Djuraev, after fitness problems, so his 2028 form is an open question.

At 8:50 PM on a Friday night, this is a session built for big lifts and big noise.

WLF09.blurb:
Lasha Talakhadze came out of retirement for a fourth straight title. He has won three, including Paris 2024 with a 470kg total. At the 2026 Worlds he did not reach the podium.

The new names are the story now. Iraq's Ali Ammar won the 2026 world +110kg title with 466kg and became Iraq's first world champion in a Games sport, according to the IWF. Iran's Alireza Yousefi was second with a 263kg clean and jerk world record, and Armenia's Varazdat Lalayan, the Paris silver medalist, took bronze. Talakhadze's 225kg snatch world record was annulled after the category changes, and Ammar's 219kg is the recognized mark.

The heaviest men take the platform in the late afternoon, with a bar that bends under the weight.

The last weightlifting medal of the 2028 Games goes to the heaviest women, with Li Yan of China as the one to beat. She won the 2026 world +86kg title with a 317kg total, 31kg ahead of silver medalist Park Hye-jeong, and a world-record 147kg snatch.

The field has a notable gap in the form of Li Wenwen, the Paris 2024 super-heavyweight champion, who was not among the Paris champions entered at the 2026 Worlds. If she returns, it would be a Chinese showdown. If not, the chase is for the rest of the podium.

Saturday night at 8:50 PM is a fitting finish for the sport, with the biggest lifts in the women's program closing out the weightlifting event.

WPO01.blurb:
Water polo has been on the Games program since 1900, the oldest team sport in the lineup, and the 2028 men's tournament starts at 10 AM in a temporary pool built on a Long Beach convention center lot.

The defending champion arrives in turmoil. Serbia won its third straight gold at Paris 2024, but its head coach resigned in May 2026 and 11 players from the European title-winning squad said they would not play under the current federation leadership. Hungary, Spain and Greece will be circling.

The pool is open-air, near the downtown waterfront, so you watch the opening whistle in coastal summer air.

potentialContenders.name: Serbia
potentialContenders.note: Paris 2024 gold medalist, beating Croatia 13-11 in the final. Its roster is in question after the May 2026 coach resignation and player stand-off, which makes it the most intriguing team to watch.

potentialContenders.name: United States

WPO02.blurb:
Serbia lost to Australia, Spain and Hungary in the Paris 2024 group stage and still won gold. That is the lesson of early water polo: nobody is safe, and nobody is dead.

Australia proved it first, beating Serbia in Paris and later winning two of three games against the U.S. men in a 2025 series. Spain arrives as world champion, and Greece as the 2026 World Cup winner.

The afternoon block gives you two matches under open sky at a purpose-built pool, with enough at stake to matter and enough room to watch the favorites sweat.

potentialContenders.name: Australia
potentialContenders.note: Beat Serbia in the Paris 2024 group stage and won two of three against the U.S. men in 2025. Could appear as a group-stage spoiler.

potentialContenders.name: Spain
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2025 world title in Singapore, with captain Felipe Perrone scoring the winner with 18 seconds left.

potentialContenders.name: Greece
potentialContenders.note: Won the 2026 World Cup final 15-14 over Hungary, its first major men's international title. Also took bronze at the 2025 worlds.

potentialContenders.name: Italy

WPO03.blurb:
The home team doesn't need a reminder that it has something to prove. The U.S. men took bronze in Paris, their first medal since 2008, then finished eighth at the 2025 world championships.

If the host is in the water tonight, this is the kind of late-evening crowd that can turn a group match into a pressure test for coach Dejan Udovicic's squad. Spain, the world champion and No. 1 in the April 2026 rankings, is the standard to chase.

The session closes the first day of men's play. It's the last word of the day and a first impression for whoever needs one.

WPO04.blurb:
For the first time, the women's tournament has 12 teams, matching the men. The extra seats mean more countries, more upsets and a Thursday morning with real discovery in it.

The top of the order has been reshuffled. Spain won Paris 2024 gold after winning every match and beating Australia 11-9 in the final. The United States, champion at the three Games before that, missed the podium, and as host it gets a shot at redemption in front of its own crowd.

Get there early. Group-stage water polo rewards the curious, and you can watch the sport's physical chess match up close before elimination starts to bite.

WPO05.blurb:
Greece was the 2025 world champion and the 2025 World Cup winner. In July 2026, it didn't even reach the World Cup Super Final. That is how unsettled women's water polo is heading toward 2028.

The U.S. restored some order there, beating Spain 13-9 for its seventh World Cup title and coach Adam Krikorian's 25th global title. Australia's Matilda Kearns was named best player of the event.

An afternoon session in Long Beach gives you two matches to sort the contenders from the pretenders, in an open-air pool built just for these Games.

Check the ages on the next generation: the U.S. under-20 women won the 2025 world title by beating Spain 16-15, a score that tells you how little defense a hot young group plays. Some of those players could be in this pool by 2028.

Thursday night is a good time to see the field's depth. The Netherlands kept its European title in 2026, Spain's Bea Ortiz scored 25 goals at that tournament even as Spain finished fifth, and the U.S. sits behind both in the rankings.

It's the late slot and two matches to close the day, with the evening coming off the coast.

WPO07.blurb:
Croatia took silver at Paris 2024 and then missed the semifinals at the 2026 European Championships, finishing sixth. A medal pedigree buys nothing at the opening whistle of a group match.

With three groups of four, and only the top two plus the two best third-placed teams advancing, every goal difference counts. Spain, fifth in Europe but No. 1 in the rankings, and Greece, the World Cup champion, will chase margins as much as wins.

It's open-air morning water polo near the Long Beach waterfront, with real stakes and a quick read on who is rising.

WPO08.blurb:
Felipe Perrone scored the deciding goal of the 2025 world final with 18 seconds left, at what was his 13th and final World Championships. Spain now has to find out what comes next, and a mid-tournament Saturday afternoon is where you start to see it.

Alvaro Granados, the 2025 player of the year for both World Aquatics and European Aquatics, is the obvious heir. Italy took third at the 2026 World Cup, where Greece's Panagiotis Tzortzatos was named best goalkeeper, so goals will not come cheap.

Mid-group matches shape tournaments quietly, and two games back to back give you time to read it.

WPO09.blurb:
Hungary has been runner-up in three straight major finals: the 2025 world final to Spain, the January 2026 European final to Serbia (10-7), and the 2026 World Cup final to Greece, 15-14, on a goal with 12.7 seconds left.

Saturday night gives you a team that keeps reaching the last dance, and a field full of teams that would love to stop it. Serbia, Hungary's conqueror in January, and Australia, which beat Serbia in Paris, could both be in the mix.

Three groups, with room for a third-placed team to sneak through. By the evening session, that arithmetic starts to feel real.

WPO10.blurb:
The Netherlands wins in Europe, Hungary keeps reaching finals, and Greece, the 2025 world champion, was missing from the World Cup Super Final. Sunday morning is when that jumble starts to sort itself out.

The Dutch kept their European title in Funchal in 2026 by beating Hungary, and took bronze in Paris. Hungary took silver at the 2025 worlds. The U.S., with a pipeline of under-20 world champions, is the host looking to climb back.

This is the easiest day to find a seat and a good day to pick your favorite before the knockouts.

WPO11.blurb:
Australia lost the Paris 2024 final 11-9 to Spain. At the 2026 World Cup Super Final in Sydney, the hosts took third, and Matilda Kearns was named best player.

That makes Sunday afternoon a good chance to see one of the sport's most dangerous teams without a medal on the line. It's also the first Games with 12 women's teams, so the groups hold teams you haven't seen before alongside the usual names.

Spain tops the 2026 rankings, with Italy and France at sixth and eighth, so the contrast should be easy to read.

WPO12.blurb:
The tournament has a new ending: for the first time, the women's gold medal match will follow the men's, closing water polo on July 23. Sunday night's group matches are the first draft of that story.

The U.S. is the reference point, coached by Adam Krikorian, whose 2026 World Cup win was his 25th global title, and with goalkeeper Amanda Longan, named best keeper of that Super Final. Spain, which lost that final 13-9, has a score to settle.

If you want to say you saw the finalists before anyone knew they'd get there, evenings like this are how.

WPO13.blurb:
Dusan Mandic scored 26 goals at Paris 2024 and was MVP. In January 2026 he scored four more in the European final, a 10-7 win over Hungary. If he's in the water here, Monday morning is a rare chance to see a scorer like that up close.

The big if is Serbia itself. Former captain Vladimir Vujasinovic was named head coach in June 2026 after Uros Stevanovic resigned and 11 players said they would not play for the national team under the current federation president.

Late-group Mondays matter: every result nudges the quarterfinal board.

Third place can be enough. With the two best of the three third-placed teams going through, a match that looks like an afterthought can be the last chance for a former medalist to survive.

Late group play is when you find out who is desperate. Croatia, the Paris silver medalist, was sixth at the 2026 Europeans. The U.S. men were eighth at the 2025 worlds. Italy took third at the 2026 World Cup and Australia fourth.

In other words, the scoreboard matters more than the pedigree.

Greece had never won a major men's international title until July 2026, when captain Stylianos Argyropoulos scored with 12.7 seconds left to beat Hungary 15-14 in the World Cup final.

Greece also took bronze at the 2025 worlds and the 2026 Europeans, beating Italy 12-5 in the latter. By Monday night, it isn't a surprise anymore. It's a target.

A late-evening group session in Long Beach is a good place to see how a first-time champion carries the pressure. Serbia, Hungary and Italy would each test it.

The top two in each of three groups advance automatically, along with the two best third-placed teams. That makes goal difference a currency. Spain, ranked No. 1 in 2026, and a United States side that beat the Spaniards 13-9 in the World Cup final are the names to track if their groups run down to this day.

You're outdoors in a temporary pool stadium on the Long Beach Convention Center lot, with whistles and splashes carrying over the downtown waterfront.

The field is a puzzle. Greece, the 2025 world champion, missed the 2026 World Cup final stage entirely, while the Netherlands kept its European crown. Teams that look comfortable on paper can still be one bad quarter from the wrong side of the third-place line.

The Long Beach sun is at its hottest around this slot, and the open-air pool makes it feel more like a summer final than a prelim.

Greece, the 2026 World Cup champion, is the team everyone else has to figure out.

The evening slot brings long shadows across the pool, and every goal sounds louder when the outcome is one possession away.

WPO26.blurb:
Twelve point seven seconds. That's how long Greece had left when it beat Hungary 15-14 in the 2026 World Cup final, finally winning a major men's title after five lost finals. The question now is whether Greece can win the one that matters.

The obstacle is Serbia, which has taken three straight gold medals and arrives under a new coach and with questions about its roster. Dusan Mandic won MVP at Paris and the 2026 Europeans, though his 2028 plans are unconfirmed. Hungary has lost three straight major finals and would love one more crack.

At 3 PM in Long Beach, with everything on the line, even a goalless minute will feel loud.

WPO27.blurb:
The Netherlands won bronze at Paris 2024 and came home from the 2026 Europeans with gold. A third-place match still hurts. Both teams lost a semifinal a couple of days earlier, and one of them will leave Long Beach with something to hang on the wall.

The field is full of storylines. Hungary lost two world finals to Greece and a European final to the Dutch. Australia's Tilly Kearns was the 2026 World Cup MVP. Spain or the United States could even drop in, if a semifinal goes sideways.

The pool is open to the Sunday morning air, and the whole thing feels like a warm-up for the gold match later today.

WPO28.blurb:
For the first time, the women close the water polo program, playing the last match after the men. That puts the final whistle of the whole sport, and a good share of the crowd, behind this one.

Spain won in Paris 11-9 over Australia, its first gold after silver in Tokyo. Then the United States beat Spain 13-9 at the 2026 World Cup, with Adam Krikorian collecting his 25th global title. A rematch in Long Beach would carry the weight of three straight Games of American gold before Paris.

Greece, the 2025 world champion, is hunting for a first women's gold, and the Netherlands is the reigning European champion. Anything is possible.

WRE01.blurb:
The reigning women's 50kg champion may not be the American on the mat. Sarah Hildebrandt won Paris 2024 gold, but the U.S. sent 18-year-old Morgan Turner to the 2026 World Championships, where she lost in the round of 16. Who carries the host nation's hopes in July is a live question.

This is a morning for discovery. Three brackets shrink from sixteen to four, and a single slip ends a medal run. Japan's Koto Gomi, the 2026 world champion at Greco-Roman 60kg, pinned Iran's Ali Ahmadi Vafa in the final. Early rounds at 130kg are where Iran's heavyweights begin their march.

The mats sit inside a temporary arena in a downtown exhibition hall, so you are close to every grip fight.

WRE02.blurb:
Darius Vitek has now lost two straight world finals at Greco-Roman 130kg, 7-2 in 2025 and 8-0 in 2026, both to Iranians. If he reaches this hour again, the Hungarian will have a very large point to prove.

Sixty minutes, three weight classes, and four wrestlers per bracket in the semifinals. Win and you're wrestling for gold the next night. Lose and you're in a bronze match with the clock already running.

The evening crowd arrives to watch Japan's Greco-Roman 60kg talent and a women's 50kg field that includes Paris 2024 champion Sarah Hildebrandt if she qualifies. Expect the hall to get loud whenever a throw lands.

WRE03.blurb:
Kiryl Maskevich needed a point with 20 seconds left to beat Azerbaijan's Murad Ahmadiyev 4-3 at the 2026 World Championships, then went on to win the title at Greco-Roman 97kg. That is how thin the margins run in this weight class.

This morning has three brackets in action plus repechages for the day before, so the mats stay busy. The 97kg side features Iran's Mohammadhadi Saravi, Paris 2024 champion, who fell to bronze in 2026.

Over at women's 53kg, Japan's depth is the story. Paris 2024 champion Akari Fujinami, 2025 world champion Haruna Murayama and Moe Kiyooka form a crowded line for one spot. Ecuador's Lucia Yepez is the opponent they all need to solve.

WRE04.blurb:
The first gold medals of the Games in wrestling are handed out here, three of them in one night. That's the hook.

Start with women's 50kg, where Sarah Hildebrandt won Paris 2024 gold in a final reshaped by a weigh-in disqualification. Greco-Roman 130kg follows, with Iran's two straight world champions looking to turn that run into the top step. At 60kg, Japan's Koto Gomi and Kenichiro Fumita give Japan a deep pool.

Between the medal matches, semifinals at 77kg, 97kg and women's 53kg keep the mats full. Plan on three and a half hours of nonstop wrestling, with a loud, partisan crowd.

WRE05.blurb:
Helen Maroulis lost a 4-2 quarterfinal to Japan's Sena Nagamoto at the 2026 World Championships and still left with bronze. That's what repechage can do. One loss in a single-elimination bracket does not always end a medal run.

This is a morning of volume. Greco-Roman 67kg, 87kg and women's 57kg all start here, and the 67kg bracket alone drew 31 wrestlers in 2026. Iran's Saeid Esmaeili, who won Paris 2024 gold and the 2025 and 2026 world titles, is a heavy favorite on form.

Semen Novikov of Bulgaria, the Paris 2024 champion, won the 2026 world title at 87kg. Seeing a returning champion early, before the pressure builds, is a good reason to buy a morning ticket.

WRE06.blurb:
Artur Sargsian owns world medals from 2021, 2025 and 2026, with silver in each of the last two years. He lost 3-1 to Mohammadhadi Saravi in 2025 and 7-1 to Kiryl Maskevich in 2026. Gold at Greco-Roman 97kg keeps slipping just out of reach.

He is the best story in a night built around medal matches at 77kg, 97kg and women's 53kg. Japan's Nao Kusaka, Paris 2024 champion at 77kg, has been chased by Armenia's Malkhas Amoyan and Azerbaijan's Sanan Suleymanov, the last two world champions.

The semifinals at 67kg, 87kg and women's 57kg fill the gaps. It adds up to more than three hours of high-level wrestling in a hall built for the Games.

WRE07.blurb:
Spencer Lee already knows what a Games final feels like. He lost the Paris 2024 57kg final to Japan's Rei Higuchi, and if the American qualifies, the rematch would give the host crowd a ready-made storyline.

Men's freestyle arrives with a different rhythm than Greco-Roman, with more scrambling and more leg attacks. The morning handles the round of 16 and quarterfinals at 57kg, 86kg and women's 62kg, with repechages for the day before.

The name to find at 86kg is Kyle Dake, the 2026 world champion, who beat Azerbaijan's Arsenii Dzhioev in the final. Watch how he handles Bulgaria's Magomed Ramazanov, the Paris 2024 champion, if they meet.

WRE08.blurb:
Greco-Roman says goodbye tonight. The last two Greco-Roman medal matches, at 67kg and 87kg, close a discipline that began four days ago.

Saeid Esmaeili has Paris 2024 gold and the 2025 and 2026 world titles at 67kg, and the field keeps coming at him, including Azerbaijan's Hasrat Jafarov. At 87kg, Bulgaria's Semen Novikov is the reigning Games champion and 2026 world champion, while Serbia's Aleksandr Komarov won in 2025.

The women's 57kg medal matches bring Tsugumi Sakurai and Helen Maroulis back into view. Men's freestyle semifinals at 57kg, 86kg and women's 62kg are in the mix too, so Rei Higuchi, Spencer Lee and Kyle Dake take their first big steps.

WRE09.blurb:
Amit Elor won Paris 2024 gold at 20, the youngest U.S. wrestling gold medalist at the Games. Since then she moved up to 72kg, announced a pregnancy in September 2025 and won the 72kg U.S. World Team Trials Challenge in May 2026, three months after giving birth. Whether she returns to 68kg for Los Angeles is one of the sport's most intriguing storylines.

Her weight class opens in a morning session that also starts men's freestyle 74kg and 125kg. Uzbekistan's Razambek Zhamalov and Japan's Kota Takahashi, the 2025 world champion, headline 74kg.

At 125kg, Iran's Amir Hossein Zare is the one to beat after back-to-back world titles.

WRE10.blurb:
Two Japanese champions defend at once. Rei Higuchi at 57kg and Sakura Motoki at 62kg both won gold at Paris 2024, and both medal matches land in this session. Japan won eight wrestling golds that week, and this is where the program shows its depth.

The American angle is sharper. Kyle Dake won the 2026 world title at 86kg, and a gold-medal match for him in front of a home crowd would be a major moment. Bulgaria's Magomed Ramazanov, the Paris 2024 champion, is the man who must stand in his way.

Before all that, the semifinals at 74kg, 125kg and women's 68kg fill the early hours.

WRE11.blurb:
Nobody can say for sure who won the 2026 world final at 97kg, at least not from the reports. One results list has Akhmed Tazhudinov beating Georgia's Givi Matcharashvili 2-0 for gold, while a FloWrestling standings page lists Kyle Snyder as gold. Either way, the weight class is packed with names.

Snyder won the 2025 world title, and Abdulrashid Sadulaev, a two-time gold medalist, won the 2026 European title. Tazhudinov took Paris 2024 gold.

At 65kg the field splits between Iran's Rahman Amouzad and the American Bo Bassett, the 2026 world champion. Add women's 76kg and repechages for the classes that medal later today, and this morning moves fast.

WRE12.blurb:
Geno Petriashvili beat Amir Hossein Zare for the Paris 2024 gold at 125kg. Since then, Zare has won back-to-back world titles. If both reach the 2028 final, Los Angeles could see a rematch of the highest order.

Whether Gable Steveson, the Tokyo 2020 champion, enters the picture is unclear. He has said he'd like to win gold in 2028, but in 2026 he said UFC is his priority.

The night also holds the women's 68kg medal matches, and the question of whether Amit Elor returns to the weight she won at Paris. Kennedy Blades was entered at 68kg in the 2026 U.S. Final X series, which sets up a tough battle for the American spot.

First up are semifinals at 65kg, 97kg and women's 76kg.

WRE13.blurb:
The final session of wrestling at the Games has three gold medals on the line, all in the middle of Sunday morning. Whatever happens, the mats here will be cleared for the last time.

Bo Bassett of the USA won the 2026 world title at 65kg, a year after teammate Real Woods took bronze. They could face Japan's Kotaro Kiyooka, the Paris 2024 champion, who lost the 2025 world final to Iran's Rahman Amouzad.

At 97kg the story is still being written. Tazhudinov, Snyder and Sadulaev have all been major names, and the 2026 world final results conflict across sources.

At women's 76kg, Japan's Yuka Kagami won in Paris over Kennedy Blades, but Blades competed at 68kg in 2026.
